2026-01-04.headline: Cloud-native Windows tutorial drops solution comparison and Windows 10 support note
2026-01-04.overview: This quiet period contains one Intune documentation-only edit. The Cloud Native Windows Endpoints tutorial removed its tip, comparison table, and Windows 10 support callout; the evidence does not indicate a product-behavior or availability change.
2026-01-04.adminImpact: Administrators evaluating deployment approaches should use the linked Windows in cloud configuration and cloud-native endpoint documentation directly. No configuration change or migration action is supported by this update.

keyChanges.title: Cloud Native Windows Endpoints comparison content removed
keyChanges.detail: The tutorial no longer includes the tip linking to Windows in cloud configuration, the table contrasting a custom, Microsoft-recommended configuration with the pre-built guided scenario, or the statement that the two approaches can be combined. It also removed the included Windows 10 support callout. This is an ordinary documentation clarification, not evidence of changed Intune functionality.

2026-01-05.headline: Hotpatch deployment prerequisites are spelled out as Windows driver guidance is consolidated
2026-01-05.overview: 5 January was a documentation-led Windows update day with no Message Center item. Intune added guidance for deploying restart-free Hotpatch security updates through Autopatch and a consolidated Windows Driver update policy article. The Hotpatch guidance lists Windows 11 Enterprise 24H2 or later, the latest baseline, VBS, an Intune Hotpatch policy, and Autopatch and licensing prerequisites. Driver guidance now covers automatic recommended-driver approval, manual approval, and reporting requirements. Other changes mainly repaired links, clarified that each update policy has its own prerequisites, and retired older driver and quality update page names. Planned Android, Apple, Lenovo, and managed-app filter capabilities remain roadmap items; the supplied evidence does not establish general availability or a new tenant behavior change.
2026-01-05.adminImpact: Do not treat the new articles as launch or general-availability notices. For Hotpatch planning, validate Autopatch and licensing eligibility, Windows 11 Enterprise 24H2 or later, the latest baseline, VBS, and the Intune Windows quality update policy with Hotpatch enabled. For driver reports, enable Tenant administration > Connectors and tokens > Windows data > Enable features that require Windows diagnostic data in processor configuration. Update saved references from driver-updates-overview.md to driver-updates.md and from quality-updates-policy.md to quality-updates.md. Treat the Android, Apple, Lenovo, and managed-app filter entries as future testing considerations only.

keyChanges.title: Hotpatch policy article defines a restart-free Autopatch workflow
keyChanges.detail: New Intune device-updates guidance says Hotpatch security updates are Monthly B release security updates that install and take effect without requiring a restart. It describes Hotpatch as an extension of Windows Update that requires Autopatch to create and deploy hotpatches, while existing update-ring configurations continue to be honored. The article lists Windows 11 Enterprise 24H2 or later, the latest baseline release, VBS, an Intune Windows quality update policy with Hotpatch enabled, and licensing requirements

keyChanges.title: Consolidated driver policy guidance separates automatic and manual approvals
keyChanges.detail: The new Windows Driver update management article documents automatic approval and deployment of each new recommended driver version, plus a manual mode in which newer versions remain inactive until an administrator approves them. It also describes reviewing available updates and selectively approving, pausing, or declining them.

keyChanges.title: Driver update reports specify the diagnostic-data prerequisite and admin-center path
keyChanges.detail: The reports guidance now says Windows diagnostic data must be enabled for Windows Driver update reports. The documented procedure is Microsoft Intune admin center > Tenant administration > Connectors and tokens > Windows data, then turn on Enable features that require Windows diagnostic data in processor configuration.

keyChanges.title: Legacy driver update overview URL is retired after consolidation
keyChanges.detail: The former driver-updates-overview.md article was removed as part of the consolidation into driver-updates.md. Administrators should update saved links and internal references; the change is a documentation retirement, not evidence of changed driver-policy behavior.

keyChanges.title: Android, Apple, Lenovo, and managed-app capabilities remain in development
keyChanges.detail: The in-development page adds planned capabilities including a Lenovo Device Orchestration link in the Intune admin center for Windows 11, Android settings catalog filtering by Fully managed (COBO), Corporate-owned work profile (COPE), or Dedicated (COSU), Apple DDM assignment filters for iOS/iPadOS and macOS, and additional Device Management Type values for managed apps. These entries describe planned work, not current availability.

2026-01-06.headline: MDT retirement demands task-sequence cleanup as EPM adds single-session AVD support
2026-01-06.overview: This was a documentation-heavy day rather than a broad Intune feature launch. The clearest operational changes were Configuration Manager's explicit MDT retirement warning, newly documented Endpoint Privilege Management support for Azure Virtual Desktop single-session VMs, and sharper Windows Update boundaries for Microsoft Entra registered devices. Feature Updates guidance also clarified cloud, licensing, and edition prerequisites. Separately, a Message Center notice previews February additions to Managed Home Screen role permissions.
2026-01-06.adminImpact: Remove MDT task-sequence steps before removing MDT integration, check device join type before assigning WUfB DS-backed update policies, and validate that virtual desktops are AVD single-session VMs before onboarding them to EPM. For Feature Updates, verify public-cloud tenancy, Intune Plan 1, Autopatch entitlement, and Windows edition requirements. The February Managed Home Screen RBAC change requires no immediate action.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager now documents MDT as retired and unsupported
keyChanges.detail: Retirement: the release notes state that MDT Standalone and MDT integration with Configuration Manager are no longer supported. Administrators must remove all MDT task-sequence steps and then remove MDT integration to prevent task-sequence corruption and modification failures. The guidance points to Windows Autopilot or supported Configuration Manager operating-system deployment as alternatives.

keyChanges.title: EPM support now includes Azure Virtual Desktop single-session VMs
keyChanges.detail: Support expansion: the EPM FAQ replaces the previous Azure Virtual Desktop unsupported statement with a supported-platform list that includes Azure Virtual Desktop single-session VMs, added in January 2026, alongside Windows 365. Confirm the VM is single-session before onboarding it.

keyChanges.title: Microsoft Entra registered devices cannot use WUfB DS-backed policies
keyChanges.detail: Changed scope guidance: the Windows updates overview states that Microsoft Entra registered devices cannot use Feature Updates, Quality Updates, Driver Updates, or Hotpatch policies because they rely on the Windows Update for Business Deployment Service. Windows Update client policies and update rings remain supported for those devices.

keyChanges.title: Feature Updates prerequisites now separate cloud, licensing, and edition limits
keyChanges.detail: Prerequisite clarification: Feature Updates policies are supported only in the public cloud, not GCC High or DoD. Intune Plan 1 covers core policy creation and assignment, while gradual rollout and optional feature updates require a Windows license with the Autopatch entitlement. Windows Enterprise LTSC is unsupported by Feature Updates policies; the guidance suggests alternatives such as WSUS or Configuration Manager.

keyChanges.title: February release will add two Managed Home Screen RBAC permissions
keyChanges.detail: Preview / plan for change: the Message Center says the February Intune release will add `TemporarilySuspendManagedHomeScreen` and `RestoreManagedHomeScreen` to the School Administrator and Help Desk Operator built-in roles. No administrator action is required, though role assignments and internal documentation can be reviewed for the future access change.

2026-01-07.headline: Windows driver approvals and Hotpatch guidance sharpen Intune update planning
2026-01-07.overview: The substantive work centered on Windows update administration rather than a new Intune policy launch. A new Windows Driver Update Management overview documents approval, pause, and automatic-versus-manual deployment choices; refreshed prerequisites state public-cloud scope, Intune Plan 1, and a Windows license with the Autopatch entitlement. Autopatch guidance says it orchestrates existing Intune policies and should not be paired with custom rings, while the quality-updates overview folds Hotpatch into the policy description and says eligible security patches can apply without a reboot. Feature-update reporting also gains a precise initial-scan note. Most other edits were link, title, formatting, or wording maintenance: the removed Markdown driver FAQ was an md-to-yml migration, not a capability retirement. Admin Tasks should not be treated as confirmed GA: its article removes the public-preview label, but the in-development entry still says general availability is forthcoming and supplies no date.
2026-01-07.adminImpact: Before deploying driver-update policies, confirm public-cloud scope, Intune Plan 1 for core policy functions, and a Windows license that includes the Autopatch entitlement. Choose automatic approval only when recommended drivers should deploy without intervention; otherwise plan manual review of new versions. Keep custom rings off Autopatch-managed devices. In feature-update reports, expect Last Scanned Time to remain Not scanned yet until a user logs on and USO initiates a scan, and configure data collection before expecting report data. For Enterprise App Management catalog apps, continue validating compliance, authorization, authenticity, and integrity independently. For co-managed Windows 10 devices, follow the updated FAQ's recommendation to move the Windows Update workload to Intune,

keyChanges.title: Windows Driver Update Management overview makes approval models explicit
keyChanges.detail: A new overview page describes Windows Driver Update Management as a controlled workflow: admins can review, approve, or pause updates. Automatic-approval policies deploy each new driver version identified as recommended, while manual-approval policies add newer versions but leave them inactive until approved. This is new documentation for the capability, not evidence of a new service launch.

keyChanges.title: Quality-update guidance folds Hotpatch alongside expedited updates
keyChanges.detail: The Windows updates index removes the standalone Hotpatch block and folds it into quality updates. The revised text defines monthly cumulative updates as security and reliability updates, with expedited updates able to override deferrals and deadlines and Hotpatch applying eligible security patches without reboot. This clarifies placement and documented behavior; it is not a separate Intune policy launch.

keyChanges.title: Autopatch guidance says its own rings replace custom assignments
keyChanges.detail: The revised comparison describes Windows Autopatch as integrated with Intune and orchestrating existing update policies instead of introducing new policy types. It says Autopatch creates and manages its own rings, so administrators shouldn't assign custom rings to Autopatch devices. This is guidance clarification, not evidence of a new Autopatch rollout.
keyChanges.product: Windows Autopatch and Intune update rings

keyChanges.title: Feature-update reporting clarifies the initial Last Scanned Time state
keyChanges.detail: The Feature Updates article now states that End user update status Last Scanned Time returns Not scanned yet until a user logs on and Update Session Orchestrator initiates a scan. It also points readers to the dedicated feature-update reports article. The edit clarifies report interpretation and navigation rather than announcing changed scan behavior.

keyChanges.title: Enterprise App Management expands its catalog due-diligence disclaimer
keyChanges.detail: The catalog guidance now explicitly says Microsoft doesn't assert compliance, authorization, authenticity, or integrity for apps distributed through Intune; customers remain responsible for their requirements. It also states that Service Level Objectives are guidelines, not guarantees. This is security and due-diligence guidance, not a change to catalog app validation.

2026-01-08.headline: Autopatch entitlement and driver-blocking settings anchor revised Intune update guidance
2026-01-08.overview: The period was dominated by documentation consolidation rather than a demonstrated product release. Intune’s feature, quality, and driver update material now points to shared Autopatch-backed prerequisites, while driver policy guidance spells out settings that can block driver installation. Separate guidance emphasizes Platform Single Sign-On for macOS registration, and Endpoint Privilege Management support for Azure Virtual Desktop single-session VMs remains listed as in development.
2026-01-08.adminImpact: Review the consolidated Windows update prerequisites and verify the exact driver-blocking settings before rollout. Check device join state because Microsoft Entra registered devices remain limited to Windows Update client policies and update rings, and ensure the Microsoft Account Sign-In Assistant service is not disabled where applicable. Treat EPM support on AVD as roadmap information only. Consider PSSO and SSO-extension enforcement in macOS registration plans as security guidance, not a newly announced enrollment requirement. Refresh links to the removed standalone driver overview article, and do not interpret removal of the gradual-rollout warning alone as proof of availability.

keyChanges.title: Windows update policies adopt shared Autopatch entitlement wording
keyChanges.detail: The Intune index describes feature update, quality update, and driver update policies as using the same cloud orchestration layer and sharing prerequisites. Licensing wording changed from Windows Enterprise E3/E5 or equivalent to a Windows license that includes the Autopatch entitlement; the Microsoft Account Sign-In Assistant remains listed as a service requirement. This is documentation consolidation and terminology clarification, not evidence of changed backend behavior.

keyChanges.title: Driver guidance identifies the settings that can block installation
keyChanges.detail: The Driver Updates Policy article warns that update rings and Settings Catalog policies can block Windows driver updates. It specifies Windows driver = Allow in update ring policy and Exclude WU Drivers in Quality Update = Allow Windows Update drivers in Settings Catalog; the guidance says both settings default to configurations that allow drivers. Review applicable policies before deployment.

keyChanges.title: Entra registered devices remain limited to update rings and client policies
keyChanges.detail: The Windows updates index clarifies that Microsoft Entra registered devices aren't supported for Feature updates, Quality updates, or Driver updates policy types using the Autopatch backend. For those devices, update management remains limited to Windows Update client policies and update rings. The edit moves an existing limitation into a callout rather than announcing a new restriction.

keyChanges.title: Platform Single Sign-On is elevated in macOS registration guidance
keyChanges.detail: The macOS endpoints guide calls Platform Single Sign-On the most secure approach for device attestation and registration, and describes enforcing the SSO extension during registration as a Zero Trust best practice that replaces traditional Company Portal registration. This is security guidance, not evidence of a new enrollment capability.

keyChanges.title: Endpoint Privilege Management support for AVD is listed as in development
keyChanges.detail: The Endpoint Privilege Management roadmap page restores an entry for deploying EPM policies to users on Azure Virtual Desktop single-session virtual machines. The entry says EPM elevation policies will work in that environment when support is added, but provides no general-availability indication or date.

2026-01-09.headline: Certificate Sync guidance and expedited-update prerequisites sharpen Intune patch planning
2026-01-09.overview: The 9 January period is dominated by substantive Microsoft Learn reorganization around Windows update policy surfaces and Mobile Threat Defense connector guidance. The most actionable material documents prerequisites that can block expedited quality updates and adds certificate-inventory sharing details for iOS/iPadOS MTD connectors. New feature-update guidance also clarifies safeguard holds and persistent version targeting, while Autopatch documentation reinforces service-managed update rings. The supplied evidence shows no Message Center announcements, removals, retirements, or confirmed preview/general-availability changes; reviewer-metadata edits have no administrator impact.
2026-01-09.adminImpact: Before deploying expedited quality updates, compare update-ring and Group Policy settings with the documented prerequisites. For MTD connectors, review whether certificate inventory should be shared and account for device check-in timing, especially on personally owned iOS/iPadOS devices. Avoid assigning custom update rings to Autopatch-managed devices according to the revised guidance. Use the new feature-update procedure and the updated Properties Catalog applicability list, which now includes Microsoft Entra hybrid joined devices.

keyChanges.title: Quality update guidance spells out expedited-update prerequisites and conflicts
keyChanges.detail: The new Windows quality update policy how-to says Beta and Dev preview builds aren't supported with expedited updates, so Enable pre-release builds should be Not configured. It recommends Automatic update behavior = Reset to default and a notification setting other than Turn off all notifications, including restart warnings. It also identifies CorpWuURL, AutoUpdateCfg, DeferFeatureUpdates, and Disable Dual Scan as Group Policy settings that can interfere and should be restored to device defaults. This is explicit s

keyChanges.title: MTD connector guidance documents certificate synchronization for iOS/iPadOS
keyChanges.detail: The connector setup guidance now documents Enable Certificate Sync for iOS/iPadOS devices, allowing an MTD partner to request installed-certificate lists for threat analysis. Certificate data is updated during device check-in. Personally owned devices have a separate full-inventory setting: On shares managed and unmanaged certificates, while Off sends no certificate data; the setting has no effect on corporate devices, for which Intune sends both types when requested.

keyChanges.title: Autopatch guidance emphasizes service-managed update rings
keyChanges.detail: The Windows Update rings policy overview says rings control deferrals, restart settings, deadlines, active hours, and notifications, and can stage test, pilot, and production groups. Its Autopatch note says the service may create and maintain rings for rollout cadence and restart behavior, so administrators typically shouldn't assign custom rings to Autopatch-managed devices. The removal of the earlier Microsoft Entra registered-device limitations section is a documentation change, not evidence of expanded support.
keyChanges.product: Intune Windows Update rings and Windows Autopatch

keyChanges.title: New feature-update guidance clarifies holds, version freezes, and deployment steps
keyChanges.detail: The new Windows feature update policies article states that a device already running a later Windows version remains on that version, while a safeguard hold blocks installation until the known issue is resolved. Unlike an update-ring pause, which expires after 35 days, the feature-updates policy remains until modified or removed. The article also says cloud-deployed feature updates automatically include the latest monthly quality update and documents the Devices > Windows > Windows updates > Feature updates >Create

keyChanges.title: Driver-update documentation adds controlled approval guidance
keyChanges.detail: The revised Manage Windows driver updates article explains that OEM driver and firmware releases can affect reliability, security, and hardware support. It describes Intune driver updates policies as supporting automatic or manual approval workflows, giving administrators a documented way to review recommended drivers before deployment rather than deploying them automatically.

2026-01-12.headline: Expedited Windows quality updates and PowerShell installers sharpen Intune operations
2026-01-12.overview: The strongest operational signal is newly explicit guidance for expediting eligible Windows security updates in Intune, including a required Update Health Tools check for Windows versions earlier than 24H2. The period also adds a gated feature-update migration sequence, a co-management timing caveat, a Hybrid Entra joined Autopilot OOBE issue, and a PowerShell installer workflow for Win32 apps. Most remaining Update Rings edits are table, heading, navigation, or link restructuring rather than evidence of policy-behavior changes; no preview or general-availability transition is identified.
2026-01-12.adminImpact: Verify Update Health Tools on pre-24H2 devices before using expedited policies and use Update Rings for ordinary monthly quality updates. For feature-update migrations, wait for all devices to show OfferReady before setting ring feature deferral to 0, and plan for the temporary co-management handoff delay. Review Enrollment Status Page profiles using Allow OOBE Updates for Hybrid Entra joined Autopilot deployments, and account for execution context and return codes when designing Win32 script installers. Do not change policy solely because of routine reference-formatting edits.

keyChanges.title: Expedited quality updates get explicit scope and prerequisites
keyChanges.detail: The Quality Updates Policy article now describes expedited Windows quality updates in Intune. Only eligible Windows security updates can be expedited; regular monthly quality updates remain an Update Rings workload. The guidance says expedited policies temporarily override deferrals and other settings, select one update by release date, and require Microsoft Update Health Tools on Windows versions earlier than 24H2, installable through KB4023057 or manually.

keyChanges.title: Feature-update migrations gain an OfferReady checkpoint
keyChanges.detail: Feature Updates Policy guidance now warns that applying update-ring deferrals alongside a feature-updates policy can delay an update because both policy conditions must be met. The prescribed sequence is to create and assign the feature-update policy, wait until the Windows feature updates Organizational report shows OfferReady for all devices, and then set Feature update deferral period (days) in the update ring to 0. Windows Update processing can take up to 10 minutes. This is migration guidance, not a stated new

keyChanges.title: Hybrid Entra joined Autopilot OOBE may miss quality updates
keyChanges.detail: The Windows Autopilot Known Issues page adds an issue, dated January 13, 2026, in which Quality Update scans offered during OOBE may time out during Hybrid Entra joined provisioning when Allow OOBE Updates is configured in the Enrollment Status Page profile. Affected devices do not receive those Quality Updates during OOBE. The issue affects KB5041571 and later and is under investigation.

keyChanges.title: Win32 app installs can use PowerShell scripts
keyChanges.detail: The What's New entry for the week of January 12 describes a PowerShell script installer for Win32 apps. Administrators can upload a script instead of specifying a command line; Intune packages it with the app content, runs it in the same context as the app installer, and reports installation results from the script's return code. The workflow supports prerequisite checks, configuration changes, and post-install actions.

keyChanges.title: Co-management handoffs may delay feature-update enforcement
keyChanges.detail: Feature Updates Policy now adds a co-management warning: when the Windows Update policies workload is newly configured for Intune, feature-update policies might not take effect immediately. The temporary delay can initially allow devices to update to a later feature-update version than the one configured in policy. This is a rollout caveat added to the guidance, not a stated change to policy behavior.
keyChanges.product: Intune Feature Updates policy and co-management

2026-01-13.headline: Hotpatch and expedited guidance sharpen Windows update eligibility and policy boundaries
2026-01-13.overview: Windows update guidance is the period’s substantive center. New and revised Intune articles distinguish routine monthly servicing through Windows Update and update rings from targeted expedite policies and Hotpatch, while adding concrete prerequisites and eligibility limits. The evidence indicates documentation restructuring rather than a new general-availability announcement; the Quality Updates Policy page is marked removed, while Defender for Endpoint guidance is clarified around risk-based compliance.
2026-01-13.adminImpact: Rebaseline Windows servicing procedures: routine monthly updates do not require a Windows quality updates policy, and update rings retain control of deferrals, deadlines, restarts, and notifications. Use an expedite policy for one urgent eligible security update, and reserve quality updates, Autopatch, and Hotpatch workflows for advanced orchestration or reporting. Before expedited deployment, check that Enable pre-release builds is Not configured, Automatic update behavior is Reset to default, and Change notification update level is not Turn off all notifications, including restart warnings. Restore the listed conflicting Group Policy settings to Not configured; Windows versions earlier than 24H2 require Update Health Tools. For Hotpatch, verify VBS eligibility and note that Arm64 support

keyChanges.title: Quality updates policy is optional for routine monthly servicing
keyChanges.detail: Revised Quality Updates guidance says devices without a Windows quality updates policy continue receiving monthly quality updates through standard Windows Update behavior. Update rings and Windows Update client policies still control deferrals, deadlines, restarts, and notifications. Create the policy for cloud-based orchestration, Windows Autopatch-managed deployments, Hotpatch, or policy-based reporting; an expedite policy can be used without creating one. This is a documentation clarification of policy scope,not

keyChanges.title: Expedite guidance is now a separate, targeted policy path
keyChanges.detail: The article formerly titled Windows quality updates policy is now Expedite Windows quality updates. It defines expedite policies as accelerating one specific supported Windows security update, bypassing deferrals and normal deployment timing without pausing or editing monthly policies. The guidance describes the path as targeted and time-bound, with no change to future quality-update deployment.

keyChanges.title: Hotpatch guidance makes VBS mandatory and marks Arm64 preview
keyChanges.detail: The new Hotpatch article documents eligible Monthly B security updates taking effect without an immediate restart through Windows Autopatch. It states that VBS must be enabled for a device to be offered Hotpatch updates and explicitly identifies Arm64 device support as public preview. The article also points administrators to Hotpatch quality update reporting.
keyChanges.product: Intune – Hotpatch with Windows quality updates

keyChanges.title: Driver guidance adds staged approvals and one-policy targeting
keyChanges.detail: Driver Updates Policy guidance now asks administrators to assign approval ownership, stage deployments through test groups, align driver and firmware cadences, and ensure each device is targeted by only one driver update policy. It also spells out automatic approval behavior: new recommended drivers are approved and deployed automatically, the prior recommended version moves to the other drivers list, previously approved drivers remain approved, and Windows Update installs only the latest approved version newerกว่า

keyChanges.title: Defender integration guidance ties high risk to compliance access
keyChanges.detail: The revised integration article is retitled Integrate Microsoft Defender for Endpoint with Intune for Device Compliance and explicitly frames Defender as a Mobile Threat Defense solution. It describes real-time device-risk assessment, with compromised high-risk devices automatically marked noncompliant and blocked from corporate resources. The guidance also requires sufficient Intune permissions, citing Endpoint Security Manager as an example; this is clarified integration guidance rather than a launch announcement
keyChanges.product: Intune – Defender for Endpoint device compliance

2026-01-14.headline: Expedite policy guidance sets CVSS 9.0 triage and Windows prerequisites
2026-01-14.overview: 14 January was primarily a documentation-consolidation day, but several updates have direct planning value. A new Expedite Policies for Windows Quality Updates how-to defines emergency-update scope and prerequisites, while Vulnerability Remediation Agent guidance points “Expedite” recommendations at CVEs with CVSS risk values of 9.0 or greater. Updated Win32 app guidance describes PowerShell script installers, and Windows feature-update guidance clarifies optional installation and persistent version targeting. Rollout Options adds specific offer-group and Windows Autopatch processing requirements, while Advanced Analytics documents saved device-query workflows. The removed Expedite Quality Updates item is a documentation-page retirement, not evidence that expedite policies themselves were retired; no preview or general-availability status is supplied.
2026-01-14.adminImpact: Administrators with critical-vulnerability workflows should review expedite prerequisites against update-ring and Group Policy assignments, because the guidance identifies settings that can interfere. Teams considering Win32 script installers need to account for the 50 KB limit, silent execution, return-code reporting, and the Multi-Admin Approval creation limitation. Windows update owners should validate optional feature-update communications, rollout dates, and offer-group assignments. Device-query owners should finalize personal queries before converting them to shared queries, because shared queries cannot be edited or deleted. Most remaining edits are naming, metadata, link, formatting, or wording cleanups; the evidence contains no preview or GA announcement and no demonstrated Intune

keyChanges.title: Expedite policies define targeted security-update acceleration and prerequisites
keyChanges.detail: New Intune guidance describes an expedite policy as targeting one supported Windows security update. It says the update installs as soon as possible, bypassing deferral settings and normal deployment timing without pausing or changing monthly quality-update policies; regular monthly servicing remains with update rings or Windows quality-update policies. Before using it, the page calls for Windows quality-update prerequisites, **Enable pre-release builds = Not configured**, **Automatic update behavior = Reset to
keyChanges.product: Intune — Windows quality updates / Expedite policies

keyChanges.title: Win32 app instructions describe PowerShell script installers
keyChanges.detail: Updated Win32 app guidance describes an **Installer type** choice between **Command line** and **PowerShell script**. The script is packaged with app content, replaces the standard install command, runs in the app installer's system or user context, and uses its return code for Intune success or failure reporting. Scripts are limited to **50 KB** and should run silently. With Multi-Admin Approval enabled, scripts can't be uploaded during app creation; create the app first, then add or modify scripts. keyChanges.title: Feature-update guidance clarifies optional installs and persistent version targeting
keyChanges.detail: Updated feature-update policy guidance says a device already on a newer Windows version isn't downgraded, and the policy remains in effect until modified or removed; an update-ring pause expires after **35 days**. For an **Optional** feature update, users must open **Windows Update** in device settings and select **Download**; without that action, it isn't installed unless an admin later changes it to **Required**. This is an explicit user-experience and policy-behavior clarification in the guidance, not a stated

keyChanges.title: Rollout Options adds offer-group timing and intelligent-rollout prerequisites
keyChanges.detail: Updated Rollout Options guidance says **First group availability** must be at least two days in the future; **Final group availability** controls when remaining devices receive the offer, and **Days between groups** determines offer-group frequency. Groups are assigned randomly and evenly with a minimum of 100 devices; changing dates or spacing recalculates groups for devices that have not yet received the offer. For intelligent rollouts, enable **Allow Windows Update for Business Cloud Processing** in a settings-c
keyChanges.product: Intune — Windows rollout options / Windows Autopatch

keyChanges.title: Advanced Analytics documents personal and shared saved device queries
keyChanges.detail: Updated Advanced Analytics guidance documents the **Saved Queries** workflow in **Devices > Device query**. Admins can save **Personal queries** visible only to themselves or **Shared queries** available to other Intune admins; personal queries can be changed or deleted, while shared queries can't be edited or deleted. A personal query can be converted to shared, so the page advises finalizing it first. This is a documented workflow addition; no preview or GA state is stated.

2026-01-15.headline: Edge for Business and Windows Update guidance add clearer policy guardrails
2026-01-15.overview: The period was led by Intune documentation covering Edge for Business policy selection, Windows driver-update controls, and feature-update rollout timing. The supplied evidence does not identify a preview, general-availability announcement, service retirement, or tenant-wide behavior change; the removed Edge security-baseline page appears to reflect a walkthrough reorganization rather than feature retirement.
2026-01-15.adminImpact: Prioritize the Windows Update guidance when creating or revising policies: check driver-blocking settings, assign only one driver-update policy per device, and choose an availability schedule for feature updates. For Edge for Business, separate enrolled and non-enrolled populations and avoid conflicting policy types. If using iOS/iPadOS Mobile Threat Defense connectors, review the opt-in inventory-sharing settings. Do not infer a product rollout or retirement from the documentation additions and page moves alone.

keyChanges.title: Windows driver update policies get a new approval and deployment playbook
keyChanges.detail: New Intune how-to documentation—not a stated feature launch—covers viewing available driver updates, approving or pausing individual updates, and sending assignments to Windows Update. It adds two concrete checks: set the Windows update ring policy's Windows driver setting to Allow, and set Settings catalog > Windows Update client policies > Exclude WU Drivers in Quality Update to Allow Windows Update drivers. The guidance also says each device should be targeted by only one driver-update policy.

keyChanges.title: Feature update policies are documented as durable version targeting
keyChanges.detail: New Intune guidance says a feature-update policy remains in effect until modified or removed, unlike pausing feature updates in update rings, which expires after 35 days. It also states that policies don't downgrade devices already running a newer Windows version, and that the latest applicable monthly quality update is included when a feature update installs. A safeguard hold can still prevent installation.

keyChanges.title: Feature-update rollout guidance now names gradual offer availability
keyChanges.detail: Updated Intune guidance defines three availability behaviors for feature-update policies: make the update available as soon as possible, make it available on a specified date, or make it available gradually using offer groups. The page clarifies that availability makes devices eligible at their next Windows Update scan; actual installation remains affected by user behavior, deadlines, and restart controls.

keyChanges.title: Edge for Business guidance separates enrolled and non-enrolled policy paths
keyChanges.detail: The updated Intune walkthrough directs non-enrolled devices to App Configuration Policies through the Managed Apps channel. For enrolled Windows devices, it says to choose either Settings Catalog policies or the Microsoft Edge Security Baseline—not both—and never to deploy App Configuration Policies and Settings Catalog policies to the same client. The former Step 6 security-baseline link is replaced by end-user experience guidance, with troubleshooting moved to Step 7; this is documentation reorganization, not​e​v

keyChanges.title: Mobile Threat Defense inventory sharing is clarified as opt-in
keyChanges.detail: Updated Intune security guidance says App Sync and Certificate Sync for iOS/iPadOS are opt-in, with no information shared by default. When enabled, app and certificate inventories from both corporate- and personally-owned enrolled devices are sent to MTD providers during device check-in intervals. The revised page lists certificate data such as Account ID, Entra ID Device ID, Device Owner, Certificate List, Common Name, and Is Identity, and identifies Zimperium as a supported partner.

2026-01-16.headline: “Deny access to this computer from the network” blocks local Autopilot Reset
2026-01-16.overview: 16 January was a documentation-maintenance day rather than a product-release day: all 27 supplied changes were updates, with no new, removed, or Message Center items. The standout was a newly added Windows Autopilot known-issue entry documenting that a specific local-account denial setting prevents local Autopilot Reset. Other meaningful edits clarify Microsoft Edge policy-conflict scope, Azure Monitor reporting latency, and which Windows update policies control client-side behavior. Nothing supplied establishes a new feature, preview, general availability release, retirement, or changed service behavior.
2026-01-16.adminImpact: Review devices that rely on local Windows Autopilot Reset. If an Intune policy sets “Deny access to this computer from the network” for the Local account, remove that setting or exclude reset-dependent devices, as Microsoft’s documented workaround directs. For operations, allow for the documented Azure Monitor transfer window and keep restart, deadline, notification, and deferral controls in update rings or Windows Update client policies. Treat the remaining edits as documentation clarification unless they expose a gap in your procedures.

keyChanges.title: Local Autopilot Reset has a newly documented local-administrator failure mode
keyChanges.detail: Windows Autopilot documentation adds a known issue dated January 16, 2026: when an Intune policy sets “Deny access to this computer from the network” for the Local account, a local Windows administrator cannot initiate local Windows Autopilot Reset. The issue is under investigation; the documented workaround is to remove the setting or exclude affected devices.

keyChanges.title: The Edge policy-conflict warning is now explicitly scoped to Microsoft Edge
keyChanges.detail: The Mamedge Settings Catalog guidance changes the warning from a broad statement about App Configuration Policies and Settings Catalog policies to one covering policies targeting Microsoft Edge. Administrators should still avoid deploying both policy types to the same client for Edge; the edit is a documentation clarification, not evidence of a policy-engine change.

keyChanges.title: Azure Monitor guidance clarifies the full Intune log-delivery window
keyChanges.detail: The Review Logs Using Azure Monitor article now states that Device Compliance Organizational Logs and Intune Devices report data is sent once every 24 hours, at any time during that period. It can therefore take up to an additional 24 hours to reach Azure Monitor, after which it typically appears within 30 minutes. This clarifies reporting expectations rather than announcing a telemetry change.

keyChanges.title: Quality update guidance separates targeting from client-side update controls
keyChanges.detail: Intune’s quality update guidance now explicitly assigns restart settings, deadlines, notifications, and deferral periods to update rings and Windows Update client policies. Quality update policies remain the surface for targeting quality updates and scenarios such as expedited updates and hotpatch. The change clarifies administrative boundaries rather than launching a capability.

2026-01-20.headline: Managed Home Screen remote-action guidance names Android Enterprise scopes and RBAC permissions
2026-01-20.overview: The 20 January period was documentation-led: two new Intune how-to pages cover suspending and restoring Managed Home Screen, while revisions add the most useful operational detail around those actions. Other notable changes clarify Windows quality-update enforcement, app-protection assignment scope, and least-privilege trial setup. Most of the remaining 23 changes are routine metadata, wording, title, navigation, or link updates; the Windows Autopilot entry only changes a linked section anchor.
2026-01-20.adminImpact: Validate Managed Home Screen device scope and role permissions before using the actions, review Enrollment Status Page testing against the 2026-01 B quality update, and ensure app protection policies target user-containing groups rather than device groups. For trial tenants, follow the revised least-privilege role guidance instead of relying broadly on Global Administrator.

keyChanges.title: Restore guidance specifies COBO/COSU support and its RBAC permission
keyChanges.detail: This is a documentation clarification, not evidence of a new rollout. The revised restore page identifies Android Enterprise corporate-owned Fully Managed (COBO) and Dedicated (COSU) devices, names Remote tasks/Restore Managed Home Screen as the custom-role permission, and says restoration re-enforces Managed Home Screen policies. Administrators using the action should check both enrollment mode and delegated permissions.

keyChanges.title: Suspend guidance specifies COBO/COSU support and its temporary-suspend permission
keyChanges.detail: The revised page replaces the generic Android platform reference with Android Enterprise corporate-owned Fully Managed (COBO) and Dedicated (COSU), and identifies Remote tasks/Temporarily Suspend Managed Home Screen for custom roles. It also states that suspension stops Managed Home Screen policy enforcement and returns the user to the standard home screen and apps.

keyChanges.title: Install Windows quality updates enforcement is listed in the 2026-01 B release
keyChanges.detail: The Enrollment Status Page guidance now states that OS enforcement for the Install Windows quality updates Intune setting is included in the 2026-01 B quality update. This replaces the previous wording that the setting was available but not yet enforced and that enforcement was only planned. Review ESP rollout expectations and testing for devices receiving that release.

keyChanges.title: App protection assignments explicitly require user-containing groups
keyChanges.detail: The app-protection procedure now tells administrators to select a users group and explicitly states that app protection policies can be applied only to groups containing users, not groups containing devices. Assignment plans or runbooks that rely on device-only groups need to be corrected.

keyChanges.title: Trial setup adds explicit least-privilege roles for Intune administrators
keyChanges.detail: The free-trial walkthrough now identifies the EMS subscription contents—Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2 and Intune—and adds an admin-team step. It identifies Intune Administrator for Intune setup and Domain Name Administrator only when configuring an optional custom domain, while noting that the subscription-creating account receives Global Administrator and has more access than most Intune tasks require.

2026-01-21.headline: Win32 .msu deployment guidance now carries an explicit not-recommended warning
2026-01-21.overview: The period was documentation-only: all eight supplied entries were updates, with no new, removed, or Message Center items. The most consequential clarification is an explicit warning against deploying Windows update packages as Win32 applications. A separate note documents battery optimization as a possible cause of missed custom notifications; the remaining changes mainly improve onboarding links, terminology, and Microsoft Graph references.
2026-01-21.adminImpact: Admins using the Win32 application method for .msu updates should note that Microsoft now describes it as not recommended and provides the article AS-IS; the update does not establish a retirement or unsupported status. For custom notifications, review battery optimization on devices where reliable delivery matters—the guidance suggests disabling optimization for the Company Portal or Intune app. No evidence indicates a new feature rollout, preview, general-availability change, or tenant-wide configuration requirement.

keyChanges.title: Win32 .msu update deployment is explicitly marked not recommended
keyChanges.detail: The Win32 deployment page now states: “Deploying updates using application method is not a recommended way of deploying updates,” and says the article is provided AS-IS. This is documentation guidance, not evidence that the method was retired or made unsupported.

keyChanges.title: Custom notification guidance adds a battery-optimization delivery caveat
keyChanges.detail: The Custom Notifications page now warns that battery optimization settings on some devices can prevent notifications from being delivered. It suggests disabling battery optimization for the Company Portal or Intune app to improve reliable delivery.

keyChanges.title: Free-trial onboarding adds license and role-assignment pointers
keyChanges.detail: After configuring the EMS free trial, the page now points administrators to confirm their trial licenses and links to built-in Intune role assignment for the admin team. It also describes the Intune admin center as the place to manage devices, apps, and policies.

keyChanges.title: Managed Home Screen restore documentation switches to current Graph paths
keyChanges.detail: The Device Restore Managed Home Screen page now references /graph/api/resources/intune-devices-manageddevice for the managed-device resource and adds the restoreManagedHomeScreen action path /graph/api/intune-devices-manageddevice-RestoreManagedHomeScreen. This is a reference correction, not evidence of changed API capability.
keyChanges.product: Intune Managed Home Screen and Microsoft Graph

2026-01-22.headline: Approved-client Conditional Access control retires in June; guided scenarios exit in March
2026-01-22.overview: The main operational signals are two planned retirements: the Microsoft Entra Conditional Access “Require approved client app” control is scheduled to retire in June 2026, while Intune guided scenarios will be removed in March except for Windows 365 Boot. The remaining updates are documentation and security-guidance clarifications rather than new feature launches or general-availability announcements.
2026-01-22.adminImpact: Inventory Conditional Access policies that use “Require approved client app” and plan to replace the control with “Require application protection policy” before June. No action is required for the guided-scenario removal, and existing configurations remain unaffected. For Windows update packages, prefer Intune Windows Update policies over .msu deployment as a Win32 app. Review the revised migration and macOS Platform SSO guidance when planning those deployments.

keyChanges.title: Microsoft Entra retires the approved-client Conditional Access control in June 2026
keyChanges.detail: The “Require approved client app” control will no longer be enforceable after retirement. Microsoft directs organizations to use “Require application protection policy” for equivalent and enhanced protection, making affected Conditional Access policies the clearest deadline-driven administrator task in this period.

keyChanges.title: Intune guided scenarios will be removed from the admin center in March
keyChanges.detail: All Intune guided scenarios except Windows 365 Boot are scheduled for removal beginning in March 2026. Existing configurations are unaffected and Microsoft says no administrator action is needed; replacement guidance is available through the resources in the message.

keyChanges.title: Windows .msu Win32 deployment guidance now favors Windows Update policies
keyChanges.detail: The deployment guide now explicitly says that deploying updates as Win32 apps is not the recommended approach. It points administrators to Update rings, Feature updates, and Quality updates, while retaining the Win32 method for cases that need more granular control. This changes the documented recommendation, not the deployment capability itself.
keyChanges.product: Intune Win32 app management and Windows Update policies

keyChanges.title: The Basic Mobility and Security migration guide clarifies license-driven transition steps
keyChanges.detail: The renamed guide now includes policy mapping and license-assignment steps. Its procedure states that assigning Intune licenses to users or groups automatically switches them to Intune device management and leaves users and devices ready to receive newly created Intune policies; the earlier reference to switching at the next refresh cycle was removed. This is a procedural documentation clarification, not evidence of a newly launched migration capability.
keyChanges.product: Intune migration from Basic Mobility and Security

keyChanges.title: Microsoft strengthens the Platform SSO recommendation for macOS registration
keyChanges.detail: The macOS endpoint guidance now recommends enforcing Platform SSO during device registration, describing it as a Zero Trust best practice that supports strong device identity and replaces traditional registration typically performed through the Company Portal. The update provides security guidance rather than announcing a new Platform SSO feature or availability change.
keyChanges.product: Intune macOS enrollment and Platform SSO

Edge for Business pages were mostly refreshed, but one policy-conflict warning was shortened—an editorial change that does not by itself prove a product rule changed.

Update Device Query templates to use a scalar property such as `Device.DeviceId` in `distinct`, `summarize`, or `order by`, and review joins against the newly documented list. Do not rely on Run remediation delivery when a device lacks Intune or WNS connectivity. For Edge, keep policy selection aligned with enrollment status and do not interpret the removed prohibition as proof that co-targeting is supported. In Configuration Manager, use the High-impact selection when a

The guide also links to the procedure for removing no-longer-needed Basic Mobility and Security policies. This is a migration-procedure and RBAC clarification, not evidence of a new migration，

keyChanges.title: Device Query guidance lists four more supported join types and a Device limitation

The edit updates query guidance and does not establish a service-side capability rollout.

keyChanges.title: Remediations now states Run remediation will not arrive offline
keyChanges.detail: The Remediations page changes “might not receive” to “will not receive” the Run remediation device action when a device is offline or can't successfully communicate with Intune or Windows Push Notification Service when the action is sent. Administrators should plan around that documented no-delivery condition.

keyChanges.title: Edge guide removes its explicit prohibition on co-targeting two policy types
keyChanges.detail: Step 4 no longer includes: “Never deploy both App Configuration Policies and Settings Catalog policies targeting Microsoft Edge to the same client.” The remaining guidance says to choose the appropriate policy type based on device enrollment status to avoid conflicts. This is a wording change in the guide, not evidence that co-targeting is now supported.

keyChanges.title: High-impact task sequence placement in Software Center is spelled out
keyChanges.detail: New Configuration Manager guidance says a task sequence deployed as High-impact appears under Software Center's Operating Systems node. If it isn't marked High-impact, the deployment appears under Applications, clarifying the user-facing placement.

2026-01-24.headline: Defender for Android ends personal-profile protection on enrolled devices by March 2026
2026-01-24.overview: The period's consequential change is a Microsoft 365 Message Center major update: Microsoft Defender for Android will stop protecting personal profiles on enrolled devices by March 2026 and focus on corporate work profiles. Microsoft says work profiles and unenrolled devices are unaffected and no administrator action is required. The other updates concern Advanced Analytics documentation; the supplied join diffs expose the same reference text before and after, so they do not establish a changed query capability.
2026-01-24.adminImpact: No tenant configuration or rollout action is indicated. Administrators should distinguish the affected personal profile on enrolled Android devices from corporate work profiles, which remain in scope, and unenrolled devices, which are unaffected. The Advanced Analytics edit is query-authoring clarification rather than evidence of a service behavior change.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Android narrows enrolled-device protection to work profiles
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Defender for Android will end support for protecting personal profiles on enrolled devices by March 2026, focusing solely on corporate work profiles. The change does not affect work profiles or unenrolled devices, and the Message Center notice says no administrator action is required.

keyChanges.title: Device Query clarifies that scalar properties are required by query operators
keyChanges.detail: The Advanced Analytics Device Query Multiple Devices page now states that the Device entity cannot be used directly with scalar-requiring operators such as distinct, summarize, and order by. Query authors should use a specific scalar device property, with Device.SerialNumber and Device.OSVersion given as examples; this is a documentation clarification, not a reported product behavior change.

2026-01-26.headline: Autopilot device preparation reaches 25 apps amid Cloud PKI’s CA-guide overhaul
2026-01-26.overview: The period is mostly a Cloud PKI documentation move: path and image-link fixes accompany eight legacy `/intune/intune-service/protect` pages being replaced by `/intune/cloud-pki` pages for deployment, CA configuration, monitoring, deletion, audit logs, and fundamentals. That is documentation reorganization—not evidence of a Cloud PKI launch or product retirement. The significant operational items are a documented 25-app Windows Autopilot device-preparation limit and a status update saying the previously delayed Enrollment Status Page security-update capability is included in Windows `2026-01 B`. An Intune Mobile Threat Defense/App Protection example also changes its block thresholds, but the evidence supports a documentation example change only.
2026-01-26.adminImpact: Update bookmarks, internal runbooks, and links to the new Cloud PKI paths, but do not treat the removed pages as a service retirement. Review Autopilot device-preparation policies at the former 10-app boundary and revisit deployment timeouts if adding apps; test the ESP capability on devices receiving Windows `2026-01 B`. For Cloud PKI operations, follow the documented deletion order: anchored issuing CAs must be removed before the root CA, and active leaf certificates must be revoked before an issuing CA can be revoked. Revoke and delete actions are permanent. Audit-log access requires a Cloud PKI license, Intune service administrator role, access token, and the listed Microsoft Graph permissions. Compare the revised MTD/App Protection example thresholds with the tenant’s intended risk14`

keyChanges.title: Windows Autopilot device preparation now documents a 25-app limit
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance changes the managed-application example from 10 to 25. It says up to 25 apps can be configured in a Windows Autopilot device-preparation policy for both user-driven and automatic modes, including all Cloud PC offerings. It warns that deployments with more apps may need longer deployment timeouts. The evidence does not label this change preview or generally available.

keyChanges.title: Autopilot ESP guidance now says the security-update capability is included
keyChanges.detail: The page replaces a September 2025 delay notice with: “As of January 13, 2026, this capability is included in the Windows `2026-01 B` quality update.” The earlier note specifically said automatic installation of monthly security update releases and the new user interface were unavailable. This is an availability/status update in the What’s New guidance, not a supplied general-availability announcement.

keyChanges.title: Cloud PKI guidance defines cloud-root and BYOCA deployment paths
keyChanges.detail: The new deployment-model guidance lists two options: create Microsoft Cloud PKI root and issuing CAs in the cloud, producing a two-tier hierarchy with multiple issuing CAs; or create a private cloud issuing CA anchored to an on-premises or private CA, including external private CA N+1 hierarchies. This is newly organized guidance, not evidence of a new service launch.

keyChanges.title: Cloud PKI deletion guidance spells out pause, revoke, and permanence
keyChanges.detail: The new procedure distinguishes Pause, Resume, Revoke, and Delete. Pausing stops leaf issuance while the CA continues responding to CRL and AIA requests. A root CA cannot be deleted until all anchored issuing CAs are deleted, active leaf certificates must already be revoked before an issuing CA can be revoked, and revocation or deletion cannot be undone. The page also names the Intune Administrator or a custom Intune role with Read CAs, Disable and reenable CAs, and Revoke issued leaf certificates permissions.

keyChanges.title: MTD App Protection examples change their blocked threat thresholds
keyChanges.detail: In Step 3, one Max allowed device threat level example changes from Low to High, with Block access in both versions; another changes from Medium to Low, also with Block access. This is a Mobile Threat Defense/App Protection documentation example change. The supplied diff does not say that existing policies, defaults, or enforcement behavior changed.
keyChanges.product: Intune App Protection with Mobile Threat Defense

2026-01-27.headline: Windows enrollment guidance shifts setup from Global Administrator to Intune Administrator
2026-01-27.overview: 27 January was a documentation-only period: all 14 Intune entries were updates, with no new capabilities, retirements, or Message Center announcements. Report consumers should also retain the expectation that iOS 16 and later app protection reports show a generic Device Name.

keyChanges.title: Windows Enroll now lists Intune Administrator as the admin-center role

The previous prerequisite named a Microsoft Entra Global Administrator. The diff changes the documented prerequisite, but does not establish a backend permission change.

keyChanges.title: Trial guidance separates initial Global Administrator use from routine tasks
keyChanges.detail: Free Trial Sign Up now suggests signing out of the Global Administrator account and using the account needed for the Intune task. Its role table says Intune Administrator can set up Intune and Automatic Enrollment for Windows devices, while the earlier Global Administrator entry was removed. keyChanges.title: Filters table now marks Settings catalog (DDM) unsupported
keyChanges.detail: Two Settings catalog (DDM) entries changed from supported (✅) to unsupported (❌). The diff gives no rollout explanation or additional scope, so administrators should verify existing filter assignments involving DDM settings catalog workloads before relying on them.

2026-01-28.headline: Configuration Manager log guidance narrows modern-component scope and reshapes reference navigation

2026-01-31.headline: Cloud PKI CA expirations require replacement CAs and SCEP profile updates
2026-01-31.overview: The period’s main administrator-relevant change is new and expanded Cloud PKI guidance for expiring issuing CAs. It documents a customer-managed replacement procedure and the potential certificate, connectivity, and authentication impact of taking no action. Endpoint Privilege Management documentation also clarifies child-process elevation semantics. The remaining Cloud PKI edits are wording and heading maintenance; renewal of an existing CA is described as coming soon, not as an available feature.
2026-01-31.adminImpact: For any expiring Cloud PKI issuing CA, create a replacement CA using the same Root CA Source and matching properties, including Extended Key Usages and key sizes. Update every referencing SCEP certificate profile to use the replacement CA’s SCEP URI; do not add a second URI, and note that changing the URI does not trigger certificate reissuance. Review EPM rules that allow child processes to run elevated, particularly for applications that launch command shells or script engines.

keyChanges.title: Cloud PKI documents the customer-managed CA replacement path
keyChanges.detail: The new guidance says Microsoft cannot automatically update a Cloud PKI CA or its SCEP profiles. Administrators must create a new issuing CA, replace the expiring CA’s SCEP URI in each affected profile, and verify all profiles reference the new CA. After expiration, affected profiles stop issuing new certificates, potentially causing Wi-Fi, VPN, email, corporate-resource, or certificate-authentication failures. The article says the ability to renew an existing CA is coming soon, so this is operational guidance for

keyChanges.title: EPM clarifies when child processes bypass elevation rules
keyChanges.detail: The updated Endpoint Privilege Management page distinguishes three choices: require the child’s own rule, deny elevation to all child processes, or allow child processes to run elevated automatically. With the last option, child rule evaluation is skipped, including deny rules, so a child can run elevated despite an explicit denial. Microsoft’s documented best practice is to avoid overly broad rules for applications that can launch shells or script engines.

2026-02-02.headline: Planned 802.1x iPadOS wired networking leads Intune’s documentation-heavy update day
2026-02-02.overview: Intune had a documentation-only day: all five recorded items were Microsoft Learn updates, with no new or removed items and no Message Center posts. The most consequential change is an in-development iOS/iPadOS 802.1x Wired Networks profile supporting EAP methods including TLS, PEAP, and TTLS. Other updates clarify custom-role permissions and Managed Home Screen permission requirements. The Android app-protection edit shows no visible change to the offline-grace-period value or behavior, while a second OEMConfig update only changes the page date from 02/27/2025 to 02/02/2026.
2026-02-02.adminImpact: No immediate tenant change or rollout is supported by this evidence. Treat the iOS/iPadOS wired-network profile as planned rather than generally available because the page says Microsoft is adding it. Administrators designing custom roles or Zebra Managed Home Screen deployments should use the revised reference tables, but the diffs do not establish that service behavior or portal availability changed. The offline-grace-period and date-only edits require no demonstrated configuration action.

keyChanges.title: iOS/iPadOS gains a planned 802.1x Wired Networks profile
keyChanges.detail: The In Development page describes an upcoming 802.1x Ethernet device configuration profile for iOS/iPadOS. It supports EAP protocols such as TLS, PEAP, and TTLS and is intended to let M-series iPads securely connect to hot-desk docks and monitors. The same diff removes earlier entries about Endpoint Privilege Management support on Azure Virtual Desktop and a Lenovo Device Orchestration portal link; that removal is not evidence of retirement.

keyChanges.title: Custom-role documentation adds four Admin tasks permissions
keyChanges.detail: The permission table now lists Admin tasks/Create, Admin tasks/Delete, Admin tasks/Read, and Admin tasks/Update, describing creation, deletion, read access, and updates to device-management administrative tasks. Android Enterprise and Android FOTA entries are also reordered and reformatted. The diff documents these permission names but does not state that a new service capability was introduced.

keyChanges.title: Managed Home Screen matrix marks two permissions in an additional configuration
keyChanges.detail: For both Alarms & Reminders and Write Settings, the permission matrix changes from ✅ / n/a / n/a to ✅ / ✅ / n/a. The page also adds links for those permissions and Zebra Managed Configurations. The supplied evidence presents this as a documentation-matrix change and does not specify a product behavior change.
keyChanges.product: Intune — Android OEMConfig Managed Home Screen

keyChanges.title: Android offline-grace-period wording shows no changed duration
keyChanges.detail: The Android app-protection entry continues to define the offline grace period as the number of minutes managed apps can run offline before access requirements are rechecked. The visible old and new text does not provide a different value, prerequisite, or resulting behavior, so this appears to be wording or formatting maintenance rather than a documented policy change.

2026-02-03.headline: Intune RBAC guidance now lists Android enrollment and cloud-attached device actions
2026-02-03.overview: The 3 February period was documentation-only: 12 existing Intune pages were updated, with no new or removed items and no Message Center entries. The most operationally relevant revisions clarify custom-role permissions, make Microsoft Edge mobile PAC failure behavior explicit, and document where Intune service notices appear in the admin center. The supplied evidence does not announce a new feature, preview, general-availability release, retirement, or product behavior change.
2026-02-03.adminImpact: Most tenants need no immediate configuration change. RBAC administrators should use the documented Permission/Action terminology and review custom roles against the listed Android Enterprise and cloud-attached device actions. The removal of the earlier VPP-apps permission note does not, by itself, establish a change to access rights. Administrators using PAC files with Edge for iOS and Android should verify that their intended policy matches the documented default: invalid or unavailable PAC scripts block network access unless the organization configures failed-open behavior. Service notices can be checked in the Microsoft 365 admin center at Health > Message center or in the Intune admin center at Tenant administration > Tenant status > Service health and message center.

keyChanges.title: Custom-role page now lists Android enrollment and cloud-attached actions
keyChanges.detail: The Create Custom Role page now documents Android Enterprise/Enrollment time device membership assignment for Android Enterprise, which allows Intune to assign devices to Entra ID groups during enrollment. It also lists Cloud attached devices actions for running CMPivot queries, running scripts, taking application actions, and viewing applications. Android Enterprise descriptions now use Managed Google Play terminology. The same diff removes the previous VPP-apps permission note; it does not say that the underlying

keyChanges.title: RBAC guidance changes the documented selection model to Permission and Action
keyChanges.detail: The Role Based Access Control page changes its documented workflow from selecting a permission category and permission to selecting a permission and a specific action. It likewise describes user permissions as Permission and Action rather than Category and Permission. This is a terminology and procedure clarification in the documentation, not evidence of a newly introduced RBAC model.

keyChanges.title: Edge mobile guidance makes PAC failure handling explicit
keyChanges.detail: The Manage Microsoft Edge page now states that Microsoft Edge for iOS and Android blocks network access by default when a PAC script is invalid or unavailable. Organizations can change the default to PAC failed open. The revision clarifies the documented default; it does not announce that Edge's runtime behavior changed.

keyChanges.title: Service guidance adds the Intune admin center notice location
keyChanges.detail: The service description now identifies both notice locations: Microsoft 365 admin center notices appear at Health > Message center, while Intune admin center service change and service health notices appear at Tenant administration > Tenant status > Service health and message center.

keyChanges.title: Service overview removes the 100-user trial wording and onboarding paragraph
keyChanges.detail: The service description reframes Intune from a mobile-focused EMM service to an endpoint management service, describes a 30-day free trial without the previous qualification that it included 100 user licenses, and removes the Intune Onboarding benefit paragraph. The supplied diff is a page-content revision only; it does not announce a licensing change or retirement of the onboarding benefit.

2026-02-04.headline: Endpoint Privilege Management adds Azure Virtual Desktop support as Windows catalog gains controls
2026-02-04.overview: 4 February was documentation-heavy: all 32 tracked items were updates, with no new or removed entries and no Message Center posts. Most edits involved reviewer metadata, headings, anchors, or reference cleanup. The meaningful exceptions are the service release 2601 entries for Endpoint Privilege Management on Azure Virtual Desktop, Windows settings catalog additions, Lenovo Device Orchestration and protected apps, plus Configuration Manager SQL and CMG guidance. The supplied evidence does not label the Intune capabilities as preview or general availability; it presents them as service-release updates.
2026-02-04.adminImpact: Prioritize validation if your organization uses EPM on Azure Virtual Desktop, Windows settings catalog policies, Lenovo devices, or Intune protected apps. Configuration Manager administrators should review SQL Server 2014 estates, verify SQL Server 2022 compatibility assumptions, and revisit CMG certificate requirements. The remaining Intune edits are largely editorial; for example, the RBAC reference now says Cloud PC roles might appear rather than stating that administrators will find them, and removes an embedded permission-generation script. That wording change is documentation clarification, not evidence of a tenant permission change.

keyChanges.title: EPM elevation policies support AVD single-session users
keyChanges.detail: The Intune service release 2601 entry states that Endpoint Privilege Management elevation policies can now be deployed to users on Azure Virtual Desktop single-session virtual machines. EPM remains identified as an Intune Suite add-on capability; the documented scope is specifically single-session AVD environments.

keyChanges.title: Windows settings catalog adds Edge controls and Share Sheet suppression
keyChanges.detail: The Windows settings catalog adds Microsoft Edge policies up to version 143.0.3650.23, including tenant-approved browsing-history sharing with Microsoft 365 Copilot Search, RAM resource controls, and the option to opt out of Local Network access restrictions. It also adds Experience > Disable Share App Promotions; when enabled, Windows doesn't show promotional apps in the Windows Share Sheet. Administrators can find these in Devices > Configuration profiles > Create profile > Windows 10 and later > Settings catalog

keyChanges.title: Lenovo portal access and four protected apps appear in the service-release listing
keyChanges.detail: Intune now includes a direct Partner portals link to Lenovo Device Orchestration in the admin center for supported Windows 11 Lenovo devices, opening Lenovo-specific management capabilities in the LDO portal. The same entry lists Clarity Express for Intune, Datadog, Qlik Analytics, and Tier1 for Intune (iOS) as newly available protected apps.

keyChanges.title: SQL Server 2014 is explicitly marked deprecated for Configuration Manager 2409
keyChanges.detail: The Configuration Manager SQL support matrix now marks SQL Server 2014 as deprecated in version 2409 and notes that SQL Server 2014 support ended in July 2024. It also states that SQL Server 2022 requires a lifecycle-supported update and does not support native compatibility level 160; SQL Server 2019 requires CU5 or later.

keyChanges.title: CMG authentication guidance narrows when PKI certificate export is required
keyChanges.detail: The revised Configuration Manager guidance says to export the certificate only when clients are not joined to Microsoft Entra ID and instead use PKI certificates. It also states that management points enabled for CMG traffic can use either Enhanced HTTP or HTTPS. This is a documentation clarification of authentication configuration, not evidence of a newly announced CMG behavior.

2026-02-05.headline: Endpoint Privilege Management support is coming to AVD single-session VMs
2026-02-05.overview: The period contains 123 documentation updates and no new or removed items. Most of the 115 Windows Autopilot updates are mechanical metadata cleanup, including removal of high-priority collection markers. The meaningful changes are an Autopilot known-issue status update and several capabilities listed as in development on Intune’s roadmap page.
2026-02-05.adminImpact: No broad tenant change or rollout action is supported by the supplied evidence. Administrators using Endpoint Privilege Management with Azure Virtual Desktop should track the in-development support rather than treat it as generally available. The Autopilot known-issue entry should be reviewed, but it does not identify the issue or prescribe a configuration change.

keyChanges.title: EPM support is being added for AVD single-session environments
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft says it is adding support to deploy Endpoint Privilege Management policies to users on Azure Virtual Desktop single-session virtual machines. EPM elevation policies are expected to work in those environments once supported. The entry is explicitly in development, gives no general-availability date, and identifies EPM as an Intune Suite add-on capability.
keyChanges.product: Endpoint Privilege Management and Azure Virtual Desktop

keyChanges.title: Windows Autopilot device preparation issue is marked resolved
keyChanges.detail: The known-issues page now adds an updated date of February 5, 2026 and states, “This issue was resolved in February 2026.” The supplied diff does not identify the issue or the fix, so this is a documentation status clarification rather than evidence of a newly released Autopilot behavior.

keyChanges.title: Android settings catalog will filter settings by management mode
keyChanges.detail: An in-development filter for Android settings catalog policies will narrow available settings by enrollment type: Fully managed (COBO), Corporate-owned work profile (COPE), or Dedicated (COSU). The change describes policy authoring and settings discovery; it does not state that existing policy behavior changes.

keyChanges.title: Apple catalog updates add an exemption setting and new security terminology
keyChanges.detail: The planned iOS/iPadOS Settings Catalog update adds Restrictions > Rating Apps Exempted Bundle IDs. It also reflects Apple’s rebranding of Rapid Security Responses as Background Security Improvements. No availability date or migration requirement for existing profiles is supplied.

keyChanges.title: Intune is developing a direct Lenovo Device Orchestration link
keyChanges.detail: A Partner portals integration in development will let administrators open the Lenovo Device Orchestration Portal directly from the Intune admin center for supported Windows 11 devices. The entry describes a portal link, not new Lenovo management controls inside Intune, and says it will apply when the feature becomes available.
keyChanges.product: Intune Partner portals and Lenovo Device Orchestration

2026-02-06.headline: Intune clarifies silent Win32 installs as Apple settings references are consolidated
2026-02-06.overview: The 6 February feed contains 75 changes—5 new, 70 updated, and no removals—across Intune and Configuration Manager. The supplied new Apple articles and numerous link updates are primarily documentation consolidation, not evidence of a product launch. The clearest administrator-facing changes are the explicit Win32 silent-install support boundary, new Remote Help network endpoints, and a Configuration Manager software-update synchronization warning. Endpoint Privilege Management support for Azure Virtual Desktop single-session VMs and Android management-mode filtering are explicitly listed as in development, not generally available.
2026-02-06.adminImpact: Win32 application owners should validate silent or unattended installation and avoid unsupported UI-forcing workarounds such as serviceui.exe. Teams that restrict Remote Help traffic by hostname should update their allowlists for the added and replaced endpoints. Configuration Manager software-update-point administrators should limit Products & Categories to relevant, deployable items. Apple administrators should use the consolidated references and keep sensitive Wi-Fi and authentication settings in built-in profiles; the new pages do not by themselves establish a tenant-side feature rollout.

keyChanges.title: Win32 app guidance explicitly rules out interactive installations
