keyChanges.detail: The updated Add and Assign Win32 Apps guidance adds an IMPORTANT notice that Intune-deployed applications must install silently and cannot require dialog boxes, prompts, or other UI input. It also says serviceui.exe and similar techniques that force interaction with the signed-in user session are unsupported and may produce inconsistent or unpredictable behavior. This is a documented support boundary and packaging requirement, not evidence of a new installer-engine behavior.

keyChanges.title: Remote Help network endpoints change
keyChanges.detail: The Intune endpoints table for the MEM Remote Help Feature adds *.dm.microsoft.com and replaces *.trouter.skype.com with *.trouter.communications.svc.cloud.microsoft. Organizations using proxy or firewall hostname allowlists for Remote Help should update them; the evidence supplies no deadline or broader Remote Help behavior change.

keyChanges.title: Apple custom-profile guidance warns against sensitive settings
keyChanges.detail: The new Apple custom-settings article covers bringing iOS/iPadOS and macOS settings from Apple Configurator or Apple Profile Manager into Intune for settings not built into the service. It specifically says not to use custom profiles for sensitive information such as Wi-Fi connections or authentication, directing administrators to built-in Wi-Fi and certificate profiles instead. The article lists iOS/iPadOS and macOS support and the Policy and Profile Manager minimum RBAC role. This is new guidance, not a stated re

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager warns against oversized update synchronizations
keyChanges.detail: A new warning in the software update point procedure says selecting too many Products & Categories harms performance because devices scan every update in the SUSDB, whether deployed or not. It advises selecting only relevant and necessary products and avoiding items that Configuration Manager cannot deploy, including Dynamic Updates, Servicing Drivers, legacy Office and operating systems, and broad Rollups, Feature Packs, and Service Packs categories.

keyChanges.title: EPM on AVD and Android management-mode filtering are listed as in development
keyChanges.detail: The In Development page says Microsoft is adding Endpoint Privilege Management policy deployment for users on Azure Virtual Desktop single-session virtual machines. It also says the Android Settings Catalog will gain a management-mode filter for Fully managed (COBO), Corporate-owned work profile (COPE), and Dedicated (COSU). These are roadmap statements; the supplied evidence does not establish preview availability or general availability.
keyChanges.product: Intune — Endpoint Privilege Management and Settings Catalog

2026-02-07.headline: Remote Help monitor now documents Policy CSP guidance for blocked notifications
2026-02-07.overview: The period contains one Remote Help documentation update. The Troubleshoot Monitor page adds a diagnostic entry stating that the device has blocked applications from using notifications and links administrators to Policy CSP - Notifications, specifically the DisallowCloudNotification setting. The evidence indicates documentation guidance, not a confirmed product behavior change.
2026-02-07.adminImpact: When investigating notification-related Remote Help troubleshooting results, review the referenced Policy CSP - Notifications setting. No tenant configuration change, rollout action, or deadline is supported by this update.

keyChanges.title: Blocked-notification troubleshooting gains a direct CSP reference
keyChanges.detail: The Remote Help Troubleshoot Monitor guidance now identifies the condition “The device has blocked applications from using notifications” and directs administrators to Policy CSP - Notifications through the DisallowCloudNotification reference.

2026-02-09.headline: Endpoint Privilege Management now supports single-session Azure Virtual Desktop users
2026-02-09.overview: The substantive service-release content centers on Endpoint Privilege Management (EPM): elevation policies now support deployment to users on Azure Virtual Desktop single-session virtual machines. Intune also adds Windows 11, version 25H2, to two feature-update readiness reports, introduces new Windows Settings catalog controls, and adds a Lenovo Device Orchestration link plus four protected apps. Separately, Windows Autopilot guidance records a Hybrid Entra join timeout and the OS updates that resolve it. The Settings insight rewrite clarifies documented scope and interpretation; much of the remaining activity is editorial or procedural maintenance.
2026-02-09.adminImpact: Admins using AVD single-session environments can use EPM elevation policies for those users, with EPM identified as an Intune Suite add-on capability. Windows servicing teams can select Windows 11 25H2 in the compatibility-risk and device-readiness reports. For affected Hybrid Entra join Autopilot deployments, verify the applicable OS update is installed: KB5065789 or later for 25H2, KB5065426 or later for 24H2, or KB5070312 or later for 23H2. The Managed Home Screen restore and suspend pages now state that Alarms & Reminders permission must be granted before those remote actions run. Settings insight should be treated as informational peer benchmarking, not prescriptive security guidance; the SQL, typo, metadata, and archive edits provide no evidence of product behavior changes.

keyChanges.title: Service release expands EPM and Intune app-management entry points
keyChanges.detail: The service release 2601 entry states that EPM elevation policies support deployment to users on AVD single-session virtual machines. It also adds a direct Intune admin center link to Lenovo Device Orchestration for supported Lenovo devices and lists four protected apps as newly available: Clarity Express for Intune, Datadog, Qlik Analytics, and Tier1 for Intune (iOS).

keyChanges.title: Windows Settings catalog adds Edge and Share Sheet controls
keyChanges.detail: The Windows Settings catalog adds Microsoft Edge policies through version 143.0.3650.23, including Allow sharing tenant-approved browsing history with Microsoft 365 Copilot Search, Enable RAM (memory) resource controls, and Specifies whether to opt out of Local Network access restrictions. Experience > Disable Share App Promotions prevents promotional apps from appearing in Windows Share Sheet when enabled. The profile path is Devices > Configuration profiles > Create profile > Windows 10 and later > Settingsカタログ.

keyChanges.title: Windows 11 25H2 enters feature-update readiness reporting
keyChanges.detail: The Windows feature update compatibility risks report and Windows feature update device readiness report now support Windows 11, version 25H2, as a selectable target OS under Select target OS. The reports provide readiness and compatibility-risk insights for that target.

keyChanges.title: Autopilot guidance identifies fixes for Hybrid Entra join timeouts
keyChanges.detail: The Windows Autopilot Known Issues page records deployment timeouts with error code 0x80004005 for Hybrid Entra join Autopilot deployments. The issue is resolved in KB5065789 or later for 25H2, KB5065426 or later for 24H2, and KB5070312 or later for 23H2.

keyChanges.title: Settings insight scope is documented for two security baselines
keyChanges.detail: The revised guidance says Settings insight is available for the Microsoft Edge Baseline and Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise Security Baseline, but not currently for the Security Baseline for Windows 10 and later or the Microsoft Defender for Endpoint baseline. Light-bulb icons indicate that similar organizations commonly use Microsoft's recommended default; the feature does not suggest alternative values. This is a documentation clarification, not evidence of changed baseline behavior.
keyChanges.product: Intune Settings insight and security baselines

2026-02-10.headline: Apple app-list guidance now distinguishes Intune reporting from actual blocking
2026-02-10.overview: The clearest administrator-facing correction concerns iOS/iPadOS device restrictions: approved and prohibited app lists report matching app activity in Intune rather than stopping installation or execution. The Settings Catalog is the documented path for preventing an app from running or appearing. The period otherwise centers on Apple reference restructuring, Configuration Manager performance guidance, and Settings Insight scope clarification. The removed Apple articles represent documentation restructuring alongside refreshed combined references, not evidence of a product capability retirement. Windows Autopilot maintenance standardizes “Microsoft Entra hybrid join” terminology and reformats the existing KB guidance; the listed remediation versions remain unchanged.
2026-02-10.adminImpact: Audit iOS/iPadOS policies that rely on approved or prohibited app lists and use the documented Settings Catalog restrictions when prevention is required. For Apple custom profiles, follow the corrected custom-device-profile prerequisite and verify exported payload compatibility. Validate Apple SSO profiles against the newly explicit realm and domain guidance. Configuration Manager administrators should review software update point product selections to reduce WSUS metadata and scan overhead. Settings Insight users should not expect insights on baselines outside its documented scope.

keyChanges.title: Apple app lists are reporting signals, not blockers
keyChanges.detail: Documentation clarification—not a reported product behavior change: the approved and prohibited app lists do not stop users from installing or running apps. If a listed app is installed or run, Intune reports it. To prevent an app from running or appearing on iOS/iPadOS, the page directs administrators to Settings Catalog > Restrictions > Allow Listed App Bundle IDs or Blocked App Bundle IDs.

keyChanges.title: Custom Apple settings now use the correct profile prerequisite
keyChanges.detail: The prerequisite changed from a VPN device configuration profile to a custom device configuration profile. The procedure also adds Apple Configurator payload-compatibility guidance and Apple Profile Manager steps to enable mobile device management, add devices, configure them, download the profile, and enter it in Intune. This is a documentation procedure correction, not a feature announcement.

keyChanges.title: Apple SSO guidance adds explicit realm and domain constraints
keyChanges.detail: The device-features reference now documents that the authentication realm should be capitalized, such as CONTOSO.COM. SSO domains are case-insensitive, must begin with a period, and must be unique across all Intune SSO app-extension profiles, including profiles using different extension types. This newly explicit guidance does not establish a change in Intune enforcement behavior.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager warns against unnecessary update products
keyChanges.detail: The software update point warning now says unnecessary products enlarge the WSUS metadata catalog and can hurt scan performance; clients evaluate update metadata during every scan, even for updates that are not deployed. It specifically advises removing unused legacy Windows and Office products and products Configuration Manager cannot deploy, such as Dynamic Updates and Servicing Drivers.

keyChanges.title: Settings Insight scope is limited to documented Intune baselines
keyChanges.detail: The reference now explicitly says Settings Insight is currently available for the listed Intune security baselines, but not for other Intune baselines including the Security Baseline for Windows 10 and later or the Microsoft Defender for Endpoint baseline. It also clarifies that the model does not use customer data directly: usage is aggregated at the organization level and converted to categorical values or ranges where possible. This is scope and terminology clarification, not an availability expansion.

2026-02-11.headline: Intune reports will omit devices inactive for 12 months or more starting late February
2026-02-11.overview: The period is maintenance-heavy, but it contains one clear planned behavior change: Message Center says Intune reports will omit devices inactive for 12+ months from late February. Other administrator-relevant material is guidance rather than a feature launch: Cloud PKI’s customer-managed CA replacement path, Configuration Manager HSTS warnings, a corrected Connected Cache hotfix scope, and updated Edge mobile Copilot policy guidance. Many remaining records simply normalize Apple links, dates, and wording. The removed 2603 Connected Cache pages and Apple DDM assignment-filters entry do not, by themselves, prove a product retirement or GA event.
2026-02-11.adminImpact: Rebaseline report-count expectations before the late-February filter, and ensure devices that need to remain represented check in. Audit expiring Cloud PKI issuing CAs and the SCEP profiles that reference them; verify Configuration Manager branch scope before applying Connected Cache guidance; and review HSTS role dependencies and Edge mobile Copilot policies where used. The Apple cross-reference and formatting edits require no tenant action on the supplied evidence.

keyChanges.title: A 12-month inactivity filter is planned for Intune reports
keyChanges.detail: Starting late February 2026, Intune will exclude devices inactive for 12+ months from reports. Reported counts may decrease to reflect active devices only. Message Center says no action is needed, but devices must check in to remain included.

keyChanges.title: Cloud PKI guidance details the customer-managed CA replacement path
keyChanges.detail: The current expiration guidance says Microsoft cannot automatically renew or replace a Cloud PKI CA or update associated SCEP profiles. Administrators should create a replacement issuing CA with matching properties, copy its SCEP URI, and replace the old URI in every referencing SCEP certificate profile; otherwise those profiles stop issuing new certificates after expiry. Direct renewal of an existing CA is still described as coming soon.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager HSTS guidance flags FSP and SUP breakage
keyChanges.detail: The communications guidance warns that HSTS requires HTTPS, is incompatible with Enhanced HTTP, and is unsupported for client communication because Configuration Manager clients do not honor HSTS headers. Enforcing it stops the HTTP-only Fallback Status Point and blocks WSUS update payloads delivered over HTTP. HTTPS must be enabled on an applicable site system before configuring HSTS.

keyChanges.title: Edge mobile guidance documents default-enabled Copilot chat and context access
keyChanges.detail: The updated Microsoft Edge guidance says M365 Copilot chat on iOS and Android is enabled by default and can access browsing context such as opened tabs and browsing history by default. It identifies Chat and ChatPageContext policy controls. M365 Copilot Mode currently shows suggestion prompts on the new-tab page, with default enablement planned for a future version and CopilotMode available as an MAM opt-out policy.

keyChanges.title: Connected Cache documentation narrows hotfix scope from 2603 to 2509
keyChanges.detail: The Connected Cache hotfix reference now applies to Configuration Manager current branch 2509 rather than 2603. Its stated prerequisite range changes from versions 1910 through 2603 to versions 1910 through 2509. Verify the site branch before following the hotfix instructions; this is a documentation scope correction, not evidence of a new Connected Cache feature.

2026-02-12.headline: EPM support-approved elevation guidance now covers all users of a device
2026-02-12.overview: This was a documentation-led period, not a release announcement: all supplied items were Microsoft Learn updates, with no Message Center evidence of a preview, general availability release, retirement, or tenant-wide rollout. The most consequential edits clarify EPM support-approved elevations, a 1,000-entry limit for Edge URL lists, Settings catalog (DDM) filter support, Android maximum-OS triggers, and Microsoft Tunnel DNS guidance. A separate Apple update-policy page removes an old DDM filter limitation warning but does not state that a replacement capability was added.
2026-02-12.adminImpact: Review support-approved EPM workflows for shared or non-primary-user devices. Audit Microsoft Edge allowed and blocked URL lists because entries after 1,000 are ignored. Use the revised DDM workload matrix when evaluating assignment filters, and update Android app-protection runbooks to reflect the documented Max OS version direction. For Microsoft Tunnel split tunneling with corporate DNS, check that the DNS addresses are in the include rules. Treat the wording changes as documentation clarification unless other release evidence or tenant testing confirms a product behavior change.

keyChanges.title: EPM support-approved requests are no longer described as primary-user-only
keyChanges.detail: The support-approved elevation page now states that requests can be submitted by all users of a device and aren't limited to its primary user. Administrators should revisit approval workflows for shared or multi-user devices, while recognizing that the supplied evidence is a documentation update rather than a separate rollout notice.

keyChanges.title: Edge allow/block URL policies now document a 1,000-entry ceiling
keyChanges.detail: For com.microsoft.intune.mam.managedbrowser.AllowListURLs and BlockListURLs, corresponding to the Allowed URLs and Blocked URLs UI settings, the guidance now says each policy is limited to 1,000 entries and subsequent entries are ignored. Audit lists at or near that limit.

keyChanges.title: Settings catalog (DDM) is marked supported in the assignment-filter matrix
keyChanges.detail: The Filters Supported Workloads table changes Settings catalog (DDM) from unsupported to supported in two entries. This is a support-matrix update; the supplied diff does not identify the affected workload rows or announce a separate feature rollout.

keyChanges.title: Android app protection corrects the Max OS version trigger direction
keyChanges.detail: The App Protection Policy Settings Android page now says OS versions above the configured Max OS version trigger Warn or Block access. The Min OS version condition remains for versions below the minimum. The change corrects the documented condition rather than introducing a new setting.

keyChanges.title: Microsoft Tunnel guidance adds corporate DNS to split-tunnel include rules
keyChanges.detail: When corporate DNS is used in the server configuration, the updated guidance says those addresses should be added to the include rules for split tunneling. The page also retains the warning that 0.0.0.0 must not be used in include or exclude ranges because Tunnel Gateway can't route traffic with that range.

2026-02-13.headline: Defender Vulnerability Management prerequisites are clarified for Intune administrators
2026-02-13.overview: This was a documentation-only period, not a feature-launch or retirement cycle. The most consequential update adds actionable prerequisites and setup detail for the Defender Vulnerability Management–Intune integration. Windows MDM automatic enrollment remains in public preview, while its rollout caveat is removed and the guide now reports no known issues. The remaining changes are a security-overview restructure and a minor wording correction.
2026-02-13.adminImpact: For Defender Vulnerability Management integration, verify Intune Plan 1 and Microsoft Defender for Endpoint coverage, the service-to-service connection, the Microsoft Intune connection enabled in the Defender portal, and device onboarding with risk assessment enabled. Do not interpret the Windows enrollment edits as general availability: the feature is still documented as public preview. Treat the revised platform list as an overview-page change, and consult detailed platform documentation before making support or deployment decisions.

keyChanges.title: Defender Vulnerability Management integration guidance adds concrete prerequisites
keyChanges.detail: The article replaces older “Threat & Vulnerability Management” terminology with Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management and adds a Prerequisites section. It lists Microsoft Intune Plan 1 and Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, requires a service-to-service connection with the Microsoft Intune connection enabled in the Defender portal, and calls for onboarding devices and enabling risk assessment. The stated workflow covers creating Intune security tasks, tracking remediation, and reducing vulnerability exposure;11

keyChanges.title: Windows MDM automatic enrollment guidance drops its rollout caveat
keyChanges.detail: The Windows enrollment page still identifies MDM automatic enrollment as public preview, but removes the wording that it is “undergoing rollout” and that some users may not see the setting. This is a change to the published preview guidance, not a general-availability announcement.

keyChanges.title: Windows enrollment documentation now reports no known issues
keyChanges.detail: The known-issues section now states: “There are no known issues in Microsoft Intune with MDM automatic enrollment for Windows.” This updates the documented status while the feature remains publicly previewed.

keyChanges.title: Security overview separates platform support from on-premises extension
keyChanges.detail: The Protect data and devices overview is reframed around Zero Trust, adds a Platform support section, and now lists Android, iOS/iPadOS, and Windows. Tenant attach and co-management are moved into an “Extend to on-premises devices” section. Linux and macOS no longer appear in this overview list, but the diff contains no support-retirement or deprecation statement, so this should be treated as a documentation-scope change rather than proof of capability removal.

2026-02-14.headline: Intune’s February development roadmap arrives with January 2026 service update
2026-02-14.overview: The period contains two Microsoft 365 Message Center notices and no new, updated, or removed documentation entries. One publishes an updated February 2026 In Development feature list for readiness; the other announces the January 2026 Intune service build and directs administrators to Tenant Status and current feature resources.
2026-02-14.adminImpact: Review the February In Development list, brief helpdesk staff, and update user guidance as needed before features roll out in the next month or later releases. For the January service update, check the release number in the Tenant Status blade and review the What's New page and related blogs. The supplied notices do not identify individual features or establish specific preview or general-availability changes.

keyChanges.title: February 2026 In Development list becomes available
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft published an updated Intune In Development features list to support organizational readiness. The notice says the features may roll out in the next month or in later releases, but it does not identify the individual capabilities or their availability states.

keyChanges.title: January 2026 Intune service build is announced
keyChanges.detail: The Intune service has been updated to the January 2026 build. Administrators can find the release number in the Tenant Status blade and are directed to review the latest What's New page and related blogs for changes and new capabilities.

2026-02-15.headline: Configuration Manager state-messaging guidance moves under Update Management
2026-02-15.overview: The only change this period is a low-impact Configuration Manager documentation relocation. The State Messages reference now points to the Update Management path; the evidence does not indicate a product-behavior or configuration change.
2026-02-15.adminImpact: Administrators maintaining bookmarks or links to the State Messages article should update them to /troubleshoot/mem/configmgr/update-management/state-messaging-description. No tenant, rollout, or configuration action is supported by the supplied evidence.

keyChanges.title: State Messages article path was relocated
keyChanges.detail: The reference changed from /troubleshoot/mem/configmgr/state-messaging-description to /troubleshoot/mem/configmgr/update-management/state-messaging-description. This is a documentation-path change only; no change to state-message behavior, settings, or prerequisites is identified.

2026-02-17.headline: Configuration Manager hotfix stops co-managed updates falling back to WSUS
2026-02-17.overview: The period’s most consequential change is KB36495448 for Configuration Manager: it addresses incomplete Windows Update scan-source policies that could redirect Intune- or WUfB-targeted Feature and Quality Updates to WSUS on co-managed devices using third-party updates. Connected Cache guidance also documents selective HTTPS delivery, while HSTS guidance adds an important site-system compatibility warning. Most remaining edits are mechanical replacements of sample GUIDs, identifiers, links, and examples rather than evidence of new Intune service behavior.
2026-02-17.adminImpact: Administrators using Configuration Manager 2503 or 2509 with co-management and third-party updates should assess the KB36495448 client fix, especially where Feature or Quality Updates are unexpectedly sourced from WSUS. Teams or Intune-managed Win32 delivery through Connected Cache over HTTPS requires a valid TLS certificate from the organization’s PKI. Review HSTS or HTTPS-redirection changes against Configuration Manager site-system roles; the other highlighted Intune edits are documentation clarification and do not indicate a required tenant change.

keyChanges.title: KB36495448 fixes partial scan-source policies on co-managed devices
keyChanges.detail: The new Configuration Manager client-fix reference covers versions 2503, with Update rollup 32851084 installed, and 2509. With third-party updates enabled, the client could set only part of the Windows Update scan-source policy, causing Feature Updates and Quality Updates intended for Intune or Windows Update for Business to come from WSUS or Configuration Manager instead. The fix stops Configuration Manager from setting or modifying the affected scan-source values and cleans up incomplete values left by earlier###

keyChanges.title: Connected Cache guidance adds selective HTTPS delivery
keyChanges.detail: The Connected Cache update now applies to Configuration Manager 2409, 2503, and 2509. It documents proxy support for environments requiring absolute URLs and lets distribution point cache nodes deliver Intune-managed Win32 application content over HTTPS, including Microsoft Teams content for the first time. Cache nodes need a valid TLS certificate generated through the organization’s PKI; other content types continue to use HTTP.

keyChanges.title: HSTS guidance warns of HTTP-role breakage in Configuration Manager
keyChanges.detail: The revised communications guidance says Configuration Manager does not support HSTS configuration in IIS, clients do not honor HSTS headers, and mandatory HTTPS redirection is incompatible with HTTP or Enhanced HTTP site-system roles. The Fallback Status Point is HTTP-only, while WSUS-based Software Update Points still deliver update payloads over HTTP, so HSTS or HTTPS redirection can break those functions. This is a security and compatibility clarification, not a new Intune control.

keyChanges.title: Device Protect guidance clarifies mixed-management and managed-app coverage
keyChanges.detail: This is an editorial clarification rather than evidence of a new capability. The page is retitled “Protect data and devices with Microsoft Intune,” explicitly references third-party compliance and Mobile Threat Defense signals, separates Microsoft Entra Conditional Access for MFA from Intune sign-in settings, and states that app-based Conditional Access can require managed apps while personal data remains unaffected. It also more specifically describes co-management and tenant attach for on-premises and hybrid-held

2026-02-18.headline: Remote Help guidance now requires dedicated Android devices for unattended access
2026-02-18.overview: The clearest administrator-relevant change is Remote Help’s revised unattended-access prerequisite: the updated guidance names Android Enterprise dedicated devices and no longer lists fully managed devices. Configuration Manager also received updated 2509 Connected Cache hotfix instructions, while Intune and co-management updates mainly clarify applicability, supported Windows terminology, and administrator roles. The remaining edits are largely documentation maintenance, including shared Global Administrator callouts, capitalization, screenshot metadata, and Connected Cache wording.
2026-02-18.adminImpact: Review Remote Help designs that rely on unattended access for fully managed Android devices. If applying the Configuration Manager 2509 Connected Cache hotfix, use DoincInstall.exe version 1.5.6.44280 on every applicable site server. Use the updated Multi Admin Approval and co-management pages for current documented scope; the supplied evidence does not establish a separate service-side feature rollout.

keyChanges.title: Remote Help guidance narrows the Android unattended-access prerequisite
keyChanges.detail: The updated Remote Help page states that unattended access requires an Android device enrolled as an Android Enterprise dedicated device. The previous wording also allowed fully managed devices. This is a documentation change, so validate the requirement in affected designs without assuming the service behavior itself changed.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager 2509 hotfix guidance updates the Connected Cache installer
keyChanges.detail: The instructions replace DoincInstall.exe version 1.5.5.9002 with version 1.5.6.44280, listed as a 31.1 MB file dated 2/18/2026. When applying the hotfix, the procedure says to copy the executable to {SMSInstallDir}\bin\x64 on all site servers, including the CAS if present and passive sites.

keyChanges.title: Multi Admin Approval scope now explicitly includes compliance and Settings catalog policies
keyChanges.detail: The Intune guidance now lists creating and managing compliance policies and creating and managing configuration policies through the Settings catalog as covered activities. It continues to state that app deployments are covered while app protection policies are not. The evidence supports an applicability clarification, not a newly announced workflow.

keyChanges.title: Co-management enrollment guidance now points to supported Windows versions
keyChanges.detail: The Configuration Manager enablement procedure changes the **All** automatic-enrollment description from clients running Windows 10 version 1709 or later to clients running supported Windows versions. It also removes the Windows 10-or-later qualifier from the co-managed-device workload description. Administrators should use the linked supported-devices list rather than infer that the supported platform range expanded.

keyChanges.title: Autopilot OEM registration guidance names the approving role explicitly
keyChanges.detail: The OEM registration page now says that the organization’s Microsoft Entra Global Administrator must approve the OEM, replacing the more general wording that the organization must grant permission. The page also adopts a shared Global Administrator guidance include; the supplied evidence indicates terminology and documentation consolidation rather than a changed authorization workflow.

2026-02-19.headline: Automated Device Enrollment needs alternate MFA for iOS Setup Assistant
2026-02-19.overview: All 25 supplied changes are documentation updates, with no message-center announcement. The most actionable guidance adds an explicit iOS/iPadOS enrollment MFA limitation, clarifies failure conditions for macOS Direct Enrollment, and tightens Configuration Manager BitLocker policy guidance. Other notable edits correct a task-sequence imaging instruction and document a Company Portal path for unmanaged Android line-of-business apps. The evidence does not establish a new feature launch, preview, general availability milestone, or retirement during the period.
2026-02-19.adminImpact: Prioritize the Automated Device Enrollment, macOS enrollment, and Configuration Manager BitLocker notes in operational runbooks. Check that iOS/iPadOS modern-authentication enrollments have an alternate MFA method, avoid unsupported Apple enrollment-restriction assignments, and look for conflicting domain BitLocker policies. The supplied evidence supports documentation and configuration review, not a broad rollout change.

keyChanges.title: iOS/iPadOS ADE documentation adds a phishing-resistant MFA limitation
keyChanges.detail: The Automated Device Enrollment Authentication page adds a caution that phishing-resistant MFA is currently unsupported in Setup Assistant for iOS/iPadOS. Users enrolling through Automated Device Enrollment with modern authentication must have an alternate MFA method available to complete enrollment. This is newly documented guidance; the evidence does not say that the service behavior itself newly changed.

keyChanges.title: macOS Direct Enrollment now spells out restriction-related enrollment failures
keyChanges.detail: The guidance says enrollment restrictions are not supported for this enrollment method. A device platform restriction targeted at any Apple device can cause profile download to fail, and using a profile downloaded before an enrollment restriction was configured—after that restriction is enabled—will also cause enrollment to fail.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager BitLocker guidance emphasizes domain GPO precedence
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance explicitly distinguishes standalone MBAM domain policies from Configuration Manager local BitLocker policies: domain policies override the local Configuration Manager policies. It now recommends avoiding group policies for BitLocker and configuring all settings through Configuration Manager BitLocker management policies.

keyChanges.title: Task-sequence imaging guidance reverses the cached-scan instruction
keyChanges.detail: For the option controlling use of cached Windows Update Agent scan results, the article now says to disable the option when using a task sequence to capture and build an OS image. Disabling it also instructs the agent to download the latest catalog from the software update point; the previous text incorrectly said to enable it for image capture.

keyChanges.title: Unmanaged Android app guidance adds a Company Portal LOB scenario
keyChanges.detail: The Apps deployment article now documents that unmanaged Android users can browse and install available line-of-business applications from the Company Portal instead of the Play Store. It specifies Android-Line-of-Business apps with Target platform set to Device Administrator, while also linking an end-of-support note for Android device administrator devices. This is documentation coverage, not evidence of a new rollout or availability change.

2026-02-20.headline: Endpoint Privilege Management guidance specifies add-on licensing and Windows-only scope
2026-02-20.overview: This was a documentation-only day: ten updates, with no new, removed, or Message Center items. The consequential change is an Intune endpoint-security clarification that explicitly documents Endpoint Privilege Management (EPM) as a least-privilege control, requires an additional Intune add-on license—standalone or through the Intune Suite—and limits EPM policies to Windows. Separate enrollment guidance adds a precise macOS failure message and documents that bring-your-own VPN configurations aren't supported during Windows Autopilot pre-provisioning; the Configuration Manager work is chiefly version labeling and sample cleanup.
2026-02-20.adminImpact: The supplied evidence does not establish a new EPM launch, preview, general availability status, retirement, or licensing change; it clarifies the documented requirement and platform scope. Verify the required add-on or Intune Suite entitlement before assigning EPM policies. For direct-enrolled macOS devices, avoid Apple-targeted device platform restrictions and use the exact documented error when troubleshooting. Do not plan bring-your-own VPN configurations for Windows Autopilot pre-provisioning. The Connected Cache formatting and reference edits alone do not support a rollout change.

keyChanges.title: EPM guidance adds explicit licensing and platform boundaries
keyChanges.detail: This is a documentation clarification, not a launch announcement. The revised endpoint-security guidance places Endpoint Privilege Management in the Zero Trust and least-privilege model, describing temporary elevation through application elevation rules. It explicitly says EPM requires an additional Intune add-on license, available standalone or through the Microsoft Intune Suite, and that EPM policies are available only for Windows devices.

keyChanges.title: Direct-enroll macOS guidance adds the precise profile-download error
keyChanges.detail: The existing limitation remains: this enrollment method doesn't support device enrollment restrictions, and Apple-targeted device platform restrictions can cause the enrollment profile download to fail. The revised warning adds the diagnostic text: `File download error. Failed to dynamically fetch target download uri.` It also retains the failure condition for profiles downloaded before a restriction is enabled and then used afterward.

keyChanges.title: Windows Autopilot pre-provisioning guidance excludes bring-your-own VPN
keyChanges.detail: The Windows Autopilot Hybrid article now states that bring-your-own (BYO) VPN configurations aren't supported during Windows Autopilot in pre-provisioning mode. Administrators planning that phase should not rely on a BYO VPN configuration.

keyChanges.title: Connected Cache guidance is labeled for ConfigMgr 2409, 2503, and 2509
keyChanges.detail: The Configuration Manager article title and description now identify Microsoft Connected Cache updates for versions 2409, 2503, and 2509 rather than only 2509. Other changes are ordinary reference maintenance: PowerShell examples are placed in fenced code blocks, the RFC link points specifically to section 5.1.2, and punctuation is corrected in the Enhanced HTTP warning and `resetdps.trn` instruction. The supplied diff indicates no new Connected Cache capability or behavior change.

2026-02-22.headline: Configuration Manager PXE guidance clarifies the RamDisk TFTP block-size setting
2026-02-22.overview: A single Configuration Manager documentation edit clarifies that the registry customization on PXE-enabled distribution points concerns the RamDisk TFTP block size, not the TFTP window size. This is a terminology correction in operating-system-deployment guidance; the supplied evidence does not indicate a changed default, registry path, value, or product behavior.
2026-02-22.adminImpact: Administrators using the PXE deployment guidance should interpret the registry-key instruction as controlling RamDisk TFTP block size. No configuration or rollout change is supported by this documentation edit alone.

keyChanges.title: PXE guidance replaces “TFTP window size” with “TFTP block size”
keyChanges.detail: In Prepare Site System Roles for Operating System Deployments, the instruction for customizing the setting on PXE-enabled distribution points now refers to the RamDisk TFTP block size rather than the RamDisk TFTP window size. The evidence supports a documentation clarification, not a confirmed product-setting change.

2026-02-23.headline: Certificate Connector 6.2510.3.2002 enforces an allow list for SCEP extensions
2026-02-23.overview: The strongest administrator-facing change is a security enforcement: Certificate Connector 6.2510.3.2002 blocks unknown SCEP certificate extensions and enforces a six-OID list. Intune service release 2602 also documents changed Advanced Analytics Device query syntax, expanded multi-administrator approval, new Apple DDM and Settings Catalog options, and the approaching end of legacy Apple software-update policy creation. The new Configuration Manager 2509 reference is informational, detailing collected data by diagnostic level and clarifying that Basic and Enhanced levels don't collect IP addresses, user names, computer names, physical addresses, or email addresses. The remaining diffs are largely maintenance: Autopilot workflow text and formatting changes, archive backfills, and ConfigMgr note or code formatting.
2026-02-23.adminImpact: Validate SCEP certificate extensions against the permitted OID list when adopting Certificate Connector 6.2510.3.2002. Audit saved Device query queries for the unsupported Device.DeviceId join and bare Device references in operators. Review use of legacy Apple software-update policies because Intune says support for creating them will soon end, although this update supplies no cutoff date or migration procedure. The Apple DDM, Settings Catalog, and multi-administrator approval entries are presented as current capabilities, not explicitly as preview or GA. No tenant action is indicated by the primarily editorial and archival changes.

keyChanges.title: Certificate Connector adds an allow list for SCEP certificate extensions
keyChanges.detail: Starting with Certificate Connector version 6.2510.3.2002, the SCEP validation service blocks unknown certificate extensions. The documented list includes 2.5.29.19 (Basic Constraints), 2.5.29.14 (Subject Key Identifier), 1.3.6.1.4.1.311.21.8 (Certificate Authority Version), 1.3.6.1.4.1.311.20.2 (Certificate Template Name), 2.5.29.1 (Authority Identifier, deprecated), and 2.5.29.3 (Certificate Policies, deprecated).

keyChanges.title: Device query changes join syntax and operator references
keyChanges.detail: The service-release entry adds leftsemi, rightsemi, leftanti, and rightanti joins. Joins using `on Device.DeviceId` are no longer supported; queries should use `on Device` or omit the on clause when joining on the device entity. Using `Device` alone in operators such as `distinct`, `summarize`, or `order by` is also no longer supported; a specific device property is required. Device-involving results now show the device as a clickable link, with clearer invalid-query messages.
keyChanges.product: Advanced Analytics — Device query for multiple devices

keyChanges.title: Apple DDM assignments and Settings Catalog gain new options
keyChanges.detail: Service release 2602 says assignment filters can be used in policy assignments for DDM-based configurations such as software updates on iOS/iPadOS. The Apple Settings Catalog adds AirPlay > Device Name for iOS/iPadOS and macOS, and the macOS Microsoft Defender category receives new settings.
keyChanges.product: Intune — Apple DDM and Settings Catalog

keyChanges.title: Multi-administrator approval expands to Settings Catalog and compliance policies
keyChanges.detail: Multi-administrator approval now supports device configuration policies created through the Settings Catalog and device compliance policies. When enabled, creating, editing, or deleting a policy requires approval from a second administrator before the change takes effect.

keyChanges.title: Legacy Apple MDM software-update policy creation is nearing retirement
keyChanges.detail: Apple deprecated legacy MDM software-update commands and payloads with iOS 26, iPadOS 26, and macOS 26. Intune says it will soon end support for creating legacy iOS/iPadOS and macOS software-update policies. The supplied entry does not provide an end date or replacement procedure.

2026-02-24.headline: Intune assignment filters gain granular management types as legacy values are replaced
2026-02-24.overview: An Intune managed-app assignment-filter rollout is the clearest operational change: Android and iOS/iPadOS management-type values are becoming more granular, legacy values are automatically mapped, and the update is expected to reach all customers by late March 2026. A new tenant-level how-to spells out the Windows diagnostic-data toggle and license attestation, while the Zero Trust material is planning guidance and the Automated Device Enrollment item clarifies an existing MFA limitation. The remaining Configuration Manager edits are predominantly terminology, link, formatting, and role-guidance maintenance; no Message Center announcement is supplied.
2026-02-24.adminImpact: As the filter rollout approaches, audit managed-app assignment filters, especially for devices without Microsoft Entra registration and a Microsoft Entra Device ID or devices managed by a third-party MDM; automatic mapping will not match those cases. If you depend on Windows compatibility or update-failure reporting, review the Windows data toggle and tenant license attestation. For Automated Device Enrollment through Setup Assistant with modern authentication, provide an alternate MFA method. Treat the Zero Trust sequencing as recommended planning guidance, not an automatic policy change.

keyChanges.title: Managed app assignment filters move from legacy values to enrollment-specific types
keyChanges.detail: This is a staged Intune capability rollout, not merely a wording edit. Android lists granular corporate-owned work-profile, fully managed, dedicated-device, and personally-owned work-profile values; iOS/iPadOS adds Automated Device Enrollment user-associated and userless devices, Account Driven User Enrollment, and Device Enrollment with Company Portal and Web Enrollment. The legacy Android Enterprise and Managed values are being deprecated. Existing filters are automatically mapped, but the mapping requires a user

keyChanges.title: Windows diagnostic-data and license-attestation controls get a tenant-level how-to
keyChanges.detail: The new Intune article gives the exact path Tenant administration > Connectors and tokens > Windows data and names the toggle Enable features that require Windows diagnostic data in processor configuration, whose default is Off. Turning it Off disables Intune features that rely on this configuration, although it might not disable processor configuration enabled by other methods. The guidance also explains tenant license attestation for dependent features and says attestation confirms entitlement rather than activat

keyChanges.title: A new seven-layer Zero Trust framework spans app protection to endpoint DLP
keyChanges.detail: Intune's new deployment approach presents a recommended seven-layer progression for Zero Trust device security, starting with app protection and extending to endpoint data loss prevention. It is a planning framework and conceptual guidance, not evidence that Intune has introduced a new enforcement feature or that administrators must reorder existing policies.

keyChanges.title: Zero Trust guidance recommends compliance and enforcement before configuration profiles
keyChanges.detail: The revised deployment plan explicitly places layers 3–4—compliance policies and enforcement—before layer 5, configuration profiles, describing an “assess and block first, configure second” approach. This is security and rollout guidance; the diff does not indicate that Intune automatically changes policy order or tenant settings.

keyChanges.title: ADE Setup Assistant guidance clarifies the modern-authentication MFA limitation
keyChanges.detail: The Automated Device Enrollment page now explicitly says phishing-resistant MFA isn't supported on iOS/iPadOS Setup Assistant and that users enrolling with Setup Assistant plus modern authentication need an alternate MFA method. This is a scope and wording clarification of the documented enrollment limitation, not evidence that the limitation was newly introduced.

2026-02-25.headline: Collection, residency, sharing, and user rights shape Intune's expanded privacy guidance
2026-02-25.overview: 25 February was primarily an Intune privacy-content expansion and path reorganization. New or newly surfaced Learn pages cover what Intune collects, where Customer Data is stored and processed, what it shares with Apple, Google, Jamf, and Zebra, and how admins handle personal-data requests. An added compliance overview and removed older compliance page appear to be a documentation move, not a product certification or feature retirement. The supplied diffs identify no Intune feature launch, preview, GA transition, deadline, or tenant-behavior change; many remaining edits are link, path, wording, and formatting corrections.
2026-02-25.adminImpact: Use the privacy pages as governance references rather than as evidence that tenant settings changed. Check the tenant's geography in endpoint.microsoft.com under Tenant Administration > Tenant Status, update internal links and bookmarks to the new /privacy paths, and use the documented audit, export, and deletion routes for data-subject requests. Cloud PKI's index retains the limitation that a data residency option is currently unavailable. For Zero Trust planning, involve the identity team because the revised guidance places Conditional Access policy creation in Microsoft Entra ID, not Intune.

keyChanges.title: Privacy overview defines Intune's data-processing scope and user rights
keyChanges.detail: The new Privacy and personal data in Intune overview states that Intune operates as a data processor under the Microsoft Online Services Terms. It covers collection, storage, retention, processing, security, sharing, auditing, export, review, correction, and deletion; says Intune does not use service-collected personal data for profiling, advertising, or marketing; and points to Company Portal terms and conditions for displaying an organization's privacy statement before enrollment. This is newly organized guidance

keyChanges.title: Storage guidance sets geography at Entra provisioning and preserves existing locations
keyChanges.detail: The storage and processing reference says Intune operates in North America, Europe, and Asia Pacific, with local geographies in Australia, India, and Switzerland. A tenant's geography is selected from the country or region in its Microsoft Entra directory at first provisioning and cannot be changed later; later deployments do not move existing tenants. The page also notes that preview, beta, or other prerelease services typically store Customer Data in the United States but might store it globally. Existing-tenants

keyChanges.title: Personal-data procedures document two-year audit retention and three handling routes
keyChanges.detail: The audit, export, or delete article documents two-year retention for user and device audit logs, automatic deletion after two years, and that admins cannot delete logs; admins can request them through the support form. Export is available from the All devices node or through Export-IntuneData.ps1. For deletion, it lists deleting the user from Microsoft Entra ID, resetting the device, or user self-removal. These are documented procedures, not evidence that a new deletion control shipped.

keyChanges.title: Apple integration reference lists account prerequisites and exchanged fields
keyChanges.detail: For Apple DEP, APNs, ASM, and VPP, the reference says Intune establishes a connection with Apple when the service is enabled and requires an Apple account for each service. Its tables identify exchanged values including APNs message type, topic, device UDID, OS and build version, product name, and ASM/DEP server, organization, device, and profile-status fields. It documents the data flow; the diff does not say that Apple integrations changed.

keyChanges.title: Zero Trust Layer 4 now emphasizes healthy, compliant devices
keyChanges.detail: The deployment guide changes the section from Conditional Access enforcement to Require healthy and compliant devices. It frames Layer 4 as requiring healthy and compliant devices before access and directs admins to work with the identity team to create Conditional Access policies in Microsoft Entra ID. This is a terminology and workflow clarification, not a new Conditional Access capability.

2026-02-26.headline: Azure Monitor export guidance warns Intune log consumers about duplicate data
2026-02-26.overview: 26 February was dominated by documentation maintenance: all 21 supplied changes were updates, with no new or removed items and no message-center notices. The clearest operational exception is Azure Monitor guidance documenting possible duplication of up to 100% of data published in a 24-hour period and identifying Intune Audit and Operational logs as routable. Other meaningful edits clarify deployment-plan paths for macOS and Apple passcodes, state a 180-day Device actions report window, and update the supported-apps catalog. The evidence does not establish a feature launch, preview, general availability change, retirement, or newly changed service behavior.
2026-02-26.adminImpact: If your tenant routes Intune Audit or Operational logs through Azure Monitor, ensure consuming systems can handle duplicates of up to 100% within a 24-hour publication period. For deployment planning, use the revised macOS endpoint detection and response and Apple DDM Passcode references, while treating the table changes as documentation guidance rather than proof of a new rollout. Set reporting expectations around the documented 180-day Device actions window. The app-catalog and Configuration Manager link changes are reference updates and do not by themselves require tenant changes.

keyChanges.title: Azure Monitor export guidance documents possible duplicate Intune log data
keyChanges.detail: The Review Logs Using Azure Monitor page adds a Known Issues note that the export pipeline may duplicate up to 100% of data published in a 24-hour period, and says consuming systems should be prepared for duplicated data. It also identifies Intune Audit logs and Operational logs as available for routing. This clarifies an export behavior; it does not show that the behavior began during this period.

keyChanges.title: Deployment plan points macOS to EDR and prefers Apple DDM passcodes
keyChanges.detail: The Deployment Plan Configuration Profile table changes macOS from “Not available” to the Intune endpoint detection and response profile for Microsoft Defender for Endpoint. It also marks Intune settings catalog > Declarative Device Management (DDM) > Passcode as preferred for iOS/iPadOS and macOS, while retaining other passcode paths. The evidence supports a guidance update, not a product-launch claim.

keyChanges.title: Device actions report scope is documented as 180 days
keyChanges.detail: The Reports page now states that the Device actions report contains data for the past 180 days. This clarifies the documented report window; the change does not state that the underlying retention policy changed.

keyChanges.title: Supported-apps catalog lists DeepL, EasyPlant, Foxit, PerfectServe, and Synigo
keyChanges.detail: The supported Intune apps table adds entries for DeepL for Intune, EasyPlant QC Inspections, Foxit PDF Editor, PerfectServe Clinical Collab, and Synigo Pulse. The supplied evidence shows a catalog update, not a separately announced Intune capability, availability change, or rollout date.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager overview refreshes diagnostic-data links for 2509 and 2503
keyChanges.detail: The Levels Overview page adds links for diagnostic and usage data for Configuration Manager 2509 and 2503 and removes links for 2403 and 2309. This is index maintenance; no change to diagnostic-data collection behavior is stated.

2026-02-27.headline: Windows diagnostic-data and stale-device cleanup guidance sharpens Intune tenant administration
2026-02-27.overview: The supplied evidence is documentation-led rather than a feature-release bulletin: there are no Message Center items, and it does not establish a preview, general-availability launch, retirement, or product behavior change. The most consequential material adds concrete tenant setup, cleanup, RBAC, compliance-synchronization, and Configuration Manager upgrade guidance. Other sampled edits are mainly link moves, support-navigation corrections, and wording cleanup.
2026-02-27.adminImpact: Prioritize review where these workflows are in use: verify Windows diagnostic-data and license-entitlement settings before relying on dependent reports or alerts; set cleanup thresholds with the no-wipe/no-retire and certificate behavior in mind; grant Tenant Status access using the documented read permissions or built-in roles; and validate the role-specific registry data after Configuration Manager site upgrades. The cross-document link repairs alone do not justify tenant changes.

keyChanges.title: Windows diagnostic-data and license verification setup is spelled out
keyChanges.detail: A new Intune how-to identifies Tenant administration > Connectors and tokens > Windows data as the configuration location. The setting **Enable features that require Windows diagnostic data in processor configuration** defaults to Off; turning it Off disables Intune features that rely on that configuration, although it might not undo processor configuration enabled elsewhere. Dependencies listed include Windows Update compatibility and expedite reports plus failure alerts for driver, expedited quality, and feature-

keyChanges.title: Device cleanup rules hide stale records rather than wipe or retire devices
keyChanges.detail: New how-to guidance says scheduled cleanup rules hide devices from the Intune portal and reports after a configured period, with the setting accepting 30 to 270 days. One rule can be created per platform and applies to all devices on that platform. Cleaned-up devices can reappear before their device certificate expires; after expiration, re-enrollment is required. The rules aren't available for Jamf-managed devices.

keyChanges.title: Tenant Status access requires three Intune read permissions
keyChanges.detail: The new Tenant Status guidance documents the path Tenant administration > Tenant Status and the information shown there, including tenant details, service release versions, licenses, enrolled devices, connector status, and health messages. Access requires `Organization.Read`, `ManagedDevice.Read`, and `ManagedApp.Read`; the Intune Read Only Operator role grants them, while a custom role or the Intune Administrator Microsoft Entra role can also be used. PIM roles must be elevated before viewing the page.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager upgrades need role-specific registry validation
keyChanges.detail: The revised post-upgrade procedure says to inspect `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\SecurePipeServers\Winreg\AllowedPaths`, value `Machine`, after upgrading a central administration site, primary site, secondary site, or distribution point. CAS, primary, and secondary sites should include `Software\Microsoft\SMS`; distribution points should include `Software\Microsoft\SMS\DP`. If the role-specific data is missing, the guidance says to add it manually to avoid site-system inbox upload issues and possible DP, ,

keyChanges.title: Compliance-partner guidance makes Workspace ONE UEM synchronization explicit
keyChanges.detail: The updated Intune partner-compliance article states that changes saved in the Intune admin center must be manually synchronized from the Workspace ONE UEM console. Until synchronization, UEM is unaware of the configuration changes and users in newly assigned groups do not successfully report compliance. Azure services synchronize changes made after the initial configuration or the last manual synchronization. This is a procedural documentation clarification, not evidence of a changed integration rollout.

2026-03-02.headline: Unlicensed-admin caps and device-cleanup behavior gain precise Intune guidance
2026-03-02.overview: 2 March is primarily a documentation-reorganization day, not a feature-release bulletin. A large cluster of pages replaces legacy licensing links with the new `/fundamentals/licensing/` index and assignment paths; the new licensing guidance reiterates that users need an Intune license before enrollment and that unenrolled app-protection users also require one. Meaningful exceptions include newly published procedures for unlicensed administrators, device cleanup, Tenant Status, and Honeywell OEMConfig, plus in-development entries for EPM, MAM, macOS Recovery Lock, and Remote Help networking. The supplied evidence does not establish general availability for those additions. Other edits are mechanical—for example, the Android app-protection settings diff shows a date and grammar correction, not a stated policy-value change.
2026-03-02.adminImpact: Action is selective. For unlicensed-admin access, note the irreversible enablement, 350-direct-member-per-security-group limit, and possible 48-hour delay. For device cleanup, validate the required RBAC permissions and the 30–270-day threshold. Tenant Status delegation requires the documented read permissions or the Intune Read Only Operator role. Network teams should update Remote Help firewall rules only when the new endpoint becomes available. The licensing URL edits themselves do not indicate a tenant configuration change.

keyChanges.title: Unlicensed-admin access has one-way enablement and a 350-admin ceiling
keyChanges.detail: New guidance documents the path **Tenant administration** > **Roles** > **Administrator Licensing** > **Allow access to unlicensed admins**. Selecting **Yes** cannot be undone, access changes can take up to 48 hours, and Intune supports up to 350 unlicensed admins per security group, limited to direct members. Assigned roles continue to define each administrator’s access scope. This documents an access option; it is not evidence of a new launch in this period.

keyChanges.title: Device cleanup rules hide stale records without wiping or retiring devices
keyChanges.detail: The new procedure says scheduled cleanup rules hide devices from the Intune portal and reports after a specified period without check-in, but do not wipe or retire them. A cleaned-up device can reappear if it checks in before its device certificate expires; after certificate expiry, re-enrollment is required. Admins can create one rule per platform and set the threshold from 30 to 270 days. Jamf-managed devices are excluded, and configuration requires the documented cleanup-rule and managed-device permissions.

keyChanges.title: Tenant Status guidance names dashboard data and least-privilege permissions
keyChanges.detail: Newly added guidance directs administrators to **Tenant administration** > **Tenant Status** for tenant name and location, service release information, licensed users, enrolled devices, connector status, and Intune or tenant messages. Access requires `Organization.Read`, `ManagedDevice.Read`, and `ManagedApp.Read`; those permissions are granted by the **Intune Read Only Operator** role, or can be provided through a custom role. The Intune Administrator role and elevated PIM access are also supported.

keyChanges.title: Endpoint Privilege Management and MAM items remain in development
keyChanges.detail: The **In Development** tracker describes an EPM reporting fix in which report viewers’ assigned scope limits visible users and devices. It also describes Multiple Managed Accounts for Intune MAM on iOS/iPadOS and Android, with app-protection policies enforced independently for each account. The same edit lists macOS Recovery Lock settings-catalog controls to turn on the feature, set a recovery password, configure rotation, or clear the password. No delivery date or general-availability designation appears in the-s‌

keyChanges.title: Remote Help connectivity planning adds a Windows-specific endpoint
keyChanges.detail: For launching Remote Help from the Intune admin center on Windows devices, Microsoft says it is working on improved connectivity and identifies `*.trouter.communications.svc.cloud.microsoft.com` as an endpoint to add. The guidance recommends updating firewall rules once the endpoint becomes available, so the entry does not support treating it as an immediate new firewall requirement.

2026-03-03.headline: Apple outlines userless visionOS/tvOS enrollment and DDM for iOS/iPadOS apps
2026-03-03.overview: The most consequential updates are planned Apple capabilities on Intune’s In Development page: service-access controls for organization-owned Apple devices, userless automated device enrollment (ADE) for visionOS and tvOS, and Declarative Device Management (DDM) for required line-of-business apps on iOS/iPadOS 18 and later. None is identified as generally available. Separate guidance clarifies Android prerequisites for Device Locate and documents a macOS LAPS issue affecting versions earlier than macOS 26.4. The remaining edits are largely editorial or documentation clarification, including adding Honeywell UEMConnect to the Managed Home Screen OEMConfig description and correcting What's New markup. The Message Center item only points to the February 2026 service build in Tenant Status and provides no feature-level detail.
2026-03-03.adminImpact: Treat the Apple and TeamViewer entries as forward-looking planning information rather than immediate rollout instructions; no availability dates are supplied. For Android Device Locate, verify that administrators have Device configuration/Read and scope-tag visibility to the location policy. For ADE-enrolled macOS devices earlier than 26.4, manually rotate the local administrator password after an unexpected reset to keep Intune and the device synchronized, or upgrade to macOS 26.4.

keyChanges.title: Apple’s roadmap adds userless ADE and service-access controls
keyChanges.detail: The In Development page says Intune will add userless ADE for visionOS and tvOS through Apple Business Manager or Apple School Manager, including custom configuration uploads, default enrollment restrictions, and remote device actions. It also describes future Apple access-management settings for organization-owned iOS/iPadOS and macOS devices, allowing administrators to control which devices users can sign in to and which apps and services are available. These are planned capabilities, not a general-availability (
keyChanges.product: Apple automated device enrollment and Apple service access

keyChanges.title: DDM support is planned for required Apple line-of-business apps
keyChanges.detail: Intune is adding Declarative Device Management support for configuring required line-of-business apps on iOS/iPadOS 18 and later. The described Managed App configuration uses policy-based deployment and configuration, real-time app status, and expanded per-app associated-domain attributes. The page says administrators will configure this by changing the app’s management type in App information; the entry remains an In Development announcement.

keyChanges.title: Android Device Locate prerequisites are stated more precisely
keyChanges.detail: The Device Locate guidance now explicitly says the Android remote action is available only when the administrator can read the policies configuring device location. The account must have the Device configuration/Read permission and scope-tag visibility to the device restriction or settings catalog policy controlling location settings. This is documented as a prerequisite clarification, not evidence of a newly announced product behavior change.

keyChanges.title: macOS LAPS guidance isolates the pre-26.4 password-reset issue
keyChanges.detail: The known issue affects macOS versions earlier than 26.4 when ADE enrollment uses a configured local administrator account and a targeted passcode profile. The device can prompt for an administrator password reset even when Change at next auth is disabled or Max Age (days) has a value; the standard account is unaffected. Microsoft’s documented workaround is to manually rotate the administrator password after the reset, while upgrading to macOS 26.4 resolves the issue.

keyChanges.title: A replacement TeamViewer connector experience is planned
keyChanges.detail: The In Development page says Intune will update its TeamViewer integration to simplify onboarding and improve reliability, replacing the existing connector experience in the Intune admin center. Organizations using the older connector will need to migrate after it is retired, but the supplied update does not provide a complete retirement date or migration window.

2026-03-04.headline: Windows settings catalog gains Edge silent printing and site-specific geolocation controls
2026-03-04.overview: The strongest Intune update identifies new Windows settings catalog policies for Edge: silent printing, an Edge for Business informational page after major browser updates, and URL-pattern controls that allow precise geolocation or block geolocation requests. The Autopilot comparison now lists up to 25 essential applications during OOBE, while iOS/iPadOS Company Portal guidance documents v5.2509.2 rather than v5.2311.1 as the minimum supported version. Other meaningful changes are operational: the Intune endpoint reference changes its destination list, and Microsoft Tunnel records version 20260129.1 with updated base images and security packages. Smaller edits clarify applicability and Android OEMConfig prerequisites; the only removal was a Configuration Manager hotfix article, which does not by itself show that the hotfix was retired.
2026-03-04.adminImpact: For Edge policy design, enabling Silent Printing closes print preview and uses the default printer; if the default printer is Save as PDF, output is saved to Downloads. The geolocation URL-list policies can allow high-accuracy access without a prompt or block sites from requesting location. The Edge for Business informational-page policy applies only to Microsoft Entra ID profiles, not Microsoft account profiles. If using the Autopilot comparison for rollout planning, update the OOBE assumption to up to 25 essential applications and up to 10 essential PowerShell scripts. Check iOS/iPadOS communications or baselines against Company Portal v5.2509.2; the evidence says older versions prompt users to update at sign-in, not that they are blocked. Network teams should compare proxy and firewall-

keyChanges.title: New Windows settings catalog policies list four Edge controls
keyChanges.detail: The March 4 What's New entry directs administrators to Devices > Configuration profiles > Create profile > Windows 10 and later > Settings catalog. It lists controls for the Edge for Business informational new-tab page after major browser updates, Silent Printing, allowing precise geolocation on specified sites, and blocking geolocation on specified sites. The informational-page policy shows the page when enabled or not configured for Microsoft Entra ID profiles, hides it when disabled, does not apply to Microsoft

keyChanges.title: Autopilot comparison now lists up to 25 essential OOBE applications
keyChanges.detail: The comparison table changes the OOBE provisioning figure from up to 10 to up to 25 essential line-of-business, Win32, Microsoft Store, or Microsoft 365 applications. It continues to list up to 10 essential PowerShell scripts and distinguishes device-based OOBE from device and user ESP. Because the evidence is a documentation-table diff, this should be treated as revised comparison guidance rather than proof of a separate feature rollout.

keyChanges.title: Company Portal's documented iOS/iPadOS minimum moves to v5.2509.2
keyChanges.detail: The minimum supported Company Portal version for iOS/iPadOS changes from v5.2311.1 to v5.2509.2. The guidance says users running an older version are prompted to update when they sign in; it provides no hard-block date or separate enforcement behavior.

keyChanges.title: Intune endpoint guidance now lists more identity, Store, and service hosts
keyChanges.detail: The revised endpoint reference adds entries including *.powershellgallery.com, cdn.oneget.org, go.microsoft.com, displaycatalog.mp.microsoft.com, purchase.md.mp.microsoft.com, licensing.mp.microsoft.com, storeedgefd.dsx.mp.microsoft.com, *.events.data.microsoft.com, enterpriseregistration.windows.net, login.microsoftonline.com, graph.windows.net, config.office.com, ecs.office.com, Teams, and regional lgmsape blob hosts. The diff also removes earlier swda, swdb, swdc, swdd, swdin, and content-auth asset hosts, so a6

keyChanges.title: Microsoft Tunnel records a maintenance image with refreshed security packages
keyChanges.detail: The March 2 release entry records Microsoft Tunnel version 20260129.1, with agent image digest sha256:abbdcd854aa5ac376aed32c828e4c84917e776a701855cd1e3febed18a3e4dae and server image digest sha256:ad57d6a7ffe21f64fc1577713063ae9b180914cf65bc70b4e49be21299cfc1d3. The listed changes are minor bug fixes, diagnostic improvements, and updated base container images and security packages; no new Tunnel capability or mandatory rollout is stated.

2026-03-05.headline: Configuration Manager hotfix fixes co-managed Feature and Quality Update redirection to WSUS
2026-03-05.overview: The standout operational change is KB36495448 for Configuration Manager: on co-managed devices running version 2503 with Update rollup 32851084 or version 2509, third-party-update integration could leave partial Windows Update scan-source policies and send Feature or Quality Updates to WSUS/Configuration Manager instead of Intune or Windows Update for Business. The hotfix stops Configuration Manager from setting those scan-source values and cleans up incomplete prior state. Intune also added Recovery Lock configuration guidance, expanded its security-baseline reference to Windows 11 version 25H2, and recorded service release 2602 support for Apple DDM assignment filters. Most other entries are ordinary link, table, metadata, or support-page relocation edits; the old support article was removed after its content moved to a new path.
2026-03-05.adminImpact: First identify co-managed environments matching the KB36495448 conditions and assess the hotfix, because the documented defect can source Feature and Quality Updates from WSUS/Configuration Manager instead of Intune or Windows Update for Business. Recovery Lock applies only to Intune-enrolled, supervised Macs running macOS 11.5 or later with Apple silicon; viewing or rotating the recovery password requires the documented custom remote-task permissions. Before adopting the Windows 11 25H2 security baseline, compare its documented defaults—especially SMB v1, UAC, SEHOP, and source-routing settings—with existing policy; the diff establishes updated baseline guidance, not a tenant-wide policy change. DDM assignment filters are available for DDM-based configurations on iOS/iPadOS and macOS. The

keyChanges.title: KB36495448 repairs Windows Update scan-source policies in co-managed Configuration Manager
keyChanges.detail: The fix applies to Configuration Manager 2503 with Update rollup 32851084 and version 2509 when third-party updates are enabled in a co-managed environment. The affected client could set only UseUpdateClassPolicySource and SetPolicyDrivenUpdateSourceForOtherUpdates, causing Feature and Quality Updates intended for Intune or Windows Update for Business to be redirected to WSUS/Configuration Manager. After the hotfix, Configuration Manager no longer sets those scan-source values on co-managed devices and cleans up an

keyChanges.title: Recovery Lock guidance sets a narrow macOS eligibility boundary
keyChanges.detail: New Intune settings-catalog guidance documents Recovery Lock for macOS. Intune generates a strong random password, requires it to access the recovery partition environment or update/remove the password, protects the Startup Options screen, and supports time-based rotation. The documented scope is macOS 11.5 or later on Apple silicon with Intune enrollment and supervision; Intel Macs are unsupported. Device actions can rotate the passcode, with custom permissions required to view or rotate it.

keyChanges.title: Intune security-baseline guidance adds Windows 11 version 25H2
keyChanges.detail: The security-baseline page now includes a Version 25H2 pivot based on the Windows 11 version 25H2 baseline, limited to settings that apply to Windows devices managed through Intune. Documented defaults include enabled prevention of the lock screen camera and slideshow, enabled UAC restrictions for local-account network logons, a disabled SMB v1 server, enabled SEHOP, and highest protection for IP source routing.

keyChanges.title: Service release 2602 documents Apple DDM assignment filters and protected apps
keyChanges.detail: The Intune service-release notes state that assignment filters can be used with policy assignments for DDM-based configurations such as software updates on iOS/iPadOS and macOS. They also list Jump by Accio Inc. and Mijn InPlanning by Intus Workforce Solutions for Android as newly available protected apps.

keyChanges.title: Windows account-registration MDM control enters public preview; Admin tasks reaches GA
keyChanges.detail: The public-preview setting Disable MDM enrollment when adding work or school account on Windows controls MDM enrollment during the Microsoft Entra account-registration flow. Its default is No, which allows enrollment, and the update says no action is required unless administrators want to change that behavior. The same release-note update says Admin tasks under Tenant Administration is out of preview and generally available, with search, filtering, and sorting.

2026-03-06.headline: Configuration Manager hotfix addresses co-managed devices redirected from Intune updates
2026-03-06.overview: 6 March is dominated by documentation maintenance, but one item has direct operational weight: a new Configuration Manager hotfix reference says KB36495448 fixes partial Windows Update scan-source policies on co-managed devices with third-party updates, which can send Intune or Windows Update for Business Feature and Quality Updates to WSUS or Configuration Manager. Intune changes refine Security Baselines, iOS app wrapping, and Windows automatic-enrollment guidance; the supplied diffs do not establish a new Intune feature, preview, GA announcement, or product retirement. A same-day removed record contains the same KB36495448 material as the new entry, with no evidence that the hotfix itself was retired.
2026-03-06.adminImpact: Prioritize review of KB36495448 for Configuration Manager 2503 environments with Update rollup 32851084 installed and for version 2509, where third-party updates are enabled on co-managed devices. The documented post-hotfix behavior stops Configuration Manager from setting the named scan-source values and cleans up incomplete prior state once. For Intune, compare the refreshed 25H2 baseline reference and iOS wrapper -mp rules with rollout assumptions. Treat the enrollment role change as a documentation prerequisite change until product behavior is independently confirmed; do not alter delegated roles solely from this diff.

keyChanges.title: KB36495448 targets co-managed Intune update-source redirection
keyChanges.detail: The new reference says Configuration Manager versions 2503, with Update rollup 32851084 installed, and 2509 can set UseUpdateClassPolicySource and SetPolicyDrivenUpdateSourceForOtherUpdates while leaving related Feature, Quality, and Driver policy values unset or removed when third-party updates are enabled on co-managed devices.
