Windows Update can then redirect Feature Updates and Quality Updates intended for Intune or Windows Update for Business to WSUS or Configuration Manager. After the hotfix, Configuration‌ ‌

keyChanges.title: Security Baselines page adds a Version 25H2 settings link
keyChanges.detail: The Security Baselines index now includes a Version 25H2 link to security-baseline-settings-mdm-all.md?pivots=mdm-25h2. Its ms.date also changes from 02/12/2025 to 03/23/2026. This evidence shows a reference and navigation update, not a GA rollout or automatic assignment of a baseline.

keyChanges.title: Baseline reference revises RPC, auditing, and default-setting descriptions
keyChanges.detail: The settings reference changes “Protocol to allow for incoming RPC connections” to “Protocol to use for outgoing RPC connections,” corrects RPC/TCP labels, adds “Include command line in process creation events” with a baseline default of Enabled, and adds “Block process creations originating from PSExec and WMI commands” with a default of Audit. It no longer lists “Scan packed executables”; other edits include Min Smb2 Dialect defaulting to “SMB 3.0.0” and describing preconfigured SIDs as present but unselected by​

keyChanges.title: Automatic-enrollment guidance replaces Intune Administrator with Global Administrator
keyChanges.detail: The Windows MDM automatic-enrollment page now lists the built-in Global Administrator Microsoft Entra role instead of the built-in Intune Administrator role. The diff establishes a change in the published prerequisite, but does not establish that Intune’s authorization enforcement changed.

keyChanges.title: iOS wrapper -mp guidance explicitly excludes ContainingAppBundleId
keyChanges.detail: The App Wrapping Tool guidance now explicitly identifies MultiIdentity, MAMPolicyRequired, AutoEnrollOnLaunch, and ContainingAppBundleId as unsupported through the -mp custom plist parameter. These settings are automatically configured by the wrapping process, while supported custom settings are merged into the app’s IntuneMAMSettings dictionary.

2026-03-07.headline: Configuration Manager offline feedback hotfix now documents 2409, 2503, and 2509 prerequisites
2026-03-07.overview: The period was quiet and limited to five Configuration Manager documentation edits. The substantive change updates the KB36419222 offline-feedback hotfix page: it now applies to Configuration Manager 2409 with update rollup 30385346, 2503 with update rollup 32851084, and 2509. The other edits are formatting, punctuation, or page metadata changes; there is no evidence of a new Intune cloud capability or changed tenant behavior.
2026-03-07.adminImpact: Administrators troubleshooting offline feedback submission with UploadOfflineFeedback.exe should check the revised hotfix prerequisites before applying KB36419222. The documentation does not provide evidence of a broader Intune rollout or require tenant configuration changes.

keyChanges.title: KB36419222 applicability is documented for three Configuration Manager versions
keyChanges.detail: The hotfix page replaces the narrower offline-feedback issue framing with prerequisites stating that Configuration Manager 2409 must have update rollup 30385346, version 2503 must have update rollup 32851084, and version 2509 is supported. The page also adds links to the 2409 and 2503 rollup articles and a downloadable KB36419222 file list.

2026-03-09.headline: Recovery Lock guidance details macOS prerequisites, roles, and passcode procedures
2026-03-09.overview: The strongest Intune material is a Recovery Lock documentation cluster: the rotate-action guidance now records a specific supported Mac configuration, while Settings Catalog guidance clarifies who can run the related device actions. Other changes with direct operational value clarify that ASR Application control still uses a legacy template and that AppLocker CSP deployment can prompt a reboot, while Managed Home Screen exit passwords cannot be viewed after setup. Most remaining edits are terminology, punctuation, metadata, or navigation cleanup. A View macOS Recovery Lock Password page appears as both added and removed in the supplied records, so the evidence does not establish a stable launch or retirement.
2026-03-09.adminImpact: For Recovery Lock operations, verify that target devices are supervised Apple-silicon Macs running macOS 11.5 or later and have a policy enabling Recovery Lock before using the rotate action. Review RBAC assignments against the documented Intune administrator or custom-role requirements. Treat Managed Home Screen exit lock-task passwords as non-viewable after configuration and change them by deploying a new profile value. For ASR Application control, account for the documented reboot prompt during AppLocker CSP deployment. These are documentation-led checks, not evidence of a tenant-wide feature launch, preview, GA event, or behavior change.

keyChanges.title: Rotate Recovery Lock guidance adds a concrete macOS eligibility boundary
keyChanges.detail: The revised Intune guidance documents the action for macOS in Supervised Mode running macOS 11.5 or later on Apple silicon; Intel-based Macs are not supported. It also requires a device policy that enables Recovery Lock and directs administrators to **Passwords and keys** > **View Recovery Lock Passcode** after rotation. This is a documentation clarification, not a stated availability announcement.

keyChanges.title: Recovery Lock RBAC guidance now includes the Intune administrator role
keyChanges.detail: Settings Catalog guidance changes the prerequisite from a custom role alone to either the Intune administrator Microsoft Entra role or a custom role with **Remote tasks/Rotate macOS recovery lock password** and **Remote tasks/View macOS recovery lock password** permissions. The page also links to the dedicated rotate-action procedure.

keyChanges.title: Application control stays outside Settings Catalog, with an AppLocker reboot warning
keyChanges.detail: The Endpoint Security ASR page now states that the Application control profile has not been updated to the Settings Catalog format and remains an older template-based profile in the admin center. Existing policies remain functional, while AppLocker CSP deployment currently prompts the end user to reboot. This replaces the former profile-migration note and should be treated as documentation clarification rather than evidence of changed policy behavior.

keyChanges.title: Managed Home Screen exit passwords are documented as non-viewable after setup
keyChanges.detail: For the **Exit lock task mode password** setting, the documentation now says the 4–6-digit value is obfuscated and cannot be viewed again once set. To rotate or change it, administrators must configure a new value in the device configuration profile.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager LTSB guidance addresses out-of-support dependencies
keyChanges.detail: New lifecycle guidance says Configuration Manager LTSB continues to be supported through its defined end of support even when a dependent component reaches end of support earlier, provided the reported issue is not caused by that out-of-support component. This is a Configuration Manager support clarification, not an Intune service change.

2026-03-10.headline: Planned GCC High STIG auditing baseline leads Intune’s March capability guidance
2026-03-10.overview: The period’s most consequential item is an upcoming Windows security baseline for GCC High tenants. Unlike a configuration baseline, it will audit devices against recommended STIG settings and produce detailed compliance reports. The iOS/iPadOS line-of-business app procedure also now documents a choice between default MDM and DDM management for iOS/iPadOS 18 and later. A removed Configuration Manager article covered a co-management update-source issue; its removal does not establish that the hotfix or product behavior was retired.
2026-03-10.adminImpact: GCC High administrators can include audit-only STIG reporting in future planning, but no release date or immediate deployment action is supplied. Administrators managing iOS/iPadOS 18 or later line-of-business apps should review the documented Management type choice and determine whether MDM or DDM fits their deployment. Teams that relied on the removed Configuration Manager article should preserve or relocate the relevant hotfix reference; the evidence does not say that KB36495448 was retired.

keyChanges.title: Upcoming GCC High baseline will audit Windows devices against STIG recommendations
keyChanges.detail: The Intune In Development page says Microsoft is adding a security baseline available for GCC High tenants. It will focus on audits rather than configuration, apply to Windows devices, and generate detailed reports showing which devices meet recommended STIG settings. This is an upcoming capability, with no release date supplied.

keyChanges.title: iOS/iPadOS line-of-business app procedure now documents MDM and DDM choices
keyChanges.detail: The app procedure now documents a Management type selector: MDM, which is the default, or DDM. It describes DDM as Apple’s policy-based management model for iOS/iPadOS 18 and later, with efficient app delivery, real-time app status reporting, and expanded app attribute options for per-app associated domains. This is a documentation clarification, not evidence of a new rollout.

keyChanges.title: Removed Configuration Manager article covered co-managed update-source misrouting
keyChanges.detail: The removed KB36495448 article described Configuration Manager versions 2503, with update rollup 32851084 installed, and 2509 when third-party updates were enabled. A partial scan-source policy could redirect Feature Updates and Quality Updates intended for Intune or Windows Update for Business to WSUS/Configuration Manager. The article documented post-hotfix cleanup and removal of UseUpdateClassPolicySource and SetPolicyDrivenUpdateSourceFor* values on co-managed devices. The evidence records article removal only,

2026-03-11.headline: Windows Autopatch will default hotpatching for eligible Intune devices in May
2026-03-11.overview: The period’s significant change is a Message Center plan to make Windows Autopatch hotpatch security updates the default for eligible Intune devices starting in May 2026. The remaining updates clarify existing Intune compliance-policy behavior and Configuration Manager LTSB database-support wording.
2026-03-11.adminImpact: Review device eligibility and prerequisites, including Virtualization-based Security, ahead of the May change. An opt-out setting is expected from April 2026. For compliance-policy unassignments, administrators can manually sync devices when they need the policy state to refresh; the documentation updates do not announce a behavior change.

keyChanges.title: Hotpatch updates will become the Windows Autopatch default
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft plans to enable hotpatch security updates by default from May 2026 for eligible Intune devices. Hotpatching is intended to accelerate security updates without restarts, and an opt-out setting will be available from April 2026. Devices must meet prerequisites such as enabling Virtualization-based Security.

keyChanges.title: Compliance-policy unassignment guidance now documents enforcement until sync
keyChanges.detail: The Intune troubleshooting page clarifies that a compliance policy unassigned from a device with an associated user remains assigned and enforced until the device syncs with the Intune service. It also points administrators to manual device sync and policy refresh guidance. This is a documentation clarification of existing behavior, not a newly announced policy change.

keyChanges.title: LTSB support wording now specifies SQL Server 2016 ESU-licensed hosting
keyChanges.detail: Configuration Manager guidance now states that Configuration Manager LTSB continues to be supported when the site database is hosted on SQL Server 2016 ESU-licensed servers, replacing the broader note that SQL Server 2016 ESU licenses would continue to be supported for Configuration Manager LTSB. The evidence indicates a documentation clarification rather than a separate support announcement.

2026-03-12.headline: Recovery Lock rotation rollout leads Intune’s refreshed privileged-role security guidance
2026-03-12.overview: The 12 March period was dominated by documentation maintenance: 45 updates, one new page, one removal, and no Message Center items. The meaningful exceptions were concentrated in Intune security administration and remote actions, alongside new Configuration Manager feedback guidance. Many other edits were mechanical, such as removing the “| Microsoft Docs” title suffix, changing audience metadata, or correcting links.
2026-03-12.adminImpact: Plan Recovery Lock operations around the device’s next successful Intune check-in and the expected late-April 2026 full-availability milestone. Review assignments of the broad Intune Administrator role, validate Multi Admin Approval permissions, and prepare Configuration Manager feedback workflows for authenticated requests from 26 June 2026. No administrator action is indicated by the title-, metadata-, and link-only edits.

keyChanges.title: Recovery Lock rotation now depends on a successful device check-in
keyChanges.detail: The Intune remote-action guidance says Rotate Recovery Lock passcode is gradually rolling out, with full availability expected by late April 2026. Confirming the action starts rotation, but the new passcode is applied only at the device’s next successful Intune check-in; an offline or non-checking-in device retains its existing passcode.

keyChanges.title: Intune Administrator guidance emphasizes privileged, broad access
keyChanges.detail: Revised Intune RBAC guidance describes Intune Administrator as a Microsoft Entra privileged role with global read/write access across Intune. It recommends built-in or custom roles for routine administration and limiting the broad role to the time required, then removing it. This is strengthened security guidance, not evidence that the role’s permissions changed.

keyChanges.title: Multi Admin Approval requirements now separate policy and approval permissions
keyChanges.detail: The updated Intune guidance recommends a custom role with Create, Read, Update, and Delete access-policy permissions for administrators who create or manage policies. Approvers must belong to the policy’s approver group and have the Approval for Multi Admin Approval permission in their Intune role.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager feedback will reject unauthenticated requests from 26 June
keyChanges.detail: Updated Configuration Manager feedback guidance says authentication will be required for security and reliability, and unauthenticated requests will no longer be accepted starting 26 June 2026.

keyChanges.title: A new Configuration Manager page flags standalone offline-feedback failures
keyChanges.detail: The new offline-feedback update documents a System.IO.FileLoadException caused by a Microsoft.Identity.Client version mismatch when using UploadOfflineFeedback.exe. The page says the standalone tool will be fixed in a subsequent release and directs administrators to use embedded feedback experiences meanwhile.

2026-03-13.headline: Intune RBAC guidance adds PIM-based time-bound administrator elevation
2026-03-13.overview: This was a documentation-only period, with no message-center announcements or evidenced tenant behavior changes. The most consequential update adds optional Privileged Identity Management guidance for the Intune Administrator role; other edits clarify deployment-plan wording, record a slow rollout target for an unnamed feature, and correct a Linux guide link.
2026-03-13.adminImpact: Administrators with Microsoft Entra ID P2 or Microsoft Entra ID Governance can optionally use PIM to provide time-bound elevation for the Intune Administrator role. The supplied changes do not require a tenant configuration change, but teams should distinguish the new RBAC security guidance from ordinary documentation corrections and wording changes.

keyChanges.title: PIM is now documented as an option for Intune Administrator elevation
keyChanges.detail: The Role-Based Access Control guidance still recommends assigning the Intune Administrator role only for the required duration, and now adds that organizations with Microsoft Entra ID P2 or Microsoft Entra ID Governance can use Privileged Identity Management for time-bound elevation. This is security guidance clarification, not evidence of a newly released Intune RBAC capability.

keyChanges.title: Deployment-plan guidance changes the existing-device email sequence
keyChanges.detail: For existing devices, the documented sequence now says to deploy the email app at any time and then deploy the email device configuration policy. The page also presents the settings catalog before built-in templates and removes the macOS-and-Windows qualifier from the sentence describing antivirus and scanning built in with Microsoft Defender for Endpoint; the diff does not establish a product-behavior change.

keyChanges.title: The What’s New page adds a late-March target for an unnamed rollout
keyChanges.detail: A note now says the referenced feature is rolling out slowly and should be available to all customers by late March 2026. The supplied diff does not identify the feature, its prerequisites, or any administrator action, so this should not be treated as a specific feature launch announcement.

2026-03-15.headline: Windows app protection setup guidance now links directly to its Intune Learn guide
2026-03-15.overview: The period contains one documentation-only change to the Intune Windows app installation article. Its companion link for Intune app protection for Windows changed from the fwlink URL to the direct Learn path `/intune/intune-service/apps/protect-mam-windows`; the supplied evidence does not indicate a product-behavior or policy change.
2026-03-15.adminImpact: No tenant configuration or rollout action is supported by this change. Administrators following the article will use the direct Intune app protection for Windows guide, which covers policy enforcement, app deployment, and corporate-data protection guidance.

keyChanges.title: The Windows app installation article replaces its app-protection companion link
keyChanges.detail: The article’s companion link changed from `https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=2309605` to `/intune/intune-service/apps/protect-mam-windows`. The edit changes navigation to the setup guide, not the documented Intune configuration or app-protection behavior.

2026-03-16.headline: Intune endpoint guidance adds three Remote Help communication hosts
2026-03-16.overview: The period was quiet and documentation-led. The clearest administrator-facing change is an Intune Endpoints entry listing three hosts for the Remote Help Feature. Intune Management Extension guidance also adds a notification log reference, while a Configuration Manager MDT sample replaces literal passwords with placeholders. The other edits are formatting, wording, metadata, or issue-marker changes; the supplied evidence does not establish a new feature, preview, general-availability change, retirement, or service-behavior change.
2026-03-16.adminImpact: Administrators maintaining outbound allowlists for Remote Help can compare them with the three newly listed hosts, although the evidence does not say they are newly required. For Intune Management Extension notification troubleshooting, NotificationInfra.log is now identified as the log tracking notifications through the Microsoft real-time communication channel. Teams using MDT samples should replace credential placeholders with appropriate values rather than copy literal example passwords.

keyChanges.title: Remote Help endpoint guidance lists three regional trouter hosts
keyChanges.detail: The Intune Endpoints page adds go-amer.trouter.communications.svc.cloud.microsoft, go-apac.trouter.communications.svc.cloud.microsoft, and go-eu.trouter.communications.svc.cloud.microsoft alongside the Remote Help Feature endpoint information. This is a documentation addition, not evidence of a service-side behavior change.

keyChanges.title: Intune Management Extension guidance adds NotificationInfra.log
keyChanges.detail: The page now documents NotificationInfra.log as tracking notifications sent through the Microsoft real-time communication channel, giving administrators a specific log to consult when investigating notification delivery.

keyChanges.title: MDT sample credentials are replaced with explicit placeholders
keyChanges.detail: The Configuration Manager Samples Guide replaces literal example values such as P@ssw0rd and a_secure_password with <complex_password> in password-related examples. The change improves the safety of copied documentation examples but does not indicate a change to Configuration Manager credential handling.

2026-03-17.headline: Intune’s Scoped permissions preview contains RBAC access within tagged assignments
2026-03-17.overview: 17 March was primarily a Microsoft Learn maintenance day: all 22 recorded items were updates, with no new, removed, or Message Center entries. Most remaining edits are wording, formatting, or metadata, but the Scope Tags and RBAC material documents an opt-in Scoped permissions preview with concrete evaluation and delegation guidance. Additional actionable updates cover Apple VPP licensing and Configuration Manager firewall prerequisites.
2026-03-17.adminImpact: Prioritize a scope-tagged RBAC review: use the Permissions Assessment Report before opting into Scoped permissions, inspect the named monitoring views, and verify delegated custom-role access. Separately, check VPP assignments for device/user-license overlap and validate Configuration Manager Endpoint Protection prerequisites before creating firewall policies. The mechanical wording, icon, and date edits provide no evidence of tenant configuration changes.

keyChanges.title: Scoped permissions preview contains permissions within each scope tag
keyChanges.detail: The Scope Tags reference describes an opt-in public preview. Under the documented default behavior, permissions from multiple role assignments using different scope tags but the same permission category can be merged, granting broader access than intended. When Scoped permissions is enabled, each assignment remains confined to its own scope-tag context. The documentation directs administrators to Tenant administration > Roles > Settings > Permissions Assessment Report to preview the impact and says this behavior is

keyChanges.title: RBAC guidance now distinguishes effective and assignment-level permission views
keyChanges.detail: The RBAC reference identifies the monitoring path as Tenant administration > Roles > Monitor. It describes My permissions as the signed-in user’s effective permissions view and Roles by permission as the view of permissions granted by each role assignment. This is a documentation clarification that helps administrators trace access; it is not evidence of a separate RBAC capability launch.

keyChanges.title: Custom-role tables map access to Scoped permissions assessment and enablement
keyChanges.detail: The Create Custom Role reference now states that Organization Read also allows viewing the Scoped permissions setting and running the Permissions Assessment Report, while Organization Update also allows enabling Scoped permissions. The clarification gives administrators a precise way to review delegated access around the preview workflow.

keyChanges.title: VPP guidance warns against mixing device and user licenses
keyChanges.detail: The iOS VPP Apps guidance adds a note telling administrators to avoid assigning both device licenses and user licenses to the same device or user because doing so can lead to unexpected behavior. This is operational guidance, not a stated licensing-enforcement change.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager firewall policies now list Endpoint Protection prerequisites
keyChanges.detail: Before creating Windows Firewall policies, the updated procedure says to have a site system server with the Endpoint Protection role installed and an Endpoint Protection Client Setting with “Manage Endpoint Protection client on client computers” set to “Yes.” It explicitly clarifies that “Install Endpoint Protection client” does not need to be enabled.

2026-03-18.headline: Scoped permissions guidance flags an irreversible action for Intune preview
2026-03-18.overview: The most consequential update is revised scope-tag guidance: Scoped permissions is described as an opt-in public preview, and enabling it is a one-time tenant action that cannot be undone. The same guidance directs administrators to run the Permissions Assessment Report at Tenant administration > Roles > Settings first. A separate user-help note states that Windows Company Portal 11.1.254.0 is the minimum supported version. Other notable edits clarify the Application control exception in attack surface reduction profiles, document Samsung Android 15 Remote Help visual latency without connectivity impact, and revise China endpoint tables. The remaining updates are chiefly wording, navigation, metadata, and deployment-series maintenance rather than evidence of launches, general availability, or confirmed product-behavior changes.
2026-03-18.adminImpact: Treat Scoped permissions as an irreversible preview decision and run the Permissions Assessment Report before enabling it. Update Windows Company Portal installations below 11.1.254.0 as soon as possible, as the guidance warns of potential loss of functionality on older versions. For attack surface reduction, use the documented template-based Application control profile rather than assuming every ASR profile uses Settings Catalog. For Samsung devices running Android 15, plan for possible minor Remote Help visual refresh latency; no connectivity workaround is indicated. Administrators maintaining China-cloud endpoint allowlists should compare them with the revised published table, but the evidence does not establish that removed hostnames represent a service retirement.

keyChanges.title: Scope-tag guidance adds preview and irreversibility warnings
keyChanges.detail: The revised Intune guidance identifies Scoped permissions as an opt-in public preview. It says enabling the setting is a one-time tenant action that cannot be undone and recommends using the Permissions Assessment Report at Tenant administration > Roles > Settings to preview permission changes first. This documents the preview and its constraint; it does not establish a launch date.

keyChanges.title: Windows Company Portal guidance sets 11.1.254.0 as minimum
keyChanges.detail: A new note states that version 11.1.254.0 is the minimum supported Windows Company Portal version and advises updating older versions as soon as possible to avoid loss of functionality. The diff adds guidance; it does not by itself prove that the underlying support policy changed on this date.

keyChanges.title: Application control remains the ASR template-based exception
keyChanges.detail: The Endpoint Security attack surface reduction guidance now explicitly says most ASR profiles use the Settings Catalog format, while the Application control profile remains in the older template-based format. This is a profile-format clarification, not evidence of a new deployment model or feature release.

keyChanges.title: Remote Help documents visual latency on Samsung Android 15
keyChanges.detail: The updated Remote Help article warns that Samsung devices running Android 15 might show minor visual latency, with portions of the screen refreshing after a slight delay. It explicitly says the behavior does not affect session connectivity.

keyChanges.title: China endpoint tables remove listed azureedge.net addresses
keyChanges.detail: For CNPASU01, the revised China endpoints table lists only the three imeswdsc-afd-*.manage.microsoft.com hosts, removing the sovereignprodimedata and azureedge.net entries shown previously. The macsidecarap row now lists only macsidecarap.manage.microsoft.com, removing macsidecarprodap.azureedge.net and its migration note. This is a published-table edit, not proof from the diff that those services were retired.

2026-03-19.headline: Direct LOB APK deployment expands Android Enterprise options as Defender onboarding guidance arrives
2026-03-19.overview: This period’s substantive Intune content centers on Android app deployment. A new guide provides a single path for deploying and configuring Defender for Endpoint on Android, while updated LOB-app guidance explicitly documents direct APK upload and required assignment for Android Enterprise fully managed and dedicated devices without Managed Google Play. A service release 2603 entry also describes macOS Recovery Lock and new Apple DDM settings. Other edits are mainly clarifications: LOB installation-error details now cover Android Enterprise, the Defender integration page points to the new guide, and the Configuration Manager firewall article restates prerequisites and corrects procedure numbering.
2026-03-19.adminImpact: Defender rollouts should use the new guide’s prerequisites: personally owned work profile, corporate-owned work profile, or corporate-owned fully managed user device enrollment, plus an enabled Intune–Defender for Endpoint service-to-service connection. Required LOB apps on Android Enterprise fully managed and dedicated devices can be uploaded directly to Intune and assigned as required apps to corporate-owned devices. For macOS Recovery Lock, viewing the password requires the Remote tasks/View macOS recovery lock password permission. The Inventus OEMConfig update provides a package identifier but no rollout date; no retirement or tenant-wide migration is evidenced.

keyChanges.title: New Defender for Endpoint Android guide consolidates deployment and configuration
keyChanges.detail: This new how-to covers acquiring Microsoft Defender for Endpoint from Managed Google Play, assigning and verifying it, configuring app configuration policies, setting up always-on VPN, and low-touch onboarding. It states that Google Play updates the app automatically and requires one of three Android Enterprise enrollment types plus the Intune service-to-service connection with Defender for Endpoint.

keyChanges.title: Updated LOB guidance documents direct APK deployment for Android Enterprise
keyChanges.detail: The revised guide explicitly says required LOB apps on Android Enterprise fully managed and dedicated devices can be deployed without Managed Google Play: upload the APK directly to Intune and assign it as a required app to corporate-owned devices. Related app-management pages repeat this scope, making this a clarified deployment option rather than evidence of a newly launched feature.

keyChanges.title: macOS Recovery Lock entry details password rotation and privileged retrieval
keyChanges.detail: The added Week of March 23, 2026 service release 2603 entry describes a Recovery OS password for company-owned Macs that prevents booting into recovery mode, macOS reinstallation, and bypassing remote management. Settings catalog policies can enable Recovery Lock and set a rotation schedule; a Recovery Lock device action can manually rotate the password. The password appears in the per-setting status report under Passwords and keys.

keyChanges.title: Apple DDM catalog adds Intelligence, keyboard, Siri, and external-intelligence controls
keyChanges.detail: The service-release entry adds iOS/iPadOS DDM settings for External Intelligence, Apple Intelligence features such as Genmoji, Image Playground, Image Wand, and Writing Tools, Mail/Notes/Safari summaries, on-device dictation and translation, keyboard controls, and Siri controls. The supplied macOS diff explicitly lists External Intelligence settings for Allow Sign In and Allowed Workspace IDs. Administrators find these under the platform’s Settings catalog profile.

keyChanges.title: Inventus OEMConfig package appears on Android Enterprise in-development listing
keyChanges.detail: The updated In Development page lists Inventus, package `com.inventus.oemconfig.gen`, as a supported OEMConfig app available in Intune for Android Enterprise. Because the item appears on an In Development page, the supplied change is a status listing and provides no general-availability date or rollout procedure.

2026-03-20.headline: Windows cloud configuration’s automatic guided deployment is deprecated in Intune
2026-03-20.overview: The period’s main operational change is a retirement: Intune says the guided automatic deployment path for Windows in cloud configuration is deprecated and being removed from the admin center, with the manual setup guide now directed instead. The same sweep removes or marks older guided-scenario guidance for retirement. Separate updates record system-proxy telemetry and multi-device query improvements, add Inventus OEMConfig support for Android Enterprise, and clarify iOS/iPadOS DDM limits. The remaining edits are mainly documentation cleanup or support guidance.
2026-03-20.adminImpact: Use the Windows client cloud config setup guide instead of the deprecated automatic scenario. No action is required for system-proxy telemetry when Endpoint analytics or EPM is enabled. For iOS/iPadOS line-of-business apps that need app configuration policies, select MDM. Android administrators using Inventus can reference the listed OEMConfig package, and macOS support teams should account for the documented Company Portal minimum version of v5.2401.0.

keyChanges.title: Automatic Windows cloud configuration deployment is deprecated
keyChanges.detail: Retirement/deprecation: The Cloud Configuration guidance removes the former automatic/manual choice and says the guided automatic deployment of Windows in cloud configuration is deprecated and being removed from the Intune admin center. It directs administrators to the Windows client cloud config setup guide for step-by-step manual deployment. The supplied evidence gives no deadline or migration instruction for existing configurations.
keyChanges.product: Windows cloud configuration and guided deployment

keyChanges.title: Analytics updates add system-proxy telemetry and multi-device query tools
keyChanges.detail: Capability update: Windows devices using system-level (WinHTTP) proxy settings can now send telemetry to endpoint analytics and Advanced Analytics, while Endpoint Privilege Management includes elevation-usage data from those devices. When Endpoint analytics or EPM is enabled, telemetry and events automatically appear in the User Experience (Device blade), endpoint Analytics reports, and EPM; no admin action is required. Device query for multiple devices also adds search across all result rows, column-header value​​
keyChanges.product: Endpoint analytics, Advanced Analytics, Endpoint Privilege Management, and device query

keyChanges.title: iOS DDM guidance limits MAM-enabled LOB app management
keyChanges.detail: Documentation clarification: for DDM app management, an MAM-enabled app integrated with the Intune App SDK has no Management type setting and can only be created for MDM. App configuration policies work only with MDM-based apps; the guidance says to use MDM when those policies are needed for a line-of-business app. This documents a limitation rather than announcing a new feature.
keyChanges.product: iOS/iPadOS line-of-business apps and Declarative Device Management

keyChanges.title: Inventus OEMConfig is listed for Android Enterprise
keyChanges.detail: New supported-app listing: Intune identifies Inventus, package com.inventus.oemconfig.gen, as an available OEMConfig app for Android Enterprise. No additional prerequisite is stated in this update.

keyChanges.title: macOS Company Portal minimum supported version is v5.2401.0
keyChanges.detail: Support guidance: the minimum supported Company Portal version for macOS is v5.2401.0. Users on older versions are prompted to update when they sign in. No separate enforcement date is supplied.

2026-03-23.headline: Remote Help macOS reporting improves with Intune deployment and version visibility
2026-03-23.overview: This was mostly a documentation-maintenance period, but the What's New entry records a concrete Remote Help improvement for macOS: Intune deployments of client version 1.0.26012221 expose the full client version in inventory and during upgrades, while registering installations with Microsoft AutoUpdate. Other notable updates clarify support permissions, adopt Omnissa Workspace ONE UEM terminology, and correct a Windows Update reference; they do not by themselves indicate a new rollout, retirement, or policy-behavior change.
2026-03-23.adminImpact: Prioritize deployment verification for macOS Remote Help version 1.0.26012221 and use inventory or upgrade views to confirm the full client version. If administrators need to create or manage support tickets, verify that their Microsoft Entra role includes microsoft.office365.supportTickets; guest users still cannot file tickets. Treat the Workspace ONE and Win32 changes as documentation and reference maintenance rather than evidence of connector or update-policy changes.

keyChanges.title: Remote Help on macOS gains fuller version reporting and update management
keyChanges.detail: Intune's What's New entry says that after deploying Remote Help client version 1.0.26012221 through Intune, administrators can view the full client version in device inventory and during app upgrades. Intune-deployed macOS installations are also registered with Microsoft AutoUpdate, allowing managed devices to automatically receive future Remote Help updates. This is the period's substantive product improvement, although the evidence does not label it preview or general availability.

keyChanges.title: Support Assistant guidance separates troubleshooting access from ticket permissions
keyChanges.detail: The updated Intune admin center guidance says all authenticated users can access Support Assistant for solutions and troubleshooting guidance. Creating and managing support tickets still requires a Microsoft Entra role containing the microsoft.office365.supportTickets action, and guest users cannot file tickets even when that action is assigned. This is a clarification of access guidance, not evidence of a new support-ticket role.

keyChanges.title: Device Compliance Partners adopts Omnissa Workspace ONE UEM terminology
keyChanges.detail: The partner entry replaces “VMware Workspace ONE UEM (formerly AirWatch)” with “Omnissa Workspace ONE UEM” and replaces the VMware documentation link with an Omnissa Conditional Access and Microsoft Entra ID link. The supplied diff shows a terminology and link update only; it does not describe a change to the compliance-partner integration.

keyChanges.title: Win32 update guidance keeps Windows Update policies as the recommended route
keyChanges.detail: The article continues to state that deploying updates as Win32 apps is not the recommended approach and points administrators to Update rings, Feature updates, and Quality updates instead. The visible change is the Quality updates link changing from expedite-updates.md to expedite-policy.md; the Win32 method remains described as an option when more granular control is needed.
keyChanges.product: Intune Win32 app deployment and Windows Update policies

2026-03-24.headline: Intune retires guided scenarios while its redesigned device page is in public preview
2026-03-24.overview: The clearest tenant-facing change is a retirement: all Intune admin-center guided scenarios except Windows 365 Boot are no longer accessible. Alongside that, the redesigned single-device page is explicitly in public preview, while Android Managed Home Screen suspend and restore actions are only planned. The remaining notable work is mostly guidance and reference maintenance rather than feature availability: passwordless documentation adds license and OS matrices, Defender integration guidance adds precise RBAC requirements, and Advanced Analytics links move to a new data-platform schema reference.
2026-03-24.adminImpact: Existing objects created by removed guided-scenario wizards remain available and manageable, and Microsoft says no action is required; teams that relied on the wizards can use the listed prescriptive and administration guides instead. The preview device page retains existing management capabilities, so its immediate effect is navigation and terminology. Do not treat the Managed Home Screen actions as available yet. For passwordless planning, verify the listed Entra and Intune licenses and platform floors; for Defender integration, check the specified Intune permissions and the separate Entra role needed for Conditional Access.

keyChanges.title: Guided-scenario wizards are removed from the admin center
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft says all guided-scenario wizards are removed from the Intune admin center except Windows 365 Boot, which remains available from the Windows 365 overview page. Intune objects previously created by the wizards remain available and manageable, and the notice says no action is required. Replacement links point to Microsoft Learn, prescriptive guides, administration guides, and scenario-specific guidance.

keyChanges.title: The single-device page enters public preview
keyChanges.detail: In `Devices` > `All Devices`, selecting a device now presents a full-page single-device layout in public preview. Its tabs are `Device action status`, `Tools + reports` formerly called `Overview`, `Properties`, and `Device details` formerly called `Hardware`. Action status can be searched, sorted, and filtered; properties expose scope tags; and destructive actions require confirmation. Existing device-management capabilities remain available.

keyChanges.title: Managed Home Screen suspend and restore actions are forthcoming
keyChanges.detail: Intune will soon add two remote actions for Android Enterprise corporate-owned Fully Managed (COBO) and Dedicated (COSU) devices: suspend Managed Home Screen for a defined duration and restore it automatically when time expires or manually. Suspension lets users reach the default launcher without removing policies or requiring a PIN. This remains an in-development capability, not a generally available feature.

keyChanges.title: Defender integration guidance now spells out Intune RBAC
keyChanges.detail: The updated Microsoft Defender for Endpoint and Intune integration guidance specifies three Intune permission sets: Mobile Threat Defense — Modify and Read; Endpoint Detection and Response — Assign, Create, Read, and Update; and Device compliance policies — Assign, Create, Read, and Update. These permissions can be added to a custom role, while Endpoint Security Manager is described as the least-privileged built-in role covering all of them. Conditional Access remains an Entra ID configuration requiring a separate,

keyChanges.title: Passwordless guidance adds explicit license and OS matrices
keyChanges.detail: The updated passwordless overview lists Entra ID P1 for Windows Hello for Business, FIDO2, passkeys, Authenticator phone sign-in, Temporary Access Pass, and authentication strength policies; P2 for risk-based Conditional Access; the Intune Suite or standalone Cloud PKI add-on for Microsoft Cloud PKI; and Intune Plan 1 for device compliance and configuration profiles. It also lists minimum versions, including Windows 11 23H2, macOS 13, iOS 17, and Android 14 for synced passkeys, plus iOS 16 and Android 11 for Authen

2026-03-25.headline: Passwordless guidance adds platform gates, recovery planning, and clearer Intune boundaries
2026-03-25.overview: 25 March was primarily a documentation-refinement day centered on a substantial rewrite of Intune passwordless guidance. The revised material adds licensing and OS prerequisites, phishing-resistance and Conditional Access context, hybrid-Windows caveats, and recovery planning; a separate iOS App SDK page adds a security-critical integration warning. The supplied evidence shows guidance and terminology changes—not a new Intune feature, preview, GA announcement, or product-behavior rollout. One removed item is an Outline page; nothing supplied describes a capability retirement.
2026-03-25.adminImpact: Do not infer tenant-side behavior changes from these edits. Passwordless owners should use the revised prerequisites and licensing tables when planning methods, include emergency-access and Temporary Access Pass recovery in Conditional Access designs, and check hybrid Windows trust and legacy-application dependencies. Teams shipping iOS apps with the Intune App SDK should verify that identity switches are reported to the SDK; otherwise app protection policy may not be applied to the active identity or may incorrectly restrict unmanaged data.

keyChanges.title: Entra-versus-Intune ownership is stated more explicitly
keyChanges.detail: The updated Passwordless article says Intune does not issue passwordless credentials: it prepares devices, apps, and user experiences, while Microsoft Entra ID provides the identity controls and authentication methods. Intune configures device settings and compliance that those methods depend on. This is an administrator-facing scope clarification, not evidence of a changed service boundary.

keyChanges.title: Passwordless prerequisites spell out licensing and platform minimums
keyChanges.detail: The revised table lists Microsoft Entra ID P1 for Windows Hello for Business, FIDO2, passkeys, Authenticator phone sign-in, Temporary Access Pass, and authentication-strength policies; P2 for risk-based Conditional Access; Intune Plan 1 for device compliance and configuration; and an Intune Suite or standalone Cloud PKI add-on for Microsoft Cloud PKI. Its minimum-version table lists passkeys on Windows 11, all supported macOS and iOS/iPadOS versions, and Android 14 or later. This is documentation guidance, so use‌‎

keyChanges.title: Conditional Access guidance adds explicit passwordless recovery safeguards
keyChanges.detail: New dependency text says authentication-strength policies can require phishing-resistant MFA and block weaker methods such as passwords or SMS. It also directs administrators to maintain at least two break-glass accounts excluded from Conditional Access and passwordless enforcement, and to use Temporary Access Pass to register a replacement credential after device loss. These are planning recommendations in the article, not a report that Microsoft changed default policies.

keyChanges.title: Hybrid Windows caveats are made more visible
keyChanges.detail: The Windows section now says its passwordless examples assume a cloud-first direction with Microsoft Entra-joined devices. For hybrid Entra-joined deployments, additional infrastructure may be needed depending on the trust model; on-premises resource access requires Cloud Kerberos Trust or certificate-based trust, and applications requiring NTLM or direct LDAP bind may need additional planning. The article identifies Cloud Kerberos Trust as the recommended model because it avoids deploying certificates for Kerberos

keyChanges.title: iOS App SDK guidance warns that identity changes depend on the app
keyChanges.detail: The Intune App SDK for iOS Phase 5 page now highlights that the SDK cannot independently detect identity changes and relies entirely on the app to report them. If the app fails to notify the SDK when the active identity changes, policies may not be enforced for that user, managed data may be accessible without app protection restrictions, or unmanaged data may be incorrectly restricted.

2026-03-26.headline: Intune Data Warehouse update will reset historical data and discontinue the beta Power BI connector
2026-03-26.overview: The most consequential notice is an expected mid-June 2026 Intune Data Warehouse change: historical data will reset to about 30 days, surrogate keys will refresh, licensing definitions will change, and the beta Power BI connector will be discontinued. Microsoft directs administrators to move to the Intune admin center’s OData feed and back up data beforehand. The day’s other substantive Intune activity centers on settings catalog restructuring and new scenario/reference guidance, not evidence of broad new tenant functionality.
2026-03-26.adminImpact: Back up Data Warehouse data before the planned change, replace the beta Power BI connector with the OData feed, and account for shorter history, refreshed surrogate keys, and revised licensing definitions in reporting. For settings catalog changes, update internal links and procedures where needed; the supplied documentation diffs do not establish changed policy behavior. Apple administrators should review the stated migration direction while retaining templates that the guidance says should still be used. Microsoft 365 E5 administrators should assess Security Copilot capacity and potential costs for advanced capabilities during the phased rollout.

keyChanges.title: Intune Data Warehouse is slated for a mid-June infrastructure change
keyChanges.detail: The Message Center notice says historical data will reset to about 30 days, surrogate keys will refresh, licensing definitions will change, and the beta Power BI connector will be discontinued. Administrators must switch to the OData feed from the Intune admin center and back up data beforehand. This is a planned infrastructure change, not an immediate tenant behavior change.

keyChanges.title: Apple settings catalog guidance maps payloads and template migration
keyChanges.detail: A new Intune Apple reference covers Apple declarative configurations and MDM payloads, links to Apple YAML requirements such as OS version, enrollment type, and supervision, and maps template settings to settings catalog equivalents. It recommends using settings catalog for new policies where possible, identifies Device features, Device restrictions, Endpoint protection, and Extensions as templates on a future migration/deprecation path, and says certificate, email, Wi-Fi, and wired-network templates should still使用

keyChanges.title: New Universal Print guidance directs admins to settings catalog provisioning
keyChanges.detail: The new Windows Intune how-to says to create a settings catalog printer policy that deploys a list of registered Universal Print printers and automatically installs them on managed devices. It explicitly calls the PrintProvisioning tool and printers.csv process deprecated, and lists the required printer identifiers—Device ID, shared ID, and shared name—along with Universal Print licensing and the Policy and Profile Manager role.

keyChanges.title: Security Copilot inclusion in Microsoft 365 E5 enters a phased rollout
keyChanges.detail: The Message Center notice says Security Copilot will be included with Microsoft 365 E5 from April 20 through June 30, 2026, providing 400 Security Compute Units per 1,000 users and core agentic features across Microsoft security products. Additional advanced capabilities may incur extra costs, so this is a planned entitlement rollout rather than a statement that every capability is included.

keyChanges.title: Android settings catalog reference defines corporate-owned enrollment scope
keyChanges.detail: The new Android reference lists Android Enterprise and AOSP settings and explicitly supports COPE, COBO, COSU, AOSP corporate-owned userless/shared, and corporate-owned user-associated/single-user devices. It requires corporate-owned devices enrolled in Intune, a settings catalog policy, and at least the Policy and Profile Manager role to configure the policy. This adds reference coverage; the supplied diff does not establish a newly released Android capability.

2026-03-27.headline: Microsoft Tunnel sets March 31 Android 10 cutoff as Autopilot adds managed installer support
2026-03-27.overview: Two administrator-facing changes stand out: Windows Autopilot device preparation now documents managed installer policy application during OOBE before Win32, Microsoft Store, and Enterprise App Catalog apps install, while Microsoft Tunnel guidance sets March 31, 2026 as the Android 10 support cutoff and requires Android 11 or later. Intune’s hotpatch and Windows Update pages also revise how default protection, policy control, and Windows Autopatch approval are described. Cloud configuration’s guided deployment path is explicitly deprecated and being removed. Most remaining edits are ordinary documentation maintenance, especially image-path corrections and minor formatting changes, rather than additional feature launches.
2026-03-27.adminImpact: Inventory Microsoft Tunnel devices running Android 10 and plan upgrades to Android 11 or later. Recheck Autopilot OOBE app sequencing and managed-installer assumptions, since app types previously skipped during preparation are now documented as installing under the policy. For Windows updates, review hotpatch tenant-level and quality-update policy controls, baseline-month restart behavior, and Autopatch policy targeting. If you use the cloud configuration guided scenario, move runbooks to the manual setup guide. The image-path and formatting corrections require no evident tenant action.

keyChanges.title: Microsoft Tunnel sets March 31 Android 10 support cutoff
keyChanges.detail: Support retirement: the updated prerequisites state that support for Android 10 ended March 31, 2026. Devices running Android 10 must upgrade to Android 11 or later to continue using Microsoft Tunnel. This is a minimum-version change, not a new capability.

keyChanges.title: Autopilot device preparation adds managed installer policy support
keyChanges.detail: New capability guidance: Windows Autopilot device preparation now supports the managed installer policy during OOBE. Intune applies it before Win32, Microsoft Store, and Enterprise App Catalog apps install; those app types were previously skipped to avoid installation conflicts and deployment failures. The supplied change does not identify a preview or general-availability status.

keyChanges.title: Hotpatch guidance now documents default enablement and restart exceptions
keyChanges.detail: Updated security and behavior guidance says hotpatch security updates are enabled by default for all eligible devices in Intune, with control through a tenant-level setting or quality update policies. During a hotpatch month, a device missing the latest baseline receives both the restart-required baseline and the hotpatch update; upgrading to the latest Windows version during a hotpatch month switches the device to standard updates and requires a restart.

keyChanges.title: Intune update policies are framed as Windows Autopatch approval controls
keyChanges.detail: Documentation clarification: the overview now says Intune sends policy configuration to Windows Autopatch, which determines what update content is approved, while devices download approved updates from Windows Update. A device assigned to a policy is enrolled in Autopatch for that content type and receives only approved content; without targeting for that content type, the latest Windows Update content is deployed.

keyChanges.title: Cloud configuration’s guided deployment scenario is being removed
keyChanges.detail: Retirement and procedure change: the page says the automatic guided scenario is deprecated and being removed from the Intune admin center. It now directs administrators to the Windows client cloud config setup guide to create all policies manually. This changes the deployment procedure; it does not announce a new cloud configuration feature.

2026-03-28.headline: Require Custom Compliance guidance loses an extraneous character in policy setup
2026-03-28.overview: The period contains one low-impact Intune documentation correction. Step 3 of the Create Compliance Policy guidance now correctly ends after “True.”, removing an extraneous trailing “T” rather than changing the setting or its behavior.
2026-03-28.adminImpact: No tenant configuration, rollout, or policy change is supported by the supplied evidence. Administrators using the page will see a cleaner instruction for setting Require Custom Compliance to True.

keyChanges.title: Create Compliance Policy step corrected
keyChanges.detail: The instruction now reads: “Switch Require Custom Compliance to True.” The prior version ended with an additional “T” after the period. This is an ordinary documentation clarification, not a product or policy-behavior change.

2026-03-30.headline: Recovery Lock guidance specifies macOS prerequisites and a late-April availability target
2026-03-30.overview: 30 March’s meaningful changes are concentrated in substantive guidance for Recovery Lock, Windows settings-catalog policies, and Security Copilot in Intune. The evidence is documentation work rather than a Message Center announcement: new pages explain capabilities, prerequisites, permissions, and rollout status, while many other edits mainly move Copilot links into the /intune/copilot structure or polish Hotpatch wording and references. Do not treat the new Copilot pages alone as proof of a new launch or changed tenant behavior.
2026-03-30.adminImpact: Review Recovery Lock eligibility and rollout before planning deployment: the documented scope is macOS 11.5 or later on Apple silicon with supervised enrollment, Intel Macs are excluded, and the device action is gradually rolling out. Full availability is expected by late April 2026. For Copilot, confirm Security Copilot is enabled and that administrators have the required Security Copilot role; Intune data remains permission-scoped. For Windows, interpret the new policy behavior against its Windows Insider and uninstall prerequisites rather than assuming broad availability.

keyChanges.title: Windows settings-catalog guidance names two new policies
keyChanges.detail: The updated What’s New entry lists Connectivity > Disable Cross Device Resume, which uses the DisableCrossDeviceResume CSP; when disabled, Windows receives no CrossDeviceResume notifications and users see no “resume from your phone” prompts. It also lists Windows AI > Remove Microsoft Copilot App. That policy applies when Microsoft 365 Copilot and Microsoft Copilot are installed, the Microsoft Copilot app was not user-installed, and it has not been opened for 14 days; enabling it uninstalls the app, although users'

keyChanges.title: Recovery Lock procedure sets macOS and permissions prerequisites
keyChanges.detail: The new settings-catalog procedure says Recovery Lock automatically generates a strong, random password, protects the recovery environment and Startup Options, and supports time-based reset. It applies to macOS 11.5 or later on Apple silicon with supervised Intune enrollment; Intel Macs are unsupported. After assignment, admins can rotate the passcode through device actions, requiring the Intune Administrator role or a custom role with Remote tasks/Rotate macOS recovery lock password.

keyChanges.title: Recovery Lock device-action rollout is gradual, with late-April full availability expected
keyChanges.detail: An updated Recovery Lock note says the feature is gradually rolling out and may not yet be available in a tenant; full availability is expected by late April 2026. Administrators should check tenant availability before relying on the remote rotation action.

keyChanges.title: Copilot guidance separates embedded Intune and standalone Security Copilot experiences
keyChanges.detail: The new overview distinguishes Microsoft Copilot in Intune, embedded in the Intune admin center with an IT admin/IT Pro focus and access to Intune and Windows 365 Cloud PC data, from standalone Microsoft Security Copilot in its portal with a SOC-oriented, cross-service focus. It also states that Copilot in Intune is included with Security Copilot and has no additional licensing or Intune-specific license requirement.

keyChanges.title: Explorer guidance documents natural-language queries that can drive policy targeting
keyChanges.detail: The new Explorer article describes natural-language queries matched to built-in views, Copilot summaries, recommendations, and actions. It says query results can add users or devices to groups, create custom reports, and create policies targeting users and groups in those results. Prerequisites are Security Copilot enabled and an account with Copilot owner or contributor access; results are scoped to the administrator’s Intune permissions.

2026-03-31.headline: Linux broker guidance flags new Intune and Entra device IDs after upgrades
2026-03-31.overview: 31 March combined a significant Linux identity-transition note with several precise Intune guidance changes. The Linux enrollment guide documents automatic re-registration and re-enrollment when Identity Broker 2.0.2 or later updates, creating new Intune and Microsoft Entra device IDs. Intune now lists RHEL 9 and 10 LTS as supported while RHEL 8 support has ended; expedite guidance covers security and non-security updates; and macOS LAPS is tied to post-reset ADE. Security Copilot material lists four Intune agents, but the move from /agents to /copilot/agents is documentation reorganization rather than evidence of retirement or GA. Vulnerability Remediation remains limited public preview. The filters matrix also marks Antivirus, Disk encryption, and Firewall as supported workloads.
2026-03-31.adminImpact: Expect new Linux device identity records after broker upgrades; the guidance says no user action is required. For RHEL 8, identify devices under Devices > All devices by filtering OS to Linux and adding OS version columns, then notify users to upgrade; already enrolled RHEL 8 devices remain enrolled. If using expedite policies, review update-ring settings, set Automatic update behavior to Reset to default, and do not install Update Health Tools on Windows 11, version 24H2 and later. For macOS LAPS, use a factory-reset ADE enrollment with a LAPS-enabled profile; terminal Sudo profiles renew enrollments aren't supported. Update agent links that use the old /agents paths and treat Vulnerability Remediation access as limited preview.

keyChanges.title: Linux broker migration guidance documents automatic re-enrollment
keyChanges.detail: The Linux enrollment guide adds that Microsoft Identity Broker 2.0.2 and later, included with the Microsoft Intune app for Linux, introduces a major architectural change. When devices update from earlier broker versions, Intune automatically re-registers and re-enrolls them and creates new Intune device IDs and Microsoft Entra device IDs. The documented behavior requires no user action.

keyChanges.title: RHEL 8 support ends while RHEL 9 and 10 remain supported
keyChanges.detail: The Intune What's New guidance states that RHEL 9 LTS and RHEL 10 LTS are supported, while support for RHEL 8 LTS has ended. Devices already enrolled on RHEL 8 remain enrolled. Administrators can find them under Devices > All devices by filtering OS to Linux and adding OS version columns, then notify users to upgrade.

keyChanges.title: Expedite guidance adds non-security updates and Windows 11 caveats
keyChanges.detail: The Expedite Policies article now describes accelerating specific Windows security and non-security updates, rather than security updates alone. It says existing settings don't have to be modified but recommends configurations that avoid conflicts, including Automatic update behavior set to Reset to default; settings that prevent scanning can block the expedited scan, and download approval can delay updates. For Windows 11, version 24H2 and later, it says not to install Update Health Tools. This is a documentation-

keyChanges.title: macOS LAPS guidance adds a post-reset ADE prerequisite
keyChanges.detail: The macOS LAPS article now specifies that the feature is enabled during automated device enrollment only after a factory reset. Previously enrolled devices must reenroll with Intune using a LAPS-enabled ADE profile after the reset. ADE enrollments initiated from terminal Sudo profiles renew aren't supported.

keyChanges.title: Vulnerability Remediation Agent remains limited public preview
keyChanges.detail: New setup material explicitly says the Vulnerability Remediation Agent is in limited public preview and available only to a select group of customers; interested organizations should contact their sales team. The agent uses Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management data to identify CVEs, prioritize remediation, and provide step-by-step Intune guidance. The material describes a preview capability, not general availability.

2026-04-01.headline: Windows Autopatch hotpatching defaults change in May; Intune opt-out opens today
2026-04-01.overview: The most consequential notice is a planned Windows Autopatch behavior change: hotpatch updates will be enabled by default for eligible devices starting with the May 2026 Windows security update, while an Intune opt-out becomes available on April 1. The period also clarifies the RHEL 8 support deadline and documents supported macOS LAPS enrollment and Windows expedite-policy behavior. Several remaining edits are mechanical link, punctuation, or formatting changes.
2026-04-01.adminImpact: Review Windows Autopatch readiness and decide whether to use the tenant-level opt-out or configure hotpatch behavior through quality update policies for specific groups; quality update policies override the tenant setting. Inventory RHEL 8 devices and plan upgrades before July 2026. Update macOS LAPS enrollment procedures and expectations for expedite-policy update selection. No administrator action is indicated by the link- or punctuation-only edits.

keyChanges.title: Hotpatch becomes the Windows Autopatch default in May
keyChanges.detail: The updated Intune What's new entry says hotpatch updates will be enabled by default for all eligible devices managed through Windows Autopatch starting with the May 2026 Windows security update. A tenant-level opt-out is available in the Intune admin center on April 1, 2026. Alternatively, a quality update policy can control hotpatch behavior for a specific device group, and that policy overrides the tenant-level setting.
keyChanges.product: Intune — Windows Autopatch and quality update policies

keyChanges.title: RHEL 8 support is stated to end in July 2026
keyChanges.detail: The What's new text changes the status from “Support for RHEL 8 LTS has ended” to “Support for RHEL 8 LTS will end in July 2026.” Devices already enrolled on RHEL 8 remain enrolled. Administrators can find them under Devices > All devices by filtering OS to Linux and adding OS version columns; Intune supports RHEL 9 LTS and RHEL 10 LTS.

keyChanges.title: macOS LAPS enrollment guidance distinguishes initial setup from re-enrollment
keyChanges.detail: The macOS LAPS page now states that ADE enrollments occurring during the initial device setup experience are supported. ADE enrollment scenarios re-initiated from an existing macOS installation, such as using the `profiles renew` command, aren't supported. This is a documentation clarification of the supported enrollment path, not a newly announced LAPS capability.

keyChanges.title: Expedite Policy documentation clarifies which updates appear in the selector
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance says the drop-down displays the two most recent security updates, including out-of-band security updates. Non-security updates appear only when no newer security update exists; when eligible, the list includes the latest non-security update and the previous non-security update only if that previous release was out of band. This documents selection logic rather than announcing a new policy feature.

2026-04-02.headline: Change Review Agent enters Multi Admin Approval preview as Recovery Lock rolls out
2026-04-02.overview: Intune’s most consequential signals on 2 April were a public-preview approval workflow and a staged macOS security action. The In Development material describes an Agent Response column for Windows PowerShell scripts in Multi Admin Approval, with Change Review Agent risk recommendations inline, while Recovery Lock passcode rotation is rolling out gradually and is expected to reach full availability by late April 2026. Most remaining entries are a remote-device-action documentation reorganization—new per-action pages under `device-management/actions` alongside removals of older paths—so they should not be read as proof of new launches or changed service behavior. There was no Message Center item.
2026-04-02.adminImpact: Evaluate the inline Agent Response view for approvers handling Windows PowerShell scripts, and use Recovery Lock rotation only where it is available and devices meet the documented requirements: supervised macOS 11.5 or later on Apple silicon with Recovery Lock enabled by policy. Track the Android location-setting change and macOS ADE Platform SSO procedure as in-development guidance; the latter currently requires two sign-ins and Company Portal 5.2604.0 or later. Update links and runbooks to the new remote-action paths, verify platform and enrollment before using Delete, and back up the BitLocker recovery key and local administrator credentials before retiring or deleting a protected Microsoft Entra joined device.

keyChanges.title: Change Review Agent recommendations move inline in Multi Admin Approval
keyChanges.detail: Security Copilot guidance identifies a public preview that adds an **Agent Response** column for Windows PowerShell scripts in the Intune Multi Admin Approval experience. Approvers can view Change Review Agent risk-based recommendations inline instead of navigating to the separate agent experience.

keyChanges.title: macOS Recovery Lock passcode rotation is rolling out gradually
keyChanges.detail: The Intune remote action may not yet be available in every tenant; full availability is expected by late April 2026. It supports supervised macOS 11.5 or later on Apple silicon, not Intel Macs, and requires a policy that enables Recovery Lock. The newly generated passcode appears in the admin center and becomes effective on the device at its next successful Intune check-in.

keyChanges.title: Android Enterprise Block location is slated to become a three-option setting
keyChanges.detail: In-development settings catalog guidance says **General > Block location** will be renamed **Location** with **Device default**, **Location enabled**, and **Location disabled** options. Enabled forces location services on and prevents users from turning them off; disabled forces them off and prevents users from turning them on. The guidance applies to COPE devices running Android 10 and earlier, COBO, and COSU devices; no availability date is given.

keyChanges.title: macOS ADE Platform SSO registration guidance requires two enrollment sign-ins
keyChanges.detail: The in-development procedure requires an `EnableRegistrationDuringSetup` settings catalog policy assigned through Setup Assistant’s **Await final configuration** step. During enrollment, users sign in once for regular enrollment and again in Company Portal to authenticate and obtain the SSO extension. Devices must use ABM or ASM ADE with modern authentication, and Company Portal 5.2604.0 or later must be deployed as a line-of-business app; a future reduction in sign-ins has no ETA.
keyChanges.product: Intune – macOS Automated Device Enrollment and Platform SSO

keyChanges.title: Delete guidance distinguishes Retire from Wipe by platform and enrollment
keyChanges.detail: The new remote-action page documents that Delete triggers **Retire** for Windows, iOS/iPadOS, macOS, Android device administrator, and Android BYOD. It triggers **Wipe** for Android COBO, COSU, COPE, and AOSP. This is a documentation clarification rather than evidence of a same-day behavior change. The page also warns that retiring or deleting a BitLocker-protected Microsoft Entra joined device removes key protectors and suspends BitLocker on the OS volume, so administrators should back up the recovery key and aÂ

2026-04-03.headline: TeamViewer’s new Intune connector guidance covers Android, iOS, and Windows
2026-04-03.overview: The period’s clearest substantive item is new Intune guidance for a TeamViewer remote-assistance experience. It covers all listed Android enrollment options, iOS/iPadOS, and Windows, and documents connector setup, licensing, permissions, and data sharing. The evidence does not classify the capability as preview or generally available. Other meaningful updates clarify compliance-report interpretation, correct a Windows Autopilot proxy example, and expand Configuration Manager upgrade guidance. Security-baseline changes shown here only update publication dates, while other edits fix links or wording.
2026-04-03.adminImpact: Administrators evaluating TeamViewer should verify the eligible TeamViewer license, the Intune license requirement for the configuring administrator, and the Remote assistance connectors/Read and Remote assistance connectors/Update permissions, or use the Intune Administrator or Global Administrator role. TeamViewer is documented as unsupported in GCC and GCC High. For compliance reports, account for device check-in timing, multi-user devices, Pending states, multiple records, and different summary/detail refresh cadences; this is planned clarification rather than an announced reporting behavior change. Use the revised Autopilot proxy example when creating or revising configuration guidance, but the evidence does not require changes to deployed settings. Configuration Manager operators can

keyChanges.title: New TeamViewer connector experience is documented for Intune
keyChanges.detail: A new how-to describes configuring the new TeamViewer connector, starting remote-assistance sessions, and the data Intune shares with TeamViewer. The documented scope includes Android BYOD, COSU, COBO, COPE, AOSP, and DA enrollment options, plus iOS/iPadOS and Windows. The article requires an eligible TeamViewer license and notes that GCC and GCC High are unsupported; the evidence does not establish preview or general-availability status.

keyChanges.title: Compliance reporting guidance will clarify check-in and user-state edge cases
keyChanges.detail: The In Development page says Intune will add guidance explaining that compliance reports refresh during device check-in and policy-refresh cycles; shared-device reports show the last user who checked in; Pending can persist until the next reporting cycle; multiple user and system records can appear; and summary and detailed views may temporarily differ. This is documentation clarification, not evidence of a new reporting behavior.

keyChanges.title: Autopilot proxy XML now shows an HTTPS scheme
keyChanges.detail: The Hybrid Connector Proxy example changes the proxyaddress value from `<PROXY ADDRESS HERE>:<PORT HERE>` to `<https://PROXY ADDRESS HERE>:<PORT HERE>`, leaving the other shown attributes unchanged. The diff corrects the documented example but does not establish a runtime behavior change or a requirement to modify existing configurations.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager guidance adds Windows Server 2025 upgrade paths
keyChanges.detail: The supported upgrade guidance now lists Windows Server 2019 to 2022 or 2025; Windows Server 2016 to 2019, 2022, or 2025; and Windows Server 2012 R2 to 2016, 2019, or 2025. It also adds an important requirement that site systems running the Software Update Point role use the same Windows Server version for synchronization, including relevant Central Administration and primary site servers with WSUS Administration Tools.

2026-04-06.headline: TeamViewer’s old connector is being deprecated as Intune documents custom notifications
2026-04-06.overview: The supplied evidence is dominated by documentation path maintenance: many remote-action links move from legacy `remote-actions` URLs to `device-management/actions`. The substantive guidance covers the TeamViewer connector transition, a newly documented custom-notification action, and specific macOS DMG and Defender for Endpoint Android procedures. The diffs do not establish a same-day feature launch or tenant-setting change.
2026-04-06.adminImpact: Administrators using the old TeamViewer connector should plan setup of the new integration, with no retirement deadline supplied. Teams using custom notifications should verify platform support, app installation, push permissions, battery-optimization settings on Android, and the required RBAC permissions. Review macOS DMG assignment intent and update Defender Android runbooks; update bookmarks and internal links for the new remote-action URLs.

keyChanges.title: The legacy TeamViewer connector is now explicitly marked for deprecation
keyChanges.detail: The previous TeamViewer connector article now says the new remote-assistance experience replaces it, identifies the old connector as being deprecated, and recommends the new integration for the latest experience and ongoing support. This is deprecation guidance, not a supplied retirement date.

keyChanges.title: A new page documents Intune’s send-custom-notification remote action
keyChanges.detail: The action can send push notifications to individual devices or users in groups through Company Portal or the Intune app. The documented scope is Android Enterprise personally-owned work profile (BYOD) and iOS/iPadOS. Requirements include the relevant app and user-granted push permissions; Android battery optimization can block delivery. RBAC includes Help Desk Operator or a custom role with Remote tasks/Send custom notifications, plus Organization/Update for group notifications.

keyChanges.title: macOS DMG guidance clarifies that automatic updates require Required intent
keyChanges.detail: The macOS apps (DMG) article now states that only apps deployed with **Required** intent automatically update. The existing update procedure still requires the same bundle identifier and Microsoft Intune agent for macOS version 2304.039 or later. The diff documents the condition but does not announce a service-behavior change.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Endpoint Android setup adopts the Managed Google Play app name
keyChanges.detail: The procedure now tells administrators to select **Microsoft Defender: Antivirus** in Managed Google Play, then uses the revised Intune path of **Apps > Android > Create > Managed Google Play app**, followed by **Select** and **Sync**. This is a naming and procedure clarification, not evidence of a new Defender capability.

keyChanges.title: Remote-action links move from legacy paths to device-management actions
keyChanges.detail: The Endpoint Security Manage Devices article now points platform actions, Sync, Restart, and bulk device actions to `device-management/actions` locations instead of `remote-actions` locations. Similar supplied edits show a broader documentation navigation migration; these changes do not alter the documented action semantics.

2026-04-07.headline: Endpoint Privilege Management now enforces scope tags on elevation requests
2026-04-07.overview: April 7 was a high-volume documentation day: 327 records included 290 updates, 19 new pages, and 18 removals. Most representative edits were mechanical path and cross-reference repairs across Autopilot, endpoint security, RBAC, Configuration Manager, and certificate content. The substantive exceptions were enforced EPM scoping and new certificate-management guidance for derived credentials and S/MIME.
2026-04-07.adminImpact: Review delegated Endpoint Privilege Management administration because elevation-request visibility and management are now limited by applicable scope tags.
