For certificate deployments, the new guidance documents tenant configuration with one supported derived-credential issuer, a required trusted root, and a current Windows VPN limitation; S/MIME guidance requires PKCS certificates and the Certificate Connector for Microsoft Intune. Path-only documentation edits do not indicate tenant or service behavior changes.

keyChanges.title: EPM elevation requests are now constrained by scope tags
keyChanges.detail: The Intune What's New entry says applicable scope tags are now enforced when administrators view Endpoint Privilege Management elevation requests. Administrators can view and manage only requests for devices and users within their assigned scope, strengthening administrative boundaries.

keyChanges.title: Derived-credential setup is documented with a one-issuer tenant limit
keyChanges.detail: A new Intune how-to explains configuring a supported third-party derived-credential issuer and selecting Derived credential for Android Enterprise fully managed, iOS/iPadOS, and Windows authentication scenarios. Only one issuer can be used per tenant, and a trusted root certificate is required. Windows VPN authentication with derived credentials is currently not working as expected, with no ETA for the fix.

keyChanges.title: New S/MIME guidance details certificate delivery across mail clients
keyChanges.detail: The new Intune article covers S/MIME certificates for Android, iOS/iPadOS, and Windows. Intune automatically delivers certificates and associates them with native iOS mail and Outlook on iOS and Android; users must manually enable S/MIME in Windows, macOS, and other mail clients. Signing certificates use PKCS and require the Certificate Connector for Microsoft Intune.

2026-04-08.headline: Intune adds security-task and Android migration guidance amid documentation restructuring
2026-04-08.overview: On 8 April, the most operationally relevant additions were new guidance for Intune security tasks with Defender Vulnerability Management, Android device-administrator migrations, and Apple automated device enrollment authentication. These are Microsoft Learn documentation additions—not evidence of a new preview, general-availability launch, or changed service behavior. The broader set is dominated by page moves, link and image-path corrections, and paired additions and removals; the older vulnerability article now appears under a new filename, and no Message Center item is supplied.
2026-04-08.adminImpact: Treat this primarily as a documentation-review day. Where applicable, validate the Defender–Intune connection, subscriptions, device onboarding, and risk-assessment setup; plan Android migration around the stated compliance setting, enrollment prerequisites, and temporary device-limit headroom; and review Apple automated enrollment assignments for the documented account-driven Apple User Enrollment conflict. Update bookmarks and runbooks that use the older vulnerability article path, but do not change tenant configuration solely because a page was added.

keyChanges.title: Defender vulnerability guidance connects scans to Intune security tasks
keyChanges.detail: The new how-to documents the integration prerequisites: Intune Plan 1 and Defender for Endpoint, a service-to-service connection with the Microsoft Intune connection enabled in the Defender portal, and device onboarding with risk assessment enabled. Security admins create remediation tasks in Defender, while Intune admins act on them in the Intune admin center; only compatible vulnerabilities generate tasks, which include type, priority, status, and remediation steps. This is security guidance, not a stated feature
keyChanges.product: Intune security tasks and Microsoft Defender for Endpoint integration

keyChanges.title: Android device-administrator migration uses a compliance-driven work-profile checklist
keyChanges.detail: The migration procedure tells admins to set the Android device administrator compliance setting **Block devices managed with device administrator** to **Yes**. Users can then select **Resolve** and follow a checklist to unenroll from device administrator management, enroll a personally owned work profile, and resolve compliance issues. Prerequisites include Android Company Portal 5.0.4720.0 or later, an Android Enterprise connection, work-profile enrollment, and possible increases to Microsoft Entra and Intune per-
keyChanges.product: Intune Android Enterprise enrollment and compliance

keyChanges.title: Android MAM guidance offers a no-enrollment path away from device administrator
keyChanges.detail: A separate migration guide positions mobile application management without device enrollment for personal devices where full MDM controls such as Wi-Fi or email configuration are not needed. It lists the required Managed apps permissions—Assign, Create, Delete, Read, Update, and Wipe—and identifies the built-in Application Manager role as sufficient. The Company Portal app is required so users can receive app protection policies; the article documents a migration approach rather than announcing new MAM availability

keyChanges.title: Apple automated enrollment guidance enumerates four authentication choices and one block
keyChanges.detail: The new iOS/iPadOS guidance covers the Intune Company Portal app, Setup Assistant with modern authentication, Just in Time Registration for Setup Assistant with modern authentication, and legacy Setup Assistant. The methods apply to corporate-owned devices with user affinity purchased through Apple Business Manager or Apple School Manager. It also documents a specific limitation: Intune blocks Company Portal authentication when the user is targeted with an account-driven Apple User Enrollment profile, requiring the

keyChanges.title: Device enrollment manager guidance makes scale and licensing explicit
keyChanges.detail: The new DEM guidance states that a device enrollment manager can enroll and manage up to 1,000 devices, compared with 15 for a standard nonadministrator account. A DEM account requires an Intune user or device license and an associated Microsoft Entra user, and supports provisioning-package enrollment, DEM-initiated Company Portal enrollment, and DEM-initiated Microsoft Entra join. It also identifies Windows Autopilot, co-management, and automatic enrollment with Group Policy as methods that can exceed the standard

2026-04-09.headline: Cloud PKI expiration guidance and staged Windows rollouts lead the Intune briefing
2026-04-09.overview: This was a documentation-led period: 285 tracked changes, including 59 new, 167 updated, and 59 removed, with no Message Center entries. The most consequential material is operational guidance for Cloud PKI certificate continuity, Intune device cleanup, and Windows update deployment. Many other representative edits are link or image-path corrections, so the supplied evidence does not establish a broad product launch or general-availability change. Apple update pages do carry a deprecation notice, but no retirement date or replacement procedure is provided.
2026-04-09.adminImpact: Prioritize operational review rather than blanket tenant changes. Map expiring Cloud PKI issuing CAs to SCEP profiles, audit Windows update policies for blocking conflicts and staged-rollout settings, and treat device cleanup as a visibility control rather than a device-lifecycle action. Review the Apple deprecation notice in update planning, but do not infer an immediate retirement deadline from this period’s evidence.

keyChanges.title: Cloud PKI guidance adds a customer-managed CA-expiration runbook
keyChanges.detail: The new Microsoft Cloud PKI guidance says SCEP profiles that reference an expired issuing CA stop issuing new certificates, potentially affecting Wi-Fi, VPN, email, and certificate-based authentication. Administrators are directed to create a replacement issuing CA with the same Root CA Source and matching properties such as EKUs and key sizes, then replace the old SCEP URI in each affected profile. Cloud PKI does not support multiple SCEP URIs, and changing the URI does not trigger certificate reissuance; the page

keyChanges.title: Device cleanup rules are documented as hide-only, not wipe or retire
keyChanges.detail: New Intune guidance states that scheduled cleanup rules hide records for devices that have not checked in, removing them from the Intune portal and reports without wiping or retiring the devices. Records can reappear if the device checks in before its certificate expires; after certificate expiry, re-enrollment is required. The documented threshold is 30 to 270 days, Jamf-managed devices are excluded, and configuration requires the specified cleanup-rule RBAC permissions.

keyChanges.title: Feature-update guidance defines immediate, dated, and gradual availability
keyChanges.detail: New Intune guidance documents three rollout behaviors for Windows feature update policies: make an update available as soon as possible, on a specific date, or gradually through offer groups. For gradual deployment, the first-group availability date must be at least two days in the future. Availability makes devices eligible after their next Windows Update scan; actual installation remains influenced by deadlines, restart controls, and user behavior.

keyChanges.title: Driver-policy guidance calls out blocking settings and one-policy assignments
keyChanges.detail: The Windows driver update procedure tells administrators to check that the update-ring Windows driver setting is set to Allow and that Settings Catalog > Windows Update client policies > Exclude WU Drivers in Quality Update is set to Allow Windows Update drivers. It also recommends assigning each device to only one driver update policy and using test groups and phased deployments before broader approval.

keyChanges.title: Supervised Apple update guidance carries a deprecation notice and operating limits
keyChanges.detail: The new supervised iOS/iPadOS update guide includes the Apple MDM software updates deprecation notice and documents support for supervised iOS 10.3 through 18 and iPadOS 13.0 through 18. Deploying an older OS version also requires a device restrictions profile to restrict update visibility. Shared iPad updates install only while the device is charging and no users are signed in. The supplied evidence gives no deprecation date or replacement path, so this is a planning signal rather than a dated retirement notice.

2026-04-10.headline: Edge for Business guidance maps Intune controls across managed and BYOD devices
2026-04-10.overview: 10 April is dominated by newly added and reorganized Microsoft Learn content around Intune app protection and Microsoft Edge for Business. The main addition is a Secure Enterprise Browser framework covering Intune MAM and MDM on Windows, macOS, iOS, and Android. With no message-center entries supplied, this should be treated as security and deployment guidance—not evidence of a new feature launch, preview, general availability announcement, retirement, or backend behavior change. A separate notable documentation change updates the Windows Autopilot device-preparation guidance from 10 to 25 managed applications. Other representative edits are largely link-path migrations and date or known-issue refreshes.
2026-04-10.adminImpact: Use the Edge guidance as a design and runbook input: match Settings Catalog, App Configuration Policies, or App Protection Policies to the device's enrollment state, and avoid combining policy types that the guidance identifies as conflicting. If adopting Mobile Threat Defense-based app protection, configure connectors before onboarding users and designate a primary connector when Defender for Endpoint and another partner coexist. For Windows Autopilot, validate the documented 25-app statement against the tenant portal and deployment tests before changing profiles. The supplied evidence does not justify a production change solely because a Learn page was added.

keyChanges.title: Secure Enterprise Browser overview links Edge, Intune MAM, and MDM
keyChanges.detail: A newly added overview describes a Secure Enterprise Browser strategy for Microsoft Edge for Business using Intune MAM and MDM on Windows, macOS, iOS, and Android. It frames the approach around Conditional Access, app protection, and Level 1, Level 2, and Level 3 data-protection configurations. This is new security guidance, not a reported product launch or availability change.
keyChanges.product: Intune and Microsoft Edge for Business

keyChanges.title: Settings Catalog guidance separates enrolled Edge devices from MAM scenarios
keyChanges.detail: The Step 5 guidance says Settings Catalog provides device-level Edge controls for enrolled Windows and macOS, while App Protection Policies and App Configuration Policies are intended for unmanaged or non-enrolled devices. It warns not to target App Configuration Policies and Settings Catalog policies at the same Edge client; on enrolled Windows, choose Settings Catalog or the Microsoft Edge Security Baseline, not both. This is a documented deployment rule, not evidence that Intune newly enforces a conflict.
keyChanges.product: Intune Settings Catalog and App Management

keyChanges.title: MTD connector order and default-primary behavior are spelled out for APP
keyChanges.detail: The new Mobile Threat Defense guidance says to configure MTD connectors before onboarding users to the policies. Only users enrolled in MAM send health-state data; if Microsoft Defender for Endpoint and another MTD partner are configured without a designated primary, Intune defaults to Defender for Endpoint. App protection policies can use Max allowed device threat level to block or selectively wipe protected apps based on vendor risk.
keyChanges.product: Intune Mobile Threat Defense and App Protection Policies

keyChanges.title: Autopilot device-preparation guidance changes the documented app cap from 10 to 25
keyChanges.detail: The Entra Join Autopilot Policy page now says the Apps section allows up to 25 managed applications, replacing the previous value of 10. Because the supplied evidence is a documentation diff, administrators should validate whether their tenant's Device Preparation experience accepts the expanded selection before redesigning deployment profiles; the data does not independently confirm a service-limit change.

keyChanges.title: Enterprise App Catalog guide documents update timelines and Autopilot blocking support
keyChanges.detail: The new Enterprise App Catalog procedure says Enterprise App Management is an Intune Suite add-on available for trial and purchase. It documents that most app updates are available within 24 hours after automated validation, while updates requiring manual testing typically complete within seven days, and says catalog apps can be selected as blocking apps in Windows Autopilot Enrollment Status Page and Device Preparation Page profiles. This is onboarding and service-level guidance, not a launch announcement.

2026-04-11.headline: Microsoft Entra passkey on Windows guidance now covers unmanaged and shared devices
2026-04-11.overview: The period’s substantive Intune change is an expansion of passwordless guidance to describe Microsoft Entra passkey on Windows. The documentation identifies it as a FIDO2 passkey using Windows Hello biometric verification without requiring device join or registration, and positions it alongside Windows Hello for Business for managed-device scenarios. A second update is editorial, changing the page date and normalizing markup.
2026-04-11.adminImpact: Administrators planning passwordless deployments should account for the documented passkey scenario on shared devices, unmanaged endpoints, and devices without Windows Hello for Business provisioning. The supplied evidence does not show an Intune setting change, rollout, availability milestone, or required tenant action.

keyChanges.title: Passwordless guidance adds Microsoft Entra passkey on Windows
keyChanges.detail: The revised Intune guidance describes Microsoft Entra passkey on Windows as a FIDO2 passkey that uses Windows Hello for biometric verification without device join or registration. Users can register multiple passkeys for multiple Microsoft Entra accounts on one device, making the scenario relevant to shared devices and unmanaged endpoints. The page also clarifies that it complements Windows Hello for Business on managed devices; this is documentation content, not evidence of a new Intune launch.

keyChanges.title: Passwordless page metadata is dated 13 April 2026
keyChanges.detail: The companion update changes the page's ms.date from 03/24/2026 to 04/13/2026. The remaining diff only normalizes column and row markup, with no changed setting, prerequisite, procedure, or administrator behavior shown.

2026-04-13.headline: New Intune guidance details macOS Platform SSO, Windows inventory, and VPN caveats
2026-04-13.overview: The period was primarily a documentation expansion and reorganization rather than a release bulletin. New Intune pages add setup and reference coverage for macOS Platform SSO, Windows properties-catalog inventory, VPN profiles, Apple restrictions, and Group Policy migration, while many updates simply repoint links from legacy intune-service/configuration locations to device-configuration paths. The former Group Policy Analytics migration article was removed, but a new migration page documents the same import, review, and Settings Catalog workflow. The supplied evidence identifies no preview, general-availability event, capability retirement, or service-behavior change.
2026-04-13.adminImpact: Most administrators should update bookmarks and internal runbooks rather than change tenant settings. When planning deployments, use the new Platform SSO and Group Policy migration procedures; verify the properties catalog ownership, join-state, and RBAC prerequisites; deploy VPN apps before their profiles and place VPN, certificate, and trusted-root profiles in the same groups for certificate authentication. Also review the documented Windows 11 VPNv2 CSP issue, the Apple user-enrollment per-app VPN limitation, and the GPO scope-tag requirement. The Apple restriction page documents a Yes/Not configured control; it does not indicate that the default behavior changed.

keyChanges.title: macOS Platform SSO receives a dedicated Intune configuration guide
keyChanges.detail: A new how-to explains configuring Platform SSO through a Settings Catalog policy and deploying it to macOS. It covers Microsoft Entra ID credentials, passwordless authentication, smart cards, and Touch ID, and says Platform SSO includes the Enterprise SSO app extension. This is new configuration guidance, not evidence of a launch or availability change.

keyChanges.title: Properties catalog guidance defines Windows inventory scope and roles
keyChanges.detail: The new guide documents collecting selected Windows hardware properties such as BIOS, TPM, disk, memory, battery, and network-adapter information. The described scenario covers corporate-owned, Intune-managed devices, including co-managed devices, that are Microsoft Entra hybrid joined or Microsoft Entra joined. Configuration requires the Policy and Profile manager role or a custom role with Device Configurations > Create and Organization > Read.

keyChanges.title: VPN guidance calls out app sequencing, certificate grouping, and Windows 11 caveat
keyChanges.detail: The new VPN profile guide says to deploy the VPN app before creating the profile. For certificate-based authentication, the VPN profile, certificate profile, and trusted-root profile should target the same groups. It also states that iOS/iPadOS and macOS user enrollment supports only per-app VPN, and flags an issue between the Windows 11 client and the Windows VPNv2 CSP.

keyChanges.title: Apple restriction reference spells out unmanaged-app document blocking
keyChanges.detail: The new Apple device restriction reference documents the iOS/iPadOS setting Block viewing corporate documents in unmanaged apps: Yes blocks viewing corporate documents in unmanaged apps, while Not configured is the default and leaves Intune unchanged; the operating system might otherwise allow viewing in any app. Its example says setting Yes can prevent OneDrive content from being saved to Dropbox after the policy is received, such as after a restart. This clarifies documented setting behavior rather than reporting

keyChanges.title: GPO migration guidance adds scoped-role and scope-tag prerequisites
keyChanges.detail: A new Windows how-to describes importing on-premises GPOs, reviewing which settings are available in Intune, and migrating them into a Settings Catalog policy assigned to users or devices. It requires an Intune administrator or a role with Security baselines and Device configurations/Create permissions. Only administrators scoped to the GPO can create the policy, and an omitted scope tag defaults to Default. The page documents the workflow; it does not establish a new migration capability.

2026-04-14.headline: Edge MAM gains cross-tenant support as Intune compliance guidance is reorganized
2026-04-14.overview: On 14 April, Microsoft explicitly announced one product-level change: Microsoft Edge for Business now supports opt-in cross-tenant Intune MAM policies for devices managed by different tenants, with app protection, OneDrive download redirection, and leak controls. The much larger Learn batch is chiefly a compliance-content reorganization: new platform references and procedures sit alongside link and path rewrites. The supplied diffs do not establish broad availability changes for those documentation entries, so the day should not be read as a mass feature launch.
2026-04-14.adminImpact: Prioritize the Edge scenario if contractors or partner users work across tenants: decide whether to opt in and review the app-protection, download-routing, and leak-control design. For WSL, EPM, and partner-compliance work, act only if adopting those documented configurations; the WSL procedure requires both the Intune WSL plugin and the Microsoft Intune management extension. Link-only navigation edits require no tenant change.

keyChanges.title: Cross-tenant Edge MAM adds protection for partner-managed devices
keyChanges.detail: The Message Center update says Edge for Business supports cross-tenant Intune Mobile Application Management policies for devices managed by different tenants. The opt-in scenario enforces app protection, redirects downloads to OneDrive, and activates leak controls. This is the period’s explicit service-behavior update.

keyChanges.title: Intune records 16 generally available compliance-partner integrations
keyChanges.detail: The new partner-compliance overview lists supported solutions as generally available for Android and/or iOS, including Jamf Pro, Kandji, Ivanti, Omnissa Workspace ONE UEM, and SOTI MobiControl. The documented flow is to configure Intune and user groups, configure the partner to send data, and enroll devices with that partner; assigned devices use the partner as MDM authority. This is a support statement in guidance, not a dated rollout announcement.

keyChanges.title: WSL compliance guidance spells out plugin and management-extension prerequisites
keyChanges.detail: The new Windows Subsystem for Linux compliance procedure requires the Intune WSL plugin and the Microsoft Intune management extension on target devices. It directs administrators to deploy the plugin as a Win32 app and to unassign and remove existing custom WSL compliance policies before setup. This documents deployment requirements and limitations; it does not establish a capability launch on 14 April.

keyChanges.title: EPM’s least-privilege migration procedure begins with audit-only reporting
keyChanges.detail: For transitioning Windows users from administrator to standard user, the Endpoint Privilege Management guide’s first phase enables auditing. The specified policy values are Endpoint Privilege Management: Enabled; Default elevation response: Not Configured; Send elevation data for reporting: Yes; and Reporting scope: Diagnostic data and all endpoint elevations. The guide says portal reports can take 24 hours to update. This is deployment guidance, not a claimed behavior change.

keyChanges.title: Android AOSP compliance reference details OS and patch-level gates
keyChanges.detail: The new reference says administrators must first create an Android AOSP compliance policy, then can block rooted devices, specify minimum and maximum OS versions, and require a minimum security patch level entered as YYYY-MM-DD. Devices below the specified patch level are noncompliant, while OS-version and patch-level values are unconfigured by default. This is reference clarification, not evidence that these controls were newly introduced.

2026-04-15.headline: macOS endpoint protection template deprecated amid new Intune security guidance
2026-04-15.overview: This was a high-volume period, but the supplied representative diffs show that many updates were ordinary Learn maintenance: links moved into reorganized Fundamentals, RBAC, and reporting paths, alongside author metadata changes. The consequential exceptions are an explicit macOS endpoint protection template deprecation and new guidance for Defender for Endpoint onboarding, tenant-attached firewall management, Intune security posture, and add-on licensing. The April 2026 In Development Message Center item is an advance-planning notice, but supplies no feature-level details.
2026-04-15.adminImpact: For new macOS endpoint protection profiles, use Endpoint security policies or Settings catalog rather than the deprecated template; existing policies are stated to remain unchanged. If using Defender for Endpoint, review EDR onboarding paths and avoid overlapping device-configuration and EDR policies, which can create conflicts. Tenant-attach administrators can use the new firewall reference to verify settings, while the Preview security and Intune Suite pages should be treated as guidance and licensing references rather than evidence of a new feature launch.

keyChanges.title: macOS endpoint protection template is explicitly deprecated
keyChanges.detail: The new macOS reference says existing policies remain unchanged, but new policies can no longer be created with the endpoint protection template. It directs administrators to Endpoint security policies for FileVault or Firewall, or Settings catalog for FileVault, Firewall, and System Policy Control (Gatekeeper).

keyChanges.title: EDR guidance separates Defender onboarding from other security controls
keyChanges.detail: The new Intune how-to covers automatic connector-based and manual deployment for Windows, macOS, and Linux. EDR policies onboard devices to Microsoft Defender for Endpoint and send security telemetry, but do not configure attack surface reduction, firewall, antivirus, threat-hunting rules, response automation, or investigation workflows. Device-configuration onboarding does not support tenant-attached devices, and overlapping policy types can create conflicts.

keyChanges.title: Tenant-attached Configuration Manager devices get a dedicated firewall reference
keyChanges.detail: The new Windows Firewall (ConfigMgr) reference applies to devices managed with Configuration Manager after tenant attach is configured and an Intune Firewall policy is in place. It enumerates settings such as CRL verification, where Not configured uses the client default that disables verification; stateful FTP True or False; packet queue Disabled, Queue Inbound, or Queue Outbound; and selectable IPsec exceptions.

keyChanges.title: Preview security guidance defines a recommended Intune control baseline
keyChanges.detail: The explicitly labeled Preview article recommends, where licenses are available, enforced scope tags, enrollment notifications, Windows automatic enrollment, and compliance policies for Windows, macOS, and fully managed or corporate-owned Android devices. The table lists Intune Plan 1 for these controls and Microsoft Entra ID P1 for Conditional Access with Windows automatic enrollment; more controls will be added over time.

keyChanges.title: Intune Suite guidance clarifies add-on coverage and cloud limits
keyChanges.detail: The new add-ons guide says licenses are available at additional cost and that Intune add-ons are not supported in Sovereign clouds. Its matrix lists Endpoint Privilege Management, Enterprise App Management, Advanced Analytics, and Remote Help as standalone add-ons and Intune Suite capabilities, while Microsoft Tunnel for Mobile Application Management is listed under Intune Plan 2 and Intune Suite.

2026-04-16.headline: Intune compliance reports now document check-in lag and shared-device user-state behavior
2026-04-16.overview: This was primarily a documentation-maintenance period, but several diffs contain operationally useful detail. The largest clarification is that compliance state is evaluated continuously while compliance reports refresh at device check-in and can reflect the last checking user on shared devices. New how-to content covers Remote Help requirements and Enterprise App Catalog procedures, while Advanced Analytics and Endpoint Privilege Management references gain concrete schema and policy-limit details. The supplied evidence shows no preview, general-availability announcement, retirement, or confirmed product-behavior change.
2026-04-16.adminImpact: Prioritize interpretation and configuration review rather than rollout work. For compliance investigations, allow for check-in-driven report freshness and last-user attribution on shared devices. If deploying Remote Help, verify tenant-wide enablement, organizational Microsoft Entra sign-in, RBAC scope, and audit coverage for unenrolled devices. If consuming Advanced Analytics schema data, review handling for the documented mobile platforms and fields. For Endpoint Privilege Management, design each elevation-rules policy within the documented 100-rule maximum. Enterprise App Management administrators can use the documented default app settings, Windows Autopilot ESP/DPP support, and update SLOs—most updates within 24 hours and manually tested updates typically within seven days—for rollout

keyChanges.title: Compliance reporting clarifies check-in freshness and shared-device attribution
keyChanges.detail: This is a documentation clarification, not evidence that evaluation or reporting behavior changed. Device compliance state is continually evaluated, but compliance policy reports refresh when a device checks in and show the last confirmed state. On shared or multi-user devices, reports can reflect the last user who checked in; pending states can persist until the next reporting cycle, duplicate user or system records can appear, and summary and detailed views can update at different times. Use these caveats when4

keyChanges.title: New Remote Help guide documents enablement, authentication, RBAC, and auditing
keyChanges.detail: A new how-to page states that Remote Help is disabled by default and, when enabled, applies tenant-wide. Both the helper and sharer must sign in with Microsoft Entra accounts from the organization, and users outside the organization cannot be assisted. The page also documents pre-connection compliance warnings, RBAC for helper scope and elevated actions, active and historical session reporting, audit logs, and limited auditing for unenrolled devices. This is a documentation addition, not a supplied feature-launch,،

keyChanges.title: Enterprise App Catalog guidance adds default settings, Autopilot, and update timing
keyChanges.detail: The new guide describes Enterprise App Catalog apps as Microsoft-prepared Win32 apps within Enterprise App Management, an Intune Suite add-on available for trial and purchase. It says Microsoft configures and confirms default installation, requirements, and detection settings; catalog apps can be assigned to users or devices and used as blocking apps in Windows Autopilot Enrollment Status Page and Device Preparation Page profiles. Its stated service-level objectives are availability of most automatically validated​

keyChanges.title: Advanced Analytics schema documents broader platform coverage and mobile fields
keyChanges.detail: The reference data-platform schema now lists Android, iOS, iPadOS, macOS, and Windows for network-adapter Identifier and Type. It adds Android IpAddressV4, SubnetAddressV4, and AndroidSecurityPatchLevel fields, and documents expanded SIM/eSIM data including SlotId for iOS and iPadOS, Iccid and Imei for Android, iOS, and iPadOS, Imsi for Android, Eid across Android, iOS, iPadOS, and Windows, IsActive for Android and Windows, and carrier fields for iOS and iPadOS. This is schema documentation; the diff does not claim

keyChanges.title: Endpoint Privilege Management documents a 100-rule elevation-policy limit
keyChanges.detail: The Create Elevation Rules guidance now explicitly notes that administrators can add up to 100 elevation rules per elevation-rules policy from the Microsoft Intune admin center. This records a concrete policy limit; it does not indicate a new rollout or retirement.

2026-04-17.headline: Managed Home Screen guidance warns Overview can expose Android system settings
2026-04-17.overview: 17 April was mainly a documentation-maintenance day: 90 updates and one removal, with representative diffs dominated by link and path corrections. The administrator-relevant exceptions are added Android kiosk security warnings and a macOS Platform SSO re-registration note. The Security Copilot change removes an agents requirements page, but the supplied evidence does not show a product retirement or a licensing or availability change. Nothing supplied indicates a feature launch, preview, or general-availability announcement.
2026-04-17.adminImpact: Audit Android Enterprise kiosk profiles for the combination of Overview and End-user access to device settings; explicitly block device-settings access where the kiosk must prevent system access, network or security changes, or a reset. For macOS Platform SSO, account for device re-registration when changing Authentication Method or Use Shared Device Keys, and when removing and re-targeting a profile for other settings. No tenant action follows from the Security Copilot page removal alone. Most remaining changes repair documentation paths—for example, encryption pages now point to device-management/monitor-encryption and education setup pages to device-enrollment, app-management, and fundamentals paths—so update internal references only where they still use old links.

keyChanges.title: Managed Home Screen is documented as insufficient by itself for kiosk lockdown
keyChanges.detail: The updated Configure Managed Home Screen page warns that Managed Home Screen provides a controlled experience but does not, by itself, block access to all Android system features. It says kiosk security depends on the combination of Managed Home Screen settings and device configuration restrictions, and advises administrators to ensure users cannot access system settings, modify network or security configuration, or perform a device reset. This is added security guidance, not evidence of a product behavior change.

keyChanges.title: Overview and device-settings controls now carry a specific Android kiosk warning
keyChanges.detail: The updated Android Enterprise device restrictions reference retains the behavior that enabling the Overview button lets users skip or ignore sign-in and session PIN screens, while adding IMPORTANT and WARNING callouts. If End-user access to device settings is not explicitly blocked, users may be able to access Android system settings, change network or security configuration, or perform a full device reset. Check both controls in profiles where that access is not intended; this is a documentation clarification and

keyChanges.title: macOS Platform SSO profile edits are documented to trigger re-registration
keyChanges.detail: A new note in Configure Platform SSO for macOS says that, after successful PSSO registration, updating Platform SSO > Authentication Method or Platform SSO > Use Shared Device Keys in the same profile causes device re-registration. For all other settings, removing and re-targeting the profile causes device re-registration. This clarifies behavior administrators should account for when modifying or redeploying profiles.

keyChanges.title: Security Copilot agents requirements page is removed from Learn
keyChanges.detail: The sole removal is ref-requirements.md, a Security Copilot page covering Microsoft Security Copilot agents in Intune, including the Vulnerability Remediation Agent, licensing, permissions, RBAC, plugins, and its manual trigger. The evidence establishes page removal only; it does not establish agent retirement or a change to licensing or availability.

keyChanges.title: Education setup references switch to reorganized Intune management paths
keyChanges.detail: The updated Setup Intune page replaces links for Company Portal configuration, Terms and conditions, Windows automatic enrollment, Enrollment Status Page, Apple MDM push certificates, Apple VPP, Automated Device Enrollment, licensing, and enrollment restrictions with paths under app-management, device-enrollment, and fundamentals. The diff shows navigation maintenance, not a change to settings, prerequisites, or enrollment behavior.

2026-04-20.headline: Apple ADE token workflows and Android credential controls sharpen Intune guidance
2026-04-20.overview: 20 April was primarily a documentation-consolidation and guidance-refresh day, not an evidenced product-announcement cycle. The biggest workstream reorganizes Apple ADE for iOS/iPadOS and macOS into platform overviews, standalone token setup, and device/token-management procedures; the new macOS overview also records ACME support on macOS 13.1 or later and says already-enrolled Macs need to re-enroll to receive an ACME certificate. Other high-value material documents Android Enterprise controls, a cloud-native endpoint authentication limitation, App Inventory navigation, and an inline Change Review Agent workflow. No Message Center entry is supplied, and the evidence does not establish GA, preview, retirement, or a deployment deadline for these selected items.
2026-04-20.adminImpact: Update runbooks and operator links rather than assume a tenant-wide rollout: use the Apple ADE token/profile prerequisites and sync limits, review Android credential-provider and Location policies, and audit cloud-native workloads for machine-account dependencies. Move App Inventory operators to the per-device All Apps path, and if Multi Admin Approval is in use, verify whether Change Review Agent suggestions are available for PowerShell requests. These actions are grounded in the supplied procedure and behavior details; no broad migration deadline or mandatory configuration change is identified.

keyChanges.title: Apple ADE management guidance now spells out token prerequisites and sync limits
keyChanges.detail: New iOS/iPadOS ADE management guidance makes two prerequisites explicit: set up an ADE token, then create and assign an enrollment profile. It documents a full-sync limit of once every seven days, automatic delta sync every 12 hours, manual Sync no more than once every 15 minutes, and the fact that a device deleted in Intune reappears on the next full sync if it remains assigned to Apple’s MDM server. Released devices can remain listed for 30–45 days before automatic deletion. This is an operational procedure and-­

keyChanges.title: Android Enterprise release notes document credential-provider and Location controls
keyChanges.detail: The updated service-release entry says admins can control which apps act as system-level credential providers on managed Android Enterprise devices running Android 14 and later. It points to Apps > Android > Configuration > Managed Devices with Android Enterprise selected, and lists allowing specific apps and enabling passkey-based sign-in. It also says General > Block location is now called Location, with Device default, Location enabled, and Location disabled options. Google Password Manager remains blocked as a

keyChanges.title: Cloud-native endpoint guidance warns that machine authentication will fail
keyChanges.detail: The new troubleshooting guidance says Microsoft Entra-joined cloud-native Windows endpoints do not support on-premises AD machine authentication. File shares, applications, or services configured to accept only computer or machine accounts will fail; Microsoft directs administrators to identify those dependencies and switch to user-based or service-account-based authentication. This is security and migration guidance about a documented limitation, not a new Intune authentication model.

keyChanges.title: Enhanced App Inventory moves its documented workflow to per-device All Apps
keyChanges.detail: The updated article changes the navigation from Apps > Monitor > All apps > App Inventory to Devices > All devices > a device > All Apps > App Inventory. It also clarifies that inventory includes every application detected on the device regardless of installation method, including apps that are also managed, and that the comparison table now lists multi-user installed-app support. This is a navigation and scope clarification in the documentation, not an announced collection-frequency change.

keyChanges.title: Multi Admin Approval guidance adds inline Change Review Agent responses
keyChanges.detail: When Change Review Agent is configured and has completed a run, the updated Multi Admin Approval guidance says the All requests tab displays an Agent Response column for Windows PowerShell script requests when a suggestion is available. Selecting the suggestion opens and completes the approval workflow without leaving the Multi Admin Approval node; suggestions remain available in the agent’s primary experience. The evidence describes a workflow integration but does not classify it as preview or general availability

2026-04-21.headline: Legacy Power BI reports face Intune Data Warehouse connector retirement
2026-04-21.overview: The period’s most consequential item is the retirement rollout for Intune Data Warehouse (beta) connector v1 in Power BI. Affected reports must move to connector v2 or the OData Feed. The period also adds or restructures Apple ADE guidance across iOS/iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, and visionOS, plus new how-to coverage for suspending and restoring Managed Home Screen on Android Enterprise. Most other representative edits are terminology or navigation cleanup and do not show a product behavior change.
2026-04-21.adminImpact: Inventory Power BI reports created before November 2025 and identify those still using connector v1; migrate them before the transition completes. For Apple deployments, use the platform-specific ADE guidance and verify token, ownership, enrollment, and operating-system prerequisites. For Android Enterprise COBO/COSU devices, confirm the Managed Home Screen Alarms & Reminders permission and required RBAC permissions before using suspend or restore. The supplied evidence does not identify a preview or general-availability announcement for the newly documented capabilities.

keyChanges.title: Power BI beta connector retirement is rolling out now
keyChanges.detail: The updated Intune index says the Intune Data Warehouse (beta) connector v1 in Power BI is retired. Reports created after November 2025 already use connector v2, while older reports may still use the beta connector. The transition rolls out gradually over two weeks starting April 20, 2026, with customer communications beginning in late April. Move affected reports to connector v2 or the OData Feed; customers already using supported data-access options are not expected to be disrupted.

keyChanges.title: Apple ADE overview covers userless tvOS and visionOS enrollment
keyChanges.detail: A new Apple mobile ADE overview lists iOS/iPadOS, tvOS, and visionOS. For tvOS and visionOS, it specifies enrollment without user affinity, corporate-owned enrollment, device-targeted policies, and configuration through custom configuration profiles. BYOD and personal devices are explicitly unsupported. This is new or reorganized guidance, not an explicit availability-stage announcement.

keyChanges.title: Apple account service-access guidance sets OS and enrollment prerequisites
keyChanges.detail: The new how-to says service-access settings are configured in Apple Business or Apple School Manager, not directly in Intune; Intune instead issues a management token that Apple uses during device activation. Devices must be owned by the organization in Apple Business, enrolled through ADE, and run iOS/iPadOS 17 or later or macOS 14 or later. The settings apply to all Apple accounts, and changing them can automatically sign out accounts on devices that no longer meet the requirement.

keyChanges.title: Managed Home Screen suspension temporarily removes kiosk restrictions
keyChanges.detail: New action guidance describes Suspend Managed Home Screen for Android Enterprise corporate-owned Fully Managed (COBO) and Dedicated (COSU) devices. While suspended, Managed Home Screen policies are not enforced and users receive the standard home screen and apps. The action requires the Managed Home Screen Alarms & Reminders permission; built-in Help Desk Operator or School Administrator roles can run it, while custom roles need Remote tasks/Temporarily Suspend Managed Home Screen plus device-visibility permissions

keyChanges.title: Managed Home Screen restore re-applies configured policies
keyChanges.detail: The companion guidance covers Restore Managed Home Screen on the same Android Enterprise COBO and COSU platforms. Restoring re-enables Managed Home Screen and enforces its policies again, limiting access to the apps and settings defined by those policies. Custom roles need Remote tasks/Restore Managed Home Screen and device-visibility permissions, and Alarms & Reminders must be granted to Managed Home Screen.

2026-04-22.headline: Apple TV and Vision Pro ADE guidance adds enrollment prerequisites and limits
2026-04-22.overview: Apple Automated Device Enrollment (ADE) dominates the meaningful Intune changes: two new Learn how-to pages describe userless enrollment procedures for corporate Apple TV and Apple Vision Pro devices, while related guidance adds platform-specific limits, scope-tag behavior, and a macOS Platform SSO prerequisite. These are documentation additions and clarifications, not evidence of a separate product launch. The rest of the period is largely editorial: Apple pages replace “enrollment profile” with “enrollment policy,” Linux compliance guidance changes Ubuntu Desktop from 22.04/24.04 to 24.04/26.04, and a Configuration Manager application-deployment troubleshooting reference was removed.
2026-04-22.adminImpact: For Apple TV or Vision Pro ADE deployments, verify Apple Business or Apple School Manager access, an active .p7m token, an Intune Apple MDM push certificate, and new or wiped devices. The ADE overview lists Intune Plan 2 as required for tvOS and visionOS device management. For visionOS, deploy Company Portal from Intune as a required, device-licensed VPP app rather than from the App Store, and enable automatic app updates if required. For tvOS, plan around the documented absence of compliance policies, Setup Assistant screen configuration, and Settings Catalog profiles; use custom .plist profiles instead. Create a Platform SSO policy before macOS enrollment if Entra ID sign-in is needed during Setup Assistant. Set token scope tags before creating tvOS or visionOS policies because later tag

keyChanges.title: tvOS ADE setup guidance is newly documented for userless Apple TV enrollment
keyChanges.detail: A new Intune Learn how-to describes creating a tvOS ADE enrollment policy for devices without user affinity. Its prerequisites are Apple Business or Apple School Manager access, an active .p7m token, an Intune Apple MDM push certificate, and new or wiped Apple TV hardware. It also states a limit of 1,000 enrollment profiles per token and says devices must be assigned an enrollment policy before activation. This is a documentation addition, not evidence of a separate product launch.

keyChanges.title: visionOS ADE guidance requires Intune deployment of Company Portal
keyChanges.detail: A new visionOS how-to describes userless ADE for corporate Apple Vision Pro devices. It directs administrators to deploy Company Portal through Intune as a required VPP app with device licensing, not through the App Store. Setting Automatic app updates to Yes enables automatic updates, while the App Store version is described as incompatible with ADE.

keyChanges.title: tvOS ADE limitations now specify custom .plist configuration instead of Settings Catalog
keyChanges.detail: Updated tvOS guidance says enrollment is without user affinity; compliance policies and Setup Assistant screen configuration aren't supported. Settings catalog–based configuration profiles also aren't supported, so administrators must use uploaded custom .plist files. The page additionally warns that tvOS ADE hardware inventory currently reports storage capacity as 0 rather than actual device storage.

keyChanges.title: macOS ADE requires a Platform SSO policy before Setup Assistant enrollment
keyChanges.detail: A new section says administrators who want Microsoft Entra ID single sign-on during Setup Assistant must create a Platform SSO policy before devices enroll. The policy is deployed to enrolling macOS devices during ADE and enables users to sign in with organizational credentials during setup.

keyChanges.title: tvOS and visionOS ADE policies inherit token scope tags only at creation
keyChanges.detail: Updated token guidance says tvOS and visionOS ADE policies inherit the scope tag assigned to the enrollment program token when the policy is created. Later changes to the token's scope tag aren't reflected in existing policies, so the intended tag should be assigned before policy creation to preserve correct RBAC visibility.

2026-04-23.headline: Guidance now highlights version-targeted policies for Android direct LOB updates
2026-04-23.overview: This was primarily a documentation-clarification period. The most actionable updates cover Android Enterprise direct line-of-business app versioning, macOS Platform SSO enrollment prerequisites, the Microsoft Edge for Business threat-level value, and Microsoft 365 Apps assignment behavior. A new device-security overview and related link cleanup are organizational changes; the supplied evidence does not establish a feature launch, preview, general-availability change, or product retirement.
2026-04-23.adminImpact: Admins deploying Android APKs directly through Intune should create and assign a new app configuration policy when updating to a new app version, and note that direct LOB app configuration is limited to fully managed and dedicated Android Enterprise devices. Teams using macOS Automated Device Enrollment with Platform SSO should verify every listed prerequisite before enrollment. Edge policy authors should review the documented threat-level value, while Microsoft 365 Apps administrators should account for overwrite and possible uninstall behavior when using multiple assignments. The navigation changes do not imply a tenant configuration change.

keyChanges.title: Updated Android LOB versions need newly targeted app-configuration policies
keyChanges.detail: The revised Android app-configuration guidance now covers directly deployed LOB apps and says policies associated with a previous app version are not automatically applied after an update. Administrators must create and assign a policy targeting the new version. Direct-LOB app configuration is supported on Android Enterprise fully managed (COBO) and dedicated (COSU) devices, not personally owned work profile or corporate-owned work profile (COPE) devices. This is explicit documentation guidance, not evidence of a ￼

keyChanges.title: Direct APK deployment takes precedence over Managed Google Play
keyChanges.detail: The Android LOB deployment article clarifies that when the same app is deployed through Managed Google Play and as an APK uploaded directly to Intune, the directly uploaded app is installed regardless of the Managed Google Play version. If multiple directly uploaded versions are assigned, the higher version is installed. This documents deployment-selection behavior rather than announcing a new rollout.

keyChanges.title: macOS Platform SSO enrollment now lists all required setup components
keyChanges.detail: The enrollment procedure now states that all of these are required: a Settings Catalog Platform SSO policy, Company Portal deployed as a line-of-business app, and an Automated Device Enrollment profile using Setup Assistant with Modern Authentication and await final configuration enabled. If any step is missing or misconfigured, the configuration fails; the documented recovery procedure removes the existing Platform SSO configuration and reenrolls the device.

keyChanges.title: Edge app protection now specifies “Secured” for the blocked threat level
keyChanges.detail: In the Microsoft Edge for Business app protection policy procedure, the documented Max allowed device threat level paired with Block access changed from Medium to Secured. The evidence shows a documentation value update only, so administrators should verify the intended policy configuration rather than infer that the service behavior changed.

keyChanges.title: Microsoft 365 Apps guidance adds a Word-uninstall assignment example
keyChanges.detail: The deployment page now gives a concrete example of the existing overwrite rule for multiple required or available assignments: if an earlier Microsoft 365 Apps assignment includes Word and a later assignment omits it, Word is uninstalled. The page explicitly says this condition does not apply to Visio or Project. This is a clarification and example, not evidence of a changed assignment engine.

2026-04-24.headline: MAM deployment guidance defines BYOD boundaries as CHID driver limits are clarified
2026-04-24.overview: The period was primarily a MAM documentation reorganization rather than a feature rollout. Intune added a deployment guide under app management, removed the former device-enrollment MAM article, and repointed related links. A separate driver-policy clarification states that Windows driver update policies do not enforce OEM Computer Hardware ID targeting.
2026-04-24.adminImpact: Update bookmarks and internal runbooks that reference the former MAM location, and use the new guide’s platform and ownership boundaries when planning unenrolled-device deployments. Administrators relying on CHID-specific driver targeting should account for the documented non-enforcement and verify expected driver outcomes.

keyChanges.title: New MAM guide defines supported use cases and enrollment boundaries
keyChanges.detail: The new Mobile Application Management guide explains that unenrolled-device MAM uses app configuration profiles together with app protection policies. It covers Android, iOS/iPadOS, and Windows, supports personal or BYOD scenarios, and says MAM is not recommended as the only method for organization-owned devices or for user-less and shared devices.

keyChanges.title: MAM references move from device enrollment to app management
keyChanges.detail: The MAM Android guidance now links to ../../app-management/protection/mam-without-enrollment.md instead of ../../device-enrollment/mam-without-enrollment.md. Related enrollment and migration pages received the same destination change, making this an information-architecture update rather than a documented behavior change.

keyChanges.title: The former device-enrollment MAM article is removed
keyChanges.detail: The file intune/device-enrollment/mam-without-enrollment.md, titled “Mobile Application Management (MAM) for unenrolled devices in Microsoft Intune,” was removed. The replacement deployment guidance is represented by the new app-management article.

keyChanges.title: Driver update policies explicitly do not enforce OEM CHID targeting
keyChanges.detail: The updated Windows driver update policy guidance says policies do not enforce Computer Hardware ID targeting defined by OEMs, even when those drivers appear as recommended. Managed devices can therefore receive newer recommended driver versions instead of CHID-targeted drivers.

2026-04-25.headline: Quiet Time policies are unavailable in sovereign cloud environments
2026-04-25.overview: A single Intune App management documentation update adds an important support limitation: Quiet Time policies rely on the Substrate service, which is unavailable in US Government Community Cloud (GCC), GCC High, Department of Defense (DoD), and Microsoft Azure operated by 21Vianet. This is a documentation clarification, not evidence of a new feature or changed tenant behavior.
2026-04-25.adminImpact: Administrators in the listed sovereign environments should not plan Quiet Time policy rollouts because the capability is explicitly unsupported there. No additional action is indicated for other environments by this update.

keyChanges.title: Quiet Time documentation adds sovereign-cloud support limitation
keyChanges.detail: The Create Quiet Time Policies guidance now states that Quiet Time policies are unsupported in GCC, GCC High, DoD, and Azure operated by 21Vianet because they depend on Substrate, a service unavailable in those environments.

2026-04-26.headline: Managed Home Screen gains Android suspend-and-restore remote actions
2026-04-26.overview: The substantive update adds two Intune remote actions for temporarily letting users leave Managed Home Screen without removing policies or requiring a PIN. The device returns to the kiosk experience automatically when the defined duration expires or when the restore action is used. No preview or general-availability status is specified.
2026-04-26.adminImpact: Administrators managing Android Enterprise corporate-owned Fully Managed (COBO) or Dedicated (COSU) devices can incorporate suspend and restore into troubleshooting or short-term access procedures. Confirm that the automatic relock behavior fits those workflows.

keyChanges.title: Suspend and restore actions added for Managed Home Screen
keyChanges.detail: Intune now provides separate remote actions to suspend and restore Managed Home Screen on eligible Android devices. Suspension gives users temporary access to the device’s default launcher without removing policies or requiring a PIN; expiration of the configured duration, or the restore action, automatically re-locks the device into the kiosk experience.

2026-04-27.headline: Co-managed compliance faces an October deadline as Configuration Manager 2603 hardens CMG
2026-04-27.overview: The most consequential material is a co-management compatibility deadline, not a broad Intune policy rollout. Configuration Manager 2603 is described as an in-console update and brings tighter Network Access Account access, Cloud Management Gateway cipher hardening, and removal of the SQL Server Native Client dependency. In Intune, Autopatch update risk visibility adds device-risk classification for Windows, while Ubuntu 26.04 LTS is supported and Ubuntu 22.04 LTS support ends in August 2026. The supplied evidence does not label the Intune items as preview or generally available. Other entries are largely reference maintenance involving build and file-list details, a regional diagnostics endpoint, and checklist-link edits; notably, 2603 checklist links were changed to the checklist-for-installing-update-2509.md path. Those edits do not establish a product behavior change.
2026-04-27.adminImpact: Prioritize co-managed environments where the Compliance workload is managed by Intune: apply the applicable Configuration Manager update before October 2026 to avoid the documented risk of Software Center compliance-check failures. For 2603, confirm the site runs version 2409 or later, update the site and console, and then bring clients to the latest version because complete scenarios require current clients. Use the Autopatch report for Windows patch-risk triage. For Linux, find Ubuntu 22.04 devices under Devices > All devices, filter by Linux, and add the OS version column; notify users to upgrade before support ends in August 2026. If applicable, review the NAA and CMG security changes and remove sqlncli from site systems. The link-only documentation edits require no tenant action based

keyChanges.title: Software Center compliance has an October 2026 co-management deadline
keyChanges.detail: Changed behavior and lifecycle warning: an internal service required for device compliance checks will be deprecated in October 2026. Afterward, Software Center compliance checks may fail in co-managed environments where the Compliance workload is managed by Intune. The documented prevention is to apply the update before October 2026.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager 2603 is in-console and removes the SQL Native Client dependency
keyChanges.detail: Release availability and dependency retirement: 2603 is available as an in-console update that can be installed at the top-tier site in a hierarchy. All Configuration Manager components and site roles now remove the dependency on deprecated sqlncli.msi; administrators can safely uninstall sqlncli from site systems, and the product no longer includes it in redistributables.

keyChanges.title: Network Access Account and CMG receive 2603 security hardening
keyChanges.detail: Security and behavior changes in 2603 restrict Network Access Account information to supported OSD media task sequence scenarios, add permission requirements, and remove legacy access paths. Cloud Management Gateway instances disable weak DHE cipher suites; remaining suites are TLS 1.3 AES_256_GCM/AES_128_GCM and TLS 1.2 ECDHE. EnableCertPaddingCheck registry keys are also set by default on CMG Virtual Machine Scale Set instances to mitigate CVE-2013-3900.

keyChanges.title: Autopatch update risk visibility adds three Windows risk classes
keyChanges.detail: New reporting capability: the Autopatch update risk visibility report extends the security update status dashboard with granular patch-compliance and risk insight. It classifies managed Windows devices as Current, Exposed, or Critical and highlights policies contributing to risk, helping administrators identify and remediate issues faster. No preview or general-availability status is stated.

keyChanges.title: Intune adds Ubuntu 26.04 LTS support as 22.04 support ends
keyChanges.detail: Platform-support change: Intune now supports Ubuntu 26.04 LTS. Support for Ubuntu 22.04 LTS ends in August 2026; devices already enrolled on Ubuntu 22.04 remain enrolled, but users should be notified to upgrade to a supported Ubuntu version. Administrators can identify them under Devices > All devices by filtering for Linux and adding the OS version column.

2026-04-28.headline: macOS ADE Platform SSO registration gets concrete prerequisites for desktop-ready access
2026-04-28.overview: 28 April was chiefly a documentation-maintenance day, not evidence of a broad Intune release. The material exceptions are a week-of-4-May entry documenting Platform SSO registration during macOS Automated Device Enrollment, more precise Enhanced App Inventory lifecycle and identifier guidance, and a new Zero Trust Assessment pointer; an Apple VPP note also clarifies an expected app limitation. Configuration Manager changes were mainly title, link, formatting, and page-removal edits, so the removed 2603 summary should not be read as a product retirement.
2026-04-28.adminImpact: Admins planning macOS ADE should validate Enable Registration During Setup, Company Portal 5.2604.0 or newer, Setup Assistant with modern authentication, Await final configuration, and macOS 26 or newer before rollout. The updated Platform SSO procedure also says assignment filters can be used on static user groups, while all related policies must still target the same groups. Update Enhanced App Inventory runbooks for a full initial upload, delta-based later syncs, and approximately three days of collection after policy removal. Use the Zero Trust Assessment for the automated checks described in the security guidance. Configuration Manager administrators should treat the title, link, and page-removal edits as documentation changes rather than evidence of a retired release.

keyChanges.title: macOS ADE Platform SSO registration gets a defined setup path
keyChanges.detail: The What's New entry for the week of 4 May documents Platform SSO during macOS Automated Device Enrollment. Before enrollment, administrators must create a settings catalog policy with `Enable Registration During Setup`, deploy Company Portal version 5.2604.0 or newer as a line-of-business app, and use Setup Assistant with modern authentication plus `Await final configuration` in the ADE profile. It applies to macOS 26 and newer and says users have Microsoft Entra ID access immediately at desktop. The evidence adds
keyChanges.product: Intune — macOS Automated Device Enrollment and Platform SSO

keyChanges.title: Enhanced App Inventory clarifies identifiers, synchronization, and removal handling
keyChanges.detail: The procedure now directs administrators to Configuration settings > `+ Add Properties` > `ApplicationProperties`. `Platform Specific App Id` maps to Package Name for Store apps and product code for MSI apps, falling back to Uninstall Registry Key Name when neither applies. The documented sequence is a full upload on the first sync and delta-based uploads thereafter; removing the policy allows collection to continue for approximately three days before collection stops and service data is removed. This is a changed,

keyChanges.title: Zero Trust Assessment is added to increased-security guidance
keyChanges.detail: The Configure Microsoft Intune for increased security page adds an Automated assessment section linking to What is the Zero Trust Assessment and describing automation that tests the listed security configuration items and more. This is a security-guidance addition; it does not state that Intune requires the assessment or that a tenant setting changed.

keyChanges.title: Platform SSO enrollment guidance adds filters for static user groups
keyChanges.detail: The ADE Platform SSO procedure now says assignment filters can be used on Assigned (static) user groups. It retains the constraint that all policies for the feature must target the same static user groups; assigning them to different groups causes Platform SSO during enrollment to fail. This is a documentation clarification of assignment scope, not an announced enrollment behavior change.
