keyChanges.title: Apple VPP guidance explains why in-app purchases appear disabled
keyChanges.detail: Apple device restrictions guidance adds a note that `In-App Purchase Disabled` is expected on VPP apps because in-app purchases and subscriptions aren't compatible with VPP, Managed Apps, or Managed Apple Accounts. It points education and enterprise customers needing deployment at scale toward a separate full-featured version, sometimes as a Custom App. This clarifies app capability expectations rather than announcing a new Intune control.
keyChanges.product: Intune — Apple device restrictions and VPP apps

2026-04-29.headline: Unlicensed admin access clarified as Apple ADE guidance shifts from profiles to policies
2026-04-29.overview: 29 April was a documentation-heavy Intune day: all 151 recorded items were updates, with no new, removed, or Message Center entries. Representative diffs show many ordinary edits—Cloud PKI image alt text, link wording, and image syntax—alongside a few operational clarifications. Nothing supplied establishes a new feature launch, preview, GA milestone, or product retirement; the SCEP change retires legacy installation instructions only.
2026-04-29.adminImpact: Check tenant age and unlicensed-admin setting state; refresh Apple ADE runbooks for the Enrollment policies workflow and published OS versions; review egress allowlists for Windows Autopilot diagnostics; and move SCEP runbooks off the deprecated installation block. Do not infer a service-side feature rollout from these documentation edits alone.

keyChanges.title: Pre-July 2021 tenants face a one-way unlicensed-admin decision
keyChanges.detail: Updated Intune licensing guidance says tenants created after July 2021 support unlicensed administrator access by default, with no action required. Tenants created before July 2021 require Intune licenses unless Allow access to unlicensed admins is enabled, and that setting can't be undone afterward. The guidance also clarifies the 350-admin-per-security-group limit, permits multiple groups, and excludes nested-group members.

keyChanges.title: Apple ADE instructions replace Profiles with Enrollment policies
keyChanges.detail: The iOS/iPadOS ADE procedure now directs administrators to select the Apple mobile tab, choose a token, open Enrollment policies, and use Create policy > iOS/iPadOS. Assignment is labeled Assign policy and the default action is Set Default Policy. This is a published terminology and procedure rewrite, not evidence of a new enrollment capability.

keyChanges.title: Apple ADE guidance specifies tvOS and visionOS 26.0 or later
keyChanges.detail: The updated Apple ADE overview lists tvOS 26.0 or later and visionOS 26.0 or later, replacing the earlier unversioned visionOS entry. Administrators should verify target OS versions against this published guidance; the diff alone does not establish a separate launch or service-side change.

keyChanges.title: Windows Autopilot diagnostics adds a Swiss blob endpoint
keyChanges.detail: The Windows Autopilot Diagnostics upload entry now includes lgmsapeswiss.blob.core.windows.net and specifies TCP 443. The page also adds a Diagnostics collection section pointing to device-action network requirements. Review proxy and firewall allowlists where diagnostic collection is filtered; this is an endpoint-documentation update, not evidence of a new feature.

keyChanges.title: Legacy SCEP connector installation steps are deprecated in guidance
keyChanges.detail: The SCEP infrastructure page comments out the old Certificate Connector installation block and labels it deprecated for the new connector and its dedicated install article. Update NDES/SCEP runbooks to follow the current dedicated installation guidance; this retires an old documentation procedure, not the SCEP capability or connector product.

2026-04-30.headline: Enhanced Windows app inventory and Apple DDM guidance headline April 30 Intune changes
2026-04-30.overview: April 30 was dominated by documentation maintenance: 45 updates—36 for Intune, 8 for Configuration Manager, and 1 for Remote Help—with no new or removed items and no message-center posts. The meaningful exception is a new Week of May 4 What's New entry describing enhanced app inventory for Windows 10/11. Apple settings-catalog and device-action pages also make DDM paths and Apple platform/version coverage more explicit. Much of the remaining evidence is editorial normalization of titles, version labels, role and licensing includes, links, table markup, and terminology. No supplied item establishes preview, general availability, retirement, or a product behavior change; the Retire-page edit is a platform-list update, not a retirement event.
2026-04-30.adminImpact: No tenant change is documented for administrators to make from this period's evidence. If Windows inventory is in rollout planning, note the What's New entry's stated Windows 10/11 scope and Week of May 4 placement. Apple administrators can use the revised DDM paths and Wipe platform notes when validating runbooks. Recheck the Universal Print and Microsoft 365 Apps procedures if those pages are operational references, because their prerequisite and setup text was restructured. Do not infer GA or preview status, licensing changes, or reversal of deprecated-tool guidance from these documentation diffs alone.

keyChanges.title: Enhanced app inventory is documented for Windows 10/11 in the May 4 What's New section
keyChanges.detail: The What's New index adds an entry describing faster data updates, more detailed visibility, richer app metadata, and controls to specify which devices are included in inventory collection. It says the capability is initially available for Windows, with additional platforms to follow. Because this is a Week of May 4 documentation entry, it is not evidence here of GA, preview status, or a launch event.

keyChanges.title: Apple settings catalog guidance now maps concrete iOS/iPadOS DDM settings
keyChanges.detail: The Apple settings catalog page adds iOS/iPadOS guidance for Declarative Device Management > Software Update, Security > Passcode, Restrictions for blocking backup and document sync, and Declarative Device Management > Safari. It also lays out separate macOS, tvOS, and visionOS sections. This clarifies documented configuration paths rather than demonstrating a change in Apple DDM behavior.

keyChanges.title: Wipe guidance now lists tvOS 10.2+ and visionOS 1.1+
keyChanges.detail: The Intune Wipe page adds tvOS 10.2+ and visionOS 1.1+ to its supported-platform list. The supplied change documents platform scope but provides no support-announcement date or rollout details.

keyChanges.title: Universal Print article points admins to the UniversalPrint CSP
keyChanges.detail: The Settings Catalog article now identifies the UniversalPrint CSP used by the Intune settings. The same revision removes the page's former warning that the PrintProvisioning tool and printers.csv process is deprecated, along with standalone Universal Print and Intune subscription bullets in the Before you begin section. This is page restructuring; it does not say deprecated tooling is restored or that requirements changed.

keyChanges.title: Microsoft 365 Apps guidance removes explicit automatic-update setup instructions
keyChanges.detail: The page now uses a shared licensing include and no longer contains the prior text requiring Microsoft Intune and a Microsoft 365 subscription, the Policy and Profile Manager role, or the addition and enablement of Microsoft 365 Apps Automatic Updates with accompanying screenshots. The diff supports a documentation rework only; it does not establish changed licensing or update behavior.

2026-05-01.headline: Windows Security Center MAM guidance adds an explicit connector enablement step
2026-05-01.overview: The most consequential update revises the Intune Mobile Threat Defense setup flow for Windows MAM: admins are now told to enable Connect Windows devices for MAM and verify the connector reaches Enabled. The remaining updates are Windows Autopilot documentation maintenance, replacing outdated Win32, Enterprise App Catalog, and Win32 management links; they do not describe enrollment or policy-behavior changes.
2026-05-01.adminImpact: For the Windows Security Center connector, open its edit view after creation, turn on Connect Windows devices for MAM, save, and verify the status is Enabled before relying on it for MAM. Autopilot administrators should use the replacement documentation links when preparing app assignments, but no configuration change is evidenced.

keyChanges.title: Windows Security Center connector status and setup instructions are revised
keyChanges.detail: The Intune Step 3 procedure now adds an explicit step to open the Windows Security Center connector, enable Connect Windows devices for MAM, and save. The documented status is now Available after creation and changes to Enabled when the toggle is turned on, replacing the previous guidance that it remained Unavailable until a policy arrived or a MAM user enrolled.

keyChanges.title: Entra join app guidance switches to current Win32 and catalog links
keyChanges.detail: The Windows Autopilot Entra join user-driven tutorial now links to /create-win32-package, /add-enterprise-catalog-app, and /win32 instead of the older Win32 packaging, Enterprise App Catalog, and Win32 overview paths. This is a documentation-navigation refresh; the diff does not describe a change to supported apps or assignments.

2026-05-02.headline: Intune adds userless Apple ADE while requiring Windows IME 1.58.103.0
2026-05-02.overview: The period’s substantive changes affect Apple enrollment and Windows agent compatibility. Intune now supports userless Automated Device Enrollment for Apple Vision Pro and Apple TV, while Windows devices running older Intune Management Extension versions lose IME-dependent configurations and updates. Apple service-access controls are also now covered in current guidance rather than listed as in development.
2026-05-02.adminImpact: Verify Windows devices can sync and are running IME 1.58.103.0 or later, especially where Win32 apps, scripts, remediations, or platform scripts are used. For Apple Vision Pro and Apple TV enrollment, confirm Intune Plan 2 licensing and tvOS 26 or visionOS 26 requirements. Review Apple Business Manager or Apple School Manager service-access settings for organization-owned Apple devices.

keyChanges.title: Userless ADE arrives for Apple Vision Pro and Apple TV
keyChanges.detail: Intune now supports Apple Automated Device Enrollment without user affinity for visionOS and tvOS devices through Apple Business Manager or Apple School Manager. The capability includes custom configuration uploads, default enrollment restrictions, and device actions; it requires Intune Plan 2 and tvOS 26 or later or visionOS 26 or later. The matching In development entry was removed, so administrators should use the current enrollment guidance rather than treat this as a planned capability.

keyChanges.title: Windows IME 1.58.103.0 becomes the minimum supported version
keyChanges.detail: Windows devices on earlier Intune Management Extension versions no longer receive IME-dependent configurations or updates, including Win32 app deployments, PowerShell scripts, remediations, and platform scripts. The extension updates automatically, but devices must be able to sync with Intune to receive the compatible version.

keyChanges.title: Apple service-access controls move into current Intune guidance
keyChanges.detail: The What's New guidance now documents Apple access-management settings in Apple Business Manager and Apple School Manager. For organization-owned iOS, iPadOS, and macOS devices, these controls determine which devices users can sign in to and which apps and services are available to Apple accounts. The related In development entry was removed.

2026-05-04.headline: Planned Windows Sync expansion spans compliance, configuration policies, apps, and scripts
2026-05-04.overview: The Intune changes on 4 May are mostly documentation clarification: enrollment and RBAC requirements were reorganized into standard sections rather than changed service behavior. The consequential signals are a planned broader Windows Sync, planned macOS, iOS/iPadOS, and Android Enterprise controls, and a Direct Android LOB rollout expected to reach full availability by mid-May 2026. A previously listed Managed Home Screen suspend/restore roadmap item was removed, but the evidence does not establish a retirement or cancellation. Separately, Configuration Manager gained a new checklist for installing update 2603.
2026-05-04.adminImpact: Keep the In development entries out of production planning until they become available, but include them in future test plans. Check Direct Android LOB availability during the stated rollout window rather than treating its absence as a tenant configuration fault. For current mobile application management, verify the documented RBAC and Company Portal prerequisites; the broader enrollment-page restructuring does not by itself require tenant changes.

keyChanges.title: Windows Sync is planned to trigger a fuller on-demand workload synchronization
keyChanges.detail: The In development entry says the Windows device Sync action will initiate a more comprehensive synchronization across compliance, configuration policies, apps, and scripts instead of waiting for scheduled check-ins. The planned enhancement is aimed at troubleshooting, incident response, and high-priority rollouts; it is not presented as currently available.

keyChanges.title: Planned device controls cover macOS Wi-Fi, iOS wired networks, and Android Bluetooth
keyChanges.detail: The roadmap lists Disable MAC address randomization for macOS 15 and later Wi-Fi profiles; a new 802.1x Wired Networks profile for iOS/iPadOS 17 and later with EAP protocols including TLS, PEAP, and TTLS; and an Android Enterprise Settings catalog Block Bluetooth sharing setting, where True prevents content sharing over Bluetooth. These remain In development items, not general-availability announcements.

keyChanges.title: Direct Android LOB is rolling out, with full availability expected mid-May
keyChanges.detail: The Intune What's New index says Direct Android LOB is gradually rolling out and may not yet be available in a tenant. Full availability is expected by mid-May 2026, so administrators should wait for rollout completion rather than treat its absence as a configuration error.

keyChanges.title: Managed Home Screen suspend and restore actions leave the roadmap listing
keyChanges.detail: The Android Enterprise In development article no longer lists remote actions to temporarily suspend and restore Managed Home Screen for corporate-owned fully managed and dedicated devices. The diff shows removal from the article only; it does not establish a retirement, launch, or replacement. Do not plan around the old notice and verify currently supported remote actions.

keyChanges.title: MAM guidance foregrounds six RBAC permissions and Company Portal installation
keyChanges.detail: The Migrate To Application Management guide groups the required Managed apps permissions—Assign, Create, Delete, Read, Update, and Wipe—and identifies the built-in Application Manager role as sufficient. This is a documentation clarification, not evidence that permission semantics changed.

2026-05-05.headline: In-development Strict Tunnel Mode will block Android traffic outside Microsoft Tunnel
2026-05-05.overview: The substantive story is a planned Microsoft Tunnel traffic-enforcement mode for Android, alongside updated Recovery Lock rollout timing. Most other notable edits are documentation clarifications covering current admin-center paths, RBAC terminology, Platform SSO prerequisites, and Endpoint analytics navigation; the supplied evidence does not show a general-availability launch or changed remote-action semantics.

For Recovery Lock, plan tenant checks and testing against the mid-May 2026 availability expectation instead of the former late-April target. Update runbooks and bookmarks for the clarified paths and role names, while retaining existing remote-action permissions where the documentation explicitly says semantics did not change.

keyChanges.title: Recovery Lock guidance now targets mid-May rather than late April
keyChanges.detail: The macOS settings catalog guidance now says Recovery Lock is gradually rolling out and that full availability is expected by mid-May 2026, replacing the previous late-April expectation. The diff changes rollout timing guidance, not the setting’s documented behavior.

keyChanges.title: Platform SSO guidance clarifies the single-policy setup sequence
keyChanges.detail: The macOS scenario guide says admins must configure Platform SSO first, create a Platform SSO settings catalog policy, and add scenario settings to that existing policy because only one SSO policy can be assigned to a group. keyChanges.title: Cleanup Rules documentation now names Intune Administrator
keyChanges.detail: The procedure now lists Intune Administrator and a custom role instead of Intune Service Administrator and a custom role. keyChanges.detail: The Configure page changes Reports > Analytics > Endpoint analytics to Reports, then under Analytics, Endpoint analytics, and changes Devices > Configuration profiles to Devices > Configuration. Direct links to those locations were added. This is an admin-center navigation clarification, with no evidence of a feature or permission change.

2026-05-06.headline: Controlled Configuration preview makes Windows Defender antivirus policy authoritative
2026-05-06.overview: The substantive product news is concentrated in three In Development entries: Controlled Configuration is coming to public preview for Windows Defender antivirus settings; Android Enterprise MTD apps will gain an enhanced-permissions path; and Windows devices will proactively request compliance reevaluation after important local state changes. The remaining updates are chiefly documentation cleanup, including navigation and wording edits. Two legacy fundamentals pages were removed, but the supplied evidence supports documentation retirement rather than a product retirement.
2026-05-06.adminImpact: Treat the three capability updates as in-development announcements, not general availability. For a Controlled Configuration preview evaluation, inventory Group Policy, Configuration Manager, and local antivirus controls because enabled CC settings override them. Scope the enhanced MTD-permission planning to Android Enterprise COPE and fully managed devices. Treat the Remote Help prerequisite edit as a documentation correction unless separate product evidence confirms a behavior change.

keyChanges.title: Controlled Configuration will centralize Windows Defender antivirus authority
keyChanges.detail: The Intune In Development page says Controlled Configuration (CC) is coming to public preview. When enabled, Defender antivirus settings delivered by Intune or Microsoft Defender for Endpoint security settings management override Group Policy, Configuration Manager, local changes, and scripts. keyChanges.title: Android Enterprise MTD apps will receive enhanced security permissions

keyChanges.title: Windows compliance evaluation will react to important local state changes

This is presented as an In Development capability, not a general-availability announcement.

keyChanges.title: Remote Help Unattended documentation now lists dedicated devices only

2026-05-07.headline: Apple 26.4 deprecates Intune’s legacy Apple Intelligence restrictions for DDM
2026-05-07.overview: The day’s meaningful Intune updates are mostly operational guidance rather than launches: Apple’s 26.4 deprecation path for Intelligence controls, an explicit compliance discovery-script output limit, and a higher documented unlicensed-admin group ceiling. keyChanges.title: Compliance discovery scripts have a documented 2,048-character output limit

keyChanges.title: Unlicensed-admin group capacity is documented as 1,000
keyChanges.detail: The Unlicensed Admins guidance changes the per-security-group figure from 350 to 1000 unlicensed admins. If more than 1000 administrators are needed for a role assignment, the guidance says to use multiple security groups. Nested-group members remain excluded, and access changes can still take up to 48 hours. This is a documented capacity and eligibility update.

keyChanges.title: Apple Wi-Fi guidance clarifies certificate choices by deployment channel
keyChanges.detail: The Apple Wi-Fi reference now says certificate profiles must align with the selected deployment channel. When the user channel is selected, certificate options are limited to user certificate profiles; the reference also includes a corresponding device-channel limitation. The edit clarifies SCEP and PKCS certificate selection rather than announcing a new Wi-Fi profile capability.

2026-05-08.headline: Android Strict Tunnel Mode and MTD permissions get sharper Intune guidance
2026-05-08.overview: The 8 May feed was documentation-only: all 41 supplied changes updated existing Intune pages, with no new or removed items and no Message Center notices. The consequential edits add explicit guidance for Android threat-defense permissions and Microsoft Tunnel enforcement, while compliance pages sharpen scheduling and platform-version boundaries. The evidence does not classify these updates as previews, general-availability releases, retirements, or confirmed service-behavior changes; much of the remaining work is heading, link, wording, and procedure cleanup.
2026-05-08.adminImpact: Prioritize Android reviews around Android Management API enrollment, Always-on VPN, MTD app targeting, and the one-partner-per-tenant constraint. For compliance, check the revised iOS 17.0 wording and noncompliance schedule values before changing policies; use Microsoft Graph for non-0.25-day increments. Linux compliance references also now list RHEL 9 and 10 rather than RHEL 8, but the documentation alone does not establish a support retirement or tenant-wide migration requirement.

keyChanges.title: MTD connector guidance documents a one-partner Android role
keyChanges.detail: The updated Intune Mobile Threat Defense connector page documents an optional **Mobile Threat Defense role** toggle for Android Enterprise corporate-owned fully managed and corporate-owned work profile devices. It grants the selected partner enhanced permissions: preventing app suspension and hibernation, exempting the app from power restrictions, and disabling user controls such as clearing app data or force-stopping the app. Only one partner can hold the role per tenant; the connector must be configured, the MTD⁣

keyChanges.title: Microsoft Tunnel guidance defines Strict Tunnel Mode’s Android prerequisites
keyChanges.detail: The Microsoft Tunnel VPN profile guidance says Android Strict Tunnel Mode is available when the connection type is Microsoft Tunnel and Always-on VPN is enabled. It forces all traffic through the tunnel and blocks traffic if the VPN drops until reconnection; an app exclusion list can bypass the tunnel. The listed scope includes Android Enterprise corporate-owned fully managed, corporate-owned work profile, and personally-owned work profile devices, with Android Management API enrollment required; legacy EMM APIxE3

keyChanges.title: MAM Tunnel separates Edge-only blocking from enrolled-device blocking
keyChanges.detail: For unenrolled MAM Tunnel devices, the `StrictTunnelMode` Microsoft Edge app-configuration key blocks Edge internet traffic when the MAM Tunnel connection is unavailable. For enrolled devices, Strict Tunnel Mode is configured at the device level in the Microsoft Tunnel VPN profile and applies to all network traffic, not just Edge. Administrators should choose the configuration path based on enrollment state; this is a clarified security procedure, not a stated rollout.

keyChanges.title: Noncompliance schedules use documented 0.25-day admin-center increments
keyChanges.detail: The revised Intune compliance-action guidance says **Schedule (days after noncompliance)** accepts whole numbers and decimal values in 0.25 increments in the admin center: `0.25` equals 6 hours and `0.5` equals 12 hours. Other decimal values, such as `0.33` for 8 hours, must be configured through Microsoft Graph. This clarifies the UI/API procedure rather than announcing a new action.

keyChanges.title: iOS/iPadOS compliance guidance now uses an iOS 17.0 floor
keyChanges.detail: The iOS/iPadOS compliance settings reference changes repeated labels from **iOS 8.0 and later** to **iOS 17.0 and later**. The supplied diff does not establish whether enforcement or underlying service support changed, so administrators should validate the impact on older devices before treating the wording as a retirement or changing policy scope.

2026-05-11.headline: Windows Autopilot automatic Cloud PC provisioning reaches general availability
2026-05-11.overview: The period’s main rollout is general availability for Windows Autopilot device preparation in automatic mode for Windows 365 Enterprise, Windows 365 Frontline dedicated and shared, and Windows 365 Cloud Apps. Policies can provision apps, scripts, and configurations when a Cloud PC is created; Windows 365 Reserve remains in public preview. Other notable updates document deployment-log retention, a Configuration Manager rollup caveat, and Intune compliance and Android app-reporting guidance.
2026-05-11.adminImpact: Add device-preparation policies to applicable Cloud PC provisioning policies and monitor deployment reports. Preserve any Autopilot deployment history needed for auditing because newer records are automatically removed after 28 days, and manually remove older records when appropriate. Before installing the Configuration Manager 2509 rollup, check for the two individually installed hotfixes it can overwrite. Use Clear for the strictest mobile threat-defense compliance threshold, and verify Android Enterprise LOB app state on devices rather than relying solely on potentially inaccurate admin-center status.

keyChanges.title: Automatic-mode device preparation is generally available for Windows 365 Cloud PCs
keyChanges.detail: Windows Autopilot device preparation policies can now be included in Cloud PC provisioning policies for Windows 365 Enterprise, Windows 365 Frontline dedicated and shared, and Windows 365 Cloud Apps. Policies apply when a Cloud PC is created and deliver apps, scripts, and configurations before user sign-in. Windows 365 Reserve remains in public preview.

keyChanges.title: Autopilot deployment records are automatically cleaned up after 28 days
keyChanges.detail: The reporting guidance specifies that deployment records created after automatic cleanup was introduced are removed every 28 days. Older Windows 365 records are not covered by automatic cleanup and require one-time manual removal; administrators should preserve any history they still need before cleanup.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager 2509 rollup documents two fixes it can overwrite
keyChanges.detail: The rollup’s known-issues section says KB 36419072, the offline feedback update, and KB 36495448, the co-management and third-party update scan source fix, are not included. Installing the rollup overwrites changes from either fix if it was previously installed individually; both are planned for a future rollup.

keyChanges.title: Clear replaces Secured as the strictest mobile threat-defense threshold
keyChanges.detail: The Intune compliance-policy guidance now labels the most secure MTD threat level as Clear rather than Secured. Clear means the device cannot have any threats present; any detected threat makes the device noncompliant. This is a terminology correction in the guidance, not evidence of changed enforcement behavior.

keyChanges.title: Android Enterprise LOB app status reports may misstate conflicts
keyChanges.detail: Directly deployed Android Enterprise line-of-business apps still install correctly, but the Intune admin center can show a lower app version as Installed instead of In-Conflict, show a matching Managed Google Play app as Waiting for install or omit it, and report mixed Install and Uninstall intents inconsistently. Verify the app on the device rather than treating these status displays as installation failures.

2026-05-12.headline: Agentic identity and device-based Conditional Access guidance sharpen Intune setup requirements
2026-05-12.overview: This was primarily a documentation-maintenance day, with one substantive new how-to and one retired page. The strongest administrator-facing changes are the new device-based Conditional Access procedure, revised Vulnerability Remediation Agent identity guidance, and explicit custom-compliance script prerequisites. The agent remains documented as limited public preview for selected customers and public-cloud-only; the update is not a general-availability announcement. Most other edits are terminology, formatting, screenshot, or metadata corrections.
2026-05-12.adminImpact: Review the Vulnerability Remediation Agent identity and permissions model before onboarding or operating it; the guidance adds a Test run and notes that authentication expires after 90 consecutive days without a run. For device-based Conditional Access, verify Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2 licensing, the required Entra role, and existing Intune compliance policies. For custom compliance scripts, confirm authors have the default scope tag and return compressed single-line JSON. Treat the removed app-based page as a documentation retirement and update bookmarks to the current guidance; the supplied evidence does not indicate that the capability itself was retired.

keyChanges.title: Device-based Conditional Access gets a dedicated setup procedure
keyChanges.detail: A new Intune how-to documents a two-phase process: configure compliance policies in Intune, report compliance to Microsoft Entra ID, and then create the Conditional Access policy in Entra through the Intune admin center. It specifies a Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2 license, a Security Administrator or Conditional Access Administrator role, and compliance policies as prerequisites. This is a new guidance page, not evidence of a new Conditional Access capability launch.

keyChanges.title: Vulnerability Remediation Agent guidance adds agentic-identity operations
keyChanges.detail: The revised operations guidance says the agent runs under an agentic identity rather than the Intune administrator account used for setup. It adds identity management, including creating a new agent identity, and a Test run to verify delegated permissions before execution. It also states that authentication expires after 90 consecutive days without a run until the identity is renewed.

keyChanges.title: Custom compliance scripts now spell out JSON and scope-tag prerequisites
keyChanges.detail: The Create Custom Script guidance now shows `return $hash | ConvertTo-Json -Compress` as the script’s last line so output is compressed into one line. It explicitly says the upload workflow does not support scope tags and that authors must have the default scope tag to create, edit, or view custom compliance discovery scripts. This is a documentation clarification with direct authoring and delegation impact, not evidence of a script-engine change.

keyChanges.title: Compliance-policy example clarifies highest-severity device status
keyChanges.detail: The Create Policy example now states that when assigned policies have Unknown severity 1, Compliant severity 3, and InGracePeriod severity 4, the device receives the InGracePeriod status. The change clarifies how to interpret the example’s device-level result; it does not indicate that the compliance evaluation behavior changed.

keyChanges.title: Older app-based Conditional Access how-to is retired from Learn
keyChanges.detail: The page identified as Create App Based Policy was removed, including its step-by-step procedure for configuring app-based Conditional Access. This is a documentation-page retirement only; the supplied evidence does not show that app-based Conditional Access itself was retired.

2026-05-13.headline: Configuration Manager adds an untrusted-domain management point deployment example
2026-05-13.overview: The new Configuration Manager article provides a step-by-step proof-of-concept for installing a management point in an untrusted Active Directory domain. In Intune, macOS Platform SSO guidance now specifies the exact Company Portal bundle ID and changes the documented Account Name token. The Multi Admin Approval page adds explicit second-administrator requirements for access-policy changes, while Configuration Manager guidance changes the stated ODBC prerequisite threshold from 18.4.4.1 to 18.4.1.1. The remaining supplied edits are largely link, wording, metadata, or formatting maintenance, making this a guidance-heavy period rather than a feature-release day.
2026-05-13.adminImpact: For macOS ADE and Platform SSO, compare existing profiles with the documented values `com.microsoft.CompanyPortalMac` and `com.apple.PlatformSSO.AccountShortName`. Update access-policy workflows to account for second-administrator approval. Configuration Manager administrators should use the untrusted-domain article as a proof-of-concept reference, observe its primary-site-only limitation, and verify the installed ODBC redistributable against the revised version text. These actions respond to changed guidance; the evidence does not establish a new Intune feature rollout.

keyChanges.title: New Configuration Manager example covers untrusted-domain management point installation
keyChanges.detail: A new step-by-step example shows how to install a Configuration Manager management point on a server in an Active Directory domain with no trust to the site-server domain. The article explicitly limits the scenario to a site system connected to a primary site; secondary sites still require a two-way domain trust. It is presented as a proof-of-concept reference, not as evidence of a newly launched deployment mode.

keyChanges.title: macOS ADE guidance specifies only the Company Portal bundle ID
keyChanges.detail: The Automated Device Enrollment procedure now says the Company Portal line-of-business app's App bundle ID list must contain only `com.microsoft.CompanyPortalMac`; administrators should remove unrelated bundle IDs. This is a configuration-procedure clarification, not a documented change to ADE or Platform SSO availability.

keyChanges.title: The documented Platform SSO Account Name token changes
keyChanges.detail: For **Token To User Mapping** > **Account Name**, the documented value changes from `preferred_username` to `com.apple.PlatformSSO.AccountShortName`. The accompanying explanation still identifies the Microsoft Entra `preferred_username` attribute as the source for the macOS account name, so administrators implementing this mapping should compare their profiles with the revised procedure.

keyChanges.title: Access-policy changes are documented as requiring second-administrator approval
keyChanges.detail: The Multi Admin Approval guidance states that changes to access policies require a second administrator's approval. It also says the automatically protected resource type isn't available as a selectable profile type when creating an access policy. This is security and workflow guidance rather than a new selectable policy type.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager guidance lowers the stated ODBC prerequisite threshold
keyChanges.detail: The Configuration Manager prerequisite text now says an upgrade is stalled when the ODBC redistributable version is lower than `18.4.1.1`, replacing the previous documented threshold of `18.4.4.1`. The evidence establishes a documentation requirement change, so administrators should verify the installed version against the revised text before an upgrade.

2026-05-14.headline: Autopilot automatic mode drops preview labels as Windows 365 guidance shifts to Flex
2026-05-14.overview: Windows Autopilot device preparation in automatic mode for Windows 365 is the period’s consequential change: the overview removes “(preview)” from titles and headings and deletes the note “This feature is in public preview.” The six-step tutorial also removes preview qualifiers from its procedure labels. The supplied evidence shows a documentation status change, not an explicit general-availability announcement. The same guidance replaces Windows 365 Frontline with Windows 365 Flex in the automatic-mode scenarios. Other meaningful Intune edits clarify Conditional Access targets, add a userless macOS ADE username recommendation, and narrow the documented Apple password-expiration range.
2026-05-14.adminImpact: Update Autopilot runbooks, screenshots, and scenario names, but confirm tenant availability before treating the removed preview wording as general availability; no retirement or explicit availability date is supplied. For Intune, review userless macOS ADE profiles and Apple restriction references: the new username recommendation is `{{serialNumber}}-admin` or `{{serialNumber}}-user`, and procedures relying on Apple expiration values above 730 days need verification. Conditional Access guidance should distinguish the Microsoft Intune application, which targets the admin center and data sources, from Microsoft Intune Enrollment, which targets enrollment. The evidence does not establish a service-behavior change for the Apple range or Conditional Access.

keyChanges.title: Automatic-mode Windows 365 guidance no longer carries preview wording
keyChanges.detail: The Windows Autopilot device preparation overview removes “(preview)” from the title, description, headings, and related process text, and removes the note “This feature is in public preview.” This establishes that the page is no longer labeled preview; it does not, by itself, prove general availability.

keyChanges.title: Windows 365 scenario tables replace Frontline with Flex
keyChanges.detail: The automatic-mode scenario matrix now lists Windows 365 Flex in shared and dedicated modes where it previously listed Windows 365 Frontline; Windows 365 Enterprise and Windows 365 Cloud Apps remain in the row. This is a terminology and guidance-scope edit, not evidence of a separate capability launch.

keyChanges.title: Conditional Access guidance separates Intune admin and enrollment targets
keyChanges.detail: The article now foregrounds two Microsoft Entra Conditional Access applications: Microsoft Intune for access to the Microsoft Intune admin center and data sources, and Microsoft Intune Enrollment for the enrollment workflow. This is a documentation organization and clarification change; the diff does not show a new Conditional Access control.

keyChanges.title: Userless macOS ADE gets a serial-number-based admin username recommendation
keyChanges.detail: For macOS ADE enrollment policies without user device affinity, the setup note recommends setting Admin account username to `{{serialNumber}}-admin` or `{{serialNumber}}-user`, tying the value to the unique identifier of userless ADE devices. Review the affected enrollment profiles; the edit is a recommendation in the setup guidance.

keyChanges.title: Apple password-expiration guidance caps the documented range at 730 days
keyChanges.detail: The Apple device-restrictions reference changes Password expiration (days) from 1–65535 to 1–730 and reiterates that expiry prompts users to create a new password, while blank or Not configured leaves the setting unchanged. This is a documentation correction or limitation; the supplied diff does not establish that enforcement changed.

2026-05-15.headline: Android COBO/COPE Defender setup prerequisites and macOS ADE identifiers clarified
2026-05-15.overview: All 18 entries were updates—17 for Intune and one for Configuration Manager—with no supplied announcement of a new preview, general-availability feature, retirement, or tenant-side behavior change. The substantive work is documentation clarification: Mobile Threat Defense connector scope and prerequisites, macOS ADE account naming and Platform SSO token mapping, a forthcoming Settings Catalog note, and updated BIOS Graph API references. Related pages also change headings and anchors from “Microsoft Defender for Endpoint” to “Defender for Endpoint,” which is ordinary terminology and link maintenance.
2026-05-15.adminImpact: Update administrator runbooks and deep links where needed rather than treating these edits as a product rollout. For the Defender connector, the automatic-launch option is documented as Microsoft Defender for Endpoint-only, limited to Android Enterprise COBO and COPE devices, and dependent on the Grant MTD role permissions toggle. For userless macOS ADE, review the serial-based administrator username recommendation and the Platform SSO Account Name mapping. BIOS procedures should use hardwarePasswordDetails references instead of hardwarePasswordInfo. The Create First User During Setup note says the Settings Catalog setting will be available soon; it does not establish current availability or a release date.

keyChanges.title: Defender MTD connector scope and launch dependency clarified
keyChanges.detail: The Enable Connector guidance now identifies “Automatically launch Microsoft Defender for Endpoint during setup on Android COBO and COPE devices” as a Microsoft Defender for Endpoint-only option for Android Enterprise corporate-owned fully managed and corporate-owned work profile devices. It also explicitly requires the Grant MTD role permissions toggle to be enabled.

keyChanges.title: Serial-based administrator usernames recommended for userless macOS ADE
keyChanges.detail: For macOS ADE enrollment policies without user device affinity, the guidance now recommends setting Admin account username to `{{serialNumber}}-admin` or `{{serialNumber}}-user`, explaining that the device serial number helps provide a unique identifier for each userless ADE device.

keyChanges.title: Platform SSO Account Name mapping lists an additional token
keyChanges.detail: The macOS Platform SSO table changes Token To User Mapping > Account Name from `preferred_username` alone to `preferred_username` or `com.apple.PlatformSSO.AccountShortName`. This is a documentation clarification for administrators configuring the mapping.

keyChanges.title: Create First User During Setup is marked as coming soon
keyChanges.detail: The Platform SSO enrollment article adds a note that the Enable Create First User During Setup setting will be available soon in Settings Catalog. The update gives no release date and does not say the setting is currently available.

keyChanges.title: BIOS password procedures now reference hardwarePasswordDetails
keyChanges.detail: Windows BIOS configuration guidance replaces Microsoft Graph `hardwarePasswordInfo` references, links, and endpoints with `hardwarePasswordDetails`, including both the device-specific and collection API examples. Administrators maintaining Graph scripts or runbooks based on this page should update those references.

2026-05-18.headline: Certificate Connector 6.2510.3.3007 requires updating as Apple enrollment grouping guidance expands
2026-05-18.overview: 18 May was entirely documentation-led: all 100 recorded items were updates, with no new or removed entries and no message-center announcements. The most consequential guidance covers a Certificate Connector security-and-maintenance release, expanded documented scope for enrollment-time grouping across Apple automated device enrollment, and a staged macOS Platform SSO setting rollout. No supplied item establishes a new preview, general-availability announcement, retirement, or broader product behavior change. Many other edits are mechanical, including Configuration Manager and Windows Autopilot metadata changes, Defender link and terminology updates, and cloud-native endpoint tutorial renaming.
2026-05-18.adminImpact: Prioritize updating the Intune Certificate Connector through the automatic or manual process and review the recommendation to use BitLocker or equivalent encryption on its installation drive. For Apple enrollment-time grouping, verify the authentication method, use a static Microsoft Entra security group, assign the required custom-RBAC permission, and remember that the Device group tab is documented only for new ADE policies. Check tenant availability of the macOS Platform SSO setting before depending on it, and update runbooks to use the Omnissa Workspace ONE UEM label. Treat the EDR link moves and Defender terminology changes as documentation maintenance rather than evidence of tenant behavior changes.

keyChanges.title: Certificate Connector 6.2510.3.3007 records security fixes and an update requirement
keyChanges.detail: The Intune Certificate Connector history records version 6.2510.3.3007 with bug fixes and security improvements. It also says the connector must be updated automatically or manually to help ensure uninterrupted certificate issuance and management. This is release and maintenance guidance, not a stated GA or retirement event.

keyChanges.detail: The updated Intune guidance now lists iOS/iPadOS and macOS automated device enrollment for enrollment-time grouping. For iOS/iPadOS, it specifies Setup Assistant with modern authentication and Company Portal for enrollment with user affinity, plus Microsoft Entra shared mode and shared iPad without user affinity. For macOS, it lists Setup Assistant with modern authentication for user affinity and enrollment without user affinity. keyChanges.detail: The macOS ADE procedure documents an optional Device group tab for selecting a Microsoft Entra security group for enrollment-time grouping. The group maps directly to the enrollment policy and can be edited after policy creation, but the tab is available only in new enrollment policies, not existing enrollment profiles. keyChanges.title: macOS Platform SSO first-user creation setting has staged May timing
keyChanges.detail: The Platform SSO guidance says **Enable Create First User During Setup** is rolling out slowly and should be available by the end of May 2026. keyChanges.title: Workspace ONE compliance partner selection now uses the Omnissa name
keyChanges.detail: For iOS/iPadOS and Android compliance partners, the documented selection changes from **VMware Workspace ONE mobile compliance** to **Omnissa Workspace ONE UEM**. The diff establishes a selector-label and terminology change, but does not indicate changed compliance behavior or an impact to existing configurations.

2026-05-19.headline: Intune Multi Admin Approval guidance expands to app-authenticated Graph mutations
2026-05-19.overview: 19 May’s consequential items center on control-plane security and certificate lifecycle. Intune’s new Multi Admin Approval how-to covers app-authenticated Graph mutations for workloads with configured access policies; Security Copilot in Intune now documents automatic role inheritance from Intune RBAC; and a new Cloud PKI article lays out staged CA renewal. Assignment-filter recommendations and compliance-report warnings are guidance clarifications, not evidence of a new launch, preview, general-availability change, retirement, or compliance-enforcement change. The remaining sampled updates are mainly metadata, link, formatting, or wording maintenance.
2026-05-19.adminImpact: Audit service principals, scripts, and third-party applications that modify MAA-protected resources; handle approval headers and the documented HTTP 403 response, and maintain a separate interactive approver because MAA is opt-in. Review inherited Security Copilot owner and contributor access, removing Intune role groups from Security Copilot contributor if the defaults are too broad. For Cloud PKI, verify the required permissions and schedule staged renewal before certificate issuance is interrupted. Migrate only Intune-only, property-based dynamic groups to assignment filters; retain dynamic groups for cross-workload, Autopilot, or user scenarios. Treat device-reported compliance values as untrusted context and verify links or files before interacting.

keyChanges.title: Multi Admin Approval guidance covers app-authenticated Graph writes
keyChanges.detail: The new Intune how-to says MAA intercepts application-authenticated Microsoft Graph calls when an access policy protects the target. Affected resources include compliance policies, configuration policies, device actions, RBAC, scripts, and Tenant Configuration. Only modifying POST, PATCH, PUT, and DELETE operations are affected; calls without required approval headers return HTTP 403, while GET requests are unaffected. keyChanges.title: Copilot in Intune inherits access from Intune RBAC by default
keyChanges.detail: When Intune is enabled as a Security Copilot data source, the Microsoft Entra ID Intune Administrator role automatically inherits Security Copilot owner access. All other built-in and custom Intune RBAC roles automatically inherit Security Copilot contributor access. This replaces the previously documented need for a separate Security Copilot or Microsoft Entra role assignment. Existing Intune RBAC permissions and scope tags still limit available data and actions.

keyChanges.detail: A new Cloud PKI how-to says renewal creates a new CA certificate and always generates a new public/private key pair; certificates and CRLs from earlier CA versions remain available. 2026-05-20.headline: Endpoint Privilege Management reports now require explicit View Reports permission
2026-05-20.overview: The period’s most consequential change is a documented EPM reporting authorization boundary: Device configurations > Read no longer suffices, and report access requires the explicit View Reports permission. Configuration Manager also gained a 2509 rollup with fixes affecting co-managed compliance and deployment, while version 2603 is marked globally available. Intune’s Managed Home Screen guidance added precise authentication-time app-silencing settings. Remaining edits were largely formatting, catalog, link, and terminology maintenance.

Ensure custom roles include Endpoint Privilege Management Policy Authoring > View Reports; callers without it receive HTTP 403 responses. Configuration Manager 2509 administrators should evaluate KB37864969 and apply it before October 2026 where the co-managed Software Center compliance workload is relevant. Administrators tracking Configuration Manager 2603 can treat it as globally available for installation as of May 27, 2026. Managed Home Screen configuration authors should review the new setting’s false default and JSON-based app exclusion list.

keyChanges.title: EPM reporting access now has an explicit role permission
keyChanges.detail: The updated EPM reporting guidance requires Endpoint Privilege Management Policy Authoring > View Reports, also called EpmPolicy.ViewReports, for reports in the Intune admin center and Microsoft Graph. 2026-05-21.headline: Vulnerability Remediation Agent guidance shifts to readiness checks and identity recreation
2026-05-21.overview: The strongest operationally relevant update concerns the Security Copilot Vulnerability Remediation Agent: revised guidance replaces Test run with Run Readiness Check, says runs remain disabled until permissions are delegated and the check succeeds, and removes the documented identity-replacement path. Other substantive updates clarify Microsoft Tunnel for Mobile Application Management and Microsoft Cloud PKI prerequisites, add a new Intune license-assignment procedure, and record Configuration Manager support for SQL Server 2022 compatibility level 160 in version 2603. Much of the remaining supplied material is ordinary link, terminology, layout, or screenshot maintenance. The evidence does not establish a new Intune feature launch, general availability milestone, retirement, or tenant-wide behavior change.
2026-05-21.adminImpact: Prioritize the revised Vulnerability Remediation Agent permission and identity procedures. Use the updated Tunnel for MAM and Cloud PKI prerequisites when checking licensing, supported platforms, SCEP, certificate-authority permissions, and scope tags. The new license-assignment article provides a concrete Microsoft 365 admin center procedure, while Configuration Manager administrators in co-managed environments should consult the updated SQL support matrix before planning compatibility-level changes.

This is a documented operational limitation, not evidence of a newly announced agent feature.

keyChanges.title: Tunnel for MAM prerequisites now emphasize platforms and additional licensing
keyChanges.detail: The Microsoft Tunnel for Mobile Application Management prerequisite section now lists Android Enterprise and iOS/iPadOS and points to additional licensing guidance. The diff establishes a documentation rewrite, but not that platform support was expanded, narrowed, or otherwise changed.

keyChanges.title: Cloud PKI guidance spells out SCEP platforms and CA permissions
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft Cloud PKI documentation now explicitly lists additional licensing, Intune-enrolled Android, iOS/iPadOS, macOS, and Windows devices, and support for the Intune device-configuration SCEP certificate profile. It also documents custom-role permissions for Read CAs, Create certificate authorities, and Revoke issued leaf certificates—the last requiring Read CA—and says scope tags can be assigned to root and issuing CAs. This is a prerequisite and delegated-administration clarification.

keyChanges.title: A new Intune article documents user-license assignment before enrollment
keyChanges.detail: The new Assign Microsoft Intune licenses how-to says every user must have a user license before enrolling devices, and that users receiving Intune app protection policies without enrolling also require an Intune license. It provides the Microsoft 365 admin center path Users > Active users > unlicensed user > Licenses and apps > Intune > Save changes, plus School Data Sync guidance for Intune for Education and the requirement to also assign Intune A Direct.

2026-05-22.headline: Pricing and Apple Business references shift across Intune licensing and enrollment guidance
2026-05-22.overview: This was a documentation-maintenance day rather than a feature rollout. Three pages replaced Microsoft Intune pricing URLs with aka.ms/MicrosoftIntunePricing, the Automated iOS tutorial changed its Apple Business support link, and the Defender for Endpoint Web protection page only updated its metadata date from 08/22/2024 to 05/22/2026. No supplied diff shows a new capability, retirement, availability change, security recommendation, or product behavior change.
2026-05-22.adminImpact: No tenant configuration, enrollment workflow, licensing entitlement, or Defender policy change is evidenced. Administrators should use the updated pricing and Apple Business links when following the affected guidance; no broader administrative action is supported by these diffs.

keyChanges.title: Licensing guidance now uses the aka.ms pricing URL
keyChanges.detail: The Intune Licensing page replaces the microsoft.com/security/business/microsoft-intune-pricing URL with aka.ms/MicrosoftIntunePricing in both the pricing link and the statement about which licenses include Intune. The licensing requirement wording itself is unchanged.

keyChanges.title: Advanced Capabilities pricing references use the same redirect
keyChanges.detail: Advanced Capabilities guidance now directs readers to aka.ms/MicrosoftIntunePricing for plan contents, current pricing, and purchasing information. Its statement that advanced capabilities are available through Intune Plan 2, the Intune Suite, and select Microsoft 365 bundles is unchanged.

keyChanges.title: Cloud PKI’s Intune Suite trial link moves to aka.ms
keyChanges.detail: The Cloud PKI index changes the Intune Suite trial link from the Microsoft pricing URL to aka.ms/MicrosoftIntunePricing. The supplied diff shows a link destination change only.

keyChanges.title: Automated iOS enrollment points to a new Apple Business help page
keyChanges.detail: The tutorial replaces the Apple Business Manager URL for assigning devices with the Apple Business guide at support.apple.com/guide/business/link-to-an-external-device-management-service-axm1c1be359d/1/web/1. The surrounding procedure still instructs administrators to assign devices to the MDM server before uploading the MDM server token.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Endpoint Android Web protection page gets a date-only update
keyChanges.detail: The supplied diff changes only the page metadata date from 08/22/2024 to 05/22/2026; it provides no change to Web protection configuration or behavior.

2026-05-25.headline: DMZ management point guide adds offline .NET Framework 3.5 installation paths
2026-05-25.overview: This was a documentation-only Configuration Manager period rather than an Intune service-feature rollout. The most consequential edit strengthens the untrusted-domain or DMZ management point example with explicit .NET Framework 3.5 prerequisites and offline installation procedures. Other substantive clarification makes the deployment sequence more explicit and lists Datacenter: Azure Edition in the supported Windows Server matrix. The remaining changes are mainly rollup terminology, link, and file-list URL maintenance; no new feature, retirement, or Message Center item is evidenced.
2026-05-25.adminImpact: Administrators following the DMZ management point example should pre-stage .NET Framework 3.5 and, in offline environments, use installation media matching the DMZ-MP server's Windows Server version. The article remains a proof-of-concept reference, so production deployments should follow the separate Active Directory forest communications guidance. These edits support a procedure review, but do not by themselves evidence changed Configuration Manager behavior or a tenant-wide Intune action.

keyChanges.title: .NET Framework 3.5 now has explicit offline installation procedures
keyChanges.detail: The example now states that .NET Framework 3.5 is not installed by default and that its feature payload may be absent from modern Windows Server images. It provides two offline methods: PowerShell with `Install-WindowsFeature Net-Framework-Core -Source D:\sources\sxs` or Server Manager's Add Roles and Features wizard using an alternate `SxS` source path. The media must match the Windows Server version on `DMZ-MP`.

keyChanges.title: DMZ management point deployment steps now separate prerequisites from role installation
keyChanges.detail: The procedure table now has a distinct step to install management point prerequisites on the site system server, including Windows features and SQL connectivity components, before installing the management point role on `DMZ-MP`; verification follows as a separate step. Firewall guidance is also changed to say that network traffic will normally need explicit permission.

keyChanges.title: Supported Windows Server listings now explicitly include Azure Edition
keyChanges.detail: The supported operating systems reference lists Datacenter: Azure Edition alongside the existing Windows Server 2025 editions, starting with Configuration Manager version 2409, and alongside the Windows Server 2022 editions, starting with version 2107. The edit clarifies the support matrix; it does not state a new starting version or announce a product-support change.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager 2509 rollup page adopts sequence-based naming
keyChanges.detail: The second 2509 update rollup page changes its title, description, and heading from “Update rollup (9141.1032)” to “Second update rollup for Microsoft Configuration Manager version 2509.” The supplied diff shows a naming clarification only, not a change to the rollup payload or availability.

2026-05-26.headline: Device-based Conditional Access guidance spells out licensing and RBAC prerequisites
2026-05-26.overview: 26 May’s most consequential Intune changes are in guidance rather than an announced service rollout. A new device-based Conditional Access how-to defines the Microsoft Entra license, administrator roles, and setup sequence; compliance references revise the stated iOS and Linux platform baselines; Cloud PKI guidance adds platform and CA-permission detail; and the Vulnerability Remediation Agent is described as public preview instead of limited public preview. Most other edits standardize requirements layouts, terminology, and links, so they should not be read as tenant-behavior changes without separate product evidence.
2026-05-26.adminImpact: Use the new Conditional Access article as a setup checklist: have Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2, a Security administrator or Conditional Access administrator, and Intune device-compliance policies ready. Treat Vulnerability Remediation Agent as preview, not general availability. Review runbooks and targeting assumptions against the iOS 17.0-and-later and Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10 references, and against Cloud PKI’s enrollment, SCEP, licensing, and RBAC requirements. The supplied diffs do not show automatic changes to existing tenant policies.

keyChanges.title: New how-to defines the device-based Conditional Access setup sequence
keyChanges.detail: The new Intune guide describes two phases: configure Intune compliance policies so they report device status to Microsoft Entra ID, then create the Conditional Access policy. It requires a Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2 license and either the Security administrator or Conditional Access administrator role. The page also confirms that the Conditional Access node in the Intune admin center is the same node used in Microsoft Entra ID. This is a new how-to page, not evidence of a newly launched Conditional Access feature.
keyChanges.product: Intune device compliance and Microsoft Entra Conditional Access

keyChanges.title: Vulnerability Remediation Agent guidance now says public preview
keyChanges.detail: The Security Copilot guidance replaces wording that called the Vulnerability Remediation Agent a limited public preview available only to selected customers with a statement that the feature is in public preview. The update does not claim general availability; administrators should continue to treat the agent as a preview capability and consult the public-preview guidance.

keyChanges.title: iOS/iPadOS compliance reference now lists iOS 17.0 and later
keyChanges.detail: The iOS/iPadOS device-compliance settings reference changes repeated support text from iOS 8.0 and later to iOS 17.0 and later across device health, operating-system, and system-security settings. This is a reference-page change; the supplied diff does not establish that existing tenant enforcement or policy assignments changed.

keyChanges.title: Custom-compliance Linux reference replaces RHEL 8 with RHEL 10
keyChanges.detail: The custom-compliance guidance for managed Linux and Windows devices changes its listed Red Hat Enterprise Linux version from RedHat Enterprise Linux 8 to RedHat Enterprise Linux 10. Administrators using Linux custom JSON and discovery scripts should check their support matrix and policy targeting against the revised reference; the evidence does not show an automatic migration of existing policies.

keyChanges.title: Cloud PKI guidance documents Apple platforms and CA permissions
keyChanges.detail: The Microsoft Cloud PKI overview now describes the service as available through Intune Suite or as a standalone capability, and lists Android, iOS/iPadOS, macOS, and Windows for enrolled devices whose platforms support Intune SCEP certificate profiles. It also documents custom-role permissions for Read CAs, Create certificate authorities, and Revoke issued leaf certificates; revocation additionally requires Read CA, and scope tags can be assigned to CAs. These are updated prerequisite and RBAC details, not an​nved?
keyChanges.product: Microsoft Cloud PKI for Microsoft Intune

2026-05-27.headline: Azure Monitor guidance flags variable timing for Intune’s 24-hour report exports
2026-05-27.overview: This is a documentation-only day, with no new, removed, or Message Center items. The most consequential edit is to Intune’s Azure Monitor integration: Device Compliance Organizational Logs and Intune Devices report data aren’t guaranteed at a particular time of day, can arrive anytime within each 24-hour export period subject to the documented delivery window, and may shift as Microsoft improves the export pipeline. Configuration Manager guidance also gains an explicit Software Update Point upgrade order and a cross-domain Kerberos/DNS prerequisite; the remaining edits are example, terminology, or procedure clarifications rather than evidence of launches, retirements, or changed product behavior.
2026-05-27.adminImpact: Teams consuming the Intune exports should stop scheduling reports, dashboards, or automation around a previously observed completion time and allow for variable timing. Configuration Manager administrators planning SUP upgrades should sequence them from the top-level site downward and apply the same-site ordering rules; for cross-domain management points, verify KDC discovery and resolution of the listed DNS SRV records. Administrators following the manual app-registration procedure should use the updated Application ID URI example as a documentation check, not treat the edit alone as proof of a tenant-wide behavior change.

keyChanges.title: Azure Monitor export timing is explicitly variable
keyChanges.detail: The Integrate Azure Monitor page adds that Device Compliance Organizational Logs and Intune Devices report data can be exported or become available at any time within each 24-hour export period, subject to the documented delivery window. It also warns that observed completion times may change and recommends schedules that tolerate variable timing for reports, dashboards, and automation.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager SUP upgrades get explicit top-down sequencing
keyChanges.detail: The revised guidance says to upgrade software update points from the top-level site downward: older WSUS versions can synchronize from newer versions, but newer versions can’t synchronize from older ones. In sites with multiple SUPs, the site server follows a different order depending on whether it hosts a SUP, and mismatched versions can cause synchronization failure.

keyChanges.title: Cross-domain management point setup adds KDC and DNS checks
keyChanges.detail: The management point deployment example now states that both the site server and management point must locate a Kerberos Key Distribution Center in the other domain. Each server must also resolve DNS SRV records such as `_kerberos._tcp.dc._msdcs.corp.contoso.com` and `_kerberos._tcp.dc._msdcs.branch.fabrikam.com`.

keyChanges.title: ConfigMgr app-registration guidance updates the Application ID URI example
keyChanges.detail: The manually registered app procedure now shows an Application ID URI similar to `https://contoso.onmicrosoft.com/ConfigMgrService`, replacing the earlier `https://ConfigMgrService` example. The diff documents a value-format clarification for the Microsoft Entra app registration; it does not announce a new product requirement.

2026-05-28.headline: Properties Catalog guidance now documents local AI-agent discovery on Windows
2026-05-28.overview: The period was dominated by documentation clarification rather than announced service changes: all 10 records were updates, with no message-center items or explicit GA, preview, retirement, or rollout notice. The strongest changes cover Windows Properties Catalog inventory, advanced-capability trial terms, Apple enrollment-time grouping scope, Azure Monitor export scheduling, and Configuration Manager synchronization status interpretation.
2026-05-28.adminImpact: Most administrators have no immediate tenant change to make based solely on these documentation edits. Review the affected guidance if you manage Windows inventory, advanced-capability trials, Apple automated device enrollment, Azure Monitor exports, or Configuration Manager software-update integrations. Azure Monitor consumers should ensure their solutions tolerate variable export timing; the Apple documentation removals should be verified against current service behavior before being treated as a support retirement.

keyChanges.title: Windows Properties Catalog article adds local AI-agent discovery
keyChanges.detail: The updated Intune article now says administrators can use the properties catalog to discover local AI agents, like OpenClaw, running on managed Windows devices. It also reorganizes the available-properties material under “Available and required properties” and points to the Intune Data Platform Schema. The diff documents this capability but does not establish a separate feature launch or required policy change.

keyChanges.title: Advanced-capability trial limits are now explicit
keyChanges.detail: Intune guidance now specifies a 90-day trial, a maximum of 250 users per tenant, one trial per capability per tenant, and a 30-day grace period before the capability becomes unavailable in the admin center. It also tells administrators to review existing licenses and use trials for capabilities not already included. This clarifies licensing and trial documentation rather than announcing new availability.

keyChanges.title: Apple grouping guidance now documents only tvOS and visionOS
keyChanges.detail: The Setup Time Grouping article now lists automated device enrollment only for tvOS and visionOS. It removes the iOS/iPadOS and macOS authentication-support descriptions, related custom-RBAC permission text, the Device group assignment during enrollment section, and links to the iOS/iPadOS and macOS setup pages. This is a documentation scope change; the supplied evidence does not establish whether underlying service support changed.

keyChanges.title: Azure Monitor guidance rejects fixed export completion times
keyChanges.detail: The Intune integration guidance now says solutions consuming exported Intune data for reports, dashboards, or automation must account for variable export timing and must not rely on a fixed or previously observed completion time. Administrators should review schedules and automation that assume a predictable export finish; the edit does not define a new export SLA.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager WMI guidance adds WSUS status codes
keyChanges.detail: The Sms Supsyncstatus Server WMI Class reference now enumerates Last synchronization state values 6702 through 6708, covering success, failure, synchronization phases, upstream content out of sync, and completion with pending license-terms downloads. The added table improves programmatic interpretation of software-update synchronization state and is a reference clarification, not an announced new status.

2026-05-29.headline: OpenClaw preview baseline details Node.js blocking and collateral-impact warnings
2026-05-29.overview: 29 May was primarily a documentation day, but several changes have concrete administrative relevance. Intune’s security-baseline overview now lists Local AI Agent Baseline - OpenClaw as Preview, Version 1, for May 2026, while its new settings reference describes controls intended to disrupt unauthorized local AI-agent execution paths. A new account-moves article explains regional relocation of Intune data at rest. Other notable edits clarify Platform SSO setup, change Configuration Manager’s evaluation guidance from 180 to 360 days, and remove the older Windows in cloud configuration overview and setup pages as related links move to cloud-native Windows endpoint guidance. The supplied evidence does not establish OpenClaw general availability or retirement of the cloud-native endpoint capability.
2026-05-29.adminImpact: For OpenClaw evaluation, use Properties catalog Local AI Agent inventory to identify candidates first, then test each baseline setting because controls involving WSL and Node.js may block processes beyond OpenClaw; disable settings that have unacceptable impact. For account moves, customer-requested relocations go through Microsoft support, while Microsoft-initiated moves receive advance notice; most data is copied about 24 hours before maintenance while Intune remains operational. Review Platform SSO profiles using the Password authentication method, and update Configuration Manager evaluation runbooks to the 360-day read-only point and Site Maintenance activation path. Use the current cloud-native Windows endpoint overview and tutorial instead of the removed cloud-configuration pages.

keyChanges.title: OpenClaw baseline is listed as Preview version 1
keyChanges.detail: The Intune security-baselines overview adds Local AI Agent Baseline - OpenClaw (Preview), Version 1, with a May 2026 listing. This establishes preview documentation, not general availability or a tenant-wide rollout.

keyChanges.title: New OpenClaw reference warns of runtime and process blocking
keyChanges.detail: The new settings reference says the baseline limits unauthorized local AI agents such as OpenClaw by disrupting common execution paths, including outbound firewall controls for Node.js and controls affecting environments such as Windows Subsystem for Linux. It warns that other processes may also be blocked, so each setting should be reviewed and tested before deployment. The reference also recommends collecting Local AI Agent inventory through Properties catalog first.

keyChanges.title: New account-move guidance defines regional data-at-rest relocation
keyChanges.detail: The new overview defines an Intune account move as a managed migration of customer data at rest between geographic datacenter regions, while preserving policies, profiles, device enrollments, app management state, and service configuration. It explicitly distinguishes the process from a tenant-to-tenant migration, and describes support coordination for customer-requested moves and advance notice for Microsoft-initiated moves.

keyChanges.title: Platform SSO guidance drops rollout timing and clarifies authentication scope
keyChanges.detail: The Enable Create First User During Setup guidance now says to configure the setting when using the Password authentication method; with other authentication methods, it isn’t required. The previous note that the setting was rolling out slowly and should be available by the end of May 2026 was removed. This is a documentation clarification, not evidence of changed product behavior.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager evaluation guidance changes the read-only threshold to 360 days
keyChanges.detail: The evaluation-install procedure now says the Configuration Manager console becomes read-only after 360 days, replacing the previous 180-day statement. The guidance still directs administrators to activate from Site Maintenance in Setup and says a full installation can be obtained before or after that period.

2026-06-01.headline: Windows Properties Catalog adds Local AI Agent discovery and OpenClaw controls
2026-06-01.overview: The substantive change this period is updated Windows Properties Catalog guidance for discovering local AI agents, including OpenClaw, and linking that inventory to Device Query and an OpenClaw security baseline in preview. The remaining updates are chiefly documentation maintenance: Recovery Lock’s rollout note was removed, Apple account service-access wording was reformatted, and other pages received date or metadata edits.
2026-06-01.adminImpact: Windows administrators can deploy the Properties Catalog policy and begin collecting data to identify devices with a Local AI Agent, then use Device Query for inventory and the Local AI Agent Baseline - OpenClaw (Preview) to block users from using OpenClaw. Do not treat the Recovery Lock note’s removal as proof of tenant-wide availability; the supplied evidence shows a documentation change, not a product-status confirmation.

keyChanges.title: Local AI Agent inventory is added to Windows Properties Catalog guidance
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance identifies Local AI Agent as a new category for discovering local AI agents such as OpenClaw on Windows devices. After deploying the policy and starting collection, administrators can use Device Query to find affected devices and the Local AI Agent Baseline - OpenClaw (Preview) to block users from using OpenClaw.

keyChanges.title: Recovery Lock rollout warning is removed without proving tenant-wide availability
keyChanges.detail: The macOS Recovery Lock page no longer includes the note that the feature was gradually rolling out and that full availability was expected by mid-May 2026. This edit alone does not establish a change in tenant availability or configuration behavior.

keyChanges.title: Apple account service-access guidance receives a formatting-only cleanup
keyChanges.detail: The page date changed to 1 June 2026 and curly apostrophes were replaced with straight apostrophes throughout. The substantive guidance remains the same: settings are configured in Apple Business or Apple School Manager, Intune supplies a management token, enrollment is still required, and Apple—not Intune—controls per-service availability.

2026-06-02.headline: Multi Admin Approval’s app-auth Graph API article is removed from Learn
2026-06-02.overview: The main story is a documentation change around Multi Admin Approval (MAA): the standalone app-authenticated Microsoft Graph API article was removed, while the core MAA article also drops explicit app-auth enforcement wording and revises approver requirements. Elsewhere, Configuration Manager guidance records a version 2509 planning endpoint for diagnostic-data changes, and Device Query documents a new Local AI Agent entity with no NL2KQL assistance yet.
2026-06-02.adminImpact: Do not infer that MAA enforcement or availability changed solely from the article removal and wording edits; administrators whose automation depends on MAA-protected app-auth Graph calls should confirm the currently supported procedure before changing scripts. Device Query users must account for the explicit Local AI Agent/NL2KQL limitation. Configuration Manager administrators may need to update saved virtualization-support links, while the version 2509 diagnostic note does not specify a tenant configuration action.

keyChanges.title: Standalone MAA app-auth Graph API article removed
keyChanges.detail: The page “Use Multi Admin Approval with the Microsoft Graph API” was removed. Its deleted content covered MAA enforcement for app-only Graph calls to protected resources, HTTP 403 responses when approval headers were absent, affected resource types including policies, device actions, RBAC, scripts, and tenant configuration, plus the required app permissions, access policies, and interactive approver. The removal is a documentation change and does not by itself establish a change in enforcement.

keyChanges.title: Core MAA article removes explicit app-auth enforcement wording
keyChanges.detail: The main article no longer states that MAA intercepts app-authenticated Graph API calls or includes the tip that automation enforcement applies only in tenants with MAA access policies configured. It also presents the approver requirements as items 2 and 3 and says the approver group must be directly assigned to an Intune role as a member group. No product-behavior change is announced in the diff.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager 2509 guidance says diagnostic-collection changes will stop
