keyChanges.detail: The diagnostics guidance now says that, with version 2509, no further changes or updates are planned for diagnostic and usage data collection. This is a forward-looking documentation note; it does not say that current collection is disabled.

keyChanges.title: Device Query adds Local AI Agent with an NL2KQL limitation
keyChanges.detail: Device Query Multiple Devices now lists Local AI Agent as an entity, but explicitly states that NL2KQL assistance for that entity is currently unsupported. Administrators using natural-language query assistance should not expect it to work for Local AI Agent.

keyChanges.title: Virtualization validation guidance gets a new destination URL
keyChanges.detail: The Configuration Manager virtualization-environment article changes the Server Virtualization Validation Program link from windowsservercatalog.com/svvp.aspx to windowsservercatalog.com/svvp/program-home. The diff changes only the link destination and does not announce a change to virtualization support.

2026-06-03.headline: Configuration Manager CMG shifts VMSS off deprecated Windows Server 2022 images
2026-06-03.overview: The period’s main operational change is Configuration Manager KB37942646 for cloud management gateway VMSS deployments. It moves CMG from the legacy Windows Server 2022 Azure Marketplace offer `windowsserver`, which includes end-of-life .NET 6, to `windowsserver2022`; the legacy image will lose support and OS image-refresh updates, and new deployments or reimaging using it will fail when enforcement begins in early 2027. The remaining Intune changes are chiefly documentation scope, security guidance, and rollout-status updates rather than confirmed feature launches.
2026-06-03.adminImpact: CMG administrators should identify deployments using the legacy VMSS image and install the applicable update: it is available directly for Configuration Manager 2603, while versions 2503 and 2409 require the listed update rollups; the same fix is already included in the second 2509 rollup, so no separate out-of-band hotfix is needed. The update requires neither a computer restart nor a site reset. For Intune, use the revised Apple wired-network prerequisites and consider collecting the recommended Host process property when detecting OpenClaw. The 2605 service update is still rolling out, so tenant availability can vary during the period.

keyChanges.title: CMG VMSS image transition removes the deprecated .NET 6 dependency
keyChanges.detail: Configuration Manager KB37942646 changes CMG VMSS deployments from Azure Marketplace offer `windowsserver` to `windowsserver2022`, which does not include the deprecated .NET 6 packages. The legacy image will no longer be compliant or supported and will not receive new OS patch updates through image refresh; new CMG deployments and reimaging operations that reference it will fail once enforcement begins in early 2027. The update applies to 2603 and 2509, and to 2503 and 2409 with the required rollups.

keyChanges.title: Wired-network guidance now explicitly covers iOS/iPadOS alongside macOS
keyChanges.detail: The Intune page was retitled for Apple devices and now explicitly lists iOS/iPadOS and macOS. It adds prerequisites for the Policy and Profile Manager RBAC role, a wired network device configuration profile, and all enrollment types; for iOS/iPadOS, Network Interface is automatically set to Any Ethernet. This is a documentation-scope and procedure update, not evidence of a newly announced feature launch.

keyChanges.title: OpenClaw collection guidance recommends capturing the Host process property
keyChanges.detail: The Properties Catalog guidance now recommends collecting Host process because OpenClaw can run under different process names, including `node.exe` and `wsl.exe`. The linked Local AI Agent Baseline - OpenClaw is no longer labeled “Preview” in this page, but the supplied change does not establish a general-availability date or a product behavior change.

keyChanges.title: Intune 2605 rollout remains in progress through the end of the week
keyChanges.detail: The Intune service-update guidance now states that the 2605 release is in progress and expected to complete by the end of the week. Monthly updates can expand over several days to a week, while some features may roll out over several weeks, so uneven tenant availability during the rollout is expected. This is release-status clarification, not a new capability announcement.

2026-06-04.headline: Configuration Manager guidance now calls legacy CMG images unsupported as 2027 enforcement approaches
2026-06-04.overview: This was a documentation-heavy day rather than a feature-launch day. The most consequential edit says legacy Configuration Manager CMG images are no longer compliant or supported, while Intune government-cloud guidance clarifies that commercial-to-government moves require device unenrollment and re-enrollment. A related GCC High and DoD service-description page replaces Common Criteria/NIAP wording with STIG lockdown guidance. Remote Help release notes describe reliability improvements, but updated entries give conflicting Windows version numbers. The remaining Intune edits are largely editorial, including Apple wired-network requirement ordering and wording corrections.
2026-06-04.adminImpact: Configuration Manager administrators should inventory CMG and VMSS references to legacy images and plan migration to the `windowsserver2022` offer before early-2027 enforcement; the evidence does not provide a new enforcement date. Government-cloud migration runbooks should include unenrollment and re-enrollment because no built-in commercial-to-government migration path is documented. Security and compliance teams should review the STIG guidance, but should not infer a certification-status change from the removal of a documentation bullet alone. Remote Help administrators should verify the Windows build through another authoritative deployment source before using the updated What's new content as a version gate.

keyChanges.title: Legacy CMG images are described as already noncompliant and unsupported
keyChanges.detail: The revised Configuration Manager hotfix text changes the wording from future to present: legacy images “are no longer compliant or supported” and won’t receive new OS patch updates through image refresh. It retains early 2027 as the point when new CMG deployments and reimaging operations that reference those images fail, and continues to identify the `windowsserver2022` image offer as the replacement. The page also presents availability in Updates and Servicing for version 2603, or versions 2503 and 2409 with KB 伽

keyChanges.title: Government-tenant guidance spells out the required migration procedure
keyChanges.detail: The reorganized Government Service page places the guidance under “Intune commercial and government instances” and “Enroll in government tenant.” It states that resources moving from a commercial tenant to government cloud require devices to unenroll from the current tenant and re-enroll in the new tenant; there is no built-in migration between the services. This clarifies the documented procedure rather than adding an in-place migration capability.

keyChanges.title: GCC High and DoD guidance shifts from certification wording to STIG help
keyChanges.detail: The service-description edit removes the statement that Intune is Common Criteria certified and on the NIAP Product Compliance List, along with the NIAP certification-material link. It adds guidance that administrators can get help locking down their Intune tenants using the Secure Technical Implementation Guide (STIG). The documentation diff alone does not establish that Intune’s certification status changed.

keyChanges.title: Remote Help reliability notes leave the Windows build reference inconsistent
keyChanges.detail: The Week of June 1 entry identifies Remote Help for Windows version 1.0.2510071 and describes general bug fixes and performance improvements to enhance reliability. A separate updated Index entry gives the same description with version 5.2.1037.0, so the supplied What's new content does not provide a consistent build reference.

2026-06-05.headline: CMG guidance names the Windows Server 2022 offer replacing legacy .NET 6 images
2026-06-05.overview: The two Configuration Manager updates document the same Cloud Management Gateway virtual machine scale set image change. The guidance now says CMG deployments transition from legacy Windows Server 2022 Azure Marketplace images using the `windowsserver` offer and end-of-life .NET 6 to the `windowsserver2022` offer without those deprecated packages. This is documentation and terminology clarification, not evidence of a new Intune capability or availability announcement.
2026-06-05.adminImpact: Administrators running CMG deployments with Virtual Machine Scale Sets should review the image-deprecation guidance and check references to the legacy `windowsserver` offer. The supplied update provides no deprecation date, migration procedure, or specific tenant-side configuration action.

keyChanges.title: CMG image guidance documents the new Marketplace offer
keyChanges.detail: The Configuration Manager article now explicitly describes the CMG virtual machine scale set transition to the `windowsserver2022` Windows Server 2022 image offer, replacing legacy `windowsserver` images that include end-of-life .NET 6. Related hotfix notes also standardize the terminology from “VMSS” to “virtual machine scale set.”

2026-06-09.headline: Office baseline reference now lists digitally signed macros outside the default block
2026-06-09.overview: This was a two-item documentation update day with one meaningful Intune setting clarification and one Configuration Manager lifecycle notice. The Ref V2 Office Settings reference changes its documented macro baseline default, while Configuration Manager records a future deprecation path for its Microsoft Connected Cache integration. No release date or Message Center announcement was supplied.
2026-06-09.adminImpact: No immediate tenant-side change is established by the evidence. Intune administrators should compare deployed Office baseline settings with the revised default before changing rollout plans. Configuration Manager administrators using the integrated Microsoft Connected Cache should begin evaluating the standalone version, although no deprecation release or deadline is provided.

keyChanges.title: Ref V2 Office Settings changes the documented macro baseline default
keyChanges.detail: The Intune reference changes the baseline default from “Disable all with notification” to “Disable all except digitally signed macros.” This is a documentation change; the supplied evidence does not establish that an existing tenant policy changed automatically.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager records future deprecation of integrated Microsoft Connected Cache
keyChanges.detail: The updated page says Microsoft Connected Cache integration in Configuration Manager will be deprecated in a future Configuration Manager release. After deprecation, no further feature development or updates will be provided for MCC within Configuration Manager, and customers should begin transitioning to the standalone version.

2026-06-11.headline: Multiple Managed Accounts brings separate app protection to Teams on iOS
2026-06-11.overview: The clearest capability change is the gradual rollout of Intune mobile application management (MAM) Multiple Managed Accounts (MMA): Teams on iOS/iPadOS is currently supported, with protection enforced independently for each managed account. The period also includes a material Cloud PKI documentation change, a required Managed Home Screen policy-path change, a new macOS Wi-Fi control, and SQL Server 2025 support for Configuration Manager 2603.
2026-06-11.adminImpact: Pilot MMA within its stated scope and confirm tenant availability and Teams version 8.10.0 or later. Move Managed Home Screen exit-password configuration to a device configuration profile. Recheck Cloud PKI capacity plans against the newly stated three-CA limit, while treating the supplied evidence as a documentation change rather than proof of changed service enforcement. Use the macOS control only where static-MAC dependencies such as NAC justify the privacy trade-off. Configuration Manager sites on version 2603 can use the supported SQL Server 2025 platforms and compatibility level 160.

keyChanges.title: MAM Multiple Managed Accounts is gradually rolling out for Teams
keyChanges.detail: This new Intune MAM capability lets users add more than one work or school account within a supported app, with app protection policies enforced independently for each account. Current support is Microsoft Teams on iOS/iPadOS version 8.10.0 or later. One account can be MDM+MAM managed while additional accounts are MAM-only, or all accounts can be MAM-only; multiple MDM-managed accounts and apps such as PowerApps are out of scope.

keyChanges.title: Cloud PKI documentation now states a three-CA tenant limit
keyChanges.detail: The Cloud PKI index replaces the previous six-CA wording with a limit of three CAs per Intune tenant. The revised text applies to both licensed Cloud PKI using Azure mHSM keys and trial Cloud PKI, and updates the example CA topologies. This is documentation evidence of a changed stated limit, not confirmation that backend enforcement changed.

keyChanges.title: Managed Home Screen exit-password setup now requires device configuration
keyChanges.detail: The published procedure now says the Managed Home Screen exit lock task mode password can no longer be configured with an app configuration policy. Administrators must create or update a device configuration profile to define the password. The change applies to Android Enterprise corporate-owned fully managed and dedicated devices.

keyChanges.title: macOS 15 Wi-Fi profiles add a MAC-randomization control
keyChanges.detail: The Disable MAC address randomization setting is now available for managed macOS 15 and later devices in Intune Wi-Fi profiles. Disabling randomization can restore functionality that relies on a static MAC address, including network access control; the release notes continue to identify randomized addresses as preferable for privacy.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager 2603 supports SQL Server 2025
keyChanges.detail: SQL Server 2025 RTM is now supported for Configuration Manager central administration, primary, and secondary sites. SQL Server 2025 Express is supported for secondary sites. The documented recommended database compatibility level is 160, and the SQL cumulative update must remain within the SQL Server support lifecycle.

2026-06-12.headline: Configuration Manager 2603 requires management-point internet access for Entra token validation
2026-06-12.overview: The consequential change is a new Configuration Manager 2603 management-point prerequisite: sites using Microsoft Entra authentication for Entra-joined users and devices, typically through a cloud management gateway, must provide internet access for MISE token validation. Supporting pages add the required proxy and endpoint details. The other notable updates change the published SQL Server 2025 support matrix and record a Microsoft Tunnel Gateway image release with package and security updates; they do not introduce a new Intune control-plane capability.
2026-06-12.adminImpact: For affected Configuration Manager 2603 environments, verify management-point outbound access before rollout and configure a system-level WinHTTP proxy where needed—the proxy in site system properties does not apply to MISE validation. Allow the documented Azure authentication endpoints and use CCM_STS_ManagedBase.log to investigate network-related MISE12034 errors. Environments using only on-premises Active Directory authentication without Microsoft Entra integration are not affected. SQL Server 2025 planners should review the revised support row, while the Tunnel update provides image and release metadata rather than a documented configuration change.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager 2603 adds a management-point connectivity requirement
keyChanges.detail: Starting in version 2603, the management point uses Microsoft Identity Service Essentials (MISE) for Microsoft Entra token validation. The server requires internet access when the site supports Microsoft Entra-joined users and devices and clients authenticate with Entra tokens, typically through a CMG. AD-only environments without Entra integration are excluded. Network failures can appear in CCM_STS_ManagedBase.log as a MISE12034 exception with a SocketException, HttpRequestException, or timeout.

keyChanges.title: MISE validation requires a system-level WinHTTP proxy
keyChanges.detail: The proxy configured in Configuration Manager site system properties does not apply to MISE token validation. Administrators must configure the proxy at the management-point server’s system level, for example with `netsh winhttp set proxy <proxyservername>:<portnumber>`; `netsh winhttp show proxy` verifies the setting and `netsh winhttp reset proxy` removes it.

keyChanges.title: Azure authentication endpoints are added to management-point requirements
keyChanges.detail: For Azure public cloud, the documented endpoints are `https://login.microsoftonline.com` and `https://sts.windows.net`. For Azure US Government cloud, they are `https://login.microsoftonline.us` and `https://sts.windows.net`. The access is required for MISE-based Microsoft Entra token validation starting in Configuration Manager 2603.

keyChanges.title: SQL Server 2025 support matrix expands its listed versions
keyChanges.detail: The SQL Server 2025 row now lists 170, 160, 150, 140, 130, 120, and 110, with 170 as the maximum, replacing the previous list of 160, 150, 140, and 130 with 160 as the maximum. This is a published support-matrix change rather than a described new Intune feature.

keyChanges.title: Microsoft Tunnel Gateway records release 20260527.1
keyChanges.detail: The Tunnel Gateway upgrade page adds version 20260527.1, agent and server image SHA-256 digests, and a release note stating: “Package and security updates.” The entry supplies release and image-identification data; it does not describe a new Tunnel capability or setting.

2026-06-15.headline: Remote Help deployment guidance now identifies version 5.2.1037.0
2026-06-15.overview: A single Remote Help documentation update changes the listed most recent version from 5.1.1998.0 to 5.2.1037.0. The evidence does not establish a new availability milestone, mandatory upgrade, or product-behavior change.
2026-06-15.adminImpact: Review the Remote Help deployment guidance and internal version tracking. The supplied evidence supports updating the documented version reference, but not changing tenant configuration or rollout plans without further validation.

keyChanges.title: The documented Remote Help version changed
keyChanges.detail: In the Deploy guidance, the most recent version is now listed as 5.2.1037.0 instead of 5.1.1998.0. This is a documentation-level version update; no upgrade procedure, prerequisite, or enforcement requirement is provided.

2026-06-16.headline: Intune guidance details a fleet-wide security update status dashboard
2026-06-16.overview: Two substantive security and management items lead this period: a new Intune concept article specifies the scope and prerequisites of the Security update status dashboard, while Configuration Manager documents KB38232642 for console-extension import security. Separately, the public-preview single device page gains behavior and navigation improvements. The Cloud PKI edit is mechanical rather than a product change.
2026-06-16.adminImpact: Dashboard users should verify public-cloud tenancy, Organization/Read RBAC, and workload-specific data paths; the article positions the dashboard for posture triage rather than root-cause analysis. Configuration Manager administrators should map KB38232642 to their branch and rollup state: direct availability for version 2603, installation after KB32851084 for version 2503, and inclusion in the second 2509 update rollup. The update requires no restart or site reset. Preview evaluators should validate the changed device actions and navigation. No administrator action follows from the Cloud PKI punctuation corrections.

keyChanges.title: New guidance defines the Security update status dashboard’s cross-workload scope
keyChanges.detail: The new Intune concept article describes a fleet-wide view of security-update currency across Windows client devices, Windows Server devices, and Microsoft 365 Apps. It is intended to identify exposure and prioritize remediation by relative risk, not to perform root-cause analysis. The documented prerequisites include the public cloud and at least Organization/Read permission in Intune RBAC; data sources and requirements vary by workload.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager documents KB38232642 for console-extension import security
keyChanges.detail: The security update enhances protection when importing console extensions and applies to current branch version 2603, plus versions 2509 and 2503 with the required update rollup. It is available directly through Updates and Servicing for 2603; 2503 requires KB32851084; and 2509 receives it through the second update rollup, so no separate out-of-band hotfix is required. Installation requires neither a computer restart nor a site reset.

keyChanges.title: The redesigned single-device page preview adds action and navigation changes
keyChanges.detail: The public-preview page, introduced in the 2604 service release, now temporarily shows passcodes and PINs in Device action status after Reset passcode, Recover passcode, Remote Lock, or Rotate BitLocker Keys. Device actions also work with multi-admin approval policies, supported actions are available for supervised iOS devices, and administrators can enable or disable Lost mode. Tools and reports move to left navigation, with Monitor becoming the default landing tab; other documented changes include removing the​‍‍

keyChanges.title: Cloud PKI renewal guidance receives punctuation-only corrections
keyChanges.detail: The Renew CA page removes a duplicated comma in the certificate-authority permissions sentence and a stray quotation mark from the Halfway to expiration lifecycle description. The supplied diff shows no change to permissions, renewal procedure, or lifecycle behavior.

2026-06-17.headline: Intune's STIG audit baseline arrives for GCC High, requiring Advanced Analytics licensing
2026-06-17.overview: The period is led by a substantive device-security capability: Intune now includes a read-only STIG audit baseline, with related pages moving the feature out of the in-development track and into current guidance. A separate Android MAM update adds a targeted privacy-consent integration for apps distributed through certain China app stores.
2026-06-17.adminImpact: GCC High tenants with Advanced Analytics licensing can assess Windows devices against DISA STIG recommendations without configuring or enforcing those settings; administrators should evaluate the audit profile and reporting workflow for compliance needs. Teams shipping MAM-enabled Android APKs through affected China app stores must use the documented deferred-startup integration, while other store builds should omit it.

keyChanges.title: New STIG baseline audits Windows configuration without enforcement
keyChanges.detail: Intune now includes the Microsoft Windows 11 STIG SCAP Benchmark, Version 2, Release 7, with a benchmark date of January 5, 2026. The baseline evaluates Windows 10 and Windows 11 devices against DISA STIG recommendations and generates detailed audit reports, but does not configure or enforce settings. It is available only to GCC High tenants and requires Advanced Analytics licensing.

keyChanges.title: Android MAM guidance adds a China app-store consent integration
keyChanges.detail: Updated Android Phase 7 guidance says apps distributed through China app stores that require privacy consent before cross-app operations should set the `OfflineStartupDeferredUntilAppSignal` manifest flag and call `setOfflineStartupReady()` after the user accepts the consent dialog. The ready state persists and the method is idempotent; the flag should not be included in APKs distributed through other stores.

2026-06-18.headline: Android BYOD shifts to Management API as Apple ADE grouping reaches general availability
2026-06-18.overview: The 18 June Intune changes are concentrated in enrollment. Personally owned Android work-profile management is moving from the Company Portal and custom-DPC path to Google's Android Management API, with web-based enrollment and an explicit migration path. Intune also says enrollment-time grouping is generally available for new Apple ADE policies on iOS/iPadOS and macOS. Separately, Microsoft 365 Apps policy authoring is moving to the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center, while existing policies remain unchanged. Most other Apple updates align setup procedures with the newer policy-creation experience.
2026-06-18.adminImpact: For Android, decide whether to enable web enrollment for new personally owned work-profile devices and deploy the Move to Android Management API policy for existing devices. Chrome or Edge is required, and tenants that accept only passkeys should wait until web-enrollment support is announced. For Apple ADE, use Enrollment policies rather than Profiles and check tenant availability before relying on enrollment-time grouping: rollout is staged, some sovereign clouds—including Azure China and Azure Government—are excluded, and the ETG group currently cannot be removed while editing an existing policy. The documented workarounds are to recreate the policy or use the Microsoft Graph beta operation. Update administrative guidance so Microsoft 365 Apps policies are authored in the Microsoft 365

keyChanges.title: Personally owned Android work profiles enter the AMAPI migration
keyChanges.detail: Intune now documents two enrollment paths: Company Portal with the custom DPC is being phased out, while browser-based enrollment uses Android Management API, is the default for new tenants and after migration, and does not require Company Portal for enrollment. The documented migration is to enable web enrollment for new devices and deploy the Move to Android Management API policy for existing enrolled devices.
keyChanges.product: Android Enterprise personally owned work profiles

keyChanges.title: Enrollment-time grouping becomes generally available for new Apple ADE policies
keyChanges.detail: Intune's What's New entry says enrollment-time grouping is now generally available for Apple automated device enrollment on iOS/iPadOS and macOS. It lets Intune identify a device's Microsoft Entra security group during enrollment so policies, apps, and settings can be applied earlier. The capability is supported in new Apple ADE enrollment policies.

keyChanges.title: Apple ADE setup guidance moves from Profiles to Enrollment policies
keyChanges.detail: The updated macOS automated-enrollment procedure identifies Enrollment program tokens > Enrollment policies as the updated creation experience and says the older Profiles experience will eventually be retired and will not receive new features. It also documents the Device group step: only static Microsoft Entra groups are selectable, and enrollment-time device membership assignment permission in a custom RBAC role under Enrollment programs is required.

keyChanges.title: Microsoft 365 Apps policy authoring leaves the Intune admin center
keyChanges.detail: A Message Center plan says that, starting with Intune's June 2026 release, Microsoft 365 Apps policy settings will only be configurable in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center. Existing policies and functionality remain unchanged, so the immediate task is to update administrative guidance and point future configuration to the other center.

keyChanges.title: A new Android re-Workplace Join procedure covers registration drift
keyChanges.detail: A new how-to addresses Android Enterprise devices that are already enrolled in Intune but have incomplete Azure AD registration, including devices affected by unfinished web enrollment or migration from the custom DPC stack to Android Management API. It directs users to open the enrollment app, select the Workplace Join notification, complete registration, and retry the work app. Work credentials and Microsoft Authenticator are prerequisites; this is an operational troubleshooting procedure, not a separate new-en

2026-06-19.headline: HTTPS delivery requirement changes how Intune Win32 apps use Connected Cache
2026-06-19.overview: Two substantive updates stand out. Intune now requires HTTPS delivery for managed Win32 app content, affecting organizations that use Microsoft Connected Cache without HTTPS-configured nodes. Windows Autopilot also documents Intune Connector for Active Directory build 6.2604.2000.3, which adds an opt-in workaround for a bring-your-own gMSA privilege-check failure. The remaining edits are documentation maintenance: reference cleanup and wording or formatting normalization.
2026-06-19.adminImpact: Administrators using Microsoft Connected Cache should review HTTPS configuration because clients can otherwise bypass cache nodes and fall back to the CDN. Organizations using a bring-your-own gMSA with the ODJ Connector should use build 6.2604.2000.3 or later and apply the opt-in setting only when the documented privilege-propagation failure occurs. No administrator action is indicated by the index and formatting edits.

keyChanges.title: Managed Win32 app content now requires HTTPS delivery
keyChanges.detail: Intune now requires HTTPS delivery for managed Win32 app content. Clients can still download Win32 apps when Connected Cache nodes are not configured for HTTPS, but those requests bypass the cache nodes and fall back to the content delivery network. The update points administrators to HTTPS setup guidance for Windows and Linux cache nodes.

keyChanges.title: ODJ Connector build adds an opt-in gMSA privilege-check bypass
keyChanges.detail: Build 6.2604.2000.3 or later adds the optional `SkipByoMsaPrivilegeCheck` `<appSettings>` key for bring-your-own gMSA configurations. Set it to `true` to skip the `SeLogonAsServicePrivilege` pre-check when that privilege has been assigned but has not propagated to the connector host; then restart configuration. The default remains `false`, so the pre-check continues unless explicitly disabled.

2026-06-22.headline: Intune guidance standardizes admin-center links and sign-in terminology, without behavior changes
2026-06-22.overview: 22 June was overwhelmingly documentation maintenance: 487 recorded changes, including 486 updates, one removal, and no new items or Message Center notices. The supplied diffs repeatedly replace inline Microsoft Intune admin center URLs with a named reference link to `https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?linkid=2109431`, normalize “sign into” to “sign in to,” and normalize curly apostrophes. The representative examples preserve existing settings, paths, and behavior; they do not show a new capability, preview, general-availability change, retirement, deadline, or security-policy change.
2026-06-22.adminImpact: Administrators generally do not need to change tenant configuration, assignments, enrollment, compliance, MAM, or Autopilot settings based on these diffs. Update internal runbooks only if they depend on the affected wording or links. The compliance overview’s corrected monitor-policy reference may improve navigation, but these edits should not be treated as product behavior changes.

keyChanges.title: Settings Catalog Step 5 centralizes Edge policy links
keyChanges.detail: Intune’s Settings Catalog Step 5 moves repeated admin-center URLs into a named link reference. The listed Edge values remain `Default geolocation setting` = `Don't allow any site to track users' physical location (2)` and `Enable network prediction` = `Don't predict network actions on any network connection (2)`. Curly apostrophes were also normalized; no policy value or assignment behavior changes in the diff.
keyChanges.product: Intune — Settings Catalog and Microsoft Edge policy settings

keyChanges.title: Compliance Overview replaces the displayed truncated monitor link
keyChanges.detail: The Intune compliance Overview diff replaces the displayed `./monito…` reference for Monitor device compliance with `./monitor-policy.md`. It retains the route **Devices > Monitor > Setting compliance** and the setting name **Is active**, making this a documentation-navigation correction rather than a compliance-engine change.

keyChanges.title: Android MAM wording preserves Strict Tunnel Mode behavior
keyChanges.detail: The Intune MAM Android guidance still documents `com.microsoft.intune.mam.managedbrowser.StrictTunnelMode` with value `True`. It continues to state that Edge blocks internet traffic when an organization-account user is signed in and the VPN is disconnected, with browsing available again after reconnection; the supplied diff changes only “sign into” to “sign in to.” Existing MAM policies have no evidenced behavior change.
keyChanges.product: Intune — Mobile application management for Android

keyChanges.title: Windows Autopilot Hybrid standardizes sign-in wording and links
keyChanges.detail: Windows Autopilot Hybrid guidance changes “Sign into” to “Sign in to” and converts admin-center URLs to named references. The documented navigation remains **Devices > By platform | Windows > Device onboarding | Enrollment > Windows Autopilot > Devices**; the diff shows no enrollment workflow or availability change.

2026-06-23.headline: Multi Admin Approval now gates app-only Intune Graph mutations
2026-06-23.overview: The period’s clearest operational change is Multi Admin Approval enforcement for app-authenticated Microsoft Graph calls: tenants with active MAA access policies can now require approval for automation modifying protected Intune resources. Other substantive items include a changed Microsoft 365 Copilot mobile control path, a Microsoft 365 packaging rollout, and a planned macOS Wi-Fi setting for MAC randomization. Most remaining updates are documentation maintenance, including icon substitutions, wording changes, and standardized prerequisite blocks rather than new product behavior.
2026-06-23.adminImpact: Inventory service principals, scripts, and third-party applications that modify MAA-protected Intune resources, then update them for the approval workflow or use the documented application-exclusion path where necessary. Do not rely on the former Copilot app-configuration key for mobile restrictions; use Integrated Apps controls or block the mobile app. Track the Microsoft 365 packaging rollout and review new policies, while treating the macOS MAC-randomization item as in-development rather than generally available.

keyChanges.title: Automation must now satisfy MAA approval enforcement
keyChanges.detail: Changed behavior for tenants with MAA access policies: app-authenticated calls from service principals, scripts, and third-party applications are intercepted when they modify protected Intune resources. POST, PATCH, PUT, and DELETE calls without the required approval headers return HTTP 403; read-only GET calls are unaffected. Protected resource types include compliance and configuration policies, device actions, RBAC, scripts, and tenant configuration. Only interactive administrators can approve or reject requests

keyChanges.title: The former Copilot mobile app-configuration switch is retired
keyChanges.detail: Changed behavior and guidance: the com.microsoft.office.officemobile.BingChatEnterprise.IsAllowed key is no longer a control for independently enabling or disabling Copilot in the Microsoft 365 mobile app. The page says Microsoft 365 is now Microsoft 365 Copilot, with Copilot as a core mobile workflow. To restrict access, administrators should use Integrated Apps settings for web, desktop, and mobile, or block the Microsoft 365 Copilot mobile app for mobile-only restriction
keyChanges.product: Intune mobile app configuration and Microsoft 365 Copilot

keyChanges.title: Microsoft 365 packaging rollout adds security and Intune changes
keyChanges.detail: A Message Center major update says the 2026 Microsoft 365 Packaging Update is rolling out from mid-June through early August. It adds features including Microsoft Defender Plan 1, URL time-of-click protection, Intune improvements, and 50 GB of additional Exchange Online storage. Microsoft 365 Business SKU backfill is scheduled to complete by September 30, and administrators are told to review and configure new policies

keyChanges.title: macOS Wi-Fi gains a planned MAC-randomization control
keyChanges.detail: In-development capability: Intune Wi-Fi profiles are planned to gain Disable MAC address randomization for managed macOS devices running macOS 15 and later. The setting addresses environments such as network access control that rely on a static MAC address, although randomized MAC addresses remain recommended for privacy. The evidence gives no general-availability date

keyChanges.title: DFCI guidance warns against mixing microphone setting categories
keyChanges.detail: Documentation clarification, not a reported product behavior change: the Windows DFCI guidance now says to configure either the Microphones and speakers category or the Microphones granular settings, not both, because combining them can cause a conflict. It also clarifies that Only not configured allows local changes except where Intune explicitly sets Enable or Disable, while None prevents changes to any UEFI or BIOS setting, including settings not shown in the profile

2026-06-24.headline: Trustd Mobile integration, required-app auto-updates, and baseline changes headline Intune guidance
2026-06-24.overview: The substantive updates center on newly documented Trustd Mobile Mobile Threat Defense integration, Enterprise App Catalog auto-update rules, and security-baseline revisions. Trustd Mobile guidance covers risk-driven compliance and Conditional Access for Android 9.0 and later and iOS/iPadOS 15.0 and later; Enterprise App Catalog auto-update is scoped to Windows 10 and Windows 11 apps with Required assignments. The Microsoft 365 Apps security baseline 2512 replaces version 2306, while older Windows 25H2 profiles need an edit-and-save to receive the newly added IE11 COM-automation control. Intune also documented self-service compliance-partner onboarding; other notable clarification includes Remote Help's different control scope for AVD desktop and RemoteApp sessions.
2026-06-24.adminImpact: These are Microsoft Learn content changes, not supplied Message Center announcements, so they do not by themselves establish a broad GA, preview, or retirement. Administrators evaluating Trustd Mobile should confirm the listed subscriptions, platform coverage, app deployment, and enrollment requirements; the setup guidance also requires one-time Global Administrator authorization. For Enterprise App Catalog, review Required assignments before enabling auto-update, while Available assignments retain the existing workflow. Baseline administrators should compare Microsoft 365 Apps version 2306 and 2512 settings, use the Security Compliance Toolkit for the full 2512 configuration, and edit and save deployed pre-update Windows 25H2 profiles if the new IE11 setting should apply. For self-service

keyChanges.title: Trustd Mobile integration is newly documented for Intune MTD
keyChanges.detail: New guidance describes Trustd Mobile sending a risk score through the Intune Mobile Threat Defense connector; the score updates device compliance and can drive Conditional Access blocking. The documented scope is Android 9.0 and later and iOS/iPadOS 15.0 and later, with Microsoft Entra ID P1, Intune Plan 1, a Trustd Mobile subscription, and the Trustd Mobile app required. This is newly added integration guidance, not a supplied GA announcement.

keyChanges.title: Enterprise App Catalog auto-update is documented for Required assignments
keyChanges.detail: The updated Enterprise App Management guidance says Intune can automatically update Enterprise App Catalog apps when a newer catalog version is available, without creating a new app or configuring supersedence for each update. The scope is Windows 10 and Windows 11 devices and apps with a Required assignment; Available for enrolled devices assignments retain the existing update workflow. Guided update supersedence remains an option for administrators who want to review updates before applying them.

keyChanges.title: Microsoft 365 Apps security baseline 2512 replaces version 2306
keyChanges.detail: The settings reference identifies Version 2512 as first made available in June 2026 and states that it replaces Version 2306. Listed defaults include Block Flash activation in Office documents set to Enabled and Restrict legacy JScript execution for Office set to Enabled. Microsoft directs administrators to the Security Compliance Toolkit's Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise 2512.zip for the complete settings list.

keyChanges.title: Older Windows 25H2 profiles need saving for the new IE11 control
keyChanges.detail: The Windows security baseline guidance says Disable Internet Explorer 11 Launch Via COM Automation was added in the June 2026 service update with an Enabled baseline default. Profiles created before the update do not apply it automatically: edit and save the profile, after which Intune deploys the setting at the next device check-in. Newly created or updated-to-25H2 profiles include the setting by default.

keyChanges.title: Self-service compliance partners gain a custom connector path
keyChanges.detail: Intune guidance now describes compliance partners onboarding and publishing their own connectors. Once a partner connector is available, administrators select Custom MDM Compliance Partner and enter the partner-provided Custom MDM Compliance Partner Entra Application ID. Configuration cannot be completed unless the ID belongs to a valid onboarded partner, and partner availability depends on completed onboarding and connector publication.

2026-06-25.headline: Intune plans iOS 18 and macOS 15 minimums later this year
2026-06-25.overview: The period is dominated by two future Apple platform support changes and three targeted documentation updates. Intune will raise its iOS/iPadOS and macOS support floors later this year; the documentation also records an Android app version requirement, an Android BYOD enrollment limitation, and revised macOS PKG update guidance. No new feature launch is evidenced in this set.
2026-06-25.adminImpact: Inventory Apple devices and plan upgrades before the announced support changes, checking Intune reports for affected devices. For Android, identify outdated Intune app versions and review enrollment restrictions where AMAPI or Custom DPC is used. Update macOS deployment runbooks to reflect the revised Company Portal behavior described in the documentation.

keyChanges.title: iOS/iPadOS 18 becomes the planned minimum after Apple’s iOS 27 release
keyChanges.detail: A Message Center plan-for-change notice says Intune will require iOS/iPadOS 18 or higher after Apple releases iOS/iPadOS 27 later this year. Administrators should check device compatibility and Intune reports; userless devices enrolled through ADE have different OS requirements.

keyChanges.title: macOS 15 will be required for new enrollments after macOS 27
keyChanges.detail: After Apple’s macOS Golden Gate 27 release, Intune will support macOS 15 and later. Devices already enrolled on macOS 14.x or earlier remain enrolled, but new enrollments on those versions will be blocked. Identify and upgrade affected devices before the change.

keyChanges.title: Android Intune app support now starts at version 2025.11.01
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance says the minimum supported Microsoft Intune app for Android is version 2025.11.01, effective May 1, 2026; older versions might cause sign-in failures. Administrators can use Apps > Monitor > Discovered apps to find affected devices, while most users should receive updates automatically.

keyChanges.title: Personally owned blocking is limited for AMAPI and newer Custom DPC devices
keyChanges.detail: The Android personal work profile guidance now warns that setting Personally owned to Block does not apply to Android Management API devices and is not reliable for Android 12 and later devices using Custom DPC enrollment. It documents corporate-owned work profiles or group-based enrollment restrictions as alternatives.
keyChanges.product: Intune Android Enterprise personal work profile enrollment

keyChanges.title: macOS available PKG updates are documented as automatic
keyChanges.detail: The updated unmanaged PKG guidance now states that uploading a new version of an available app does not require users to select Install or Reinstall in Company Portal; the app installs automatically. This is a documentation-level correction to deployment expectations, not evidence of a newly announced feature.
keyChanges.product: Intune macOS unmanaged PKG app deployment

2026-06-26.headline: Remote Help guidance tightens unattended-access warnings on recording and sensitive work
2026-06-26.overview: The period contained two Remote Help documentation updates, both focused on security guidance for unattended access. The edits strengthen the wording from recommendations to IMPORTANT guidance, but provide no evidence of a product-behavior change, new feature, or availability change.
2026-06-26.adminImpact: Review unattended-access operating procedures and user guidance. For devices using unattended access, do not install or allowlist apps that can record or mirror the screen, and instruct operators not to perform sensitive operations during unattended control sessions.

keyChanges.title: Deploy guidance prohibits screen-recording and mirroring apps
keyChanges.detail: The Remote Help Deploy page changes the notice from a recommendation not to install or allowlist screen-recording or mirroring apps to IMPORTANT guidance: on devices using unattended access, do not install or allowlist any apps that can record or mirror the screen. It also recommends avoiding sensitive operations during unattended control sessions. This is a documentation and security-guidance clarification, not evidence of an enforced product control.

keyChanges.title: Start Session guidance makes sensitive operations explicitly disallowed
keyChanges.detail: The Remote Help Start Session page changes its advice from limiting activity to nonsensitive operations to IMPORTANT guidance that operators must not perform sensitive operations during an unattended control session, even when the device screen is blocked to the end user. It repeats the prohibition on apps that can record or mirror the screen.

2026-06-29.headline: Available macOS PKG apps now auto-update with management agent 2606.013
2026-06-29.overview: The service release 2606 material documents a concrete macOS app-management behavior change: available PKG apps can update automatically after an administrator uploads a newer version. It also records Enterprise App Management auto-updates, GCC High and DoD support, and ChatGPT as a protected app. Separate updates add Vulnerability Remediation Agent RBAC timing guidance and remove legacy Azure CDN aliases from selected endpoint tables; those are operational or documentation clarifications rather than evidence of new tenant capabilities.
2026-06-29.adminImpact: For available macOS PKG apps, verify that the Microsoft Intune management agent is version 2606.013 or later and that the same policy receives the newer app version with the same bundle ID. EAM administrators can review required assignments and enable auto-update where appropriate; government-cloud administrators should assess the GCCH/DoD support if relevant. Allow several minutes for agentic-user RBAC permissions to take effect before troubleshooting access, and review network allowlists against the current manage.microsoft.com endpoint entries.

keyChanges.title: Available macOS PKG apps no longer require a Company Portal reinstall
keyChanges.detail: For an available macOS PKG app, Intune now deploys an uploaded newer version automatically when it is added to the existing app policy with the same bundle ID, provided the user already installed the app. Users no longer need to select Install or Reinstall in Company Portal. The behavior requires the macOS Intune management agent version 2606.013 or later.

keyChanges.title: Enterprise App Management adds catalog auto-updates and GCC High/DoD support
keyChanges.detail: Intune now supports automatic updates for EAM applications when auto-update is enabled on an app with a required assignment; newer catalog versions are automatically deployed to targeted devices. The release notes also say EAM now extends to GCC High and DoD, allowing government organizations to discover, deploy, and keep prepackaged Microsoft and third-party apps up to date without manual repackaging.

keyChanges.title: ChatGPT is newly available as an Intune protected app
keyChanges.detail: The service-release notes list ChatGPT as a newly available protected app for Microsoft Intune. The supplied change does not specify additional platform scope or policy settings, so it supports the protected-app availability claim but not broader configuration conclusions.

keyChanges.title: Vulnerability Remediation Agent guidance adds RBAC propagation timing
keyChanges.detail: The Security Copilot Vulnerability Remediation Agent page now adds an Important note that permissions assigned through an Intune RBAC role may take several minutes to take effect after the agentic user is added to the group. This is troubleshooting guidance about permission propagation, not evidence that RBAC behavior or the agent capability itself changed.

keyChanges.title: Selected endpoint tables remove legacy azureedge.net aliases
keyChanges.detail: The Endpoints page now lists intunecdnpeasd.manage.microsoft.com alone for the Android AOSP dependency, instead of also listing intunecdnpeasd.azureedge.net. The North America, Europe, and Asia Pacific macOS sidecar rows likewise retain only their manage.microsoft.com hostnames and remove the macsidecarprod*.azureedge.net aliases and migration notes. This is an allowlist-documentation cleanup; the supplied diff does not establish a separate endpoint retirement deadline.

2026-06-30.headline: Connected Cache HTTPS rollout ties Win32 downloads to current versions and proxy support
2026-06-30.overview: The period's most consequential material concerns Microsoft Connected Cache: updated guidance records Intune's regional HTTPS rollout for Win32 app content, beginning June 16, and ties support to current Connected Cache and Configuration Manager versions. Configuration Manager proxy requirements and the validation procedure were also made materially more specific. The remaining Intune edits are maintenance, including a partner-list replacement, grammatical cleanup, and archive-index changes; no new or Message Center item is supplied.
2026-06-30.adminImpact: Administrators using Connected Cache for Intune Win32 content should verify the documented version and proxy conditions before relying on the HTTPS path, and update troubleshooting runbooks to use the elevated 64-bit PowerShell and DOCacheHost workflow. The evidence supports an in-progress rollout and documentation change, not a universal tenant-side switch. The Iru/Kandji edit is evidenced only as a documentation-list change, with no stated enrollment or compliance behavior change.

keyChanges.title: HTTPS rollout for Win32 content now carries a Connected Cache version prerequisite
keyChanges.detail: The Connected Cache page says Intune is rolling out HTTPS for Win32 app content downloads by region starting June 16, 2026. To support the change, it specifies the latest Connected Cache version: KB33247081 for Configuration Manager versions 2409, 2503, 2509, and 2603, or Configuration Manager 2603. The page describes an in-progress rollout rather than universal availability.
keyChanges.product: Intune Win32 apps and Configuration Manager Connected Cache

keyChanges.title: Connected Cache proxy guidance now separates newer and earlier releases
keyChanges.detail: The Proxy Server Support page now says a Configuration Manager distribution point running Connected Cache can use a proxy for internet access starting with Configuration Manager 2603 or after installing KB33247081. Earlier releases require a direct internet connection or a proxy that supports relative URIs. The revised sentence also drops the previous “unauthenticated” qualifier without defining authenticated-proxy behavior.

keyChanges.title: Connected Cache validation shifts to policy targeting and elevated 64-bit PowerShell
keyChanges.detail: The troubleshooting procedure now starts with a 64-bit PowerShell window opened as administrator and requires administrators to confirm that the host is targeted by policy. If Configuration Manager or Intune has not set the policy, the supplied procedure sets DOCacheHost under HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\DeliveryOptimization to the distribution point FQDN or IP. This replaces the prior example-led check based on downloading content, Get-DeliveryOptimizationStatus, and BytesFromCacheServer.
keyChanges.product: Configuration Manager Connected Cache and Delivery Optimization

keyChanges.title: Connected Cache hotfix documentation now includes Configuration Manager 2603
keyChanges.detail: The KB33247081 title, applicability statement, and update instructions now include Configuration Manager 2603 alongside 2409, 2503, and 2509. The page states that the update applies to versions 2409, 2503, 2509, or 2603. This is a documented applicability expansion, not evidence that a new hotfix was published during the period.

keyChanges.title: Third-party compliance partner listing swaps Kandji for Iru
keyChanges.detail: The Intune Third Party Partners page removes the Kandji entry and Kandji Device Compliance link and adds an Iru documentation link. The supplied diff establishes a partner-list change only; it does not establish new integration availability, enrollment behavior, or a required tenant action.

2026-07-01.headline: Office baseline DDE labels get punctuation-only cleanup in Intune guidance
2026-07-01.overview: This was primarily a documentation-maintenance day: all 485 recorded items were updates, with no new or removed items and no Message Center notices. The clearest content diffs affect Intune security-baseline references, where curly apostrophes were changed to straight apostrophes. Other representative updates show collection, author, or reviewer metadata changes rather than documented product behavior or availability changes.
2026-07-01.adminImpact: No tenant configuration, rollout, or upgrade action is indicated by the supplied evidence. The baseline diffs do not show changed policy values, baseline versions, prerequisites, or device behavior.

keyChanges.title: Office V2 baseline reference normalizes DDE setting-label apostrophes
keyChanges.detail: In Ref V2 Office Settings, the labels “Don’t allow Dynamic Data Exchange (DDE) server launch in Excel (User)” and “Don’t allow Dynamic Data Exchange (DDE) server lookup in Excel (User)” were changed to use “Don't.” The sentence describing profile instances created before a new baseline version also changed “you’ve” to “you've.” This is a documentation punctuation edit; the diff does not show a setting-value, baseline-version, or behavior change.

keyChanges.title: Windows MDM baseline guidance receives the same apostrophe normalization
keyChanges.detail: Ref Windows Mdm Settings changes “you’ve” to “you've” in the sentence explaining that a new baseline version replaces the previous version and referring to profile instances created before its availability. No policy or profile behavior change is evidenced.

2026-07-02.headline: Android BYOD web enrollment guidance flags an irreversible tenant-level setting
2026-07-02.overview: The period was largely maintenance, but the substantive Intune changes center on Android Enterprise personally owned work-profile enrollment and forthcoming device-management capabilities. Updated guidance centers a single enrollment profile for web and Company Portal flows, while clarifying that web enrollment is tenant-level and irreversible and may conflict with device-bound phone-call MFA. Intune’s in-development page also adds Samsung Knox E-FOTA integration and Windows registry and app-inventory work. The macOS token procedure was broadened to cover both Apple Business Manager and Apple School Manager; this is a procedural clarification, not a feature launch.
2026-07-02.adminImpact: Review Android BYOD enrollment and authentication guidance before rollout. The documented web-enrollment setting applies across the tenant and cannot be reversed; phone-call MFA answered on the enrolling device might break the web flow, with secondary-device authentication or SMS listed as workarounds. Treat Knox E-FOTA and Windows inventory/query entries as future planning signals because no availability is established. Update macOS token runbooks if using Apple School Manager.

keyChanges.title: Android BYOD guidance centers one profile for web and app enrollment
keyChanges.detail: The setup article now says admins first create an enrollment profile that supports both web-based and Company Portal app-based enrollment. Web enrollment is enabled as an additional step by selecting Use web enrollment for all users enrolling into Android personally owned work profile management; when passkeys are the only authentication method, the guidance says to leave it unselected and use Company Portal enrollment instead.
keyChanges.product: Intune Android Enterprise personally owned work profile enrollment

keyChanges.title: Web enrollment is documented as tenant-level and irreversible
keyChanges.detail: The revised setup guidance explicitly states that enabling web-based enrollment applies at the tenant level and cannot be reversed. This clarifies the scope and consequence of the setting rather than announcing a product-behavior change.

keyChanges.title: Phone-call MFA might break Android web enrollment
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance records a limitation: if MFA requires a phone call that the user must answer on the device being enrolled, web enrollment might break. It lists authenticating on a secondary device or using SMS as workarounds and says the limitation will be resolved in a future update, without providing a date.

keyChanges.title: Samsung firmware control and Windows fleet visibility enter the roadmap
keyChanges.detail: The In development page adds an upcoming Knox E-FOTA integration that would surface remote firmware deployment in the Intune admin center for eligible corporate-owned Samsung Android Enterprise devices: dedicated (COSU), fully managed (COBO), and corporate-owned with a work profile (COPE). It also lists Windows properties-catalog collection of HKLM registry data through Single Value, All Values Under Key (Non-Recursive), or Same Value Across Subkeys, plus Advanced Analytics multi-device Windows app-inventory querys
keyChanges.product: Intune Android Enterprise, Windows properties catalog, and Advanced Analytics

keyChanges.title: macOS token instructions now separate Apple Business and School Manager paths
keyChanges.detail: The enrollment program token procedure now explicitly covers Apple Business Manager and Apple School Manager with portal-specific steps. It changes the Intune action label from Add to Create and explains that Apple Business Manager creates a device management service while Apple School Manager creates an MDM server; both processes produce a server token uploaded to Intune. This is a procedure clarification, not evidence of a new token capability.

2026-07-06.headline: Microsoft 365 E3 and E5 begin receiving Intune Suite capabilities
2026-07-06.overview: The main development is a gradual commercial licensing rollout that adds selected Intune Suite capabilities to Microsoft 365 E3 and E5. Eligible tenants are automatically provisioned, with no action required, and receive a Microsoft 365 admin center notification 30 days before the change takes effect. The other updates are documentation-only enrollment wording and procedure clarifications.
2026-07-06.adminImpact: Commercial Microsoft 365 E3 tenants gain Remote Help, Advanced Analytics, and Intune Plan 2 capabilities, while E5 tenants also gain Endpoint Privilege Management, Enterprise Application Management, and Microsoft Cloud PKI. Administrators should watch for the 30-day admin center notification and account for the new capabilities as they appear. The update does not apply to Education or frontline worker plans at this time; the Apple enrollment edits do not indicate a tenant configuration or product-behavior change.

keyChanges.title: Commercial Microsoft 365 E3 and E5 receive broader Intune Suite packaging
keyChanges.detail: The EMS E3 component included with commercial Microsoft 365 E3 adds Remote Help, Advanced Analytics, and Intune Plan 2, including Microsoft Tunnel for mobile application management, specialty device management, and firmware over-the-air updates for supported devices. Microsoft 365 E5 includes those capabilities plus Endpoint Privilege Management, Enterprise Application Management, and Microsoft Cloud PKI. The rollout is gradual, eligible tenants are automatically provisioned, and no action is required.

keyChanges.title: Apple token setup guidance adopts “Apple Business” terminology
keyChanges.detail: The setup and renewal instructions now refer to Apple Business instead of Apple Business Manager, while Apple School Manager remains unchanged. The documented connection and server-token process is otherwise described the same way; the edit does not indicate a change to Intune behavior.

keyChanges.title: macOS Company Portal instructions now specify the Applications folder
keyChanges.detail: After Company Portal finishes installing, the procedure now tells users to open Company Portal from the Applications folder. The step numbering was also corrected, making this a user guidance clarification rather than a documented product change.

2026-07-07.headline: Azure Services Wizard renewal now requires Microsoft Graph admin consent
2026-07-07.overview: The Azure Services Wizard guidance now states that, starting with Configuration Manager 2409, Azure services use Microsoft Graph. Renewing the secret key requires consent for Microsoft Graph `Directory.Read.All`; the Cloud Application Administrator role cannot grant that consent.
2026-07-07.adminImpact: For Configuration Manager 2409 and later, do not rely on a Cloud Application Administrator alone to renew the Azure services secret. Use a Global Administrator account or another role that can grant admin consent for Microsoft Graph permissions, as specified in the updated procedure.

keyChanges.title: Secret renewal prerequisite clarified for Configuration Manager 2409
keyChanges.detail: The Azure Services Wizard documentation replaces the earlier Cloud Application Administrator requirement with a more specific Microsoft Graph consent requirement. The account signing in to renew the secret key must be able to grant admin consent for `Directory.Read.All`; Global Administrator is one stated option.

2026-07-08.headline: Configuration Manager baseline guidance now spells out power and idle launch conditions
2026-07-08.overview: This was a quiet, documentation-only period. Configuration Manager guidance clarifies when deployed baselines are evaluated and how to troubleshoot missed schedules, while Intune Android work-profile guidance retains web-enrollment limitations without promising a future fix. No feature launch, retirement, or availability change is evidenced.
2026-07-08.adminImpact: For Configuration Manager, review baseline scheduling expectations and use the linked Scheduler.log guidance when an evaluation does not run as expected. For Intune, continue not enabling web enrollment for tenants that accept only passkeys, and use a secondary device or SMS when phone-call MFA could interrupt enrollment. The removed future-update wording is not evidence that support has arrived.

keyChanges.title: Baseline evaluation timing now includes first-launch conditions
keyChanges.detail: The deployment guidance now says computer-targeted baselines are evaluated within a two-hour randomization window of each scheduled start after the first evaluation. The first evaluation on a Windows client additionally requires the device to be powered above the low-battery threshold and the user to be idle. This is a documentation clarification of client evaluation behavior, not an announced product change.

keyChanges.title: Missed baseline schedules now link directly to Scheduler.log troubleshooting
keyChanges.detail: The compliance-monitoring page adds a tip directing administrators to the client-evaluation guidance for launch conditions and to Scheduler.log when a scheduled evaluation did not run as expected.

keyChanges.title: Android web-enrollment caveats remove obsolete future-fix wording
keyChanges.detail: Intune still documents that users in tenants accepting only passkeys can't complete web enrollment, so administrators shouldn't enable it until passkey support is announced. Phone-call MFA may also break web enrollment; the documented workarounds are authenticating on a secondary device or using SMS. The revision removes statements that these limitations will be resolved in a future update, without announcing that they are resolved.

2026-07-14.headline: Configuration Manager SQL move guidance requires collation checks; Outlook support is documented for iOS/iPadOS
2026-07-14.overview: The 14 July period contains four documentation updates, with no evidenced new launch, general-availability milestone, preview, or retirement. The most consequential clarification is that Configuration Manager's Modify SQL Server configuration maintenance path skips the collation prerequisite check performed during installation or upgrade. Intune's Multiple Managed Accounts page now lists Microsoft Outlook for iOS/iPadOS, while the remaining changes refine signed-script and external-link guidance.
2026-07-14.adminImpact: Before moving a Configuration Manager site database, administrators should verify the target SQL Server instance and site database use SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS and run the supplied verification script against CM_<sitecode>, not a system database. For AllSigned task sequences, reference signed PowerShell files through a Configuration Manager package rather than embedding their contents. Intune administrators evaluating Multiple Managed Accounts should use the documented app versions; the Managed Home Screen change is a reference-link correction with no evidenced policy behavior change.

keyChanges.title: Manual collation verification is required before the SQL configuration move path
keyChanges.detail: The Modify SQL Server configuration maintenance path doesn't run the collation prerequisite check used by a new install or upgrade. The guidance says both the target SQL Server instance and site database must use SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS. It adds a verification procedure using SQL Server Management Studio against the site database (CM_<sitecode>), not master, and says to resolve every ERROR before continuing.

keyChanges.title: AllSigned task sequences should reference signed scripts from a package
keyChanges.detail: The guidance warns that Enter a PowerShell script can alter embedded script content through the task-sequence XML, invalidating its digital signature and causing a client rejection with a “hash does not match” entry in smsts.log. For AllSigned, administrators are directed to place the signed .ps1 file in a Configuration Manager package and use the Package and Script name options.

keyChanges.title: Multiple Managed Accounts documentation adds Outlook for iOS/iPadOS
keyChanges.detail: The support table now lists Microsoft Outlook on iOS/iPadOS at version 5.2626.0 or later, alongside Microsoft Teams on iOS/iPadOS at version 8.10.0 or later. This is a documentation update to the supported-app table, not evidence of a newly launched capability in the period.

keyChanges.title: Managed Home Screen permission references move to Zebra’s current support domain
keyChanges.detail: The cited Zebra resources change from supportcommunity.zebra.com/s/article/... to support.zebra.com/article/.... The Notification Access entry for the 11.5.x.x guidance also changes from article 000026099 to 000027795. The diff shows link maintenance rather than a change to Managed Home Screen permissions.

2026-07-15.headline: macOS custom-compliance scripts and Delete status get more precise Intune guidance
2026-07-15.overview: All eight changes on 15 July were Intune documentation updates; there were no new items, retirements, or Message Center announcements. The meaningful updates cluster around custom compliance guidance that now covers macOS and a clarification of what a completed device Delete action means. Other edits propagate macOS references through policy, JSON, and overview pages or repeat the Delete clarification in reporting guidance.
2026-07-15.adminImpact: Admins developing custom compliance workflows for macOS should review the Bash-script requirements and policy procedure before rollout. Admins handling MDM device deletion should interpret Delete as a server-side completion signal, not confirmation that the client-side Retire has finished.

keyChanges.title: Custom compliance guidance now documents macOS discovery scripts
keyChanges.detail: The discovery-script guidance expands the documented platforms from Linux and Windows to Linux, macOS, and Windows. For macOS, it specifies a Bash script that runs in 10 minutes or less, includes a valid shebang such as #!/bin/bash, uses UTF-8 encoding without BOM, and returns exit code 0 for success and a non-zero code for failure. The procedure also adds macOS settings for logged-on credentials, signature checking, and hiding script notifications. This is a documentation expansion; the supplied evidence does not,

keyChanges.title: Custom-compliance scope and platform instructions are broadened to include macOS
keyChanges.detail: The main custom-compliance guidance changes its title and description from a Linux-and-Windows focus to managed devices generally, identifies macOS alongside Linux and Windows, and says Linux and macOS use a POSIX-compliant shell script. Related policy guidance now presents the discovery-script and rules-file steps for Linux and macOS, while the JSON guidance adds a macOS reference. These edits clarify the documented workflow and should not be treated as proof of a new service rollout or changed availability.

keyChanges.title: Delete action completion is clarified as server-side for MDM devices
keyChanges.detail: The updated Delete action guidance says the device is immediately hidden from the admin center and a Retire is initiated for MDM devices. In the Device actions report, Delete shows Action Status as Completed when processing is complete on the server; that status does not confirm that the client device has finished Retire. Administrators should avoid treating Completed as proof of endpoint-side retirement.

2026-07-16.headline: Packages and programs guidance clarifies WOW64 redirection and Software Center sessions
2026-07-16.overview: The sole update revises Configuration Manager’s Packages And Programs guidance rather than introducing an Intune capability. It adds an explicit 64-bit client warning and replaces a generic multi-user Software Center caveat with defined session-selection rules.
2026-07-16.adminImpact: Intune administrators who also manage Configuration Manager should review package scripts that run on 64-bit clients: command lines run as 32-bit processes, so %ProgramFiles% is redirected to %ProgramFiles(x86)% and registry writes to HKLM\Software are redirected to HKLM\Software\WOW6432Node. On shared devices, validate Software Center visibility for the active console user; if no user is signed in to that session, use the user with the lowest active session ID. The evidence supports a documentation clarification, not a confirmed product behavior change or tenant action.

keyChanges.title: 64-bit package command lines are documented as WOW64 processes
keyChanges.detail: The Packages And Programs page now states that, on a 64-bit client, the command line always runs as a 32-bit process in the WOW64 subsystem. File-system and registry access are redirected: for example, %ProgramFiles% maps to %ProgramFiles(x86)% and HKLM\Software maps to HKLM\Software\WOW6432Node. This documents an execution limitation rather than establishing a new runtime behavior.

keyChanges.title: Software Center visibility now follows explicit session-selection rules
keyChanges.detail: The multi-user guidance now says package and task sequence deployments appear in Software Center for the user in the active console session. If no user is signed in to the active console session, they appear for the user with the lowest active session ID. The page also explains that Windows assigns a unique session ID when a user signs in.

2026-07-18.headline: Software Center guidance clarifies package deployment visibility across signed-in sessions
2026-07-18.overview: This quiet period contains one Configuration Manager documentation clarification. The Packages and Programs guidance now describes package and task sequence deployment visibility on multi-user devices using the active console session and, when no user is in that session, the user with the lowest connected interactive session ID. The supplied evidence does not indicate a product behavior change.
2026-07-18.adminImpact: Administrators troubleshooting deployment visibility on shared or multi-user devices should use the clarified session terminology and inspect the Users tab in Task Manager to view each signed-in user's session ID and type. No tenant configuration change or rollout action is supported by the evidence.

keyChanges.title: Packages and Programs guidance revises multi-user session terminology
keyChanges.detail: For multiple signed-in users, deployments appear in Software Center for the user in the active console session. If no user is in the active console session, they appear for the user with the lowest connected interactive session ID. The revised text also points administrators to Task Manager's Users tab to view session IDs and types. This is an ordinary documentation clarification, not evidence of a new Configuration Manager capability or changed deployment behavior.

2026-07-19.headline: Configuration Manager software update scans separate cache reuse from WSUS connectivity
2026-07-19.overview: The period contains a substantive clarification to Configuration Manager Software Updates guidance. It separates the forced/non-forced decision, which controls cache reuse, from the online/offline decision, which controls whether a scan obtains metadata from WSUS or local storage. This is documentation clarification, not evidence of a new feature, preview, general availability change, retirement, or changed product behavior.
2026-07-19.adminImpact: Use the revised model when interpreting scan results and WSUS traffic. A non-forced scan can use cached results within the TTL, while a forced online scan contacts WSUS and a forced offline scan does not. The supplied evidence does not call for tenant reconfiguration or rollout changes.

keyChanges.title: Forced scans ignore the cached compliance results
keyChanges.detail: A non-forced scan reuses the last scan results while they remain current and within the TTL, running a new scan only when the cache is stale. A forced scan always runs a new scan and ignores the cache.

keyChanges.title: Online and offline scans use different metadata sources
keyChanges.detail: For a scan that actually runs, online mode connects to WSUS on the software update point to refresh metadata. Offline mode evaluates the client with metadata already stored locally and does not connect to WSUS. An online scan therefore does not necessarily contact WSUS when a non-forced scan can use current cached results.

keyChanges.title: One scan evaluates the entire synchronized update catalog
keyChanges.detail: A scan evaluates all update metadata synchronized on the software update point, including updates in new deployments, existing deployments, and no deployments. Targeting a client with 1 deployment or 10 deployments does not change the number of scans.

2026-07-21.headline: Client-driven compliance evaluation preview is documented for supported Windows devices
2026-07-21.overview: The period contained eight documentation updates and no new, removed, or Message Center items. The clearest substantive change is new Intune guidance for a client-driven compliance evaluation preview: supported Windows devices can detect certain local configuration or security-state changes and proactively request a compliance re-evaluation instead of waiting for the next scheduled check-in. The remaining meaningful updates clarify Microsoft Store regional app searching and add a US government endpoint; other edits were primarily presentation or wording changes.
2026-07-21.adminImpact: The compliance capability is explicitly identified as a preview, and the supplied evidence does not specify supported Windows versions, prerequisites, or tenant-side configuration. Administrators should not assume general availability or a required rollout action. For Microsoft Store app administration, use the region selector when locating apps outside the United States. US government administrators maintaining proxy or firewall allowlists should review whether the newly documented ECS wildcard endpoint is covered.

keyChanges.title: Windows devices can proactively request compliance re-evaluation
keyChanges.detail: Intune guidance now documents client-driven compliance evaluation as a preview for supported Windows devices. Certain local changes to device configuration, security posture, or other compliance-relevant settings can trigger a re-evaluation rather than waiting for the next scheduled check-in.

keyChanges.title: Microsoft Store app search now documents regional catalog selection
keyChanges.detail: The Microsoft Store app workflow states that Intune searches the United States catalog by default and directs administrators to select another region from the drop-down list when needed. The unavailable-app message is correspondingly described as applying to the selected region.

keyChanges.title: US government endpoint guidance adds the ECS wildcard domain
keyChanges.detail: The US government endpoint list now includes Experimentation and Configuration Service (ECS) at `*.ecs.gov.teams.microsoft.us`. This is an endpoint-documentation addition, not evidence of a product behavior change.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager software-update scan flow is now an image
keyChanges.detail: The Software Updates Introduction page replaces its embedded Mermaid flowchart with an image describing how Forced and Online decisions determine whether a client contacts WSUS. The supplied diff shows a presentation change, not a change to scan behavior.
