2026-07-22.headline: macOS compliance guidance warns of password expiry for LAPS and Platform SSO
2026-07-22.overview: The period was dominated by documentation maintenance: 2,489 items were updated, including 2,481 Configuration Manager pages. The substantive Intune content change is an added macOS compliance warning about password expiration. Configuration Manager and Windows Autopilot updates mainly show service-metadata normalization, with no supplied evidence of a new feature, preview, general availability change, retirement, deadline, or changed product capability.
2026-07-22.adminImpact: Review macOS compliance policies that require a password. The updated guidance says this automatically expires the existing password for every account on the device, including accounts created by LAPS and Platform SSO, and recommends managing device passwords through a settings catalog policy with Change At Next Auth set to False. The metadata-only Configuration Manager and Windows Autopilot edits do not support a configuration or rollout action.

keyChanges.title: MacOS compliance settings add an explicit password-expiry warning
keyChanges.detail: The Intune macOS settings guidance now warns that requiring a password in a compliance policy automatically expires the existing password for all accounts on the device, including LAPS and Platform SSO accounts. It recommends managing device passwords with a settings catalog policy configured with Change At Next Auth set to False. This is a documentation warning and recommendation, not evidence that the underlying product behavior was newly introduced.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager content receives service-metadata normalization
keyChanges.detail: Representative Configuration Manager diffs replace ms.subservice: core-infra with ms.subservice: core-infrastructure and add ms.service: microsoft-endpoint-configuration-manager. The same metadata pattern accounts for the dominant body of the period’s Configuration Manager updates; it is documentation classification or routing cleanup rather than a documented functionality change.

2026-07-24.headline: Samsung Knox E-FOTA guidance highlights firmware campaigns, targeting performance, and EPM scope tags
2026-07-24.overview: This was a documentation-led period with two new Intune articles and 18 updates, but no Message Center notices or retirements. The most substantive additions document Samsung Knox E-FOTA integration prerequisites and capabilities, introduce a broader targeting-method framework, warn against inefficient dynamic-group rules, and record an Endpoint Privilege Management scope-tag limitation. Other changes mainly clarify navigation, external links, dates, and related content; the new Samsung article does not by itself establish a separate preview or general-availability announcement.
2026-07-24.adminImpact: Evaluate Samsung Knox E-FOTA against the documented Android Enterprise enrollment types, Samsung and Microsoft licensing, network, tenant, and role prerequisites before planning deployment. Audit dynamic group rules for memberOf and review whether assignment filters or direct device properties are more appropriate. If EPM scope tags are used, apply the documented RBAC workaround, and update Apple token-renewal runbooks to use the revised Apple enrollment navigation.

keyChanges.title: Samsung Knox E-FOTA integration gets a new Intune setup article
keyChanges.detail: The new how-to documents an integration that, according to the article, can launch, manage, and monitor Samsung firmware campaigns from the Intune admin center; lock devices to an OS version or selected firmware; and schedule download and installation windows. It says deployments require a Samsung Knox E-FOTA license and at least Microsoft 365 E3, support Android Enterprise corporate-owned dedicated, fully managed, and COPE enrollment types, and require an Intune Administrator plus a Samsung Knox administrator for-

keyChanges.title: A new guide separates group scope from Intune policy targeting
keyChanges.detail: The new targeting guide recommends starting with a broad audience and refining it with assignment filters, rather than creating many policy-specific groups. It distinguishes groups, which define the audience, from filters, which determine which devices in that audience receive a policy, and says group membership is processed when identity attributes change while filters evaluate at each device check-in. This is targeting guidance, not evidence of a new targeting behavior.

keyChanges.title: Intune guidance says to avoid memberOf in dynamic group rules
keyChanges.detail: The performance guidance now explicitly says not to use the memberOf operator in dynamic group rules. It recommends direct comparisons such as -eq, -startsWith, and -in, explaining that transitive membership lookups can add significant processing complexity and, in large environments, lead to long evaluation times or unexpected results. Where possible, it suggests using a direct device property or an assignment filter instead.

keyChanges.title: EPM scope tags remain unsupported by two documented roles
keyChanges.detail: The known-issues page states that the built-in Endpoint Privilege Manager role and the custom Endpoint Privilege Management Policy Authoring role do not support scope tags. The documented workaround for restricting an administrator's view with scope tags is to grant permissions that include Read for Device configurations.

keyChanges.title: Apple token procedures now use the Apple enrollment tab
keyChanges.detail: The token-management procedure replaces the Intune Apple mobile tab with the Apple tab. For renewal, it now directs administrators to Apple Business's Devices and Management Services areas, or Apple School Manager's Preferences and Your MDM servers areas, then to the relevant service or server and Download Token; in Apple Business, Download Token is under the top-right Actions menu. This is a procedural and terminology clarification rather than evidence of a product behavior change.

2026-07-27.headline: Defender controlled configuration preview makes Intune authoritative for all applicable settings
2026-07-27.overview: Most of the 15 entries are documentation maintenance, but the most consequential Intune update documents Controlled Configuration for Microsoft Defender settings (preview). In the Windows Security experience Antivirus profile, the setting makes Intune—or Defender for Endpoint security settings management—the exclusive authority for configured Defender settings and applies secure defaults to unconfigured settings, addressing conflicts with Group Policy, Configuration Manager, third-party tools, and local scripts. The period also adds important Configuration Manager 2603 proxy guidance and expands the documented scope of the Properties Catalog and Windows Sync behavior. Controlled Configuration is explicitly marked preview; no supplied Message Center announcements, retirements, or general-availability notices change that status.
2026-07-27.adminImpact: Administrators evaluating Controlled Configuration should identify competing Defender management channels and choose deliberately among Not configured, Off (Default), Tamper Protection (On), and Controlled Configuration (On); the last gives Intune or Defender for Endpoint security settings management exclusive precedence. Configuration Manager 2603 sites using a proxy for Microsoft Entra token validation must configure it for the Local System account's WinINET settings, because site-system and WinHTTP-only proxies are not used. The Properties Catalog and Windows Sync updates primarily clarify documented scope and behavior rather than establish a dated product launch.

keyChanges.title: Controlled Configuration (Device) extends Defender protection beyond tamper protection
keyChanges.detail: The antivirus policy guidance now documents Controlled Configuration for Microsoft Defender settings (preview) in the Windows Security experience profile, under Defender, as the Controlled Configuration (Device) setting. It locks all applicable settings to Intune-configured values, while unconfigured settings use secure platform defaults. The documented values are Not configured, Off (Default), Tamper Protection (On), and Controlled Configuration (On); the last gives Intune-delivered settings exclusive precedence.

keyChanges.title: Properties Catalog guidance expands to registry values and application signals
keyChanges.detail: The revised article changes the documented scope from hardware information to device properties. It describes collecting selected Windows registry key values, such as configuration settings, application state, and security-posture signals, alongside hardware details, configuration data, and application signals. The prerequisites now state that the feature supports Windows devices managed by Intune, co-managed with Configuration Manager, Microsoft Entra joined, or Microsoft Entra hybrid joined.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager 2603 proxy validation requires Local System WinINET
keyChanges.detail: For Configuration Manager version 2603, Microsoft Entra token validation through MISE runs in the system (Local System) context using the .NET Framework HTTP stack. A management point using a proxy must therefore use the Local System account's WinINET settings. The updated guidance explicitly says that site-system proxy settings and a machine-wide WinHTTP proxy set with netsh winhttp set proxy are not used, and identifies ProxyEnable, ProxyServer, and optional ProxyOverride values or system-context Internet Options

keyChanges.title: Windows Sync is documented as a multi-workload on-demand action
keyChanges.detail: The Sync article now describes Windows synchronization as covering compliance evaluation, configuration policy processing, app detection and deployment-state updates, script and remediation processing, and other device-management signals. Administrators can track progress through the Device sync status tab. The article explicitly limits this described behavior and tab to Windows devices, making this a documentation clarification rather than evidence of a new sync command.

keyChanges.title: Intune servicing guidance warns against blocking ECS communication
keyChanges.detail: The servicing page now explains that Intune uses Experimentation and Configuration Service (ECS) for service configurations, controlled feature rollouts, and experimentation data. It cautions that disabling required Microsoft cloud-service communication can affect critical service updates, reliability improvements, security mitigations, and feature enablement. The page also states that Intune currently uses controlled feature rollout rather than experimental testing, with a Message Center announcement if that later

2026-07-28.headline: Security update for Configuration Manager console-extension imports resolves CVE-2026-47301
2026-07-28.overview: Both substantive changes clarify the same Configuration Manager security update: documentation for importing console extensions now explicitly identifies CVE-2026-47301 and states that the update resolves it. The supplied diffs do not indicate a new Intune tenant control, rollout deadline, prerequisite, or deployment procedure.
2026-07-28.adminImpact: Configuration Manager administrators should review KB 38232642 and assess the console-extension import security update for their environments. No tenant configuration change or additional administrator procedure is identified in the supplied evidence.

keyChanges.title: CVE-2026-47301 is now named in the console-extension import guidance
keyChanges.detail: The KB 38232642 article now states that the available Configuration Manager update, which enhances security for importing console extensions, resolves CVE-2026-47301. This is an explicit security-documentation clarification rather than evidence of a new Intune capability or changed tenant setting.

2026-07-29.headline: Configuration Manager’s SQL Server guidance now separates versions from required settings
2026-07-29.overview: The main development is a Configuration Manager documentation split, not a product feature launch. A new Supported configurations for SQL Server article now contains required and optional settings, while the existing versions article focuses on supported versions, editions, and compatibility levels. Related installation, prerequisite, international-support, database-replica, and LTSB links now point to the separated guidance. The other edits are largely mechanical: CVE-2026-47301 links lose the /en-US path, and a boundary-group procedure corrects “CGM SUP” to “CMG SUP.” Separately, an Intune Message Center notice recommends Windows KB5101684 Preview for full remediation of IT1431577.
2026-07-29.adminImpact: For Configuration Manager current-branch planning, installation, or upgrade work, consult both SQL Server articles: validate the supported version, edition, and compatibility level, then verify the required instance and database settings. The supplied changes do not announce a changed product support matrix or runtime behavior. If devices are affected by IT1431577, evaluate KB5101684 Preview through the organization’s normal pilot and validation process.

keyChanges.title: New article centralizes Configuration Manager SQL Server requirements
keyChanges.detail: The new reference article applies to Configuration Manager current branch and SQL Server installations used for site databases, including SQL Server Express. It specifies SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS for the SQL Server instance and site database, Windows authentication, and memory guidance: 50–80 percent of addressable system memory when SQL Server shares the site-server computer, 80–90 percent on a dedicated remote database server, with minimum buffer-pool reserves of 8 GB for central administration and primaryب?

keyChanges.title: Version guidance now covers editions and compatibility levels separately
keyChanges.detail: The updated Supported SQL Server versions article now covers supported versions, editions, and compatibility levels, while linking required settings to the new article. It also clarifies that only Database Engine Services is required, SQL Server replication is needed for database replicas for management points but not ordinary Configuration Manager database replication, and site databases require 64-bit SQL Server on a dedicated named or default instance.

keyChanges.title: Windows KB5101684 Preview is recommended for IT1431577 remediation
keyChanges.detail: An Intune Message Center notice recommends installing Windows cumulative update KB5101684 Preview to fully remediate the issue tracked as IT1431577. The notice describes a client fix and platform improvements; it is a preview-update recommendation, not a general-availability Intune feature announcement.

2026-07-30.headline: Service release 2607 adds Samsung Knox E-FOTA management for corporate Android
2026-07-30.overview: The substantive change is a new Intune integration with Samsung Knox E-FOTA in the week of July 27, 2026 service release 2607. The same release documentation adds Windows settings-catalog coverage and seven Microsoft Edge policy settings. Microsoft Tunnel updates are operational: one records a July 27 image release and another changes the documented Ubuntu host version. The remaining edits are largely editorial: the archive backfills earlier announcements, while the Azure Virtual Desktop page clarifies its Azure subscription and Entra ID relationship. No retirement, security advisory, or explicit GA designation appears in the supplied evidence.
2026-07-30.adminImpact: Samsung administrators can assess firmware-version targeting, unattended deployment, and scheduling for corporate-owned COSU, COBO, and COPE devices. Windows administrators should review the new catalog and Edge settings in the specified policy locations. Tunnel operators should compare version and image-digest records and verify the documented Ubuntu prerequisite before provisioning or rebuilding hosts; the evidence does not state that Ubuntu 22.04 hosts require immediate migration.

keyChanges.title: Samsung Knox E-FOTA enters the current Intune service-release documentation
keyChanges.detail: The Intune What's new entry says Intune now integrates with Samsung Knox E-FOTA, allowing administrators to control the firmware version assigned to each device, deploy updates without user interaction, and schedule downloads and installations. It applies to Android Enterprise corporate-owned dedicated (COSU), fully managed (COBO), and corporate-owned with a work profile (COPE) devices. The evidence identifies this as a service release 2607 addition but does not explicitly label it GA.

keyChanges.title: Windows settings catalog adds camera, Keyboard Filter, and WSL options
keyChanges.detail: New settings cover camera behavior, Keyboard Filter controls for Windows Insider devices, and Windows Subsystem for Linux. The documented path is Devices > Manage devices > Configuration > Create > New policy > Windows 10 and later > Settings catalog, and the entry applies to Windows 10 and Windows 11.

keyChanges.title: Edge administrative templates refresh to version 149
keyChanges.detail: The templates were refreshed to Microsoft Edge 149, version 149.0.4022.21, adding the latest Edge 148 and 149 policy settings. The named additions cover Local Fonts allow and block URL lists, M365 authentication popups in work profiles, MAM enrollment when Purview DLP is configured on the managed device, automatic Copilot contextual-insights panes for Outlook links, and Browsing with Copilot allow and block URL lists.
keyChanges.product: Intune — Microsoft Edge settings in the Windows settings catalog

keyChanges.title: Microsoft Tunnel upgrade notes record version 20260624.1
keyChanges.detail: The July 27, 2026 Tunnel release entry records version 20260624.1, agent image digest sha256:9a7316aaea439dd634b7e073dccc44977e2bb8cdbbf3245cc6288b7932334721, and server image digest sha256:fa286ab658830ded388d839b17420c13cf7fb076f806701d76d7e6867f83859b. The listed changes are minor bug fixes; no new Tunnel capability is described.

keyChanges.title: Microsoft Tunnel prerequisites now list Ubuntu 26.04 with Docker CE
keyChanges.detail: The prerequisites table replaces the Ubuntu 22.04 and Docker CE row with Ubuntu 26.04 and Docker CE. This is a documentation change to the stated host prerequisite; the supplied diff does not say that existing Ubuntu 22.04 deployments are retired or that an immediate upgrade is mandatory.

2026-08-06.headline: Firewall and ASR policy reports require security settings management for per-setting status
2026-08-06.overview: The period contained two Intune documentation updates. The substantive clarification concerns reporting for Firewall Rules and Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) Rules policies managed through MDM; the other change only renumbers steps in the Monitor Device Profile procedure.
2026-08-06.adminImpact: For MDM-managed Firewall Rules and ASR Rules policies, expect policy-level status rather than per-setting reporting. To view per-setting status, devices must be enrolled with Defender for Endpoint security settings management. The Monitor Device Profile edit does not indicate a tenant configuration or rollout change.

keyChanges.title: MDM Firewall and ASR reporting scope is clarified
keyChanges.detail: Per-setting reporting is available for most Endpoint Security policies, but Firewall Rules and ASR Rules policies managed through MDM report only policy-level status and omit per-setting statuses. The documentation states that devices must be enrolled with Defender for Endpoint security settings management to view per-setting status.

keyChanges.title: Monitor Device Profile procedure steps are renumbered
keyChanges.detail: The documented step directing admins to return to Device and user check-in status and select View report changes from step 5 to step 6, while the subsequent policy-property step changes from 6 to 7. The supplied diff shows a procedural numbering correction, not a product-behavior change.

2026-08-07.headline: Intune guidance details Graph approval coverage and RHEL 9.8 Tunnel requirements
2026-08-07.overview: The 7 August updates are documentation-led, but several carry operational weight. Intune’s Multi Admin Approval guidance now explicitly covers delegated actions and app-authenticated Graph calls; Tunnel prerequisites detail a manual kernel-module step for RHEL 9.8; and Collect Diagnostics publishes region-specific upload URLs. Configuration Manager also updates its SQL dependency guidance, while macOS ADE documentation flags a PSSO conflict for userless devices.
2026-08-07.adminImpact: Focus targeted reviews on Graph service principals and approver groups, RHEL 9.8 Tunnel hosts, firewall or network allowlists for diagnostics, Configuration Manager packaging that expects SQL support MSIs, and PSSO profile assignments to userless ADE devices. The evidence supports conditional action in these areas rather than a blanket tenant-wide change.

keyChanges.title: Multi Admin Approval guidance covers app-authenticated Graph calls
keyChanges.detail: The updated Intune guide documents MAA enforcement for delegated actions and app-authenticated Microsoft Graph API calls. Per-policy enterprise application exclusions apply only to app-auth calls, allow up to 50 applications, require second-admin approval, and are audited. Approver permissions and direct group membership are also clarified. Review service principals, scripts, third-party applications, and approver-group assignments against this documented scope.

keyChanges.title: Tunnel prerequisites call out manual ip_tables loading on RHEL 9.8
keyChanges.detail: The Microsoft Tunnel prerequisites now list RHEL 9.8 with Podman 5.8.2 or later as the default and explain that the ip_tables kernel module must be loaded manually before Tunnel installation. Administrators deploying Tunnel on RHEL 9.8 should complete that step before installation.

keyChanges.title: Collect Diagnostics adds regional blob URLs and a tenant geo lookup
keyChanges.detail: The Collect Diagnostics page now lists new blob storage URLs for each region and directs administrators to Tenant Status in endpoint.microsoft.com to identify their tenant’s geo and data center. Review network allowlists and firewall rules and permit the applicable URLs so diagnostics uploads succeed.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager guidance names SQL Server 2025 versions and missing MSIs
keyChanges.detail: The version 2603 guidance now states that SQLSysClrTypes.msi and SharedManagementObjects.msi are no longer included in Configuration Manager media. It also documents the move from deprecated SQL Server 2014 versions to SQL Server 2025 versions, including SMO 17. Administrators relying on those files should review packaging and dependency validation.

keyChanges.title: macOS ADE guidance flags PSSO conflicts on userless devices
keyChanges.detail: The automated macOS enrollment guidance warns against targeting userless ADE devices with profiles that enable PSSO registration during Setup Assistant. The combination can cause unexpected enrollment behavior and loss of expected device affinity. Review profile assignments for this configuration combination.

2026-08-11.headline: Endpoint security page date changes without altering Intune behavior
2026-08-11.overview: This was a quiet Intune period: the only change was a metadata refresh on the “Manage devices with endpoint security in Microsoft Intune” page. Its date changed from August 2, 2024, to August 10, 2026; no substantive content change is shown.
2026-08-11.adminImpact: No feature change, policy behavior change, or administrator action is supported by this diff.

keyChanges.title: Endpoint security guidance received a metadata-only date update
keyChanges.detail: The page metadata date changed from August 2, 2024, to August 10, 2026. The supplied diff shows no substantive content change, so this is ordinary documentation maintenance rather than a new capability, changed behavior, or required procedure.

2026-08-12.headline: Registry inventory guidance now flags sensitive configuration exposure and privacy risk
2026-08-12.overview: This was a quiet Intune period: one substantive documentation clarification adds security and privacy guidance for registry key inventory, while the other update only changes page metadata. No new feature, preview, retirement, or product behavior change is evidenced.
2026-08-12.adminImpact: Review who can access registry inventory and assess the security and privacy implications of exposing device configuration information. No administrator action is indicated for the metadata-only update.

keyChanges.title: Registry key inventory is documented as an accepted exposure risk
keyChanges.detail: The Collect Device Properties guidance now states that registry key inventory uses existing Device Inventory permissions and may expose sensitive device configuration information. It identifies the exposure as an accepted risk and calls for reviewing the related security and privacy implications.

keyChanges.title: Endpoint security page received a metadata-only date change
keyChanges.detail: The Manage devices with endpoint security in Microsoft Intune page date changed from 08/02/2024 to 08/10/2026. No substantive documentation or product change is shown, and no administrator action is indicated.

2026-08-13.headline: Intune plans higher Apple OS floors: iOS 18 and macOS 15 later this year
2026-08-13.overview: Microsoft announced two planned Intune support changes tied to Apple’s next major OS releases. After iOS/iPadOS 27 becomes available, Intune will require iOS/iPadOS 18 or later. After macOS Golden Gate 27 is released, Intune will support macOS 15 and later; existing devices on macOS 14.x or below will remain enrolled, but new enrollments on those versions will be blocked.
2026-08-13.adminImpact: Review Intune reports to identify incompatible iPhone, iPad, and Mac devices, then plan upgrades before the changes take effect. Pay particular attention to userless devices enrolled through Automated Device Enrollment, which have specific OS-version requirements. For Macs, upgrade devices on macOS 14.x or earlier before they need to be newly enrolled.

keyChanges.title: iOS/iPadOS support moves to version 18 or later
keyChanges.detail: After Apple releases iOS/iPadOS 27 later this year, Intune will require iOS/iPadOS 18 or higher. Administrators should check device compatibility and Intune reports, including the specific requirements for userless Automated Device Enrollment devices, and use Intune OS-version controls where appropriate.

keyChanges.title: macOS 15 becomes the supported enrollment baseline
keyChanges.detail: After macOS Golden Gate 27 releases later this year, Intune will support macOS 15 and later. Existing devices on macOS 14.x or below will remain enrolled, but new enrollments on those versions will no longer be allowed.

2026-08-14.headline: Intune sync guidance now covers iOS/iPadOS and multiple Windows workloads
2026-08-14.overview: The period is dominated by documentation clarification rather than a feature launch, preview announcement, general availability change, retirement, or confirmed service-behavior change. Sync guidance now describes policy, app, script, and remediation processing, extends the documented scope to iOS/iPadOS as well as Windows, and identifies the Device sync status tab for progress tracking. A separate Android Management API update clarifies the correct reporting location.
2026-08-14.adminImpact: For the documented sync improvements, enable the Preview new device view toggle in the Intune admin center. Use the Device sync status tab to monitor sync progress. For Android Management API reporting, go to Devices > Monitor and open the Personal Devices on Android Management API report; reporting is not shown in policy assignment status or the device configuration tab.

keyChanges.title: Sync guidance adds broader workload and device coverage
keyChanges.detail: The Sync page now states that selecting Sync triggers policy processing, app state updates, and scripts or remediations, with progress available in the Device sync status tab. The documented behavior applies to iOS/iPadOS and Windows devices, and the described improvements require the Preview new device view toggle.

keyChanges.title: Windows guidance documents combined MDM and IME check-ins
keyChanges.detail: The updated Windows Management Extension guidance says that Sync from Windows Settings or the Intune admin center initiates both MDM and IME check-ins, including policy, app, script, and remediation processing. Administrators can view progress in the Device sync status tab.

keyChanges.title: Android Management API reporting location is clarified
keyChanges.detail: Administrators are directed to the Personal Devices on Android Management API report under Devices > Monitor. The update explicitly says this reporting does not appear in the policy’s device assignment status or the device configuration tab.

2026-08-17.headline: Intune’s consolidated single-device page will replace the legacy view in September
2026-08-17.overview: Microsoft plans to make the new Intune single device page the default in the September (2609) release, replacing the legacy page. The new experience provides a consolidated device management view, while existing management features remain available.
2026-08-17.adminImpact: Administrators should familiarize themselves with the new interface and update internal documentation before the 2609 rollout. The announcement does not indicate that management capabilities are being removed or migrated.

keyChanges.title: New single device page becomes the default
keyChanges.detail: This is a planned default-view change: the new consolidated Intune device page will replace the legacy page in September (2609). Microsoft states that all management features remain available, but recommends preparation before the change.

2026-08-18.headline: Intune guidance now specifies 500 Wipe and separate 1,000 Retire and Delete daily caps
2026-08-18.overview: Intune’s device-action pages now spell out tenant-wide daily caps: 500 Wipe actions and 1,000 each for Retire and Delete. Individual, bulk, and Microsoft Graph submissions count cumulatively, while the Delete limit also applies when Delete triggers Retire or Wipe. Configuration Manager migration guidance explains how to retrieve existing MBAM groups with PowerShell and map them to equivalent BitLocker portal groups.
2026-08-18.adminImpact: Administrators running large device-action batches should plan against the tenant-wide limits and contact Microsoft Support if a limit change is needed. MBAM migration teams can reuse existing access groups by retrieving them with PowerShell and mapping them to equivalent Configuration Manager BitLocker portal groups instead of creating new mappings.

keyChanges.title: Wipe requests share a 500-action daily tenant limit
keyChanges.detail: The Wipe guidance now states that individual, bulk, and Microsoft Graph Wipe requests count toward a cumulative tenant-wide limit of 500 actions per day.

keyChanges.title: Retire requests share a 1,000-action daily tenant limit
keyChanges.detail: The Retire guidance now states that individual, bulk, and Microsoft Graph API requests count cumulatively toward a tenant-wide limit of 1,000 Retire actions per day.

keyChanges.title: Delete requests share a 1,000-action daily tenant limit
keyChanges.detail: The Delete guidance now states that individual, bulk, and Microsoft Graph requests count cumulatively toward 1,000 actions per day. The limit also applies when Delete triggers Retire or Wipe.

keyChanges.title: MBAM migration guidance adds PowerShell group mapping
keyChanges.detail: Configuration Manager guidance now explains how to retrieve existing MBAM groups with PowerShell and map them to equivalent BitLocker portal groups, allowing migrating administrators to reuse existing access groups.

2026-08-20.headline: Security Copilot agent pages add deprecation notice as Configuration Manager guidance consolidates
2026-08-20.overview: The clearest lifecycle signal is new deprecation language on Security Copilot’s Change Review Agent and Policy Configuration Agent pages. Configuration Manager diagnostic-usage guidance was consolidated for supported current branch versions, including removal of the standalone version 2509 reference.
2026-08-20.adminImpact: Administrators who rely on either Security Copilot agent should review the new deprecation notice when planning continued use; the supplied updates specify no deadline or required action. Configuration Manager administrators should use the consolidated current-branch diagnostic-data reference; no configuration change is stated.

keyChanges.title: Change Review Agent overview adds an agent deprecation notice
keyChanges.detail: The page now includes the deprecation notice while its Microsoft Intune admin center link remains unchanged. The supplied update does not specify a deadline or required administrator action.

keyChanges.title: Policy Configuration Agent page adds the same lifecycle notice
keyChanges.detail: The Intune page now includes an agent deprecation notice and retains the Intune admin center link. The diff specifies no required action or deadline.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager replaces version-specific diagnostic-data links
keyChanges.detail: The documentation now points to one consolidated article and states that diagnostic and usage-data collection is consistent across supported current branch versions.

keyChanges.title: The standalone Configuration Manager 2509 collection page is removed
keyChanges.detail: The 737-line reference covering version 2509 diagnostic and usage data was deleted as information moved into consolidated supported-current-branch guidance. No configuration change is stated.

2026-08-21.headline: Defender catch-up scan guidance distinguishes disabled defaults and two-miss triggers
2026-08-21.overview: Two device-security updates clarify Defender Antivirus catch-up scans for Intune and Configuration Manager tenant-attached devices. The guidance explains the inverse Yes/No semantics of settings named “Disable catch-up...”, documents different full- and quick-scan defaults, and specifies when catch-up scans run.
2026-08-21.adminImpact: Review Defender Antivirus policy values, particularly full-scan catch-up settings. In Intune, an unconfigured full-scan catch-up setting is documented as disabled while quick-scan catch-up remains enabled by default. The updates do not state that immediate administrator action is required.

keyChanges.title: Intune guidance clarifies inverse catch-up scan setting values
keyChanges.detail: For settings named “Disable catch-up...”, Yes disables catch-up scans and No enables them. Full-scan catch-up is disabled when not configured, while quick-scan catch-up is enabled by default; catch-up runs after two missed scheduled scans.

keyChanges.title: Tenant-attached Configuration Manager guidance changes the documented full-scan default
keyChanges.detail: The documented default for catch-up full scans is now disabled, while catch-up quick scans remain enabled by default. Catch-up scans require a configured scheduled scan and occur after two consecutive missed scheduled scans.

2026-08-25.headline: Vulnerability Remediation Agent guidance adds an Intune license prerequisite and tenant exception
2026-08-25.overview: The period’s most consequential guidance change concerns Security Copilot’s Vulnerability Remediation Agent: the agentic user must have an Intune license unless Allow admins without an Intune license is enabled under Tenant administration > Roles > Settings. Intune guidance also spells out tighter unattended-access role and endpoint prerequisites, replaces an Incident ID with log-collection status in Monitor, and removes one Diagnostic Endpoint from Microsoft Tunnel prerequisites.
2026-08-25.adminImpact: Validate the agentic user’s licensing or enable the named tenant setting. Review custom-role permissions and scopes for unattended access, verify that the required Remote Help endpoints are permitted in the network configuration, use collection status and verbose logs during troubleshooting, and refresh local Microsoft Tunnel references that include the removed endpoint.

keyChanges.title: Vulnerability Remediation Agent licensing prerequisite is now explicit
keyChanges.detail: Security Copilot guidance states that the agentic user must have an Intune license, unless Allow admins without an Intune license is enabled under Tenant administration > Roles > Settings. Check this prerequisite before relying on the agent.

keyChanges.title: Custom-role guidance separates Android unattended control from Windows remote sign-in
keyChanges.detail: The Intune custom-role guidance distinguishes Android unattended control, which requires a dedicated Intune-enrolled device, and adds Windows unattended remote sign-in for targeted physical corporate-owned devices. Both permissions must be explicitly assigned and scoped.

keyChanges.title: Remote Help Windows Remote Sign-in requires Azure Virtual Desktop session-host endpoints
keyChanges.detail: The Intune network-endpoints guidance now states that Remote Sign-in for Remote Help on Windows requires Azure Virtual Desktop session host endpoints. Administrators using unattended access should verify that these endpoints are permitted in their network configuration.

keyChanges.title: Monitor replaces Incident ID with log-collection status
keyChanges.detail: The Monitor guidance now shows whether log collection is completed, failed, or in progress instead of displaying an Incident ID. It also says Microsoft can use logs collected after an issue is reproduced during verbose log collection for investigation.

keyChanges.title: Microsoft Tunnel prerequisites drop powerlift-frontdesk.acompli.net
keyChanges.detail: The Prerequisites page no longer lists `powerlift-frontdesk.acompli.net` as a Diagnostic Endpoint. Administrators maintaining local Microsoft Tunnel log-collection guidance should remove the endpoint from those references.

2026-08-26.headline: Unattended Remote Help guidance and Apple DDM app controls headline Intune's August 26 updates
2026-08-26.overview: The highest-impact material is a Remote Help guidance expansion: unattended remote sign-in is now described for corporate Windows devices, with planning, security, and deployment boundaries. A new Apple DDM App Settings page covers supervised iOS/iPadOS 27+ and macOS 27+, while the assignment-filter deprecation and Android eSIM instructions provide concrete migration and operating rules. Most other changes are lower-impact reference additions covering Android settings applicability, enrollment panes, and inventory schema.
2026-08-26.adminImpact: If considering unattended Remote Help, review dedicated Intune-role permissions, Conditional Access, privacy, and enrollment constraints. The deployment guidance requires the Azure Virtual Desktop agent before the bootloader, with the bootloader configured to depend on the agent. Plan to migrate existing iOS app-launch restrictions from the Restrictions profile for iOS 27, use operatingSystemVersion for new assignment filters, and validate Android eSIM support, enrollment mode, OS version, carrier activation code, inventory-reported ICCID, and required permissions. Wipe guidance states that eSIMs are preserved by default on specified Android Enterprise corporate-owned devices and can be removed during a single-device wipe.

keyChanges.title: Remote Help documents unattended Windows remote sign-in
keyChanges.detail: The Windows guidance now covers initiating attended and unattended sessions from the Intune admin center. Remote sign-in lets an authorized helper troubleshoot a corporate Windows device with their own credentials without an end user present or signed in; unattended control is limited to Intune-enrolled Windows devices, and personal devices or devices missing prerequisites aren’t supported.

keyChanges.title: Apple DDM App Settings adds controls for OS 27 devices
keyChanges.detail: A new page documents Apple DDM App Settings configuration for supervised iOS/iPadOS 27+ and macOS 27+. Settings catalog controls include allowed or denied apps, binaries, and managed-app allowances. Existing iOS app-launch restrictions in the Restrictions profile must be migrated because those settings are deprecated in iOS 27.

keyChanges.title: Remote Help deployment guidance specifies the unattended Windows prerequisite chain
keyChanges.detail: The updated deployment guidance documents Windows unattended support and specifies a custom Intune role with required permissions, the Azure Virtual Desktop agent, and a bootloader as prerequisites. It directs administrators to deploy the agent before the bootloader and configure the bootloader to depend on the agent.

keyChanges.title: New assignment filters must replace the deprecated osVersion property
keyChanges.detail: The assignment-filter reference now marks osVersion as deprecated. New filters can’t use it, existing filters continue to work, and operatingSystemVersion is the replacement.

keyChanges.title: Android eSIM guidance adds activation and removal requirements
keyChanges.detail: Updated guidance covers activation and removal of eSIM plans on supported Android Enterprise corporate-owned devices. It specifies supported Android versions, a carrier activation code, an inventory-reported ICCID, and required permissions.

2026-08-27.headline: Windows Autopilot device association binds physical Windows 11 devices before enrollment
2026-08-27.overview: Windows Autopilot device preparation now supports TPM-backed device association: tenant affinity is written to UEFI before enrollment, allowing associated physical Windows 11 devices to receive device-targeted policies, naming, corporate marking, and additional OOBE customization. Related guidance covers prerequisites, the association workflow, removal, and automatic stale-record cleanup after 360 days. Elsewhere, Intune documents the Windows 365 for Agents 24H1 baseline, adds DDM controls to Apple VPP tokens, and covers enhanced log collection; Configuration Manager security guidance adds site-reset and secondary-site requirements.
2026-08-27.adminImpact: Autopilot administrators should validate Windows 11 physical-device, TPM 2.0, networking, licensing, and Intune RBAC prerequisites. Where personal enrollment is blocked, each device needs either a corporate identifier or device association before deployment; decommissioning requires MDM unenrollment and clearing Device Link UEFI variables before deleting the association. Baseline owners can review the documented defaults and CSP links before deploying or customizing. For Apple, DDM applies to iOS/iPadOS 18 and later and supports only Required or Uninstall assignments; enhanced log collection requires supervised macOS, iOS, or iPadOS 27+, remote-task permissions, and an AppleCare token. Configuration Manager operators on affected versions should install the security update through Updatesと及

keyChanges.title: TPM-backed association establishes Autopilot tenant affinity before enrollment
keyChanges.detail: Windows Autopilot device preparation now documents TPM-backed association that writes tenant affinity to UEFI before enrollment. The association enables device-targeted policies, device naming, OOBE customization, corporate marking, and stronger onboarding security.

keyChanges.title: Windows 365 for Agents gets a documented 24H1 security-baseline reference
keyChanges.detail: Intune now documents version 24H1 default settings for Cloud PCs running agentic workloads across Windows 11, Microsoft Edge, and Microsoft Defender for Endpoint, with linked CSP details for review.

keyChanges.title: Apple VPP tokens add DDM management for iOS and iPadOS 18+
keyChanges.detail: VPP token settings now offer a Management type of MDM, the default, or DDM. DDM applies to app deployment and configuration on iOS/iPadOS 18 and later and supports only Required or Uninstall assignments.

keyChanges.title: Intune documents enhanced log collection for supervised Apple devices
keyChanges.detail: A new Device Action article explains how to trigger and cancel remote enhanced log collection on supervised macOS 27+, iOS 27+, and iPadOS 27+ devices. Collected logs are sent directly to Apple for support analysis.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager security update carries site-reset and secondary-site requirements
keyChanges.detail: The update applies to Configuration Manager versions 2603, 2509, and 2503 with required rollups. Installation through Updates and Servicing requires a site reset, while existing secondary sites must be updated manually through Recover Secondary Site.

2026-08-28.headline: Tunnel Gateway guidance records version 20260818.1 as Configuration Manager metadata shifts
2026-08-28.overview: The period was dominated by a mechanical Configuration Manager documentation reclassification: 1,614 pages replace `ms.service: microsoft-endpoint-configuration-manager` with `ms.service: configuration-manager`. The meaningful Intune-specific update is the Microsoft Tunnel Gateway upgrade page, which now records version 20260818.1, agent and server image digests, and the August 18, 2026 release’s minor bug fixes, package updates, and security updates.
2026-08-28.adminImpact: Configuration Manager administrators don't need to change configuration; the metadata update affects classification and discoverability, with `ms.subservice: sdk` retained where stated. Tunnel administrators can use the recorded version and digests to track or verify server images and review the listed updates, but the supplied guidance specifies no required action.

keyChanges.title: Microsoft Tunnel Gateway page records 20260818.1 image and maintenance details
keyChanges.detail: The upgrade guidance now documents version 20260818.1, agent and server image digests, and minor bug fixes plus package and security updates for the August 18, 2026 release. Administrators can use the version and digests to track or verify Tunnel server images and review the changes.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager service metadata changes to configuration-manager
keyChanges.detail: Across the Configuration Manager update batch, pages move `ms.service` from `microsoft-endpoint-configuration-manager` to `configuration-manager`; the SMS_MigrationCollectionInfo reference explicitly retains `ms.subservice: sdk`. The effect is on Learn classification and discoverability, with no administrator action indicated.

2026-08-29.headline: Autopilot device preparation guidance details physical Windows 11 association before enrollment
2026-08-29.overview: The two updates concern one Windows Autopilot device-association capability. The guidance describes associating physical Windows 11 devices with an organization before enrollment, marking them corporate-owned and enabling device-targeted policies and naming. The related entry was moved from the general What's New page to Device preparation What's New.
2026-08-29.adminImpact: Administrators planning device association should use the Device preparation What's New page and review its linked requirements and setup guidance. Associated devices can be handled as corporate-owned and targeted with device policies and naming.

keyChanges.title: Physical Windows 11 devices can be associated before enrollment
keyChanges.detail: The Device preparation What's New guidance describes associating physical Windows 11 devices with an organization before enrollment. The associated devices are marked corporate-owned and can receive device-targeted policies and naming.

keyChanges.title: Device-association guidance moves to Device preparation What's New
keyChanges.detail: The device-association entry was removed from the general Windows Autopilot What's New page and moved to Device preparation What's New. The page date was changed to June 18, 2026, so administrators tracking this capability should consult the Device preparation page.

2026-09-01.headline: Autopilot guidance flags hybrid-join pre-provisioning failures when policies need domain controllers
2026-09-01.overview: The period was overwhelmingly mechanical: 863 of 873 updates were Configuration Manager entries, with representative pages standardizing documentation metadata from `core-infrastructure`/`microsoft-endpoint-configuration-manager` to `core-infra`/`configuration-manager`. The meaningful administrator-facing changes covered an Autopilot pre-provisioning failure condition, Remote Help licensing for Android COSU devices, and a more prominent Intune servicing warning.
2026-09-01.adminImpact: For Windows Autopilot hybrid-join pre-provisioning, avoid assigning policies that require domain controller connectivity during technician flow, particularly where a bring-your-own VPN is unavailable. For supported Zebra and Samsung Android Dedicated Device deployments, license Helpers for Remote Help; Sharers do not require a license. Review the Intune servicing note when assessing required Microsoft cloud-service communication.

keyChanges.title: Autopilot documents a hybrid-join pre-provisioning failure condition
keyChanges.detail: The Windows Autopilot known-issues guidance now explains that pre-provisioning for Microsoft Entra hybrid join can fail when policy conflict resolution requires domain controller connectivity, especially when a BYO VPN is unavailable during technician flow.

keyChanges.title: Remote Help licensing is clarified for Android COSU deployments
keyChanges.detail: Supported Zebra and Samsung devices running Android Dedicated Device (COSU) mode don't require a Sharer license; only the Helper needs a Remote Help license.

keyChanges.title: Intune servicing guidance raises its callout from Caution to Important
keyChanges.detail: The Servicing Information page changed the callout from Caution to Important. The message itself is unchanged: required Microsoft cloud-service communication can affect updates, reliability, security mitigations, and feature enablement.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager documentation adopts new service metadata identifiers
keyChanges.detail: Representative Configuration Manager pages now use `ms.subservice: core-infra` and `ms.service: configuration-manager` instead of `core-infrastructure` and `microsoft-endpoint-configuration-manager`. This is a documentation classification change with no specified administrator action.

2026-09-02.headline: Configuration Manager guidance details co-management limits and reporting gaps for Windows Update policies
2026-09-02.overview: The period’s main development is a rewritten Configuration Manager article covering co-management scenarios, scan-source policies, troubleshooting, and the effects of receiving Windows updates directly from Windows Update. The former Windows Update for Business article was deleted, while Advanced Analytics Device Query guidance tightens documented role requirements and Intune corrects the Microsoft Graph hostname for China environments.
2026-09-02.adminImpact: Review devices using Windows Update client policies because affected updates may appear as Unknown, with documented limitations for compliance reporting, Microsoft app updates, third-party updates, and software-update-based client deployment. Check Device Query custom-role assignments, use https://graph.chinacloudapi.cn for China connections, and replace bookmarks or references to the deleted Windows Update for Business article.

keyChanges.title: Windows Update client policies gain expanded co-management guidance
keyChanges.detail: The new Configuration Manager article covers co-management scenarios, scan-source policies, common pitfalls, troubleshooting, and the effects of receiving Windows updates directly from Windows Update. It notes potential Unknown status for affected updates and limitations involving compliance reporting, Microsoft app updates, third-party updates, and software-update-based client deployment.

keyChanges.title: Former Windows Update for Business guidance was deleted
keyChanges.detail: The article covering Windows Update client policies, co-management considerations, limitations, prerequisites, and client-identification procedures was removed. Administrators relying on it should locate the current guidance and update saved references.

keyChanges.title: Multi-device Device Query roles now require managed-device access
keyChanges.detail: Advanced Analytics guidance now describes custom roles as needing permissions to view and access managed devices, giving Organization/Read and Managed devices/Read as examples. The separate Managed Devices/Query permission is no longer listed.

keyChanges.title: Device Query guidance now requires a custom role
keyChanges.detail: The Device Query article now specifies that users must be assigned a custom role and no longer lists Help Desk Operator as a role option. Review assignments for administrators who need to use Device Query.

keyChanges.title: Intune’s China endpoint list switches Microsoft Graph hostnames
keyChanges.detail: The China endpoints page now lists https://graph.chinacloudapi.cn instead of https://graph.chinacloudapi.us. Update configurations or connection references that still use the previous hostname.

2026-09-16.headline: Intune will move Windows 11 health attestation to Azure Attestation by early 2027
2026-09-16.overview: Microsoft’s Message Center announced a planned Intune migration from Device Health Attestation to Microsoft Azure Attestation for Windows 11 devices. The change affects compliance evaluation for devices using health-based policies and introduces a network-access dependency on Azure Attestation endpoints.
2026-09-16.adminImpact: Administrators should plan to permit network access to the required Azure Attestation endpoints before the early 2027 migration. Without that access, Windows 11 devices using health-based policies may experience compliance-evaluation failures.

keyChanges.title: Windows Health Attestation is moving to Microsoft Azure Attestation
keyChanges.detail: Intune plans to migrate Windows Health Attestation from Device Health Attestation to Microsoft Azure Attestation by early 2027. Windows 11 devices using health-based compliance policies could fail compliance evaluation if they cannot reach Azure Attestation endpoints.

2026-09-17.headline: Intune will shift Windows Health Attestation compliance evaluation to Microsoft Azure Attestation
2026-09-17.overview: A Microsoft 365 Message Center notice announces that Intune will migrate Windows Health Attestation compliance evaluation from the current Device Health Attestation service to Microsoft Azure Attestation. The change is service-side and will occur automatically.
2026-09-17.adminImpact: The notice identifies no administrator procedure or customer-side action; administrators should understand this as an automatic Intune service migration.

keyChanges.title: Windows Health Attestation evaluation moves from DHA to MAA
keyChanges.detail: Intune will replace the current Device Health Attestation service with Microsoft Azure Attestation for Windows Health Attestation compliance evaluation. Microsoft describes the migration as an automatic, service-side change.

2026-09-24.headline: Security Copilot joins E5/E7 while Autopatch adds granular update approvals
2026-09-24.overview: The period brings two substantive Message Center announcements: Security Copilot is included with Microsoft 365 E5/E7 plans, while Windows Autopatch is rolling out more detailed control over update approvals and recovery management.
2026-09-24.adminImpact: Microsoft 365 E5/E7 organizations do not need to purchase or take action to receive Security Copilot, including monthly Security Compute Units and developer tools. Intune administrators can use the Autopatch enhancements to customize approvals, deferrals, and pauses for supported updates, with per-device reporting available as the rollout continues through October 15, 2026.

keyChanges.title: Security Copilot is included with Microsoft 365 E5/E7
keyChanges.detail: Security Copilot is now part of Microsoft 365 E5/E7, with agents integrated across Defender, Entra, Intune, Purview, and the Security Copilot portal. Included benefits are monthly Security Compute Units and developer tools; additional paid features remain available, and organizations can opt out through support.

keyChanges.title: Windows Autopatch expands update approval and recovery controls
keyChanges.detail: Enhancements rolling out from September 1 through October 15, 2026 add customizable automatic or manual approvals, deferral settings, update pausing, and per-device reporting for Windows quality, .NET Framework, and quick machine recovery updates.

2026-09-28.headline: Configuration Manager 2609 sets new SQL prerequisites and retires Asset Intelligence reporting
2026-09-28.overview: Configuration Manager 2609 is the clear story for this period. The version table records build 5.00.9152.1000 as released on 28 September 2026, with support through 28 March 2028, while the accompanying guidance establishes new SQL and ODBC gates, changes database-driver handling, removes Asset Intelligence surfaces, and narrows client support. The practical impact is concentrated in Configuration Manager infrastructure used alongside Intune.
2026-09-28.adminImpact: Before installing or updating to 2609, verify SQL Server 2017 CU2 or later, ODBC Driver 18.6.2.1 or later, and the documented incompatible-driver exclusions; unsupported versions can block setup. Confirm that secondary sites meet the SQL Server 2017 Express CU2 requirement and update the Visual C++ Redistributable where required. Review procedures that depend on SQL Server Native Client, inventory Asset Intelligence reporting dependencies and affected Windows Server 2012-era clients, and apply the version-specific TRUSTWORTHY instruction: omit it for 2609 and later, but retain it for 2603 and earlier.

keyChanges.title: ODBC Driver 18.6.2.1 and SQL Server 2017 CU2 become 2609 gates
keyChanges.detail: The prerequisite-check guidance requires ODBC Driver 18.6.2.1 or later for 2609 and later, and SQL Server 2017 CU2 or later starting with 2609. Unsupported versions can block installation or upgrades, and the page identifies incompatible ODBC releases.

keyChanges.title: 2609 installs Microsoft OLE DB Driver and drops SQL Server Native Client
keyChanges.detail: Starting in 2609, Configuration Manager automatically installs the Microsoft OLE DB Driver for SQL Server and no longer requires SQL Server Native Client. Configuration Manager 2603 and earlier retain the previous Native Client behavior.

keyChanges.title: Asset Intelligence home-page sections and reports are removed in 2609
keyChanges.detail: Catalog Synchronization and Inventoried Software Status are removed from the Asset Intelligence home page, along with Asset Intelligence reports. The earlier procedures apply only to 2603 and earlier; the updated page points administrators to the product lifecycle dashboard and Asset Intelligence client settings.

keyChanges.title: TRUSTWORTHY is no longer required for 2609 SQLCLR loading
keyChanges.detail: For 2609 and later, TRUSTWORTHY isn't needed to load Microsoft-signed SQLCLR assemblies, including databases using SQL Server Always On availability groups. Configuration Manager 2603 and earlier still require TRUSTWORTHY to be enabled.

keyChanges.title: Windows Server 2012 family leaves the 2609 client-support matrix
keyChanges.detail: Starting with Configuration Manager 2609, Windows Server 2012, Windows Server 2012 R2, and their Windows Storage Server editions are no longer supported as client operating systems.

2026-09-29.headline: VPP token reuse can erase available assignments, Intune guidance warns
2026-09-29.overview: The period is dominated by documentation consolidation, but several updates have direct operational value. Apple guidance now warns about losing available app assignments when an existing VPP token is re-uploaded for DDM, and clarifies that app configuration policies support MDM-managed apps only. New Intune guidance also documents device renaming, editable device properties, and inventory collection timing. Most other edits correct URLs or reflect the current device-overview action paths, such as Remove data > Retire and Secure > Rotate FileVault recovery key.
2026-09-29.adminImpact: Review Apple Business and Intune app-management procedures before changing token or app-management models. For device administration, use the new rename and Properties guidance, exclude hybrid-joined Windows devices from rename plans, and allow up to 24 hours for initial inventory collection. Follow the revised menu paths when performing documented device actions.

keyChanges.title: VPP guidance warns against re-uploading tokens for DDM
keyChanges.detail: The Manage VPP for Apple guidance says re-uploading an existing VPP token for DDM causes available app assignments to be lost. It recommends creating a new Apple Business token for DDM, while using MDM for available assignments and apps that require app configuration policies. Administrators should not re-upload tokens that already have available assignments.

keyChanges.title: iOS and iPadOS app configuration is documented as MDM-only
keyChanges.detail: The managed iOS guidance now states that app configuration policies support only MDM-managed apps and cannot configure DDM apps. The setup procedure was also renumbered, so DDM apps requiring this configuration path need a different management approach.

keyChanges.title: New guidance documents device renaming rules and limitations
keyChanges.detail: The new rename-device article covers renaming managed devices from the Intune admin center, supported platforms, platform-specific naming rules, and bulk-renaming variables. It explicitly documents that hybrid-joined Windows devices aren't supported, which should be accounted for when standardizing inventory names.

keyChanges.title: New Properties guidance covers editable device metadata
keyChanges.detail: A new article explains how to edit a managed device's name, ownership, primary user, notes, and scope tags from the Properties tab. Scope-tag changes affect device visibility for delegated administrators, while the primary-user workflow is now documented alongside the other editable properties.

keyChanges.title: Inventory guidance sets a 24-hour initial collection window
keyChanges.detail: The Collect device properties guidance now says active devices collect inventory multiple times per day, while initial collection can take up to 24 hours because full synchronization runs once daily. Administrators should allow that window before treating missing initial inventory as a problem.

2026-09-30.headline: Intune iOS enrollment requires the deprecated computer-sync setting set to No
2026-09-30.overview: The period contains five updated pages and no new or removed items. The most consequential Intune change is enrollment guidance requiring Run Company Portal in Single App Mode until authentication to be set to No; the page says Apple deprecated Sync with computers in iOS 13 and that it is no longer included in enrollment policies. Other updates clarify Managed Google Play onboarding scope, macOS PKG retry behavior, and Managed Home Screen terminology, while a Configuration Manager matrix adds Windows 11 26H2 support indicators.
2026-09-30.adminImpact: Set Run Company Portal in Single App Mode until authentication to No in applicable iOS enrollment policies. For other changes, account for required app installation on dedicated devices and up to three retries for failed macOS app installations while the app remains assigned. Use the updated Configuration Manager matrix when evaluating Windows 11 26H2 support.

keyChanges.title: iOS enrollment setting is marked for removal
keyChanges.detail: The updated Setup Automated iOS guidance says Run Company Portal in Single App Mode until authentication must be set to No. It also records that Apple deprecated Sync with computers in iOS 13 and that the setting is no longer included in enrollment policies; administrators should apply No in applicable policies.

keyChanges.title: macOS PKG guidance documents repeated installation retries
keyChanges.detail: Failed macOS app installations are retried at the next agent check-in, with up to three retries while the app remains assigned. Administrators should account for these attempts when monitoring deployment failures.

keyChanges.title: Managed Google Play onboarding guidance includes dedicated devices
keyChanges.detail: During onboarding, Intune, Microsoft Authenticator, and Company Portal are installed as required apps on dedicated devices, in addition to fully managed and corporate-owned work profile devices. Dedicated-device administrators should expect these installations, which support Conditional Access.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager matrix lists Windows 11 26H2
keyChanges.detail: The Support for Windows 11 matrix now lists Windows 11 version 26H2, build 10.0.26300, with support indicators shown as ❌, ✅, and ✅. Administrators can use the revised matrix when evaluating 26H2 support.

keyChanges.title: Managed Home Screen setting now uses the full product name
keyChanges.detail: The app-exclusion setting description spells out Managed Home Screen instead of using MHS when referring to authentication, making the applicable setting easier to identify.

2026-10-01.headline: Apple OS 27 inventory and MEFERI OEMConfig join Intune’s planned changes
2026-10-01.overview: Intune’s updated In Development page now lists Apple OS 27 DDM inventory data, MEFERI OEMConfig support for Android Enterprise, removal of legacy Apple MDM software-update workloads, and two Administrator protection settings for Windows 11 24H2 and 25H2. A separate Managed Home Screen update revises wording around excluding apps from the silence setting and changes authoring metadata.
2026-10-01.adminImpact: Administrators should track the planned inventory, OEMConfig, Apple software-update, and Windows Account Protection changes; no action or deadline is stated. The Managed Home Screen wording update indicates no administrator action.

keyChanges.title: Apple OS 27 and MEFERI support appear on the development roadmap
keyChanges.detail: The In Development page now lists Apple OS 27 DDM inventory data and MEFERI OEMConfig support for Android Enterprise. It also identifies removal of legacy Apple MDM software-update workloads and two Administrator protection settings for Windows 11 24H2 and 25H2.

keyChanges.title: Managed Home Screen updates the silence-setting exclusion guidance
keyChanges.detail: The Configure Managed Home Screen page revises the description for excluding apps from the silence setting and changes its authoring metadata. No administrator action is indicated.

2026-10-02.headline: EPM system-settings policy covers controlled IPv4, IPv6, and DNS changes
2026-10-02.overview: The period’s most consequential update centers on Endpoint Privilege Management’s Elevation system settings policy, which documents how standard Windows users can make selected network changes under administrator-defined controls. Intune guidance also tightens Android reset and factory reset protection expectations, while Advanced Analytics documents unavailable device identifiers.
2026-10-02.adminImpact: EPM administrators can delegate IPv4, IPv6, and DNS changes while requiring confirmation, business justification, Windows authentication, or both; an EPM elevation settings policy must be enabled. Android administrators should review Factory reset protection emails configuration and Android 15 post-reset account re-entry requirements. Analytics consumers should account for unavailable ICCID and SimInfo data in the documented device populations.

keyChanges.title: EPM documents controlled network-setting delegation
keyChanges.detail: A new Endpoint Privilege Management page describes policies that let standard Windows users change IPv4, IPv6, and DNS settings. Administrators can require confirmation, business justification, Windows authentication, or both, and devices need an EPM elevation settings policy enabled.

keyChanges.title: Android reset guidance links FRP enforcement to email configuration
keyChanges.detail: The Corporate Methods guidance states that Settings resets don’t enforce factory reset protection when Factory reset protection emails is Not configured. For Android 15 devices with a configured Google account email, the account must be re-entered after the reset.

keyChanges.title: Advanced Analytics records ICCID and SimInfo data limitations
keyChanges.detail: The schema reference now states that ICCID isn’t supported on Windows. It also continues to specify that SimInfo isn’t supported for Android Enterprise personally owned devices with a work profile.

2025-12-29.headline: Cloud-native Windows tutorial removes its Windows in cloud configuration comparison
2025-12-29.overview: This was a quiet Intune period with one documentation-only update. The Cloud Native Windows Endpoints tutorial removed its tip linking to Windows in cloud configuration, the table contrasting the two approaches, and the Windows 10 support callout. The edit does not indicate a product, policy, or configuration-behavior change.
2025-12-29.adminImpact: Administrators evaluating cloud-native Windows deployments should use the linked solution documentation directly to decide between creating a custom configuration and using Windows in cloud configuration. Existing deployments are not identified as requiring changes.

keyChanges.title: Comparison guidance removed from the cloud-native Windows tutorial
keyChanges.detail: The tutorial no longer includes the Microsoft-recommended, standardized-solution tip; the comparison table stating that the tutorial helps administrators create their own configuration while Windows in cloud configuration applies a pre-built configuration for frontline, remote, and other focused-use workers; or the note that the two approaches can be combined. The Windows 10 support include was also removed. This is an ordinary documentation change, not evidence of changed Intune functionality.

2026-01-05.headline: Entra-registered devices remain limited to Windows update rings
2026-01-05.overview: Windows Update policy and reporting content was extensively reorganized this week, but the consequential guidance is specific: Windows Update for Business Deployment Service-backed policies exclude Microsoft Entra-registered devices, Hotpatch has a defined eligibility chain, and driver approvals have documented constraints. Outside Windows servicing, Configuration Manager's MDT retirement carries an immediate cleanup sequence, while a February Intune release will extend Managed Home Screen permissions in built-in roles.
2026-01-05.adminImpact: Prioritize the documented Windows Update eligibility and prerequisite checks, and remove MDT task-sequence steps before removing MDT integration. Driver administrators should use staged deployment rings and avoid conflicting policies. The Managed Home Screen change requires no action, although role assignments and internal documentation may merit review. Treat ordinary retitles, link moves, and prerequisite consolidation as documentation maintenance. Also, removal of the “public preview” label from the Admin Tasks article does not establish general availability; the in-development page still says the capability will soon be generally available.

keyChanges.title: WUfB DS-backed update policies exclude Microsoft Entra-registered devices
keyChanges.detail: The Windows updates overview now states that Feature updates, Quality updates, Driver updates, and Hotpatch policies rely on the Windows Update for Business Deployment Service and aren't supported on Microsoft Entra-registered devices. Those devices remain supported through Windows Update client policies and update rings. This is a documented eligibility boundary, not a newly announced enforcement change.

keyChanges.title: Hotpatch guidance ties eligibility to Autopatch, Windows 11 24H2, and VBS
keyChanges.detail: The dedicated quality-update guidance documents Hotpatch as Monthly B release security updates that install and take effect without a restart. It lists Autopatch, Windows 11 Enterprise version 24H2 or later, the latest baseline release, an Intune quality update policy with Hotpatch enabled, and VBS turned on among the prerequisites. This adds concrete deployment guidance rather than announcing a new Hotpatch launch.

keyChanges.title: Driver FAQ documents approval conflicts, Autopilot, filters, and rollback limits
keyChanges.detail: The driver-update FAQ states that Driver Updates don't support Assignment Filters or Windows Autopilot, and that Windows Update client policies don't support driver rollback. Multiple policies per device are supported but not recommended: if one policy approves an update and another pauses it, the approved status wins and the driver installs. The guidance points to small deployment rings and manual approval or monitoring for safer rollout.

keyChanges.title: MDT retirement requires task-sequence cleanup before integration removal
keyChanges.detail: Configuration Manager release notes now warn that Microsoft Deployment Toolkit integration and MDT Standalone are retired and unsupported. Administrators must remove all MDT task-sequence steps first and then remove MDT integration to prevent task-sequence corruption and modification failures; Windows Autopilot or supported Configuration Manager OSD are suggested alternatives.

keyChanges.title: Managed Home Screen adds two permissions to built-in roles in February
keyChanges.detail: The planned February Intune release adds TemporarilySuspendManagedHomeScreen and RestoreManagedHomeScreen to the School Administrator and Help Desk Operator built-in roles. Microsoft says no administrator action is required, but organizations using those roles should review role assignments and update their internal permissions documentation.

2026-01-12.headline: Windows quality-update guidance now separates expedite, hotpatch, and ordinary servicing
2026-01-12.overview: This was a documentation-heavy week, with the most consequential guidance concentrated in Windows update administration. Revised Intune articles distinguish standard monthly servicing from quality-update policies, targeted expedite policies, and hotpatch, while also documenting feature-update rollout constraints, a Win32 PowerShell installer path, Edge policy conflicts, and a local Autopilot Reset issue. The supplied evidence contains no Message Center item and does not establish preview, general-availability, or capability-retirement status.
2026-01-12.adminImpact: Audit Windows update designs against the clarified division: retain update rings and Windows Update client policies for ordinary servicing, deferrals, deadlines, restarts, and notifications; use quality-update policies for cloud orchestration, Autopatch-managed deployments, hotpatch, or reporting, and expedite policies for targeted urgent updates. For gradual feature rollouts, verify the timing and cloud-processing prerequisite. For Win32 scripts, observe the 50 KB, silent-execution, return-code, and Multi-Admin Approval constraints. Review Edge policy assignments and any Autopilot devices that depend on local reset.

keyChanges.title: Quality-update guidance separates routine servicing from targeted scenarios
keyChanges.detail: The revised Quality Updates article says devices do not need a Windows quality updates policy to continue receiving monthly quality updates through standard Windows Update behavior. Update rings and Windows Update client policies continue to control deferrals, deadlines, restarts, and notifications. Create a quality-update policy when cloud-based orchestration, Windows Autopatch-managed deployments, hotpatch, or policy-based reporting is required; use an expedite policy instead when accelerating one specific update

keyChanges.title: Gradual feature-update rollouts get concrete timing and prerequisite rules
keyChanges.detail: The rollout guidance specifies that the first offer-group date must be at least two days in the future. Devices are assigned randomly and evenly, with a minimum of 100 devices per group; changing dates or spacing recalculates groups for devices that have not yet received the offer. Intelligent rollouts require a Settings Catalog profile enabling Allow Windows Update for Business Cloud Processing, assigned to the same groups as the feature-update policy. This is procedural and prerequisite guidance, not a stated GA或

keyChanges.title: Win32 app guidance documents a PowerShell-script installer path
keyChanges.detail: The Win32 app procedure now documents two installer types: Command line and PowerShell script. A script replaces the standard install command, is packaged with the app content, runs in the same system or user context as the installer, should run silently, is limited to 50 KB, and uses its return code to determine installation status. With Multi-Admin Approval enabled, scripts cannot be uploaded during app creation; create the app first, then add or modify the script. The documentation does not state preview or GA‌

keyChanges.title: Edge for Business guidance sets enrollment-based policy boundaries
keyChanges.detail: The Edge for Business guidance directs administrators to use App Configuration Policies for non-enrolled devices. For enrolled Windows devices, choose either Settings Catalog policies or the Microsoft Edge Security Baseline, not both. It also warns that deploying App Configuration Policies and Settings Catalog policies targeting the same client creates conflicts. This is an administration and security-guidance clarification, not evidence that the Edge security baseline capability was retired.

keyChanges.title: Autopilot known issue links local reset to a network-denial setting
keyChanges.detail: The Windows Autopilot known-issues page records that a local Windows administrator cannot start local Windows Autopilot Reset when an Intune policy sets “Deny access to this computer from the network” for the Local account. The documented workaround is to remove that setting or exclude devices that require local Autopilot Reset; the issue remains under investigation.

2026-01-19.headline: Require approved client app retires in June; switch to application protection policy
2026-01-19.overview: The biggest admin signal is the June 2026 retirement of Microsoft Entra Conditional Access's **Require approved client app** control; a second Message Center notice says Microsoft Defender for Android will stop protecting personal profiles on enrolled devices by March 2026. The 63-record period was otherwise mostly documentation maintenance, but it also records OS enforcement for **Install Windows quality updates** in the `2026-01 B` quality update and clarifies scalar-property rules for Advanced Analytics Device Query. New Managed Home Screen pages document suspend and restore procedures for Android Enterprise corporate-owned Fully Managed and Dedicated devices; the supplied evidence does not establish a preview or general-availability launch.
