2026-01-19.adminImpact: Before June 2026, find Conditional Access policies using **Require approved client app** and replace the control with **Require application protection policy**; after retirement, the old control will no longer be enforceable. No admin action is required for the Defender scope change, which doesn't affect corporate work profiles or unenrolled devices. If you use Device Query, change scalar operators to use properties such as `Device.SerialNumber` or `Device.OSVersion`. For normal Windows update deployment, follow the recommended Update rings, Feature updates, or Quality updates path rather than packaging `.msu` files as Win32 apps; use the Win32 method only when granular control is needed. Teams migrating from Basic Mobility and Security should use the revised license-assignment and policy-

keyChanges.title: Conditional Access control has a June 2026 retirement deadline
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft says the **Require approved client app** control will retire in June 2026 and will no longer be enforceable. Organizations should update affected policies to use **Require application protection policy** for equivalent and enhanced protection. This is a Message Center retirement notice.

keyChanges.title: Defender for Android drops enrolled personal-profile protection
keyChanges.detail: By March 2026, Microsoft Defender for Android will end support for protecting personal profiles on enrolled devices and focus solely on securing corporate work profiles. Work profiles and unenrolled devices are unaffected, and Microsoft says no admin action is required.

keyChanges.title: Windows quality-update enforcement is tied to 2026-01 B
keyChanges.detail: In the Enrollment Status Page guidance, the **Install Windows quality updates** statement changed from saying the setting was available but not yet enforced by the OS, with enforcement planned for `2026-01 B`, to saying OS enforcement is included in the `2026-01 B` quality update. This updates the documented enforcement status rather than announcing a new policy setting.

keyChanges.title: Advanced Analytics requires scalar properties in Device Query operators
keyChanges.detail: The Device Query reference now says the `Device` entity cannot be used directly in scalar-requiring operators such as `distinct`, `summarize`, and `order by`. Administrators should use a specific scalar property instead, such as `Device.SerialNumber` or `Device.OSVersion`. This is a query limitation clarification.

keyChanges.title: Intune now recommends Windows Update policies over Win32 .msu packages
keyChanges.detail: The updated Windows update package guidance explicitly says deploying an `.msu` file as a Win32 app isn't the recommended approach and points administrators to Update rings, Feature updates, and Quality updates. Win32 deployment remains an option when more granular control is needed; this is operational guidance, not a change to the Win32 capability.

2026-01-26.headline: Cloud PKI expiry guidance requires issuing CA replacement and SCEP updates
2026-01-26.overview: The week was dominated by mechanical Learn maintenance, particularly Configuration Manager reference and navigation updates, rather than service announcements. The meaningful exceptions were a customer-managed Cloud PKI expiration procedure, a Windows Autopilot device preparation limit increase, clearer Endpoint Privilege Management child-process behavior, and refreshed Windows MAM guidance. New Cloud PKI deployment, audit, and lifecycle pages appear alongside removals of older pages with matching content, which indicates documentation reorganization rather than a documented capability retirement. No Message Center items were supplied.
2026-01-26.adminImpact: Inventory Cloud PKI issuing CAs and the SCEP profiles that reference them. For an expiring CA, the documented path is to create a replacement with the same Root CA Source and matching Extended Key Usages and key sizes, then replace the SCEP URI in each profile; do not add a second URI, and remember that changing the URI does not trigger certificate reissuance. Review Autopilot deployment timeouts before assigning up to 25 apps, audit EPM rules for applications that can launch shells or script engines, and verify that Windows Security Center MTD connector targets run Windows 11 version 22631 (23H2) or later. Use the Cloud PKI audit guidance when validating required roles, licensing, Graph tokens, and permissions.

keyChanges.title: Cloud PKI expiration guidance makes CA replacement customer-managed
keyChanges.detail: The new Cloud PKI CA expiration guidance says Microsoft can't automatically update a CA or its SCEP profiles. If an issuing CA expires, profiles that reference it stop issuing new certificates, potentially causing loss of Wi-Fi, VPN, or email connectivity, resource access failures, and certificate-based authentication failures. Administrators must create a new issuing CA using the same Root CA Source, match Extended Key Usages and key sizes, and replace the SCEP URI in every affected profile. Cloud PKI doesn't支持-

keyChanges.title: Autopilot device preparation limit increases to 25 apps
keyChanges.detail: Windows Autopilot device preparation guidance records a maximum of 25 apps, up from 10. The change applies to both user-driven and automatic modes, including all Cloud PC offerings. Administrators assigning more apps during OOBE are told to adjust deployment timeout settings to help avoid unexpected timeouts.

keyChanges.title: EPM guidance exposes child-process elevation paths that bypass deny rules
keyChanges.detail: Endpoint Privilege Management guidance now explicitly distinguishes Require rule to elevate, Deny all, and Allow child processes to run elevated. In the allow mode, child processes automatically run elevated and rule evaluation is skipped, including deny rules. Microsoft recommends avoiding overly broad elevation rules for applications that can launch other processes, such as command shells or script engines.

keyChanges.title: Windows MAM guidance marks App Protection Conditional Access generally available
keyChanges.detail: The refreshed Windows Mobile Application Management prerequisites label App Protection Conditional Access as generally available and replace older fixed build references with the supported Windows versions page. They also state that the Mobile Threat Defense Connector for the Windows Security Center component is supported only on Windows 11 version 22631 (23H2) or later. The diff establishes the documented status and prerequisite, but does not provide a separate launch date.

keyChanges.title: Cloud PKI audit guidance specifies CA, certificate actions and prerequisites
keyChanges.detail: The new audit-log article lists actions including creating, searching, retrieving, updating, and deleting CAs; searching and revoking leaf certificates; uploading externally signed CA certificates; changing CA status; and revoking CA certificates. It directs administrators to Tenant Administration > Audit Logs or Microsoft Graph and lists a Cloud PKI license, Intune service administrator role, Graph access token, and DeviceManagementApps.Read.All or DeviceManagementApps.ReadWrite.All permissions as prerequisites.

2026-02-02.headline: Endpoint Privilege Management support for AVD single-session remains in development
2026-02-02.overview: The clearest service-status signal is that Intune Endpoint Privilege Management (EPM) support for users on Azure Virtual Desktop single-session virtual machines is described as being added, with no availability date or general-availability claim. The rest of the supplied evidence is overwhelmingly documentation work: five new Apple configuration pages cover custom settings, device features, restrictions, VPN, and Wi-Fi; Windows Autopilot marks a device-preparation known issue resolved in February 2026; and Remote Help adds a notification-policy troubleshooting condition. Of 248 changes, 243 were updates and no Message Center items were supplied. Several Apple enrollment pages also move links from iOS-only references to Apple-wide restriction and device-feature pages, which is navigation maintenance rather than a reported settings change.
2026-02-02.adminImpact: Do not plan on EPM support for AVD single-session as generally available; the in-development text provides no release date. Apple administrators should review the new profile guidance before using custom profiles: it says not to place sensitive Wi-Fi or authentication information in custom profiles and to use built-in Wi-Fi and certificate profiles instead. The Apple Device Features reference also says all AirPrint printers must be placed in one profile. Autopilot teams tracking the resolved known issue can update runbooks and retest, but the supplied diff does not identify the issue. Remote Help administrators need to consult Policy CSP - Notifications only when the notification-blocking symptom occurs. The Autopilot entries that only change collection metadata and the Apple link updates3

keyChanges.title: EPM on AVD single-session is an in-development capability, not a dated release
keyChanges.detail: The Intune in-development page says Microsoft is adding support to deploy Endpoint Privilege Management policies to users on Azure Virtual Desktop single-session virtual machines. It says EPM elevation policies will work in that environment when the support becomes available, and identifies EPM as an Intune Suite add-on capability. No availability date or general-availability status is provided.

keyChanges.title: Custom Apple profiles get explicit prerequisites and sensitive-data guidance
keyChanges.detail: A new Intune article documents custom profiles for iOS/iPadOS and macOS to add settings and features that are not built into Intune. It lists the minimum Policy and Profile Manager RBAC role. Its displayed device-configuration prerequisite is to create a VPN device configuration profile. The article also says not to use custom profiles for sensitive information such as Wi-Fi connections or authenticating apps; it directs administrators to built-in Wi-Fi and certificate profiles instead. This is new documentation, ￼

keyChanges.title: Apple device features reference records a one-profile AirPrint limitation
keyChanges.detail: The new Device Features reference covers iOS/iPadOS and macOS features including AirPrint, home screen layout, notifications, shared devices, single sign-on, and web content filtering. It explicitly says to add all printers to the same profile because Apple prevents multiple AirPrint profiles from targeting the same device. The page also identifies the Policy and Profile Manager RBAC role and a device-features configuration profile as prerequisites. This is reference guidance, not evidence of a feature release.

keyChanges.title: Windows Autopilot marks a device-preparation known issue resolved
keyChanges.detail: The Windows Autopilot known-issues page changed its date from November 10, 2025, to February 5, 2026, added “Date updated: February 5, 2026,” and states, “This issue was resolved in February 2026.” The supplied diff does not identify the issue or prescribe a configuration change, so affected deployment teams should validate their previously impacted workflow rather than alter Autopilot broadly.

keyChanges.title: Remote Help adds notification blocking to its troubleshooting path
keyChanges.detail: A new troubleshooting row identifies “The device has blocked applications from using notifications” and points administrators to Policy CSP - Notifications, specifically the disallowcloudnotification setting. This clarifies diagnosis for that symptom; it does not document a change to Remote Help policy behavior.

2026-02-09.headline: Endpoint Privilege Management reaches AVD single-session users, with all-user approval guidance
2026-02-09.overview: Endpoint Privilege Management carries the clearest product story this week: service-release notes add support for users on Azure Virtual Desktop single-session virtual machines, while updated support-approved guidance says elevation requests can come from any device user rather than only the primary user. Other consequential changes affect report populations, Hybrid Entra join Autopilot reliability, and Microsoft Connected Cache for co-managed Intune Win32 apps. The period was otherwise documentation-heavy; the Defender vulnerability article is a guidance clarification that now uses Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management terminology and spells out prerequisites, not evidence of a newly launched integration.
2026-02-09.adminImpact: AVD administrators using EPM can assess deployment to single-session VMs, and EPM support-approved workflows should account for requests from non-primary users. Reporting owners should expect possible lower counts from late February when devices inactive for 12 or more months are excluded; Microsoft says no action is required, but devices must check in to remain in reports. For affected Autopilot deployments, verify that the relevant OS build includes the listed KB. Co-managed sites that see an internet-based DownloadURL for Intune Win32 content should follow the Connected Cache hotfix procedure. For Defender remediation, verify the newly documented Intune Plan 1, Defender for Endpoint, connection, onboarding, and risk-assessment prerequisites before rollout.

keyChanges.title: New EPM support covers AVD single-session virtual machines
keyChanges.detail: Service release 2601 states that Endpoint Privilege Management elevation policies now support deployment to users on Azure Virtual Desktop single-session virtual machines. This is a new capability listed under the Microsoft Intune Suite.

keyChanges.title: Support-approved EPM guidance now includes all users of a device
keyChanges.detail: The updated guidance says support-approved elevation requests can be submitted by all users of a device and are not limited to its primary user. This changes the documented prior limitation; the supplied update does not provide a separate rollout date.

keyChanges.title: Intune will exclude devices inactive for 12 months from reports
keyChanges.detail: Starting in late February 2026, Intune will exclude devices inactive for 12 or more months from reports. Reported device counts may decrease, and Microsoft says no action is needed; devices must check in to remain in reports.

keyChanges.title: Hybrid Entra join Autopilot timeouts get OS-specific fixes
keyChanges.detail: A February 9 Known Issues entry says Microsoft Entra hybrid join Autopilot deployments might time out with error 0x80004005. The issue is resolved by KB5065789 or later for Windows 11, version 25H2; KB5065426 or later for 24H2; and KB5070312 or later for 23H2.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager hotfix targets co-managed Intune Win32 downloads
keyChanges.detail: New version 2603 guidance addresses Microsoft Connected Cache not being used as expected for Win32 apps deployed through Intune in a co-managed environment, where IntuneManagementExtension.log shows an internet-based DownloadURL. The procedure uses DoincInstall.exe version 1.5.5.9002, temporarily disables and re-enables MCC on affected distribution points, or uses resetdps.trn for large sites. The page lists Configuration Manager versions 1910 through 2603 as prerequisites.

2026-02-16.headline: KB36495448 fixes co-managed update-source drift as Intune EPM scope is clarified
2026-02-16.overview: Most of the week’s 87 records are documentation maintenance—renamed headings, normalized terminology, link and example replacements, and formatting. The substantive exceptions are a new Configuration Manager client hotfix article, Connected Cache HTTPS guidance, explicit Intune Endpoint Privilege Management licensing and Windows scope, an iOS/iPadOS enrollment MFA limitation, and expanded Multi Admin Approval coverage. There are no Message Center entries and no retirement record, so the supplied evidence does not establish a new preview or general-availability launch.
2026-02-16.adminImpact: Prioritize co-managed Configuration Manager estates that use third-party updates by assessing KB36495448 and its documented scan-source cleanup. If Connected Cache HTTPS delivery is relevant, prepare a valid client-trusted TLS certificate through organizational PKI. Intune administrators should verify EPM add-on licensing and Windows-only targeting, provide an alternate MFA method for modern-authentication Automated Device Enrollment on iOS/iPadOS, and review Multi Admin Approval governance for compliance and Settings Catalog policy workflows. The evidence does not support tenant action for purely editorial changes or treat these documentation updates as launch announcements.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager documents KB36495448 for co-managed update-source drift
keyChanges.detail: The new hotfix article covers Configuration Manager 2503 with update rollup 32851084 and version 2509 when third-party updates are enabled. It describes a partial Windows Update scan-source policy in which UseUpdateClassPolicySource and SetPolicyDrivenUpdateSourceForOtherUpdates could be set while related Feature and Quality Update values were absent or removed, redirecting updates intended for Intune or Windows Update for Business to WSUS/Configuration Manager. The fix stops Configuration Manager from setting the,

keyChanges.title: Connected Cache guidance describes HTTPS delivery and PKI prerequisites
keyChanges.detail: The updated hotfix article applies to Configuration Manager versions 2409, 2503, and 2509 and states that distribution point cache nodes can deliver content over HTTPS. It identifies secure delivery for Intune-managed Win32 applications and, for the first time, Microsoft Teams content; all other content types remain HTTP. HTTPS delivery requires cache nodes to present valid TLS certificates to client devices, with customers using their PKI to generate them.

keyChanges.title: Endpoint security guidance makes EPM licensing and device scope explicit
keyChanges.detail: The Endpoint security page now describes Endpoint Privilege Management as allowing standard users temporary elevation for IT-approved applications, with elevation rules supporting file hashes, publisher certificates, and file paths. It explicitly states that EPM is an Intune add-on requiring an additional license, available standalone or through the Microsoft Intune Suite, and that EPM policies are available only for Windows devices. This is a documentation clarification, not evidence of a new availability event.

keyChanges.title: iOS/iPadOS Automated Device Enrollment warns against phishing-resistant MFA
keyChanges.detail: A new caution states that phishing-resistant MFA is currently unsupported on Setup Assistant for iOS/iPadOS. Users enrolling through Automated Device Enrollment with modern authentication must have an alternate MFA method available to complete enrollment.

keyChanges.title: Multi Admin Approval guidance now includes compliance and Settings Catalog policies
keyChanges.detail: The Multi Admin Approval article now lists creating and managing compliance policies and configuration policies through the Settings Catalog within its stated scope. App deployments remain covered, while app protection policies remain excluded. The record establishes a documentation scope update, not a separate preview or general-availability announcement.

2026-02-23.headline: Apple update retirement, SCEP allowlists, and filter mappings reshape Intune administration
2026-02-23.overview: The week’s consequential Intune changes center on Apple management, authorization, certificate security, and query semantics. Service release 2602 adds assignment filters for Apple declarative device management configurations and extends multi-administrator approval to Settings Catalog device-configuration and compliance policies. Intune also says it will soon stop creating legacy Apple software-update policies after Apple deprecated the relevant commands and payloads for iOS 26, iPadOS 26, and macOS 26. Separately, updated Certificate Connector guidance records SCEP validation blocking unknown certificate extensions from version 6.2510.3.2002. Much of the remaining evidence is documentation maintenance or clarification, including privacy/data-sharing pages, tenant-status and cleanup guidance, and Windows diagnostic-data procedures; those additions do not by themselves establish new product launches.
2026-02-23.adminImpact: Inventory legacy Apple software-update policies and plan around the stated retirement; no retirement date is supplied. Test DDM assignment filters and confirm second-administrator approval workflows where enabled. Review SCEP certificate templates and requests against the documented six-OID allowlist. Recheck assignment filters using the deprecated management values, especially where devices lack Microsoft Entra registration or a Microsoft Entra Device ID, and revise device queries that use unsupported join or device references. If dependent Windows reporting or update-alert features are important, note that the Windows diagnostic-data toggle defaults to Off and disabling it disables dependent Intune features; license attestation confirms tenant entitlement rather than licensing individual

keyChanges.title: Apple DDM filters arrive as legacy software-update policies approach retirement
keyChanges.detail: Service release 2602 allows assignment filters on Apple declarative device management configurations, including software updates, for iOS/iPadOS. Separately, Apple deprecated legacy MDM software-update commands and payloads with iOS 26, iPadOS 26, and macOS 26; Intune says it will soon end support for creating legacy iOS/iPadOS and macOS software-update policies. No retirement date is supplied.

keyChanges.title: Multi-administrator approval expands to compliance and Settings Catalog policies
keyChanges.detail: Service release 2602 extends multi-administrator approval to device-configuration policies created through Settings Catalog and to device-compliance policies. When enabled, creating, editing, or deleting one of these policies requires approval from a second administrator before the change takes effect.

keyChanges.title: Certificate Connector guidance records a six-OID SCEP allowlist
keyChanges.detail: Security behavior documented for Intune Certificate Connector version 6.2510.3.2002 blocks unknown certificate extensions during SCEP validation. The allowed and enforced OIDs are `2.5.29.19` Basic Constraints, `2.5.29.14` Subject Key Identifier, `1.3.6.1.4.1.311.21.8` Certificate Authority Version, `1.3.6.1.4.1.311.20.2` Certificate Template Name, `2.5.29.1` Authority Identifier (Deprecated), and `2.5.29.3` Certificate Policies (Deprecated).

keyChanges.title: Assignment filters retire broad Android and iOS management values
keyChanges.detail: The `Android Enterprise` and iOS/iPadOS `Managed` values are being replaced and will be removed in a future update, with no ETA. Existing filters are automatically mapped: `Android Enterprise` maps to the documented corporate-owned and personally-owned Android management types, while `Managed` maps to the four documented Automated Device Enrollment, Account Driven User Enrollment, and Company Portal/Web Enrollment types. Mapping requires Microsoft Entra registration and a Microsoft Entra Device ID; third-party or​‌

keyChanges.title: Device Query adds semi and anti joins but rejects older syntax
keyChanges.detail: Advanced Analytics device queries now support `leftsemi`, `rightsemi`, `leftanti`, and `rightanti` joins. Joins using `on Device.DeviceId` are no longer supported; queries should use `on Device` or omit the `on` clause when joining on the device entity. Operators such as `distinct`, `summarize`, and `order by` must reference a specific device property rather than `Device`, while device-related results now expose clickable device links.

2026-03-02.headline: KB36495448 fixes co-managed scan-source errors that redirect Intune updates to WSUS
2026-03-02.overview: The period's most consequential change is a Configuration Manager hotfix for co-managed environments where third-party updates can leave a partial Windows Update scan-source policy, sending Feature and Quality Updates to WSUS/ConfigMgr instead of Intune or Windows Update for Business. Intune also added concrete Recovery Lock guidance for macOS and a Windows 11 25H2 security-baseline reference. Service-release notes identify a Windows MDM-enrollment control as public preview and Admin tasks as generally available. Most other edits were link restructuring, terminology corrections, and procedure cleanup.
2026-03-02.adminImpact: Check Configuration Manager 2503 deployments with update rollup 32851084 and version 2509 for applicability of KB36495448, particularly where third-party updates and co-management are used. For Recovery Lock, verify macOS 11.5 or later, Apple silicon, enrollment, supervision, and the required policy or remote-task permissions. Review 25H2 baseline defaults before updating security profiles. The Windows enrollment preview defaults to No, so no change is required unless you intend to disable MDM enrollment during account registration.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager hotfix stops co-managed update-source redirection
keyChanges.detail: Fix and administrator action: KB36495448 applies to Configuration Manager 2503 with update rollup 32851084 and to version 2509 when third-party updates are enabled on co-managed devices. The defect can route Feature Updates and Quality Updates intended for Intune or Windows Update for Business to WSUS/Configuration Manager. After the hotfix, the client stops setting the affected scan-source values and cleans up the incomplete prior state.

keyChanges.title: Recovery Lock gets macOS settings-catalog prerequisites and procedures
keyChanges.detail: New configuration guidance: the Intune how-to says Recovery Lock generates a strong random password, protects recovery-partition and Startup Options access, supports time-based rotation, and can be rotated through device actions. It applies to enrolled and supervised macOS 11.5-or-later devices using Apple silicon; Intel Macs are excluded. Creating the policy requires the documented policy-profile role, while rotation and viewing require custom remote-task permissions.

keyChanges.title: Intune security-baseline reference adds Windows 11 version 25H2
keyChanges.detail: Security guidance: the Security Baseline Settings page adds a Version 25H2 pivot based on the Windows 11 version 25H2 baseline from the Security Compliance Toolkit, limited to settings applicable to Intune-managed Windows devices. Examples include enabled lock-screen camera and slideshow prevention, enabled UAC restrictions for local-account network logons, a disabled SMB v1 server, and the recommended disabled MrxSmb10 driver. This is a reference-content addition, not evidence that existing tenant policies changed

keyChanges.title: Windows enrollment control enters public preview as Admin tasks reaches GA
keyChanges.detail: Preview and general availability: the new `Disable MDM enrollment when adding work or school account on Windows` setting controls MDM enrollment during account registration and defaults to No, which allows enrollment. The same service-release note says Admin tasks is out of preview and generally available, providing a centralized searchable and filterable view of common administrative tasks under Tenant administration.

keyChanges.title: Windows settings catalog adds Edge printing and geolocation controls
keyChanges.detail: New settings: the Windows settings catalog now documents Edge controls for showing an informational Edge for Business page after major browser updates, silent printing, and URL-based allow or block lists for precise geolocation. The informational-page policy applies only to Microsoft Entra ID profiles and is available starting with Edge version 144; the geolocation policies support wildcard URL patterns.

2026-03-09.headline: Windows Autopatch will default eligible Intune devices to hotpatching in May
2026-03-09.overview: Windows Autopatch is the week's main operational signal: Microsoft says hotpatch security updates will become the default for eligible Intune devices in May 2026, with an opt-out setting in April. Intune also documents a staged macOS Recovery Lock passcode action, clarifies the Application control exception in Attack surface reduction profiles, and refreshes privileged-role guidance. Configuration Manager feedback guidance adds a 26 June 2026 authentication deadline and records a broken standalone feedback tool. Most other entries are ordinary title, metadata, link, casing, or wording corrections; no retirement or broad general-availability event is evidenced.
2026-03-09.adminImpact: Start with Autopatch: identify potentially eligible devices, verify prerequisites such as Virtualization-based Security, and decide whether to use the April opt-out when available. For Recovery Lock, validate the documented requirements—supervised macOS 11.5 or later on Apple silicon, with Recovery Lock enabled by policy—and plan around the next successful device check-in before treating a new passcode as active. Review assignments of the privileged Intune Administrator role and use narrower built-in or custom roles for routine work. For Configuration Manager, prepare authenticated feedback before 26 June and use embedded feedback paths while UploadOfflineFeedback.exe is unavailable. The ASR edits call for review of Application control expectations and reboot messaging, not a migration or新

keyChanges.title: Hotpatch becomes the Windows Autopatch default for eligible devices
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft's Message Center says Windows Autopatch will enable hotpatch security updates by default for eligible Intune devices starting in May 2026. An opt-out setting is planned for April, and devices must meet prerequisites such as enabling Virtualization-based Security. Microsoft describes hotpatching as delivering security updates without restarts. This is a Plan for Change, not a claim that every Intune-managed device is eligible.

keyChanges.title: Recovery Lock rotation enters staged rollout with delayed device application
keyChanges.detail: An updated Intune page says the Rotate Recovery Lock Passcode capability is gradually rolling out, with full availability expected by late April 2026. Confirming the action starts the rotation process, but the new passcode is applied only at the device's next successful Intune check-in; an offline or non-checking-in device retains its existing passcode until then. Related action guidance specifies supervised macOS 11.5 or later on Apple silicon, with Recovery Lock enabled by policy; Intel-based Macs aren't समर्थित.

keyChanges.title: ASR Application control remains template-based and can prompt a reboot
keyChanges.detail: The Attack surface reduction guidance now tells administrators to select the Windows platform and then the profile they want when creating a policy. It explicitly says the Application control profile is the exception to the Settings Catalog format: existing policies remain functional, but the profile still uses the older template-based format in the admin center. AppLocker CSP deployment currently prompts the end user to reboot. These edits clarify current administration behavior rather than announce a new ASR prof

keyChanges.title: Intune Administrator guidance emphasizes privileged, time-limited access
keyChanges.detail: Updated RBAC guidance labels the built-in Microsoft Entra role Intune Administrator, while noting that Microsoft Graph and PowerShell still show Intune Service Administrator. It classifies the role as privileged and granting global read/write access across Intune, advises against using it for day-to-day administration, and directs administrators toward narrower built-in or custom roles. This is terminology and security guidance, not evidence that the role's permissions changed this week.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager feedback adds authentication deadline and tool warning
keyChanges.detail: Updated Configuration Manager feedback guidance states that unauthenticated requests will no longer be accepted starting 26 June 2026. It also records a known issue in which the standalone UploadOfflineFeedback.exe tool does not work and says the problem will be fixed in the next release; other embedded feedback experiences remain available.

2026-03-16.headline: Opt-in scoped permissions preview changes Intune RBAC as cloud configuration guidance retires
2026-03-16.overview: The period’s consequential items are a security-sensitive RBAC preview, the deprecation of automatic Windows cloud-configuration deployment, and concrete platform updates. Intune’s service-release notes list macOS Recovery Lock as available and add Apple DDM Settings Catalog entries; Android Enterprise guidance records a direct LOB-app route for fully managed and dedicated devices; and Endpoint Analytics now accepts WinHTTP-proxied telemetry. Much of the remaining material is ordinary documentation maintenance—wording, navigation, formatting, endpoint-table cleanup, and corrected examples. One useful clarification is that most attack surface reduction profiles use Settings Catalog, while Application control remains template-based.
2026-03-16.adminImpact: RBAC owners should run the Permissions Assessment Report at Tenant administration > Roles > Settings before opting in to Scoped permissions; the change is one-time and cannot be undone. Windows cloud-configuration operators should use the manual step-by-step setup guide for new deployments because automatic guided deployment is deprecated and being removed. Mac administrators can evaluate Recovery Lock and the permission required to view its password. Android Enterprise administrators can assess direct APK deployment for required apps on fully managed and dedicated corporate-owned devices. No administrator action is required for the newly documented WinHTTP proxy telemetry support.

keyChanges.title: Scoped permissions becomes an opt-in public preview
keyChanges.detail: Preview / changed behavior: When an administrator has multiple role assignments with different scope tags that share a permission category, Intune’s default behavior merges permissions and can broaden access. The new Scoped permissions setting keeps each assignment’s permissions within its own scope-tag context. Microsoft recommends running the Permissions Assessment Report at Tenant administration > Roles > Settings first; enabling the setting is a one-time tenant action that cannot be undone.

keyChanges.title: Automatic Windows cloud configuration deployment is deprecated
keyChanges.detail: Retirement / deprecation: the Cloud Configuration article says the guided scenario for automatic deployment of Windows in cloud configuration is deprecated and being removed from the Intune admin center. It directs administrators to the Windows client cloud config setup guide for manual, step-by-step deployment.

keyChanges.title: macOS Recovery Lock is listed as available in service release 2603
keyChanges.detail: Availability: Recovery Lock lets administrators configure a recovery OS password for company-owned macOS devices, preventing recovery-mode boot, macOS reinstallation, and bypass of remote management. A Settings Catalog policy can enable the feature and configure password rotation; the Recovery Lock remote action can manually rotate the password. The password appears under per-setting status > Passwords and keys, and viewing it requires Remote tasks/View macOS recovery lock password. The same release note lists newi
keyChanges.product: Intune — macOS device configuration and Apple Settings Catalog

keyChanges.title: Android Enterprise guidance adds a direct-APK LOB deployment route
keyChanges.detail: Documentation clarification / supported deployment option: updated guidance states that required Android line-of-business apps can be uploaded as APK files directly to Intune and assigned as required on Android Enterprise fully managed and dedicated corporate-owned devices, without using Managed Google Play. The limitation is explicit: this path applies to those enrollment types.

keyChanges.title: WinHTTP proxy devices can now feed Endpoint Analytics and EPM
keyChanges.detail: Changed behavior: devices configured with system-level WinHTTP proxy settings can now send telemetry to Endpoint Analytics and Advanced Analytics, while Endpoint Privilege Management includes elevation-usage data from those devices. The release note says no administrator action is required; when the capabilities are enabled, data appears in the User Experience device view, Endpoint Analytics reports, and EPM.
keyChanges.product: Intune — Endpoint Analytics, Advanced Analytics, and Endpoint Privilege Management

2026-03-23.headline: Intune Data Warehouse plans mid-June reset and beta Power BI connector retirement
2026-03-23.overview: The period’s clearest operational change is a Message Center plan for an Intune Data Warehouse infrastructure update now expected in mid-June 2026. It would reduce historical data to about 30 days, refresh surrogate keys, revise licensing definitions, and discontinue the beta Power BI connector in favor of the OData feed. Intune guidance also records hotpatch as enabled by default for eligible devices and adds managed-installer support during Windows Autopilot device preparation. Much of the remaining activity is documentation restructuring: Settings Catalog content moved to new device-configuration paths, while new platform references and how-to guides appeared. Those changes should not be treated as blanket feature launches.
2026-03-23.adminImpact: Reporting owners should back up Data Warehouse data before the expected mid-June update, review queries and dashboards for refreshed surrogate keys and licensing-definition changes, and migrate from the beta Power BI connector to the OData feed. Windows update teams should verify hotpatch tenant-level or quality-update policy settings and account for baseline updates still requiring a restart. Teams using Autopilot device preparation should review app sequencing because managed installer policy is now applied before Win32, Microsoft Store, and Enterprise App Catalog apps. Security administrators should check custom Intune roles against the newly documented Defender permissions and assign Conditional Access permissions separately in Microsoft Entra ID. For Apple management, the settings-c อ

keyChanges.title: Data Warehouse plan puts reporting migration and backup on the roadmap
keyChanges.detail: The Message Center plan says the Intune Data Warehouse update is now expected in mid-June 2026. Historical data would be reset to about 30 days, surrogate keys refreshed, and licensing definitions revised. The beta Power BI connector will be discontinued; administrators are directed to switch to the OData feed from the Intune admin center and back up data beforehand.

keyChanges.title: Hotpatch guidance now states default enablement for eligible devices
keyChanges.detail: Updated Windows quality update guidance says hotpatch security updates are enabled by default for all eligible devices in Microsoft Intune, with control available through a tenant-level setting or quality update policies. During a hotpatch month, a device missing the latest baseline can receive both the baseline update, which requires a restart, and the hotpatch update. This is a documented behavior change, not a stated preview or general-availability announcement.

keyChanges.title: Windows Autopilot device preparation adds managed installer support
keyChanges.detail: The Windows Autopilot device preparation update records support for managed installer policy during OOBE. The policy is applied before Win32, Microsoft Store, and Enterprise App Catalog apps install; those app types were previously skipped to avoid conflicts and deployment failures. The supplied evidence does not assign a preview or general-availability label.

keyChanges.title: Defender integration guidance adds an explicit least-privilege RBAC matrix
keyChanges.detail: The Intune–Defender for Endpoint guidance now specifies Mobile Threat Defense Modify and Read permissions; Endpoint Detection and Response Assign, Create, Read, and Update; and Device compliance policies Assign, Create, Read, and Update. It identifies Endpoint Security Manager as the least-privileged built-in Intune role containing all required permissions, while Conditional Access requires a separate Microsoft Entra role. This is security guidance clarification rather than evidence of a new integration feature.

keyChanges.title: Apple Settings Catalog guidance points toward future template migration
keyChanges.detail: The new Apple configuration reference recommends creating new policies in the Settings Catalog where possible and says Device features, Device restrictions, Endpoint protection, and Extensions templates are expected to migrate to the Settings Catalog in a future Intune release, after which creating new templates will be deprecated. Derived credential, Email, PKCS, SCEP, trusted-certificate, Wi-Fi, and wired-network policies remain listed as template cases. No retirement date is supplied, so this is forward-looking…

2026-03-30.headline: Intune’s beta Power BI connector starts a late-April retirement transition
2026-03-30.overview: The period is dominated by documentation restructuring: legacy remote-action and Security Copilot agent pages were removed as replacement pages appeared under new paths. That is not evidence of a product retirement or broad launch. The substantive administrator signals are a planned Intune Data Warehouse connector retirement, a future Intune Management Extension version floor, the gradual Recovery Lock rollout, a gated Vulnerability Remediation Agent preview, and clearer Delete/Retire guidance for BitLocker devices.
2026-03-30.adminImpact: Identify Power BI reports created before November 2025 and move beta-connector reports to connector v2 or the OData Feed before the late-April transition completes. Verify Windows devices can sync so the Intune Management Extension can update automatically; the roadmap entry supplies no enforcement date. For Recovery Lock, validate supervised Apple silicon Macs running macOS 11.5 or later and ensure the enabling policy is deployed. Treat Vulnerability Remediation as a select-customer preview, not general availability. For Delete or Retire decisions on Microsoft Entra joined BitLocker devices, back up recovery keys and local administrator credentials first.

keyChanges.title: Intune Data Warehouse beta connector faces planned retirement
keyChanges.detail: The In Development roadmap says the Intune Data Warehouse (beta) connector in Power BI will be retired. The transition starts in late April 2026 and proceeds gradually over two weeks; after it completes, the beta connector will no longer provide data. Reports created after November 2025 already use connector v2, while older reports may still require migration to connector v2 or the OData Feed.

keyChanges.title: Windows Intune Management Extension will require version 1.58.103.0
keyChanges.detail: A future requirement in the In Development roadmap will make Intune Management Extension version 1.58.103.0 or later necessary on Windows 10 and Windows 11 devices. Earlier versions will no longer receive dependent configurations or updates, including Win32 app deployments, PowerShell scripts, remediations, and platform scripts. The extension updates automatically, but devices must be able to sync to receive the update.

keyChanges.title: Recovery Lock passcode rotation is gradually rolling out
keyChanges.detail: The new remote-action guidance says Rotate Recovery Lock Passcode may not yet be available in every tenant, with full availability expected by late April 2026. The action supports supervised macOS 11.5 or later on Apple silicon; Intel Macs are unsupported. A policy must enable Recovery Lock, and the newly generated passcode reaches the device at its next successful Intune check-in.

keyChanges.title: Vulnerability Remediation Agent is limited to select public-preview customers
keyChanges.detail: The Security Copilot overview explicitly places the Vulnerability Remediation Agent in a limited public preview available only to a select group of customers. It uses Microsoft Defender Vulnerability Management data to identify and prioritize CVEs on managed devices, then supplies impact details, affected systems, suggested actions, and step-by-step Intune remediation guidance. Administrators can mark remediated suggestions as applied for later tracking.

keyChanges.title: Delete guidance clarifies Retire-versus-Wipe behavior and BitLocker risk
keyChanges.detail: This is documentation clarification rather than evidence of a product behavior change. The new Delete article states that Delete triggers Retire on iOS/iPadOS, macOS, and Windows; Android device administrator and BYOD devices also trigger Retire, while Android COBO, COSU, COPE, and AOSP devices trigger Wipe. For Microsoft Entra joined devices protected by BitLocker, deleting or retiring the Intune object triggers a sync that removes key protectors and suspends BitLocker on the OS volume, so the guidance says to备份ं?

2026-04-06.headline: Endpoint Privilege Management now enforces scope tags on elevation requests
2026-04-06.overview: Endpoint Privilege Management is the clearest operational change this week: applicable scope tags now constrain which elevation requests administrators can view and manage. With no Message Center announcements supplied, the other notable items are documentation-led: a seven-step Edge for Business rollout guide, a compliance-driven Android device-administrator migration path, a current Windows VPN derived-credentials limitation, and an Apple deprecation notice on supervised macOS MDM update policies. These additions clarify deployment and support boundaries; they do not by themselves establish new feature availability or retirement dates.
2026-04-06.adminImpact: Prioritize scope review for delegated Endpoint Privilege Management administrators because elevation-request visibility and management are limited to assigned users and devices. For Edge, Android migration, Windows VPN, and macOS update work, use the documented prerequisites and constraints in design reviews; do not infer launch status or an Apple retirement deadline from these documentation additions.

keyChanges.title: EPM elevation-request administration now honors assigned scope tags
keyChanges.detail: Changed behavior: the What's New entry says applicable scope tags are now enforced when viewing Endpoint Privilege Management elevation requests. Administrators can view and manage only requests for devices and users within their assigned scope. Review delegated administrator scope assignments because this changes visibility and management boundaries.

keyChanges.title: Edge for Business guidance separates app-level and device-level policy deployment
keyChanges.detail: Documentation-only: the new Step 5 guide describes Settings Catalog as an enrolled-device, device-level control for Windows and macOS, while App Configuration Policies use the Managed Apps channel for non-enrolled devices. It says never to target both policy types at the same Edge client; enrolled Windows devices should use either Settings Catalog or the Microsoft Edge Security Baseline, not both. Levels 1, 2, and 3 are non-cumulative, with only one level deployed per user or device.
keyChanges.product: Intune Settings Catalog and App Configuration Policies

keyChanges.title: Android migration guidance documents a compliance-driven work-profile path
keyChanges.detail: Documentation-only: the migration guide directs administrators to create an Android device administrator compliance policy and set **Block devices managed with device administrator** to **Yes**. The user Resolve checklist then covers unenrollment, enrollment into personally owned work profile management, and resolution of remaining compliance issues. Prerequisites include Android Company Portal 5.0.4720.0 or later, an Intune-to-Android Enterprise connection, and work-profile enrollment configured; lingering device​

keyChanges.title: Windows VPN profiles are flagged as not working with derived credentials
keyChanges.detail: Current limitation and security guidance: the Intune derived-credentials page says using **Derived credential** as the authentication method for VPN profiles is not working as expected on Windows devices. The limitation affects Windows VPN profiles only and is expected to be fixed in a future release with no ETA. Treat Windows VPN use as unvalidated and plan or test around the limitation.

keyChanges.title: Supervised macOS update-policy guidance now includes an Apple deprecation warning
keyChanges.detail: Documentation-only: the new macOS software-update guide includes an Important notice titled **Apple MDM software updates deprecation**, while still documenting MDM-based policies for supervised macOS 12 through macOS 15 and actions such as **Download and install**, **Download only**, **Install immediately**, and **Notify only**. The supplied evidence provides no retirement date or replacement, so it supports a deprecation warning—not a confirmed deadline.

2026-04-13.headline: Cross-tenant Edge MAM now protects partner devices as WSL compliance guidance sharpens
2026-04-13.overview: The clearest product change is an opt-in Microsoft Edge for Business update supporting cross-tenant Intune Mobile Application Management policies. Most of the remaining material is ordinary compliance documentation restructuring: the central policy-creation guidance now points to platform-specific reference pages and reorganized reporting and noncompliance-action content. The meaningful operational exceptions are new guidance for EPM, WSL compliance, compliance-report interpretation, and Enterprise App Catalog administration.
2026-04-13.adminImpact: Evaluate the Edge cross-tenant MAM scenario for contractors and partners, and test app protection, OneDrive download redirection, and leak controls before enabling it. For EPM, use the documented audit-first approach and allow at least 24 hours for reporting data, with longer observation periods where representative usage data is needed. Satisfy the WSL plugin and management-extension prerequisites before deployment. Update compliance-report runbooks to account for check-in lag, pending states, user-context records, and temporary differences between summary and detailed views. Do not infer a product behavior change or feature launch from the broader documentation reorganization.

keyChanges.title: Edge for Business adds opt-in cross-tenant Intune MAM support
keyChanges.detail: A Microsoft 365 Message Center major update says Microsoft Edge for Business now supports cross-tenant Intune Mobile Application Management policies. The opt-in capability can enforce app protection, redirect downloads to OneDrive, and activate leak controls on devices managed by another tenant, directly addressing contractor and partner scenarios. The supplied evidence does not label this as preview or general availability.
keyChanges.product: Microsoft Edge for Business / Intune Mobile Application Management

keyChanges.title: EPM documents an audit-first administrator-to-standard-user migration
keyChanges.detail: The new Endpoint Privilege Management security guidance recommends auditing first to identify the elevation processes users need. Its audit policy values are Endpoint Privilege Management: Enabled, Default elevation response: Not Configured, Send elevation data for reporting: Yes, and Reporting scope: Diagnostic data and all endpoint elevations. Reporting data can take 24 hours to return, and the guidance suggests observing usage for several weeks when necessary. This is migration guidance, not evidence of a new E​

keyChanges.title: WSL compliance requires a plugin, management extension, and policy cleanup
keyChanges.detail: The new Windows Subsystem for Linux compliance procedure requires the Intune WSL plugin and the Microsoft Intune management extension. The extension can be installed through an assigned PowerShell script or proactive remediation, a Win32 or Microsoft Store app, or a custom compliance policy. Administrators are also told to unassign and remove existing custom WSL compliance policies and deploy the plugin as a Win32 app. WSL results are incorporated into the host device’s overall compliance state; the page is setup​

keyChanges.title: Compliance reports now spell out check-in lag and multi-user records
keyChanges.detail: An updated monitoring article clarifies that compliance is evaluated continuously, while reports refresh when a device checks in and show the last confirmed state. Recent assignments may not appear until check-in; devices can remain Pending; shared or multi-user devices may show the previous user’s state; user and system contexts can create multiple records; and summary and detailed views may update at different times. This is a documentation clarification, not an announced change to compliance evaluation behavior.

keyChanges.title: Enterprise App Catalog guidance sets update targets and Autopilot support
keyChanges.detail: The new Enterprise App Management procedure states that catalog apps use Microsoft-configured and confirmed default installation, requirements, and detection settings. Most updates are expected to become available within 24 hours after automated validation, while updates requiring manual testing typically take up to seven days. It also documents support for using catalog apps as blocking apps in Windows Autopilot Enrollment Status Page and Device Preparation Page profiles. This is administrative guidance, not a new

2026-04-20.headline: macOS ADE guidance adds pre-enrollment Platform SSO setup
2026-04-20.overview: This was a documentation-heavy Intune week: 40 new, 269 updated, and 45 removed items, with no Message Center entries. The most consequential cluster concerned Apple enrollment: the ADE material now documents macOS Platform SSO sequencing, explicit tvOS and visionOS coverage with licensing guidance, and Apple account service-access prerequisites. Separate security guidance changes replace Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 with 24.04/26.04 in a compliance-policy page and change the Edge for Business threat-level example from Medium to Secured. The evidence identifies documentation changes, not a product launch, preview, general-availability milestone, tenant-wide policy migration, or capability retirement.
2026-04-20.adminImpact: Prioritize an Apple ADE runbook review where Platform SSO or Apple mobile enrollment is in scope. For Linux compliance and Edge app-protection settings, compare the revised values with the actual tenant configuration before changing baselines; the evidence does not show automatic changes to existing policies. Validate internal links after the Apple ADE page reorganization. No deadline or migration action is evidenced.

keyChanges.title: Platform SSO is now documented as a macOS ADE prerequisite
keyChanges.detail: Updated Intune macOS ADE guidance adds a Configure platform SSO section. It says that, if Microsoft Entra SSO should be available during Setup Assistant, administrators must create the platform SSO policy before devices enroll. The page says ADE deploys that policy to enrolling Macs, enabling organizational-credential sign-in during setup and access to Microsoft Entra-protected apps and resources afterward. This is a procedure and prerequisite documentation change, not a supplied GA announcement.
keyChanges.product: Intune — macOS Automated Device Enrollment and Platform SSO

keyChanges.title: Apple ADE guidance now lists tvOS and visionOS with Plan 2 licensing
keyChanges.detail: The refreshed Apple mobile ADE overview lists iOS/iPadOS, tvOS, and visionOS and says administrators can create, edit, delete, and assign platform-specific ADE policies. It also states that Intune Plan 2 is required for tvOS and visionOS device management, while Plan 1 is the minimum requirement for iOS/iPadOS. The record shows expanded documentation coverage; it does not label the scope as preview or general availability.

keyChanges.title: New Apple account service-access guidance keeps configuration in Apple portals
keyChanges.detail: A new Intune how-to explains that Apple account service-access settings are configured in Apple Business or Apple School Manager, not directly in Intune; Intune issues the management token Apple uses during device activation. The guidance applies to organization-owned devices enrolled through ADE, with iOS/iPadOS 17 or later or macOS 14 or later. It warns that changing the settings can automatically sign out accounts on devices that no longer meet the requirements.

keyChanges.title: Linux compliance guidance replaces Ubuntu 22.04 with 26.04
keyChanges.detail: In the Create Policy guidance, the Ubuntu Desktop version list changes from 22.04 LTS or 24.04 LTS to 24.04 LTS or 26.04 LTS. This is a documentation value replacement; the diff does not show an automated change to existing compliance policies or establish changed service behavior.

keyChanges.title: Edge for Business app protection guidance raises the threat-level example
keyChanges.detail: The Step 2 setup guidance changes Max allowed device threat level from Medium / Block access to Secured / Block access; the Block access action remains unchanged. Treat this as an updated configuration example and compare it with existing policies before changing a tenant baseline.
keyChanges.product: Intune — App Protection Policies for Microsoft Edge for Business

2026-04-27.headline: Configuration Manager 2603 brings Network Access Account hardening and an October co-management deadline
2026-04-27.overview: The 248-item period was dominated by documentation maintenance—241 updates versus four new entries—but several changes have direct operational significance. Configuration Manager 2603 is the standout release item, while Intune adds Ubuntu 26.04 LTS support and documents Platform SSO registration during macOS Automated Device Enrollment. Other high-value updates clarify the Windows Security Center MAM connector procedure and unlicensed administrator defaults; most remaining edits are terminology, link, image, or formatting changes.
2026-04-27.adminImpact: Co-managed environments should apply Configuration Manager 2603 before October 2026 where the Compliance workload is managed by Intune. Intune administrators should identify Ubuntu 22.04 devices, use the documented prerequisites before deploying macOS Platform SSO during ADE, explicitly enable the Windows Security Center MAM toggle, and check tenant creation date before changing administrator licensing. The supplied PSSO entry does not label the capability as preview or generally available.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager 2603 adds security fixes and an October compliance deadline
keyChanges.detail: The 2603 release is available as an in-console update installable at the top-tier site in a hierarchy. It restricts Network Access Account information to supported OSD media task-sequence scenarios. An internal service required for device compliance checks will be deprecated in October 2026; Software Center compliance checks may fail in co-managed environments where the Compliance workload is managed by Intune, so Microsoft says to apply the update before October. The release also removes the deprecated SQL Server

keyChanges.title: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS support arrives before Ubuntu 22.04’s August deadline
keyChanges.detail: Intune now supports Ubuntu 26.04 LTS. Support for Ubuntu 22.04 LTS ends in August 2026, although devices already enrolled on 22.04 remain enrolled. Administrators can find them under Devices > All devices by filtering for Linux and adding the OS version column, then notify users to upgrade to a supported Ubuntu version.

keyChanges.title: Platform SSO registration is documented for macOS Automated Device Enrollment
keyChanges.detail: The Intune What's new entry documents running Platform SSO during macOS ADE registration. Before enrollment, administrators must configure the settings catalog setting Enable Registration During Setup, deploy Company Portal version 5.2604.0 or newer as a line-of-business app, and configure ADE to use Setup Assistant with modern authentication and await final configuration. The scenario applies to macOS 26 and newer and gives users access to Microsoft Entra ID resources immediately at the desktop.

keyChanges.title: Windows Security Center MAM setup now requires an explicit connector toggle
keyChanges.detail: The revised Edge data-security procedure says to open the Windows Security Center connector after creating it, turn on Connect Windows devices for MAM, and save. The documented status is Available after creation and changes to Enabled only after the toggle is turned on, replacing earlier guidance that the connector remained Unavailable until an App Protection Policy arrived or a MAM user enrolled. This is a procedure and status-documentation change, not a stated preview or GA announcement.

keyChanges.title: Unlicensed administrator defaults now depend on tenant creation date
keyChanges.detail: Tenants created after July 2021 support unlicensed administrator access by default and require no action. Tenants created before July 2021 require the Allow access to unlicensed admins setting, and Microsoft says the setting cannot be undone after activation. The guidance also clarifies the limit of 350 unlicensed administrators per security group, that multiple groups can be used above that limit, and that nested-group members are not included.

2026-05-04.headline: Controlled Configuration preview makes Defender antivirus policy authoritative over legacy settings
2026-05-04.overview: Intune’s period was maintenance-heavy: 239 entries were updated, no Message Center items appeared, and many representative edits changed links, headings, terminology, or requirements formatting rather than documented service behavior. The meaningful exceptions concern security and platform changes: Controlled Configuration is explicitly headed to public preview; Apple’s 26.4 guidance redirects deprecated Intelligence controls to DDM; Strict Tunnel Mode is in development for Android; and the MTD connector guidance defines a tightly scoped Android role.
2026-05-04.adminImpact: Treat Controlled Configuration and Strict Tunnel Mode as preview or roadmap planning material, not general-availability announcements. For design reviews, account for Controlled Configuration’s precedence over Group Policy, Configuration Manager, and local changes; verify Android Management API and Always On VPN dependencies for Tunnel; and map Apple Intelligence controls to DDM for version 26.4 and later. Audit custom-compliance scripts against the 2,048-character output limit and error 65009 risk. The MTD role has a one-partner-per-tenant constraint and excludes personally owned work profiles; ordinary link and heading edits do not call for tenant changes.

keyChanges.title: Controlled Configuration enters public preview for Defender antivirus
keyChanges.detail: The In Development guidance explicitly says Intune is bringing Controlled Configuration (CC) to public preview for Microsoft Defender antivirus settings. When enabled, settings delivered by Intune or Microsoft Defender for Endpoint security settings management override Group Policy, Configuration Manager, local changes, and scripts. CC also extends Tamper Protection by allowing administrators to lock settings to defined values rather than only defaults. This is a policy-precedence change to plan for, not a general-

keyChanges.title: Apple Intelligence controls shift from deprecated MDM restrictions to DDM
keyChanges.detail: For iOS/iPadOS and macOS devices running version 26.4 and later, the guidance says Apple deprecated Intelligence-related settings in the MDM restrictions payload. It directs administrators to the DDM configurations released in March 2026. The deprecated list includes controls for Assistant, Dictation, Genmoji, Writing Tools, Siri, predictive keyboards, spell check, and related features. This is a platform-driven migration path, not a new Intune setting launch.

keyChanges.title: Strict Tunnel Mode is planned for Android Microsoft Tunnel
keyChanges.detail: The roadmap says Microsoft Tunnel will add Strict Tunnel Mode for Android Enterprise devices enrolled through Android Management API, configured with Always On VPN. It will force traffic through the tunnel and block traffic if the connection drops, while an app exclusion list allows specified apps to bypass the tunnel. The guidance also describes support for unenrolled devices using Microsoft Tunnel for Mobile Application Management. The capability remains in development.

keyChanges.title: MTD connector guidance adds Android role permissions with a one-partner limit
keyChanges.detail: The connector documentation adds a fourth category, Mobile Threat Defense role, with a toggle that grants the selected partner exemptions from app suspension, hibernation, power restrictions, and user controls on Android Enterprise corporate-owned fully managed and corporate-owned work profile devices. Only one MTD partner can hold the role per tenant; the connector must be configured, its app targeted, and devices enrolled through Android Management API. Personally owned work profiles are not supported. The change

keyChanges.title: Custom-compliance discovery output has a 2,048-character ceiling
keyChanges.detail: An added warning in Create Policy says discovery-script output is limited to 2,048 characters. Output beyond that may be truncated, producing invalid JSON and error 65009 during compliance evaluation. Administrators should keep output concise or split large rule sets across multiple policies. This is operational guidance about custom compliance, not a launch or support change.

2026-05-11.headline: Windows Autopilot automatic mode for Windows 365 drops preview label in updated guidance
2026-05-11.overview: The week was mostly documentation maintenance: 129 of 132 changes were updates involving terminology, links, numbering, formatting, and procedure clarification. The notable administrator-facing exceptions were Windows Autopilot device preparation for Windows 365, the Security Copilot Vulnerability Remediation Agent permission model, and Intune’s Defender for Endpoint and Mobile Threat Defense setup guidance. The Autopilot articles remove “preview” and replace Windows 365 Frontline references with Windows 365 Flex. A new device-based Conditional Access how-to also makes its licensing, role, and compliance-policy prerequisites explicit. One standalone app-based Conditional Access how-to was removed, which the supplied evidence supports as documentation consolidation rather than retirement of the capability.
2026-05-11.adminImpact: Treat the Autopilot edit as a documentation and availability signal, not proof of general availability; confirm current Windows 365 and Autopilot availability before changing rollout plans. For the Vulnerability Remediation Agent, review the agentic user and delegated permissions assigned in Microsoft Entra and Microsoft Defender; the guidance lists Intune Read Only Operator or a custom role with Mobile apps/read and Device configurations/read. The agent remains documented as limited public preview and public-cloud only. If enabling the Defender for Endpoint automatic-launch toggle, also enable Grant MTD role permissions for Android Enterprise COBO and COPE devices. For device-based Conditional Access, confirm a Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2 license, Security Administrator or Conditional‌ ‍‍

keyChanges.title: Windows 365 automatic-mode guidance drops the public-preview label
keyChanges.detail: The Windows Autopilot device-preparation automatic-mode article removes “(preview)” from its title, description, headings, and public-preview note. It also replaces Windows 365 Frontline shared and dedicated references with Windows 365 Flex. This is a documentation status and terminology change; it does not establish general availability on its own.

keyChanges.title: Vulnerability Remediation Agent guidance defines an agentic-user RBAC model
keyChanges.detail: Security Copilot guidance now describes an agentic-user permission model for running the Vulnerability Remediation Agent. Permissions are delegated outside the Intune admin center in Microsoft Entra and Microsoft Defender. On the Intune side, the guidance names Read Only Operator or a custom role with Mobile apps/read and Device configurations/read; users viewing results need corresponding read access.

keyChanges.title: Defender connector guidance documents automatic launch on Android COBO and COPE
keyChanges.detail: The Mobile Threat Defense connector guidance documents an “Automatically launch Microsoft Defender for Endpoint during setup” toggle for Android Enterprise corporate-owned fully managed and corporate-owned work profile devices. It is available only for the Microsoft Defender for Endpoint connector and requires the “Grant MTD role permissions” toggle to be enabled as well.
keyChanges.product: Intune Mobile Threat Defense connector / Defender for Endpoint

keyChanges.title: New device-based Conditional Access guide names setup prerequisites
keyChanges.detail: Intune added a dedicated how-to requiring a Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2 license and either the Security administrator or Conditional Access administrator role. The procedure also requires Intune device compliance policies to be configured before creating the Conditional Access policy. This is a new documentation path, not evidence of a newly introduced Conditional Access capability.
keyChanges.product: Intune device compliance / Microsoft Entra Conditional Access

keyChanges.title: Custom compliance script uploads remain unable to use scope tags
keyChanges.detail: The revised custom-script guidance makes the limitation explicit: the upload workflow does not support scope tags. Administrators must have the default scope tag to create, edit, or view custom compliance discovery scripts.

2026-05-18.headline: EPM report access tightens as Intune flags device-reported compliance values as untrusted
2026-05-18.overview: The week was dominated by documentation maintenance—licensing-link moves, metadata changes, and template reshaping—but several updates carry concrete administrator consequences. EPM reporting guidance now describes an explicit permission requirement; Security Copilot guidance expands the documented default inheritance of Intune RBAC access; the Vulnerability Remediation Agent workflow and identity handling have changed; and new Cloud PKI guidance covers staged CA renewal. The supplied evidence contains no Message Center item and does not establish a new GA launch, retirement, or tenant-wide rollout.
2026-05-18.adminImpact: Audit custom EPM roles and Graph-based reporting access for the explicit View Reports permission. Review which Intune RBAC roles should inherit Security Copilot access when Intune is enabled as a data source. Update compliance-report procedures so device-reported values are treated as untrusted context, not an enforcement signal. For the Vulnerability Remediation Agent, verify delegated permissions and readiness-check procedures, and plan human-identity transitions before support expires. Cloud PKI administrators should review renewal permissions and staged-CA activation requirements before a CA expires.

keyChanges.title: EPM reports now require explicit View Reports permission
keyChanges.detail: The updated EPM reporting article states that access through the Intune admin center or Microsoft Graph requires Endpoint Privilege Management Policy Authoring > View Reports, also identified as EpmPolicy.ViewReports. Users without it receive HTTP 403 responses from the report endpoint. The article says Device configurations > Read previously provided access. Review custom roles and reporting clients that depend on the older permission.

keyChanges.title: Security Copilot guidance expands default Intune-role access inheritance
keyChanges.detail: When Microsoft Intune is enabled as a Security Copilot data source, the updated overview says the Microsoft Entra Intune Administrator role automatically inherits Security Copilot owner access, while all other built-in and custom Intune RBAC roles inherit Security Copilot contributor access. Existing Intune RBAC permissions and scope tags still limit accessible data and actions. Administrators can remove the default access by removing Intune roles from the Security Copilot contributor role.

keyChanges.title: Compliance guidance treats device-reported Setting values as untrusted input
keyChanges.detail: The Monitor Policy update explains that some compliance reports include a Setting column populated directly by a device, application, or administrator-supplied script, including custom compliance and Android app configuration scenarios. Intune does not validate or enforce the content; values can contain free-form text, URLs, file paths, or identifying and environment-specific information, and may attempt to influence administrator behavior. Use these values only as context, confirm status through trusted workflows,

keyChanges.title: Vulnerability Remediation Agent tightens identity setup and run readiness
keyChanges.detail: Updated Security Copilot instructions require administrators to delegate all required permissions to the agentic user and pass Run Readiness Check before runs are enabled; a successful check enables the Run button and scheduled runs. Agents using human identities must transition before support expires. Identity problems are handled by removing the agent and setting it up again rather than renewing or replacing the identity.

keyChanges.title: New Cloud PKI guidance documents staged CA renewal
keyChanges.detail: A new Cloud PKI article documents renewal for Intune-managed and bring-your-own-CA issuing CAs. Renewal always generates a new public/private key pair while preserving certificates and CRLs from earlier CA versions. A CA becomes eligible at half its validity lifetime or after expiry; an expired CA can be renewed, but certificate issuance remains unavailable until the staged CA is activated. The documented permissions are Read CAs and Create certificate authorities.

2026-05-25.headline: OpenClaw baseline reference warns Node.js and WSL controls may disrupt workloads
2026-05-25.overview: The week was mostly documentation maintenance, but several changes have direct planning value. The Intune security-baseline overview now lists Local AI Agent Baseline - OpenClaw as a Preview, while its new settings reference documents outbound Node.js/runtime controls and warns they may disrupt legitimate processes. Security Copilot’s Vulnerability Remediation Agent guidance changes from limited public preview for selected customers to public preview. New Intune licensing and account-move references clarify plan structure and regional data-at-rest moves; custom-compliance guidance now lists RedHat Enterprise Linux 10 rather than 8 and makes discovery-script sequencing explicit. Separately, iOS/iPadOS compliance references now say iOS 17.0 and later rather than iOS 8.0 and later for multiple settings. The removed Create App Based Policy page is a documentation retirement, not evidence that app-based Conditional Access was retired; much of the remaining work is terminology, link, and prerequisite-layout cleanup.
2026-05-25.adminImpact: Pilot and test the OpenClaw baseline, use the Properties catalog to inventory local AI agents, and review settings that could affect legitimate Node.js or Windows Subsystem for Linux workloads. Treat the Vulnerability Remediation Agent as public preview, not general availability. Use the new licensing and account-move references for entitlement and data-residency planning. Revalidate Linux and iOS compliance assumptions against the current references before changing policy guidance, because the supplied diffs alone do not establish a service-side enforcement change.

keyChanges.title: OpenClaw reference documents runtime controls and a deployment warning
keyChanges.detail: The new Intune settings reference says the baseline limits unauthorized local AI agents by disrupting common execution paths. It includes firewall rules that restrict outbound communication from runtime environments such as Node.js, plus controls that can affect Windows Subsystem for Linux and Node.js. The reference warns that the baseline may not block every execution path and may block other processes, so each setting should be reviewed and tested; it also points admins to Properties catalog inventory for Local ‌

keyChanges.title: Vulnerability Remediation Agent guidance changes from limited to public preview
keyChanges.detail: The setup article replaces wording that the feature was in limited public preview and available only to a select group of customers with a statement that it is in public preview, linking to Public preview in Microsoft Intune. This is a documented preview-status change, not a general-availability announcement or proof that every tenant has access.

keyChanges.title: New licensing reference maps Intune Plan 1, Plan 2, and Suite
keyChanges.detail: The new Microsoft Intune licensing article defines Plan 1 as the base service, Plan 2 as additive to Plan 1 with advanced capabilities including Remote Help and Advanced Analytics, and the Intune Suite as additive to Plan 1 and including Plan 2. It also states that users or devices benefiting directly or indirectly from Intune need an Intune license and documents a device-only subscription. This is a new reference and does not by itself show that entitlements changed.

keyChanges.title: Account-move guidance separates regional data moves from tenant migration
keyChanges.detail: The new overview says an Intune account move relocates customer data at rest between geographic datacenter regions while preserving the tenant, policies, profiles, device enrollments, app-management state, and service configuration. It explicitly says the process is not a tenant-to-tenant migration, and distinguishes customer-requested moves coordinated through Microsoft support from Microsoft-initiated moves with advance notice. This is planning guidance, not evidence that a move is scheduled for a tenant.

keyChanges.title: Custom-compliance guidance now lists RHEL 10 and script sequencing
keyChanges.detail: The custom-compliance guide changes its listed Linux distribution from RedHat Enterprise Linux 8 to RedHat Enterprise Linux 10. It also spells out that administrators must prepare a JSON file and discovery script, upload the script to the Microsoft Intune admin center before creating the policy, and use one script per compliance policy even though each script can discover multiple settings. This is a documentation update; the supplied diff does not prove that backend platform support changed.

2026-06-01.headline: CMG image deprecation drives Configuration Manager’s Windows Server 2022 transition
2026-06-01.overview: Configuration Manager’s CMG VMSS update is the week’s most consequential change: gateways are moving from the legacy Windows Server 2022 Azure Marketplace offer `windowsserver`, which includes .NET 6, to `windowsserver2022`. The legacy images will lose support and image-refresh OS updates, and new CMG deployments or reimaging will fail when enforcement begins in early 2027.
