The scope is Windows 10 and Windows 11; apps assigned Available for enrolled devices retain the existing update workflow, and guided update supersedence remains an alternative. This is an added documentation description, not an explicit preview or general-availability announcement.

keyChanges.title: New STIG baseline guidance is explicitly audit-only
keyChanges.detail: New Intune guidance documents a read-only Security Technical Implementation Guide audit baseline for Windows 10 and Windows 11. The listed Microsoft Windows 11 STIG SCAP Benchmark is version 2, Release 7, with 197 rules and a January 5, 2026 benchmark date. Intune assesses current configuration and provides per-setting and per-device reports through the admin center, Graph API, or CSV, with XCCDF compliance reporting; unlike other security baselines, it does not configure or enforce settings.

2026-07.headline: Commercial E3 and E5 tenants begin receiving bundled Intune Suite capabilities automatically
2026-07.overview: Most July records are maintenance edits, but the supplied diffs identify several administrator-relevant exceptions. The largest is a gradual commercial Microsoft 365 E3 and E5 entitlement rollout: eligible tenants are automatically provisioned and receive a 30-day Microsoft 365 admin center notification. Intune also documents two previews—client-driven compliance reevaluation and controlled Defender configuration—while macOS compliance content gains a Bash workflow and an account-password warning. The evidence does not establish a general-availability release or retirement; the macOS entries are documentation and security guidance rather than proof of changed service behavior. The period’s sole Message Center item separately recommends Windows KB5101684 Preview for IT1431577.
2026-07.adminImpact: Commercial Microsoft 365 E3 and E5 administrators do not need to provision the newly bundled capabilities; monitor the advance notification and gradual rollout. Treat both Intune previews as preview features and validate their effects in controlled scopes. For macOS compliance, check script format and runtime requirements, and assess password-expiry consequences before enabling password requirements. Follow normal Windows update validation procedures for the KB5101684 Preview recommendation.

keyChanges.title: Selected Intune Suite capabilities are being bundled into commercial Microsoft 365 E3 and E5
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft is gradually adding Remote Help, Advanced Analytics, and Intune Plan 2—including Microsoft Tunnel for mobile application management, specialty device management, and firmware over-the-air updates for supported devices—to Microsoft 365 E3. Microsoft 365 E5 includes those capabilities plus Endpoint Privilege Management, Enterprise Application Management, and Microsoft Cloud PKI. Eligible tenants are automatically provisioned, no action is required, and Microsoft will post a 30-day advance notification. This

keyChanges.title: Controlled Configuration gives Defender settings an Intune authority mode in preview
keyChanges.detail: The Antivirus policy guidance adds Controlled configuration for Microsoft Defender settings (preview). In the Windows Security experience profile, under Defender, Controlled Configuration (Device) supports Not configured, Off (Default), Tamper Protection (On), and Controlled Configuration (On). The default turns off both controlled configuration and tamper protection; the controlled mode gives Intune or Defender security settings management exclusive precedence over Group Policy, Configuration Manager, third-party,

keyChanges.title: Client-driven compliance reevaluation is documented as a Windows preview
keyChanges.detail: Supported Windows devices can detect certain local state changes—including device configuration and security-posture changes—and proactively request a compliance reevaluation instead of waiting for the next scheduled check-in. Administrators should account for this alternate evaluation timing when interpreting compliance results; the supplied evidence labels the capability preview and does not establish general availability.

keyChanges.title: Custom compliance guidance adds macOS Bash scripts and strict execution requirements
keyChanges.detail: The custom compliance discovery-script procedure now documents macOS alongside Linux and Windows. macOS scripts use Bash, must run in 10 minutes or less, include a valid shebang, be UTF-8 encoded without a BOM, and return exit code 0 for success or a non-zero code for failure. This is a documentation expansion; the supplied diff does not establish a new service rollout.

keyChanges.title: macOS compliance guidance warns that password requirements expire every device account
keyChanges.detail: The macOS compliance reference now warns that requiring a password in a compliance policy automatically expires the existing password for all accounts on the device, including accounts created by LAPS and Platform SSO. It recommends managing device passwords through a settings catalog policy with Change At Next Auth configured to False. This is security guidance and a behavior clarification, not evidence that the service behavior newly changed.

2026-08.headline: Intune plans iOS/iPadOS 18 and macOS 15 floors as DDM guidance expands
2026-08.overview: August’s 1,727 records were dominated by Configuration Manager, including many metadata-only recategorizations, but the main administrator-facing changes were Intune’s planned Apple OS support updates, new Apple DDM App Settings guidance, and the September 2609 switch to the new single-device page. Firewall guidance also clarified a significant MDM reporting limitation. Other substantive additions covered TPM-backed Windows Autopilot device association and unattended Remote Help for Windows and Android. Configuration Manager’s most consequential exception was a security update requiring a site reset and manual secondary-site recovery.
2026-08.adminImpact: Inventory Apple device versions and plan upgrades before the support changes; also check the separate OS requirements called out for userless devices enrolled through Automated Device Enrollment. For Apple DDM App Settings, use the Settings catalog on supported supervised devices and migrate iOS Restrictions-profile app-launch settings deprecated by iOS 27. Set reporting expectations for MDM-managed Firewall Rules and ASR Rules: per-setting status requires devices enrolled with Defender for Endpoint security settings management. Update runbooks for the September 2609 device-page change. Configuration Manager teams on versions 2603, 2509, or 2503 with the required rollups should plan the site reset and secondary-site recovery. Use operatingSystemVersion for new assignment filters; existing‌

keyChanges.title: Intune plans an iOS/iPadOS 18 minimum after Apple’s 27 release
keyChanges.detail: Microsoft’s Message Center plan says Intune will require iOS/iPadOS 18 or later after Apple releases iOS/iPadOS 27 later this year. The notice calls for compatibility and Intune-report review and identifies separate OS requirements for userless devices enrolled through Automated Device Enrollment.

keyChanges.title: Intune support moves to macOS 15 and later after Golden Gate 27
keyChanges.detail: After macOS Golden Gate 27 releases, Intune will support macOS 15 and later. Existing devices on macOS 14.x or below remain enrolled, but new enrollments on those versions won’t be allowed.

keyChanges.title: Apple DDM guidance details supervised app and binary controls
keyChanges.detail: The new Intune page documents Apple DDM App Settings in the Settings catalog for supervised iOS/iPadOS 27+ and macOS 27+ devices, including allowed or denied apps, binaries, and managed-app allowances. Existing iOS app-launch restrictions in the Restrictions profile must be migrated because iOS 27 deprecates those settings.

keyChanges.title: MDM Firewall and ASR policies provide policy-level reporting only
keyChanges.detail: Updated Firewall guidance says per-setting reporting is available for most Endpoint Security policies, but Firewall Rules and Attack Surface Reduction Rules managed through MDM report only policy-level status. Per-setting status requires devices enrolled with Defender for Endpoint security settings management.

keyChanges.title: The new Intune single-device page becomes default in September 2609
keyChanges.detail: The new consolidated device-management page will become the default view in the September 2609 release and replace the legacy page. All management features remain, but administrators should update internal documentation and familiarize support teams with the new interface.

2026-09.headline: Intune’s Windows Health Attestation migration requires Azure endpoint access by early 2027
2026-09.overview: September’s most consequential Intune change is the planned migration of Windows Health Attestation compliance evaluation for Windows 11 from Device Health Attestation to Microsoft Azure Attestation. The service-side migration is automatic, but affected environments need network access to Azure Attestation endpoints. Intune also gained more granular Windows Autopatch approval and reporting controls, while Security Copilot became included with Microsoft 365 E5 and E7 plans. Most remaining activity was Configuration Manager documentation maintenance, with meaningful 2609 guidance covering SQL prerequisites and the removal of Asset Intelligence reporting.
2026-09.adminImpact: Prioritize Azure Attestation endpoint access for Windows 11 devices using health-based compliance policies. Review Windows Autopatch approval, deferral, pause, and reporting options during its September 1–October 15 rollout. For Configuration Manager 2609 plans, validate SQL Server and secondary-site Visual C++ prerequisites and assess dependencies on Asset Intelligence reports. Microsoft 365 E5/E7 organizations receive Security Copilot, monthly Security Compute Units, and developer tools without a new purchase or required action.

keyChanges.title: Windows Health Attestation is moving to Microsoft Azure Attestation
keyChanges.detail: Intune plans to migrate Windows Health Attestation compliance evaluation for Windows 11 from the Device Health Attestation service to Microsoft Azure Attestation by early 2027. The migration occurs automatically on the service side, but organizations must provide network access to Azure Attestation endpoints or health-based compliance evaluation can fail.

keyChanges.title: Windows Autopatch adds granular approval and recovery-update controls
keyChanges.detail: Rolling out from September 1 through October 15, 2026, the enhancements add customizable automatic or manual approvals, deferral settings, update pausing, and per-device reporting for Windows quality, .NET Framework, and quick machine recovery updates.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager 2609 guidance raises the SQL Server support floor
keyChanges.detail: The updated support guidance marks SQL Server 2016 and SQL Server 2016 Express as deprecated in version 2609. SQL Server editions earlier than SQL Server 2017 CU2 must be upgraded before installing or updating to 2609, and the Visual C++ Redistributable on secondary sites must also be updated.

keyChanges.title: Configuration Manager 2609 removes documented Asset Intelligence reporting
keyChanges.detail: The updated operations guidance says that, starting in version 2609, the Catalog Synchronization and Inventoried Software Status sections and Asset Intelligence reports are removed. Procedures on the page apply to version 2603 and earlier, so administrators should review reporting dependencies before upgrading.

keyChanges.title: Security Copilot is included with Microsoft 365 E5 and E7
keyChanges.detail: Security Copilot is now included in Microsoft 365 E5 and E7 plans, with monthly Security Compute Units, developer tools, and agents integrated across Defender, Entra, Intune, Purview, and the Security Copilot portal. No purchase or administrator action is required for the included capability; additional paid features remain optional.

2026-10.headline: Endpoint Privilege Management documents controlled network changes for standard Windows users
2026-10.overview: October’s clearest administrator-facing development is new Endpoint Privilege Management guidance for an Elevation system settings policy. It allows standard Windows users to change IPv4, IPv6, and DNS settings under confirmation, business-justification, Windows-authentication, or combined controls, with an EPM elevation settings policy enabled. Intune’s In Development page also lists Apple OS 27 DDM inventory data, MEFERI OEMConfig support, planned removal of legacy Apple MDM software-update workloads, and two Administrator protection settings for Windows 11 24H2 and 25H2. Android reset guidance and Advanced Analytics schema limitations were also made more explicit. The Managed Home Screen edit only changes authoring metadata and wording around excluding apps from the silence setting.
2026-10.adminImpact: Administrators designing delegated network changes should enable the required EPM elevation settings policy and select the appropriate confirmation, justification, and authentication controls. The In Development entries are planning signals; the supplied update gives no action or deadline. For Android 15 reset workflows, account for the configured Factory reset protection emails setting and required Google account re-entry. Analytics consumers should not expect ICCID on Windows or SimInfo for Android Enterprise personally owned devices with a work profile.

keyChanges.title: EPM documents an elevation policy for controlled IPv4, IPv6, and DNS changes
keyChanges.detail: The new Endpoint Privilege Management guidance describes allowing standard Windows users to change IPv4, IPv6, and DNS settings. Administrators can require confirmation, business justification, Windows authentication, or both; devices also need an enabled EPM elevation settings policy.

keyChanges.title: Intune’s development roadmap lists Apple, Android, and Windows administration changes
keyChanges.detail: The In Development page now lists Apple OS 27 DDM inventory data, MEFERI OEMConfig support for Android Enterprise, removal of legacy Apple MDM software-update workloads, and two Administrator protection settings for Windows 11 24H2 and 25H2. No action or deadline is stated.

keyChanges.title: Android reset guidance defines the Factory reset protection emails behavior
keyChanges.detail: The documentation states that a Settings reset doesn’t enforce factory reset protection when Factory reset protection emails is Not configured. On Android 15 devices with a configured Google account email, that account must be re-entered after the reset.

keyChanges.title: Advanced Analytics schema guidance excludes ICCID on Windows
keyChanges.detail: The schema documentation now states that ICCID isn’t supported on Windows. It also continues to identify SimInfo as unsupported for Android Enterprise personally owned devices with a work profile.
